advice-32ebff8060db05d447ff2319.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-32ebff8060db05d447ff2319.body:
Hardship can hurt a good person, but it cannot make them bad: moral evil cannot coexist with virtue.
Seneca

advice-1ea1d09bfb56d4aa4304e7d4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1ea1d09bfb56d4aa4304e7d4.body:
(Adversity as training in virtue) God bears a fatherly mind towards good men, and loves them in a manly spirit.
Seneca

advice-1d3d3385366f9578f6718f29.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1d3d3385366f9578f6718f29.body:
(Courage in facing adverse fortune) Behold a sight worthy to be viewed by a god interested in his own work, behold a pair worthy of a god, a brave man matched with evil fortune, especially if he himself has given the challenge.
Seneca

advice-147d2352b9702cabe0292559.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-147d2352b9702cabe0292559.body:
(Adversity as training in virtue) I think you unhappy because you never have been unhappy: you have passed through your life without meeting an antagonist: no one will know your powers, not even you yourself.
Seneca

advice-4e2f3b0470da917204267fdf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4e2f3b0470da917204267fdf.body:
(Excessive comfort and the weakening of character) While all excesses are hurtful, excess of comfort is the most hurtful of all; it affects the brain; it leads men’s minds into vain imaginings; it spreads a thick cloud over the boundaries of truth and falsehood.
Seneca

advice-dd3f0e1fb2bc7c9be851dbc8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dd3f0e1fb2bc7c9be851dbc8.body:
(Adversity as training in virtue) The gods deal with good men according to the same rule as schoolmasters with their pupils, who exact most labour from those of whom they have the surest hopes.
Seneca

advice-e6edd04c93b0f741e2257624.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e6edd04c93b0f741e2257624.body:
(Habit turns hardship into an ordinary way of life) There is no unhappiness in what use has made part of one’s nature: by degrees men find pleasure in doing what they were first driven to do by necessity.
Seneca

advice-42686efcab6b46989b069899.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-42686efcab6b46989b069899.body:
(The virtuous person's moral invulnerability) The wise man is safe, and no injury or insult can touch him.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-72321aa29548139c069ae85e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-72321aa29548139c069ae85e.body:
(The virtuous person's moral invulnerability) Just as sacred things escape from the hands of men, and no injury is done to the godhead by those who destroy temples and melt down images, so whoever attempts to treat the wise man with impertinence, insolence, or scorn, does so in vain.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-8000969aeb9447cede5c3595.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8000969aeb9447cede5c3595.body:
(The virtuous person's moral invulnerability) Now wisdom leaves no room for evil; to it, the only evil is baseness, which cannot enter into the place already occupied by virtue and honour.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-654e972a430f1b20e670287b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-654e972a430f1b20e670287b.body:
(The virtuous person's moral invulnerability) Virtue is free, inviolable, not to be moved, not to be shaken, and so hardened against misfortunes that she cannot be bent, let alone overcome by them.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-12e02db9e47bc157667ec919.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-12e02db9e47bc157667ec919.body:
(The virtuous person's moral invulnerability) The wise man therefore can lose nothing of whose loss he will be sensible, for he is the property of virtue alone, from whom he never can be taken away.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-70ddc9fb51fb68af148abc6d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-70ddc9fb51fb68af148abc6d.body:
(The virtuous person's moral invulnerability) Now wickedness is not stronger than virtue; therefore the wise man cannot be hurt.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-e7dd38d19cea3f77d7a848d1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e7dd38d19cea3f77d7a848d1.body:
(Peace among the virtuous and mutual harm among the vicious) Good men are at peace among themselves; bad ones are equally mischievous to the good and to one another.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-79640da1feba5cb16872ca84.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-79640da1feba5cb16872ca84.body:
(Malicious intent whether or not harm succeeds) A man is no less a brigand because his sword becomes entangled in his victim’s clothes and misses its mark.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-6b64db01c4f42783c6ecbf13.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6b64db01c4f42783c6ecbf13.body:
(The sage; true good cannot be received from the vicious) The wise man lacks nothing which he can accept by way of a present, and the bad man can bestow nothing that is worthy of the wise man’s acceptance; for he must possess it before he can bestow it, and he possesses nothing which the wise man would rejoice to have handed over to him.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-2af31aba7b0db1c3cf38d0cd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2af31aba7b0db1c3cf38d0cd.body:
(The virtuous person's moral invulnerability) Consequently, no one can do either harm or good to the wise man, because divine things neither want help nor are capable of being hurt; and the wise man is near, indeed very near to the gods, being like a god in every respect save that he is mortal.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-7a6a5864fe523c74404bd8de.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7a6a5864fe523c74404bd8de.body:
(The virtuous person's moral invulnerability) He who, trusting to reason, passes through human affairs with godlike mind, has no quarter from which he can receive injury.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-a0e8b3bf541f11efa4a27090.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a0e8b3bf541f11efa4a27090.body:
(The sage's tranquility; injury would mean losing that peace) Now, the man free from mistakes has no disturbance; he is master of himself, enjoying a deep and tranquil repose of mind; for if an injury reaches him it moves and rouses him.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-f119974ad2a88ab7edd215cf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f119974ad2a88ab7edd215cf.body:
(The sage and fighters who win through endurance) Think that the wise man belongs to this class, that of men who, by long and faithful practice, have acquired strength to endure and tire out all the violence of their enemies.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-e210ea8792c2ce4905cc3baf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e210ea8792c2ce4905cc3baf.body:
(On pain that does not destroy reason or dignity) Some other things strike the wise man, though they may not shake his principles, such as bodily pain and weakness, the loss of friends and children, and the ruin of his country in war-time.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-ae232f15a2641b32e93257e5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ae232f15a2641b32e93257e5.body:
(The virtuous person's moral invulnerability) It is from your own weakness that you form your idea of his colossal mind, and when you have thought how much you yourselves could endure to suffer, you place the limit of the wise man’s endurance a little way beyond that.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-baff43434050d6ed50dac4c9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-baff43434050d6ed50dac4c9.body:
(The virtuous person's moral invulnerability) He who says that the wise man can bear this and cannot bear that, and restrains his magnanimity within certain limits, does wrong; for Fortune overcomes us unless she is entirely overcome.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-7138074d3b3ce6ed304a9e69.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7138074d3b3ce6ed304a9e69.body:
(Consoling the offended without personal revenge) Let wounded spirits, then, console themselves with this reflexion, that, even though our easy temper may have neglected to revenge itself, nevertheless that there will be some one who will punish the impertinent, proud, and insulting man, for these are vices which he never confines to one victim or one single offensive act.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-bcc0aa45dc45cac11c1a9040.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bcc0aa45dc45cac11c1a9040.body:
(High standing brings an obligation to show courage) The nobler a man is by birth, by reputation, or by inheritance, the more bravely he should bear himself, remembering that the tallest men stand in the front rank in battle.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.work: On the Firmness of the Wise Man

advice-3a7d6ffe1d6d73bd80578300.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3a7d6ffe1d6d73bd80578300.body:
(The Stoic distinction between human anger and animal impulses) We must admit, however, that neither wild beasts nor any other creature except man is subject to anger: for, whilst anger is the foe of reason, it nevertheless does not arise in any place where reason cannot dwell.
Seneca

advice-25744dd9ed862a8696d9b2c9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-25744dd9ed862a8696d9b2c9.body:
(The Stoic distinction between human anger and animal impulses) Wild beasts have impulses, fury, cruelty, combativeness: they have not anger any more than they have luxury: yet they indulge in some pleasures with less self-control than human beings.
Seneca

advice-94d05825b46c1423735afb4b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-94d05825b46c1423735afb4b.body:
(The Stoic distinction between human anger and animal impulses) Dumb creatures have not human feelings, but have certain impulses which resemble them: for if it were not so, if they could feel love and hate, they would likewise be capable of friendship and enmity, of disagreement and agreement.
Seneca

advice-136e24b64114001bb3dbd20d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-136e24b64114001bb3dbd20d.body:
(Anger as an opponent of human nature) Man’s nature is not, therefore, desirous of inflicting punishment; neither, therefore, is anger in accordance with man’s nature, because that is desirous of inflicting punishment.
Seneca

advice-b053f99a8ed31ae204b46b70.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b053f99a8ed31ae204b46b70.body:
(Losing self-control under the rule of passion) So, also, the mind, when it has abandoned itself to anger, love, or any other passion, is unable to check itself: its own weight and the downward tendency of vices must needs carry the man off and hurl him into the lowest depth.
Seneca

advice-1dc4008207d3d182b078fe44.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1dc4008207d3d182b078fe44.body:
(Reason and virtue without the aid of vices) May virtue never come to such a pass, that reason should fly for aid to vices!
Seneca

advice-9d6c6c3729624c57faae658e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9d6c6c3729624c57faae658e.body:
(When reason relies on anger, fear, or greed) The mind can find no safe repose there, it must needs be shaken and tempest-tossed if it be safe only because of its own defects, if it cannot be brave without anger, diligent without greed, quiet without fear: such is the despotism under which a man must live if he becomes the slave of a passion.
Seneca

advice-be2a94c912ed6b6c52fa25b3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-be2a94c912ed6b6c52fa25b3.body:
(Fulfilling one's duty without anger or fear) The good man will do his duty without disturbance or fear, and he will perform the duty of a good man, so as to do nothing unworthy of a man.
Seneca

advice-4f9871c4de61e17e9a1a735e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4f9871c4de61e17e9a1a735e.body:
(Fulfilling one's duty without anger or fear) To feel anger on behalf of one’s friends does not show a loving, but a weak mind: it is admirable and worthy conduct to stand forth as the defender of one’s parents, children, friends, and countrymen, at the call of duty itself, acting of one’s own free will, forming a deliberate judgment, and looking forward to the future, not in an impulsive, frenzied fashion.
Seneca

advice-93cb9992b0ff7929918fa133.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-93cb9992b0ff7929918fa133.body:
(Anger as a substitute for courage rather than its aid) No man becomes braver through anger, except one who without anger would not have been brave at all: anger does not therefore come to assist courage, but to take its place.
Seneca

advice-abbf9a384d81ff0719f994e8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-abbf9a384d81ff0719f994e8.body:
(Punishment aimed at reform, without anger) Nothing becomes one who inflicts punishment less than anger, because the punishment has all the more power to work reformation if the sentence be pronounced with deliberate judgment.
Seneca

advice-e6de1165f025941d9c1bc008.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e6de1165f025941d9c1bc008.body:
(Punishment aimed at reform, without anger) We do not, therefore, need an angry chastiser to punish the erring and wicked: for since anger is a crime of the mind, it is not right that sins should be punished by sin.
Seneca

advice-3a02f044b195759a06d25c88.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3a02f044b195759a06d25c88.body:
(Reason and virtue without the aid of vices) We have no need of external weapons, nature has equipped us sufficiently by giving us reason.
Seneca

advice-4e33a6ec525a46973b472e36.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4e33a6ec525a46973b472e36.body:
(Reason's consistency and anger's instability) Passion soon cools, whereas reason is always consistent: yet even in cases where anger has continued to burn, it often happens that although there may be many who deserve to die, yet after the death of two or three it ceases to slay.
Seneca

advice-b1842e276e88091f66bd175f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b1842e276e88091f66bd175f.body:
(Punishment aimed at reform, without anger) You see how free from any mental disturbance a man ought to be who has to weigh and consider all this, when he deals with a matter which ought to be handled with the utmost care, I mean, the power of life and death.
Seneca

advice-e07625b8126ecf20ea8cc077.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e07625b8126ecf20ea8cc077.body:
(The false grandeur of anger and luxury) Anger has no ground to stand upon, and does not rise from a firm and enduring foundation, but is a windy, empty quality, as far removed from true magnanimity as fool-hardiness from courage, boastfulness from confidence, gloom from austerity, cruelty from strictness.
Seneca

advice-2f956c08767e28682a5706a9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2f956c08767e28682a5706a9.body:
(The false grandeur of anger and luxury) There is therefore nothing great or noble in anger, even when it seems to be powerful and to contemn both gods and men alike.
Seneca

advice-f895edb81b65e7e90885a194.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f895edb81b65e7e90885a194.body:
(The false grandeur of anger and luxury) Any one who thinks that anger produces greatness of mind, would think that luxury produces it: such a man wishes to rest on ivory, to be clothed with purple, and roofed with gold; to remove lands, embank seas, hasten the course of rivers, suspend woods in the air.
Seneca

advice-79f47f234b86d6fca194a155.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-79f47f234b86d6fca194a155.body:
(On wisdom as a source of calm) Virtue alone is lofty and sublime, nor is anything great which is not at the same time tranquil.
Seneca

advice-f9a75067b70e6023f43f66f3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f9a75067b70e6023f43f66f3.body:
(The first mental stir and uncontrolled passion) A man may think himself injured, may wish to avenge his wrongs, and then may be persuaded by some reason or other to give up his intention and calm down: I do not call that anger, it is an emotion of the mind which is under the control of reason.
Seneca

advice-4a9b554803aa0334c8ddaaf1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4a9b554803aa0334c8ddaaf1.body:
(The mind's role in movements of fear and anger) There never has been any doubt that fear produces flight, and anger a rush forward; consider, therefore, whether you suppose that anything can be either sought or avoided without the participation of the mind.
Seneca

advice-55324fdf695b80b38d8bea0a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-55324fdf695b80b38d8bea0a.body:
(The first mental stir and uncontrolled passion) Furthermore, that you may know in what manner passions begin and swell and gain spirit, learn that the first emotion is involuntary, and is, as it were, a preparation for a passion, and a threatening of one.
Seneca

advice-b8e6b0cfea83c6528761db88.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b8e6b0cfea83c6528761db88.body:
(Virtue's joy and anger's sorrowful outcome) To rejoice and be glad is the proper and natural function of virtue: it is as much beneath her dignity to be angry, as to mourn: now, sorrow is the companion of anger, and all anger ends in sorrow, either from remorse or from failure.
Seneca

advice-42e27ceecbaff04f2f9776a6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-42e27ceecbaff04f2f9776a6.body:
(Why the sage does not rage at every vice) The wise man will never cease to be angry, if he once begins, so full is every place of vices and crimes.
Seneca

advice-bb0976e94ba99dc25df81076.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bb0976e94ba99dc25df81076.body:
(The multitude of vices and the limits of punishment) More evil is done than can be healed by punishment: men seem engaged in a vast race of wickedness.
Seneca

advice-f4817d8141e0c33909fc94f6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f4817d8141e0c33909fc94f6.body:
(Why the sage does not rage at every vice) If you want the wise man to be as angry as the atrocity of men’s crimes requires, he must not merely be angry, but must go mad with rage.
Seneca

advice-3e3de5d06826f45afd134ad2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3e3de5d06826f45afd134ad2.body:
(Why the sage does not rage at every vice) If you are angry with young and old men because they do wrong, you will be angry with infants also, for they soon will do wrong.
Seneca

advice-b19c9f7133a22558eaeda448.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b19c9f7133a22558eaeda448.body:
(Why the sage does not rage at every vice) The wise man will not be angry with sinners.
Seneca

advice-11c05d2d51719f378375438b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-11c05d2d51719f378375438b.body:
(Allowance for natural imperfections) No one is angry when nature excuses a defect.
Seneca

advice-f734a6b9b1a8b605e065fab2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f734a6b9b1a8b605e065fab2.body:
(Anger: a frightening mask without real strength) So, too, anger is in itself hideous and by no means to be feared; yet it is feared by many, just as a hideous mask is feared by children.
Seneca

advice-1e56042d836728a5298e5351.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1e56042d836728a5298e5351.body:
(The possibility of correcting vice and our natural leaning toward goodness) The evils from which we suffer are curable, and since we were born with a natural bias towards good, nature herself will help us if we try to amend our lives.
Seneca

advice-6f6d929bb75b0e7b48c0eff0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6f6d929bb75b0e7b48c0eff0.body:
(Reason and virtue without the aid of vices) The wise man will do his duty in all things without the help of any evil passion, and will use no auxiliaries which require watching narrowly lest they get beyond his control.
Seneca

advice-594d3d2782c29ea005bf9c5e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-594d3d2782c29ea005bf9c5e.body:
(Inspiring fear without becoming angry oneself) We must sometimes apply fear to persons upon whom reason makes no impression: yet to be angry is of no more use than to grieve or to be afraid.
Seneca

advice-31ccdda49bed548c3b9dfb6a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-31ccdda49bed548c3b9dfb6a.body:
(Firmness without cruelty or defenselessness) A man ought to be neither robber nor victim, neither tender-hearted nor cruel.
Seneca

advice-e77c8ba1181bde3dba48243f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e77c8ba1181bde3dba48243f.body:
(Forceful action without anger) Let the wise man be moderate, and when things have to be done somewhat briskly, let him call force, not anger, to his aid.
Seneca

advice-28bd0a8a227b0be3af941f43.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-28bd0a8a227b0be3af941f43.body:
(Habits that increase irritability) Habit of mind has very great power, and, if it be harsh, increases the disorder.
Seneca

advice-0adc020f31b9a6a61d3b1194.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0adc020f31b9a6a61d3b1194.body:
(Moderate recreation as a means of mental balance) Games also will be useful: for moderate pleasure relieves the mind and brings it to a proper balance.
Seneca

advice-f7b9ddb335f543259a6d1ae8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f7b9ddb335f543259a6d1ae8.body:
(Teaching respect for truth) Let a child hear the truth, and sometimes fear it: let him always reverence it.
Seneca

advice-4c3c21c98c175a6298110fa4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4c3c21c98c175a6298110fa4.body:
(The educator as a model for a child's character) It will be advantageous to furnish boys with even-tempered teachers and paedagogi: what is soft and unformed clings to what is near, and takes its shape: the habits of young men reproduce those of their nurses and paedagogi.
Seneca

advice-569c1fa5beb8f173d567488e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-569c1fa5beb8f173d567488e.body:
(Excessive comfort and the weakening of character) A man must be in a miserably bad state of health if he shrinks from a gentle breath of wind; his eyes must be diseased if they are distressed by the sight of white clothing; he must be broken down with debauchery if he feels pain at seeing another man work.
Seneca

advice-27d2e82b9c15086e6a9fc05f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-27d2e82b9c15086e6a9fc05f.body:
(Excessive comfort and the weakening of character) Nothing, therefore, nourishes anger more than excessive and dissatisfied luxury: the mind ought to be hardened by rough treatment, so as not to feel any blow that is not severe.
Seneca

advice-bbdd6f38cdcd78f0d86cb8cb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bbdd6f38cdcd78f0d86cb8cb.body:
(Understanding others' errors by acknowledging one's own) Some one will be said to have spoken ill of you: think whether you did not first speak ill of him: think of how many persons you have yourself spoken ill.
Seneca

advice-35abe8779b4580cccbdad47b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-35abe8779b4580cccbdad47b.body:
(Moral double standards) The same man who lusts after everyone’s wife, and thinks that a woman’s belonging to someone else is a sufficient reason for adoring her, will not allow any one else to look at his own wife.
Seneca

advice-324b38a7dc988e664b12a010.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-324b38a7dc988e664b12a010.body:
(Moral double standards) No man expects such exact fidelity as a traitor: the perjurer himself takes vengeance of him who breaks his word: the pettifogging lawyer is most indignant at an action being brought against him: the man who is reckless of his own chastity cannot endure any attempt upon that of his slaves.
Seneca

advice-0f7a805e89d1d2af0253083e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0f7a805e89d1d2af0253083e.body:
(Delay as a remedy for anger) The greatest remedy for anger is delay: beg anger to grant you this at the first, not in order that it may pardon the offence, but that it may form a right judgment about it: if it delays, it will come to an end.
Seneca

advice-7d27c1a245605dd50a524b6a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7d27c1a245605dd50a524b6a.body:
(Hearing both sides before punishment) You would allow both sides to be heard: you would allow them time: you would not despatch the matter at one sitting, because the oftener it is handled the more distinctly the truth appears.
Seneca

advice-32189afe50736e1bf40cf4ed.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-32189afe50736e1bf40cf4ed.body:
(Distrust of secret accusations) The man who will tell you nothing save in secret hardly tells you anything at all.
Seneca

advice-3ca218dd54f9b3ad720f3321.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3ca218dd54f9b3ad720f3321.body:
(The futility of anger at an irrational offender) Suppose that it is a dumb animal or as stupid as a dumb animal: then, if you are angry with it, you will make yourself like it.
Seneca

advice-f6e17d5583f0e2916871a9cb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f6e17d5583f0e2916871a9cb.body:
(Realistic expectations of a bad character) Think of everything, expect everything: even with men of good character something queer will crop up; human nature produces minds that are treacherous, ungrateful, greedy, and impious: when you are considering what any man’s morals may be, think what those of mankind are.
Seneca

advice-81c7a7caba391b05c417b36d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-81c7a7caba391b05c417b36d.body:
(Human kindness opposed to doing harm) Think, above all, how base and hateful is the power of doing mischief, and how unnatural in man, by whose kindness even fierce animals are rendered tame.
Seneca

advice-e993f336b8bbbbfe8adad13f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e993f336b8bbbbfe8adad13f.body:
(On cooperation and human community) As all the limbs act in unison, because it is the interest of the whole body to keep each one of them safe, so men should spare one another, because they are born for society.
Seneca

advice-05ef5b8f1365ced947b8bab3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-05ef5b8f1365ced947b8bab3.body:
(Forgiveness turning opponents into friends) Let us also reflect, how much credit the tale of our forgiveness will confer upon us, how many men may be made into valuable friends by forgiveness.
Seneca

advice-9b721cfd24b21f960f5261b6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9b721cfd24b21f960f5261b6.body:
(Ending a quarrel by returning a favor) If any one is angry with you, meet his anger by returning benefits for it: a quarrel which is only taken up on one side falls to the ground: it takes two men to fight.
Seneca

advice-c55bdf52e7acaa686d709757.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c55bdf52e7acaa686d709757.body:
(The mind's strength lies in controlling its movements) The only swiftness of which men approve is that which, when bidden, checks itself and proceeds no further, and which can be guided, and reduced from a run to a walk: we know that the sinews are diseased when they move against our will.
Seneca

advice-298a7f1380cb53eac560e050.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-298a7f1380cb53eac560e050.body:
(The mind's strength lies in controlling its movements) A man must be either aged or weakly who runs when he wants to walk: let us think that those are the most powerful and the soundest operations of our minds, which act under our own control, not at their own caprice.
Seneca

advice-1434c189b2b9324f9ef220cc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1434c189b2b9324f9ef220cc.body:
(Destructive and dangerous anger) Nothing, however, will be of so much service as to consider, first, the hideousness, and, secondly, the danger of anger.
Seneca

advice-8c7daaa1fd8396ca1abb7bdf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8c7daaa1fd8396ca1abb7bdf.body:
(Destructive and dangerous anger) No way leads more swiftly to madness: many have, consequently, remained always in the frenzy of anger, and, having once lost their reason, have never recovered it.
Seneca

advice-360acce7811643eec933e15e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-360acce7811643eec933e15e.body:
(Destructive and dangerous anger) Other passions gain a footing in the mind by slow degrees: anger’s conquest is sudden and complete, and, moreover, it makes all other passions subservient to itself.
Seneca

advice-49ae3cb555d68c1cb657e602.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-49ae3cb555d68c1cb657e602.body:
(Greed accumulates, anger squanders) Avarice scrapes together and amasses riches for some better man to use: anger spends money; few can indulge in it for nothing.
Seneca

advice-c8f387b27cab36f867f5794c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c8f387b27cab36f867f5794c.body:
(Destructive and dangerous anger) It is worse than luxury, because luxury enjoys its own pleasure, while anger enjoys another’s pain.
Seneca

advice-22c77d43e844e0ea4eade0a2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-22c77d43e844e0ea4eade0a2.body:
(Destructive and dangerous anger) Nothing is more dangerous than jealousy: it is produced by anger.
Seneca

advice-502dc929b7d4825a7f280636.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-502dc929b7d4825a7f280636.body:
(Destructive and dangerous anger) Nothing is more ruinous than war: it is the outcome of powerful men’s anger; and even the anger of humble private persons, though without arms or armies, is nevertheless war.
Seneca

advice-0f20f3e384b95fe1cd4e08c2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0f20f3e384b95fe1cd4e08c2.body:
(Excessive busyness as a source of irritation) A man’s day, if he is engaged in many various occupations, never passes so happily that no man or no thing should give rise to some offence which makes the mind ripe for anger.
Seneca

advice-0c79e78d764fe3264cd6452e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0c79e78d764fe3264cd6452e.body:
(Undertakings proportionate to one's abilities) Be assured that the same rule applies both to public and private life: simple and manageable undertakings proceed according to the pleasure of the person in charge of them, but enormous ones, beyond his capacity to manage, are not easily undertaken.
Seneca

advice-151ce176dd38405ba8898959.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-151ce176dd38405ba8898959.body:
(Undertakings proportionate to one's abilities) Let our undertakings, therefore, be neither petty nor yet presumptuous and reckless: let our hopes not range far from home: let us attempt nothing which if we succeed will make us astonished at our success.
Seneca

advice-cbcfb62d0e5251610a683d2f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cbcfb62d0e5251610a683d2f.body:
(An accommodating circle: respite for anger, risk of indulgence) If, then, we are conscious of an irascible disposition, let us especially choose for our friends those who will look and speak as we do: they will pamper us and lead us into a bad habit of listening to nothing that does not please us, but it will be good to give our anger respite and repose.
Seneca

advice-8b47a346b7c3a5e4f68b9846.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8b47a346b7c3a5e4f68b9846.body:
(Not seeking grounds for offense in others' gossip) He who seeks to know what is said about him, who digs up spiteful tales even if they were told in secret, is himself the destroyer of his own peace of mind.
Seneca

advice-079b78486210f230d1dbedb9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-079b78486210f230d1dbedb9.body:
(Viewing a quarrel from the other person's position) Let us put ourselves in the place of him with whom we are angry: at present an overweening conceit of our own importance makes us prone to anger, and we are quite willing to do to others what we cannot endure should be done to ourselves.
Seneca

advice-acb1f2f9b3c95fc0320242e7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-acb1f2f9b3c95fc0320242e7.body:
(Delay as a remedy for anger) No one will postpone his anger: yet delay is the best remedy for it, because it allows its first glow to subside, and gives time for the cloud which darkens the mind either to disperse or at any rate to become less dense.
Seneca

advice-91008882d6ccaee81480e193.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-91008882d6ccaee81480e193.body:
(Delay as a remedy for anger) Even if you gain nothing by your adjournment, still what you do after it will appear to be the result of mature deliberation, not of anger.
Seneca

advice-4aa09eaac03c2a7b01408efc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4aa09eaac03c2a7b01408efc.body:
(Finding the truth after regaining calm) If you want to find out the truth about anything, commit the task to time: nothing can be accurately discerned at a time of disturbance.
Seneca

advice-dd84d0b1a5d639bc6d8f3ce1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dd84d0b1a5d639bc6d8f3ce1.body:
(Self-control beginning with restraining anger) Fight hard with yourself and if you cannot conquer anger, do not let it conquer you: you have begun to get the better of it if it does not show itself, if it is not given vent.
Seneca

advice-e6bbe6d3a26a7b4d1f8077f6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e6bbe6d3a26a7b4d1f8077f6.body:
(A ruler's anger and the danger to his power) All is lost when a man’s position enables him to carry out whatever anger prompts him to do; nor can power long endure if it be exercised to the injury of many, for it becomes endangered as soon as common fear draws together those who bewail themselves separately.
Seneca

advice-f6d2180078aef91adf8d3c0f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f6d2180078aef91adf8d3c0f.body:
(Understanding others' errors by acknowledging one's own) Let us look back upon our own youth, and think how often we then were too slothful in our duty, too impudent in our speech, too intemperate in our cups.
Seneca

advice-e84845bfcc90fe0bb53b6857.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e84845bfcc90fe0bb53b6857.body:
(Understanding others' errors by acknowledging one's own) Every one of us therefore will find in his own breast the vice which he blames in another.
Seneca

advice-d76b99b1b8800c23a58a9a4c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d76b99b1b8800c23a58a9a4c.body:
(Mutual forgiveness among imperfect people) Let us therefore be more gentle one to another: we are bad men, living among bad men: there is only one thing which can afford us peace, and that is to agree to forgive one another.
Seneca

advice-817e6cf1626236b8b981f46c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-817e6cf1626236b8b981f46c.body:
(Judging one's character rather than a single day) Do not form your judgment by one hour, or one day: consider the whole tendency of your mind: even though you have done no evil, yet you are capable of doing it.
Seneca

advice-fb7df496675f60e17ffc715e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fb7df496675f60e17ffc715e.body:
(Different reasons to refrain from quarreling) Let different qualities in different people keep us from quarrelling with them: let us fear to be angry with some, feel ashamed of being angry with others, and disdain to be angry with others.
Seneca

advice-10e376b4a51421fbbe6f930f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-10e376b4a51421fbbe6f930f.body:
(Preparation makes adversity easier to bear) The mind is strong enough to bear those evils for which it is prepared.
Seneca

advice-ccb36e09af6a18ec67a5de43.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ccb36e09af6a18ec67a5de43.body:
(Destructive and dangerous anger) There is, then, nothing useful in that hideous and destructive passion of anger, but on the contrary, every kind of evil, fire and sword.
Seneca

advice-78bc4b67d06a283ed992c04e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-78bc4b67d06a283ed992c04e.body:
(Life's brevity as an argument against anger) Let us keep our tempers in spite of losses, wrongs, abuse or sarcasm, and let us endure with magnanimity our shortlived troubles: while we are considering what is due to ourselves, as the saying is, and worrying ourselves, death will be upon us.
Seneca

advice-6e0c2579fa3906e3233205cc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6e0c2579fa3906e3233205cc.body:
(Different means of persuasion: reason and authority) Some are guided by reason, others must be confronted with authority and the names of celebrated persons, whose brilliancy dazzles their mind and destroys their power of free judgment.
Seneca

advice-44476f33fd661305aaa8c1f4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-44476f33fd661305aaa8c1f4.body:
(The instability of Fortune's gifts) Whatever gift Fortune bestows upon a man, let him think while he enjoys it, that it will prove as fickle as the goddess from whom it came.
Seneca

advice-8d2859ae4669b9db34a17574.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8d2859ae4669b9db34a17574.body:
(Marcia: gratitude for the years with her deceased son) If, again, you admit that you have received much pleasure, it is your duty not to complain of that part which you have lost, but to return thanks for that which you have enjoyed.
Seneca

advice-2dac85b8d8c4ccb042c42b5e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2dac85b8d8c4ccb042c42b5e.body:
(Human life amid loss and uncertainty) You were born to lose others, to be lost, to hope, to fear, to destroy your own peace and that of others, to fear and yet to long for death, and, worst of all, never to know what your real position is.
Seneca

advice-c60088d2b26c5fe25d8b7760.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c60088d2b26c5fe25d8b7760.body:
(Death as the end of suffering and Fortune's power) Death is neither a good nor a bad thing, for that alone which is something can be a good or a bad thing: but that which is nothing, and reduces all things to nothing, does not hand us over to either fortune, because good and bad require some material to work upon.
Seneca

advice-cf71a57b945811413f687d1d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cf71a57b945811413f687d1d.body:
(Death as the end of suffering and Fortune's power) Fortune cannot take hold of that which Nature has let go, nor can a man be unhappy if he is nothing.
Seneca

advice-541b7584bdb97ba0fa3751ee.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-541b7584bdb97ba0fa3751ee.body:
(Death ends subjection and social humiliation) After Death no one acts any more at another’s bidding: in death no man suffers any more from the sense of his low position.
Seneca

advice-8b2d8744c611e51c3d33805e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8b2d8744c611e51c3d33805e.body:
(On the transience of human things) All human works are brief and fleeting; they take up no part whatever of infinite time.
Seneca

advice-74e8da9759d2dcd372488b7d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-74e8da9759d2dcd372488b7d.body:
(The span of life allotted by fate) To each man a varying length of days has been assigned: no one dies before his time, because he was not destined to live any longer than he did.
Seneca

advice-5a924fedb1dfec7cf3dd68a6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5a924fedb1dfec7cf3dd68a6.body:
(The span of life allotted by fate) Everyone’s end is fixed, and will always remain where it has been placed: neither industry nor favour will move it on any further.
Seneca

advice-00376ea3047711d87e656872.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-00376ea3047711d87e656872.body:
(The span of life allotted by fate) Prayers and endeavours are all in vain: each man will have as much life as his first day placed to his credit: from the time when he first saw the light he has entered on the path that leads to death, and is drawing nearer to his doom: those same years which were added to his youth were subtracted from his life.
Seneca

advice-3b2cdbd6765358134b0b4923.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3b2cdbd6765358134b0b4923.body:
(Life's successive stages as natural endings) We all fall into this mistake of supposing that it is only old men, already in the decline of life, who are drawing near to death, whereas our first infancy, our youth, indeed every time of life leads thither.
Seneca

advice-219c1acd85d094ee1adf676f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-219c1acd85d094ee1adf676f.body:
(Consolation in bereavement through life's instability) Nothing is so deceptive, nothing is so treacherous as human life; by Hercules, were it not given to men before they could form an opinion, no one would take it.
Seneca

advice-0fc8d084c621757aab700790.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0fc8d084c621757aab700790.body:
(Reasoned choice instead of imitating the majority) Now nothing gets us into greater troubles than our subservience to common rumour, and our habit of thinking that those things are best which are most generally received as such, of taking many counterfeits for truly good things, and of living not by reason but by imitation of others.
Seneca

advice-08ac7696b73889e680f4a562.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-08ac7696b73889e680f4a562.body:
(Reasoned choice instead of imitating the majority) Let us therefore inquire, not what is most commonly done, but what is best for us to do, and what will establish us in the possession of undying happiness, not what is approved of by the vulgar, the worst possible exponents of truth.
Seneca

advice-fccaed3ca5631d601d09bacd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fccaed3ca5631d601d09bacd.body:
(Seeking genuine inner goodness) Let us seek for some blessing, which does not merely look fine, but is sound and good throughout alike, and most beautiful in the parts which are least seen: let us unearth this.
Seneca

advice-643c8ec1a500a84aebe70bed.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-643c8ec1a500a84aebe70bed.body:
(A happy life according to nature) A happy life, therefore, is one which is in accordance with its own nature, and cannot be brought about unless in the first place the mind be sound and remain so without interruption, and next, be bold and vigorous, enduring all things with most admirable courage, suited to the times in which it lives, careful of the body and its appurtenances, yet not troublesomely careful.
Seneca

advice-f241bf2071afe1ecec99cce8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f241bf2071afe1ecec99cce8.body:
(On the soul submitting to pleasure and pain) See, on the other hand, how evil and guilty a slavery the man is forced to serve who is dominated in turn by pleasures and pains, those most untrustworthy and passionate of masters.
Seneca

advice-e2018e6e19a0847598e5f08b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e2018e6e19a0847598e5f08b.body:
(On well-being created by one's own character) The happy man, therefore, is he who can make a right judgment in all things: he is happy who in his present circumstances, whatever they may be, is satisfied and on friendly terms with the conditions of his life.
Seneca

advice-9cf6fd505d83e372edb17894.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9cf6fd505d83e372edb17894.body:
(On moral self-reliance) A man should be unbiassed and not to be conquered by external things: he ought to admire himself alone, to feel confidence in his own spirit, and so to order his life as to be ready alike for good or for bad fortune.
Seneca

advice-20c77c853220578f7095063c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-20c77c853220578f7095063c.body:
(Life's value is determined by its use) Life is long enough, if you know how to use it.
Seneca

sources.author: Seneca
sources.reference: De brevitate vitae, 2; source paragraph 1; sentence 2

advice-361b74b4b32bde8f3c3faf2d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-361b74b4b32bde8f3c3faf2d.body:
(The highest good as inner harmony of mind) You may, then, boldly declare that the highest good is singleness of mind: for where agreement and unity are, there must the virtues be: it is the vices that are at war one with another.
Seneca

advice-72a417a24349d32e8effdbca.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-72a417a24349d32e8effdbca.body:
(Virtue includes moderation) Too much pleasure is hurtful: but with virtue we need fear no excess of any kind, because moderation is contained in virtue herself.
Seneca

advice-ff2e4004d0accfd0141a8456.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ff2e4004d0accfd0141a8456.body:
(Virtue leads, pleasure obeys) Let virtue lead the way and bear the standard: we shall have pleasure for all that, but we shall be her masters and controllers; she may win some concessions from us, but will not force us to do anything.
Seneca

advice-5038c87e5febc4a599f9c678.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5038c87e5febc4a599f9c678.body:
(Devotion to pleasures weakens the fulfillment of duty) A man cannot be a good protector of his country, a good avenger of her wrongs, or a good defender of his friends, if he be inclined to pleasures.
Seneca

advice-163d831f75cecddceadbf5bd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-163d831f75cecddceadbf5bd.body:
(Envious criticism of another's virtue) You argue about the life and death of another, and yelp at the name of men whom some peculiarly noble quality has rendered great, just as tiny curs do at the approach of strangers: for it is to your interest that no one should appear to be good, as if virtue in another were a reproach to all your crimes.
Seneca

advice-23617e8d8e587798d3c057ff.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-23617e8d8e587798d3c057ff.body:
(Generosity to every person, including household slaves) Wherever there is a human being, there is an opportunity for a benefit: consequently, money may be distributed even within one’s own threshold, and a field may be found there for the practice of freehandedness, which is not so called because it is our duty towards free men, but because it takes its rise in a free-born mind.
Seneca

advice-6a049bd4261f4a344d7818f6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6a049bd4261f4a344d7818f6.body:
(Withdrawing from futile service to an irreparable state) If the state is so rotten as to be past helping, if evil has entire dominion over it, the wise man will not labour in vain or waste his strength in unprofitable efforts.
Seneca

advice-f3d908e512fd007d40676bc4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f3d908e512fd007d40676bc4.body:
(Helping people within one's available sphere of action) The duty of a man is to be useful to his fellow-men; if possible, to be useful to many of them; failing this, to be useful to a few; failing this, to be useful to his neighbours, and, failing them, to himself: for when he helps others, he advances the general interests of mankind.
Seneca

advice-455c5efc307dd92712128bee.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-455c5efc307dd92712128bee.body:
(Helping people within one's available sphere of action) Just as he who makes himself a worse man does harm not only to himself but to all those to whom he might have done good if he had made himself a better one, so he who deserves well of himself does good to others by the very fact that he is preparing what will be of service to them.
Seneca

advice-e0c9aa4b05d71f8ee7015ba6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e0c9aa4b05d71f8ee7015ba6.body:
(Contemplation and action according to nature) We have a habit of saying that the highest good is to live according to nature: now nature has produced us for both purposes, for contemplation and for action.
Seneca

advice-9cb50aa80c516678aa434918.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9cb50aa80c516678aa434918.body:
(Peace of mind) What you desire, to be undisturbed, is a great thing, nay, the greatest thing of all, and one which raises a man almost to the level of a god.
Seneca

advice-c2a6fcf5ee0b70bba672ec25.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c2a6fcf5ee0b70bba672ec25.body:
(Choosing carefully whom to give one's time) In all cases one should be careful in one’s choice of men, and see whether they be worthy of our bestowing a part of our life upon them, or whether we shall waste our own time and theirs also: for some even consider us to be in their debt because of our services to them.
Seneca

advice-997e64598522a239216bf0dc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-997e64598522a239216bf0dc.body:
(Choosing work suited to natural abilities) Isocrates laid hands upon Ephorus and led him away from the forum, thinking that he would be more usefully employed in compiling chronicles; for no good is done by forcing one’s mind to engage in uncongenial work: it is vain to struggle against Nature.
Seneca

advice-e2e809f3cd22cf89e8d07992.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e2e809f3cd22cf89e8d07992.body:
(The influence of friends' character) We should choose for our friends men who are, as far as possible, free from strong desires: for vices are contagious, and pass from a man to his neighbour, and injure those who touch them.
Seneca

advice-59793352bc20c1bfd4f23340.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-59793352bc20c1bfd4f23340.body:
(Simple living without ostentatious luxury) Let us then teach ourselves to be able to dine without all Rome to look on, to be the slaves of fewer slaves, to get clothes which fulfil their original purpose, and to live in a smaller house.
Seneca

advice-70caa371d202bf46bc8f4904.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-70caa371d202bf46bc8f4904.body:
(Simple living without ostentatious luxury) Let a man, then, obtain as many books as he wants, but none for show.
Seneca

advice-c4de1278b9a1833b50febd01.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c4de1278b9a1833b50febd01.body:
(Accepting limits and finding available pleasures) In every station of life you will find amusements, relaxations, and enjoyments; that is, provided you be willing to make light of evils rather than to hate them.
Seneca

advice-28f74171c3316c44e583db75.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-28f74171c3316c44e583db75.body:
(Accepting limits and finding available pleasures) All life is slavery: let each man therefore reconcile himself to his lot, complain of it as little as possible, and lay hold of whatever good lies within his reach.
Seneca

advice-60a5e72286eaa52903b1e221.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-60a5e72286eaa52903b1e221.body:
(Accepting limits and finding available pleasures) No condition can be so wretched that an impartial mind can find no compensations in it.
Seneca

advice-314dd06427891c74aa3a3048.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-314dd06427891c74aa3a3048.body:
(Preparation makes adversity easier to bear) Know then that every station of life is transitory, and that what has ever happened to anybody may happen to you also.
Seneca

advice-09a81e34efea42cece23d3b0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-09a81e34efea42cece23d3b0.body:
(Preparation makes adversity easier to bear) Among such continual topsy-turvy changes, unless you expect that whatever can happen will happen to you, you give adversity power against you, a power which can be destroyed by any one who looks at it beforehand.
Seneca

advice-48f0000799e527169d3896ec.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-48f0000799e527169d3896ec.body:
(On purpose and skillful action) Let all your work, therefore, have some purpose, and keep some object in view: these restless people are not made restless by labour, but are driven out of their minds by mistaken ideas: for even they do not put themselves in motion without any hope: they are excited by the outward appearance of something, and their crazy mind cannot see its futility.
Seneca

advice-4b57f111141f786e9394c44e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4b57f111141f786e9394c44e.body:
(On moral self-reliance) The mind ought in all cases to be called away from the contemplation of external things to that of itself: let it confide in itself, rejoice in itself, admire its own works; avoid as far as may be those of others, and devote itself to itself; let it not feel losses, and put a good construction even upon misfortunes.
Seneca

advice-2d00e8d9903b528591cc9687.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2d00e8d9903b528591cc9687.body:
(Distance from life's troubles and laughter instead of lament) We must take a higher view of all things, and bear with them more easily: it better becomes a man to scoff at life than to lament over it.
Seneca

advice-34842f6dbc99f8f25925150c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-34842f6dbc99f8f25925150c.body:
(Poetic inspiration and elevation of spirit) The mind cannot use lofty language, above that of the common herd, unless it be excited.
Seneca

advice-08fb2e348d43d528b7706f9a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-08fb2e348d43d528b7706f9a.body:
(Wealth and fame as a burden) Nay, look at those whose prosperity all men run to see: they are choked by their own good things.
Seneca

advice-953870131c1a61ef790bc20d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-953870131c1a61ef790bc20d.body:
(Losing one's time in a chain of others' demands) Investigate those men, whose names are in every one’s mouth: you will find that they bear just the same marks: A is devoted to B, and B to C: no one belongs to himself.
Seneca

advice-e295a506340422128b026f8d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e295a506340422128b026f8d.body:
(Squandering time under the illusion of immortality) It is that people live as though they would live for ever: you never remember your human frailty; you never notice how much of your time has already gone by: you spend it as though you had an abundant and overflowing store of it, though all the while that day which you devote to some man or to some thing is perhaps your last.
Seneca

advice-40b2f36a2c374d6577e56a94.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-40b2f36a2c374d6577e56a94.body:
(Squandering time under the illusion of immortality) You fear everything, like mortals as you are, and yet you desire everything as if you were immortals.
Seneca

advice-80c73b7e605b2bf422a64c7d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-80c73b7e605b2bf422a64c7d.body:
(Powerful people's longing for leisure) You will find that the most powerful and highly-placed men let fall phrases in which they long for leisure, praise it, and prefer it to all the blessings which they enjoy.
Seneca

advice-c4a17b0276b867d6c50cb2dd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c4a17b0276b867d6c50cb2dd.body:
(A busy person who has not learned to live) No man knows less about living than a business man: there is nothing about which it is more difficult to gain knowledge.
Seneca

advice-5832271ce3a68dd354dcf121.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5832271ce3a68dd354dcf121.body:
(Learning to live and die throughout life) Other arts have many folk everywhere who profess to teach them: some of them can be so thoroughly learned by mere boys, that they are able to teach them to others: but one’s whole life must be spent in learning how to live, and, which may perhaps surprise you more, one’s whole life must be spent in learning how to die.
Seneca

advice-082721e81c9b78b8de261d76.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-082721e81c9b78b8de261d76.body:
(Learning to live and die throughout life) Many excellent men have freed themselves from all hindrances, have given up riches, business, and pleasure, and have made it their duty to the very end of their lives to learn how to live: and yet the larger portion of them leave this life confessing that they do not yet know how to live, and still less know how to live as wise men.
Seneca

advice-200927f407c387530fd675c2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-200927f407c387530fd675c2.body:
(Accounting for time left for one's own life) Balance your account, and run over all the days of your life; you will see that only a very few days, and only those which were useless for any other purpose, have been left to you.
Seneca

advice-10b8e25afe52811e9d87ee42.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-10b8e25afe52811e9d87ee42.body:
(Time is worth more than financial rewards) Men set the greatest store upon presents or pensions, and hire out their work, their services, or their care in order to gain them: no one values time: they give it much more freely, as though it cost nothing.
Seneca

advice-d55522bf7ff40b3c513bb574.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d55522bf7ff40b3c513bb574.body:
(Busyness does not stop death approaching) Why! you are busy, but life is hurrying on: death will be here some time or other, and you must attend to him, whether you will or no.
Seneca

advice-28d62be00725d78c045c646d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-28d62be00725d78c045c646d.body:
(Busyness takes away time and reflection on the past) Our present consists only of single days, and those, too, taken one hour at a time: but all the days of past times appear before us when bidden, and allow themselves to be examined and lingered over, albeit busy men cannot find time for so doing.
Seneca

advice-9b002b77e78d45b52885f279.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9b002b77e78d45b52885f279.body:
(Busyness takes away time and reflection on the past) It is the privilege of a tranquil and peaceful mind to review all the parts of its life: but the minds of busy men are like animals under the yoke, and cannot bend aside or look back.
Seneca

advice-9fc384449ddbcbdb7a13c2f3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9fc384449ddbcbdb7a13c2f3.body:
(Busyness takes away time and reflection on the past) Busy men, therefore, possess present time, alone, that being so short that they cannot grasp it, and when they are occupied with many things they lose even this.
Seneca

advice-1f96eeb373d81ed878cba605.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1f96eeb373d81ed878cba605.body:
(Philosophy opens the experience of every age) The only persons who are really at leisure are those who devote themselves to philosophy: and they alone really live: for they do not merely enjoy their own lifetime, but they annex every century to their own: all the years which have passed before them belong to them.
Seneca

advice-c9880c30276e35f28f036bf7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c9880c30276e35f28f036bf7.body:
(Philosophy opens the experience of every age) The wise man’s life, therefore, includes much: he is not hedged in by the same limits which confine others: he alone is exempt from the laws by which mankind is governed: all ages serve him like a god.
Seneca

advice-67428b0437f4aa53c3f9cae1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-67428b0437f4aa53c3f9cae1.body:
(Paulinus: time for himself after public service) Your courage has been sufficiently displayed by many toilsome and wearisome proofs; try how it will deal with leisure: the greater, certainly the better part of your life, has been given to your country; take now some part of your time for yourself as well.
Seneca

advice-9c286eec0e8a47e5a3d3ada0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9c286eec0e8a47e5a3d3ada0.body:
(Helvia: fortitude at her son's exile) Let those whose feeble minds have been enervated by a long period of happiness, weep and lament for many days, and faint away on receiving the slightest blow: but those whose years have all been passed amid catastrophes should bear the severest losses with brave and unyielding patience.
Seneca

advice-fcd38421ccdc2e3921d6af29.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fcd38421ccdc2e3921d6af29.body:
(A happy life according to nature) We are born to a comfortable position enough, if we do not afterwards lose it: the aim of Nature has been to enable us to live well without needing a vast apparatus to enable us to do so: every man is able by himself to make himself happy.
Seneca

advice-c129bac4edb3f1866e5a102a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c129bac4edb3f1866e5a102a.body:
(On moral self-reliance) External circumstances have very little importance either for good or for evil: the wise man is neither elated by prosperity nor depressed by adversity; for he has always endeavoured to depend chiefly upon himself and to derive all his joys from himself.
Seneca

advice-0c48f53628d3cf09a465fe0e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0c48f53628d3cf09a465fe0e.body:
(The soul's mobility and the naturalness of changing place) Be not surprised, then, if the human mind, which is formed from the same seeds as the heavenly bodies, delights in change and wandering, since the divine nature itself either takes pleasure in constant and exceeding swift motion or perhaps even preserves its existence thereby.
Seneca

advice-b94124d98390c3cffca63c66.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b94124d98390c3cffca63c66.body:
(Nature's few needs and greed's lack of limits) Nothing is sufficient for covetous desire, but Nature can be satisfied even with scant measure.
Seneca

advice-648a26416f65c1344843e3c6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-648a26416f65c1344843e3c6.body:
(Nature's few needs and greed's lack of limits) He who restrains himself within the limits prescribed by nature, will not feel poverty; he who exceeds them will always be poor, however great his wealth may be.
Seneca

advice-56f9bc2a2e422f3df9903b31.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-56f9bc2a2e422f3df9903b31.body:
(Humanity's shared fate as consolation in grief) In my opinion, nature has made her cruellest acts affect all men alike, in order that the universality of their lot might console them for its hardship.
Seneca

advice-9b5af1a35f26bb3fc3252527.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9b5af1a35f26bb3fc3252527.body:
(Polybius: fortitude after his brother's death) Nothing however will restrain your loving nature from these useless tears so effectually as the reflexion that you ought to show your brothers an example by bearing this outrage of fortune bravely.
Seneca

advice-8e7b3b0de61fdca787773d26.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8e7b3b0de61fdca787773d26.body:
(Public standing requires self-control) Men demand much, and expect much from you: you ought not to have drawn all eyes upon yourself, if you wished to be allowed to act as you pleased: as it is, you must make good that of which you have given promise.
Seneca

advice-9869f532db5a9eea763dda35.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9869f532db5a9eea763dda35.body:
(Study and literature as consolation in grief) You ought, therefore, first to exercise your mind upon grave studies, and then to enliven it with gayer ones.
Seneca

advice-08afafdbf1ba48f3690563fe.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-08afafdbf1ba48f3690563fe.body:
(Polybius: gratitude for life shared with his brother) There is nothing more inconsistent than that a man should grieve that so good a brother was not long enough with him, and should not rejoice that he nevertheless has been with him.
Seneca

advice-41af94e0523dd3245212d8d3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-41af94e0523dd3245212d8d3.body:
(Loved ones as a temporary gift of fate) Let us enjoy what is given to us, and give it back when it is asked for: the Fates lay their hands on some men at some times, and on other men at other times, but they will never pass any one by altogether.
Seneca

advice-3037caa1bea50fce8302746a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3037caa1bea50fce8302746a.body:
(Readiness for inevitable death without constant fear) Our mind ought always to be on the alert, and while it ought never to fear what is certain to happen, it ought always to be ready for what may happen at any time.
Seneca

advice-3eb42131eef1dcf16f2c2eca.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3eb42131eef1dcf16f2c2eca.body:
(Virtue is accessible regardless of birth and rank) Albeit in all other matters rank and birth make great distinctions between men, yet virtue is open to all; she despises no one provided he thinks himself worthy to possess her.
Seneca

advice-d11331801538729e71ba8f62.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d11331801538729e71ba8f62.body:
(Study and literature as consolation in grief) Now, therefore, immerse yourself even more deeply in your studies, now surround your mind with them like fortifications, so that grief may not find any place at which it can gain entrance.
Seneca

advice-a7f7b0345bb9264f31e8ea6f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a7f7b0345bb9264f31e8ea6f.body:
(The subjects' safety and the ruler's life) Men therefore love their own safety, when they draw up vast legions in battle on behalf of one man, when they rush to the front, and expose their breasts to wounds, for fear that their leader’s standards should be driven back.
Seneca

advice-50aca715a4890fe27b1098ae.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-50aca715a4890fe27b1098ae.body:
(Clemency as a virtue of supreme power) To save men’s lives is the privilege of the loftiest station, which never deserves admiration so much as when it is able to act like the gods, by whose kindness good and bad men alike are brought into the world.
Seneca

advice-9af0af0fad50935df2df2232.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9af0af0fad50935df2df2232.body:
(A ruler's responsibility for his words) You think it a serious matter to take away from kings the right of free speech which the humblest enjoy.
Seneca

advice-052d34f88a11fa5eb444fa67.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-052d34f88a11fa5eb444fa67.body:
(A ruler's punishment frightens more widely than it harms) Just as thunderbolts when they fall endanger few men but terrify all, so the chastisement inflicted by great potentates terrify more widely than they injure, and that for good reasons; for in the case of one whose power is absolute, men do not think of what he has done, so much as of what he may do.
Seneca

advice-3940b1553ced95415912afe8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3940b1553ced95415912afe8.body:
(Cruel power breeds desperate resistance) No courage is so great as that which is born of utter desperation.
Seneca

advice-a8d89bd656db57a4bfae4c30.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a8d89bd656db57a4bfae4c30.body:
(A tyrant's fear of retribution) No prisoner at the bar is so full of agony and anxiety as a tyrant; for while he dreads both gods and men because they have witnessed, and will avenge his crimes, he has at the same time so far committed himself to this course of action that he is not able to alter it.
Seneca

advice-113f3d79b06ce6c59a4c8399.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-113f3d79b06ce6c59a4c8399.body:
(Commanders' harshness leads to desertion) If a tribune or a centurion is harsh, he will make men deserters, and one cannot blame them for desertion.
Seneca

advice-1f03024a0ba85715ca116f4e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1f03024a0ba85715ca116f4e.body:
(People are more readily guided with gentleness) No creature is more self-willed, requires more careful management, or ought to be treated with greater indulgence than man.
Seneca

advice-8a4072382687751281a6dc37.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8a4072382687751281a6dc37.body:
(Clemency as a virtue of supreme power) Nothing can be imagined which is more becoming to a sovereign than clemency, by whatever title and right he may be set over his fellow citizens.
Seneca

advice-df37a19631a8e008d43924eb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-df37a19631a8e008d43924eb.body:
(Gentle government improves morals) A good king establishes a good standard of morals for his kingdom and drives away vices if he is long-suffering with them, not that he should seem to encourage them, but to be very unwilling and to suffer much when he is forced to chastise them.
Seneca

advice-50b872b199eefed409156cb3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-50b872b199eefed409156cb3.body:
(Gentle government improves morals) Clemency in a sovereign even makes men ashamed to do wrong: for punishment seems far more grievous when inflicted by a merciful man.
Seneca

advice-f20a0cb1cc67e4f89b242885.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f20a0cb1cc67e4f89b242885.body:
(Gentle government improves morals) Where men are seldom punished innocence becomes the rule, and is encouraged as a public benefit.
Seneca

advice-5f1840f8e0bbc1e0aecc41d8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5f1840f8e0bbc1e0aecc41d8.body:
(People are more readily guided with gentleness) The human mind is naturally self-willed, kicks against the goad, and sets its face against authority; it will follow more readily than it can be led.
Seneca

advice-2e76e2d1de6b0c77e783dfb3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2e76e2d1de6b0c77e783dfb3.body:
(Wicked agents endanger the ruler himself) A bad man will not long be obedient, and will not do only as much evil as he is ordered.
Seneca

advice-a2a612a1569ca261729cee25.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a2a612a1569ca261729cee25.body:
(A ruler's happiness in saving citizens) True happiness, on the other hand; consists in saving many men’s lives, in calling them back from the very gates of death, and in being so merciful as to deserve a civic crown.
Seneca

advice-51b8550f5ef75b9e81b6c18f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-51b8550f5ef75b9e81b6c18f.body:
(A call for society's moral renewal) Now in truth we ought all to agree to love righteousness and goodness; covetousness, which is the root of all evil, ought to be driven away, piety and virtue, good faith and modesty ought to resume their interrupted reign, and the vices which have so long and so shamefully ruled us ought at last to give way to an age of happiness and purity.
Seneca

advice-05f281b654b3c563f389a62d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-05f281b654b3c563f389a62d.body:
(The ruler's character as a model for the state) Let your own goodness of heart be gradually spread and diffused throughout the whole body of the empire, and all parts of it will mould themselves into your likeness.
Seneca

advice-622e5ec33f2d82d667f7a6a5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-622e5ec33f2d82d667f7a6a5.body:
(The Stoic distinction between rational mercy and distressing pity) Just as the gods are worshipped by religion, but are dishonoured by superstition, so all good men will show mercy and mildness, but will avoid pity, which is a vice incident to weak minds which cannot endure the sight of another’s sufferings.
Seneca

advice-df472b8c8422baf35f4e8d3e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-df472b8c8422baf35f4e8d3e.body:
(The Stoic distinction between rational mercy and distressing pity) Pity considers a man’s misfortunes and does not consider to what they are due: mercy is combined with reason.
Seneca

advice-2de1f06db58280a9903ff599.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2de1f06db58280a9903ff599.body:
(The Stoic distinction between rational mercy and distressing pity) Pity is a disorder of the mind caused by the sight of other men’s miseries, or it is a sadness caused by the evils with which it believes others to be undeservedly afflicted: but the wise man cannot be affected by any disorder: his mind is calm, and nothing can possibly happen to ruffle it.
Seneca

advice-541ed036a160429faa6808b1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-541ed036a160429faa6808b1.body:
(The sage: tranquility before sorrow and fortune) Sorrow overwhelms men’s minds, casts them down, contracts them: now this cannot happen to the wise man even in his greatest misfortunes, but he will beat back the rage of Fortune and triumph over it: he will always retain the same calm, undisturbed expression of countenance, which he never could do were he accessible to sorrow.
Seneca

advice-51808a01f71d5824439fb512.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-51808a01f71d5824439fb512.body:
(The Stoic distinction between rational mercy and distressing pity) Sorrow is awkward at reviewing the position of affairs, at devising useful expedients, avoiding dangerous courses, and weighing the merits of fair and just ones: therefore the wise man will not feel pity, because this cannot happen to a man unless his mind is disturbed.
Seneca

advice-34adcc273b87c75ec29fa6f7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-34adcc273b87c75ec29fa6f7.body:
(Pardoning offenders who can be reformed) The wise man will remit many penalties, and will save many who are wicked, but whose wickedness is not incurable.
Seneca

advice-2b331e9a79d68cfe5ef59b3f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2b331e9a79d68cfe5ef59b3f.body:
(A benefit requires attention and goodwill) A benefit is received in the same temper in which it is given, and ought not, therefore, to be given carelessly, for a man thanks himself for that which he receives without the knowledge of the giver.
Seneca

advice-a8c5fcdadea19b9c9bb4278b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a8c5fcdadea19b9c9bb4278b.body:
(A disinterested benefit without expectation of payment) The man who while he gives thinks of what he will get in return, deserves to be deceived.
Seneca

advice-701cce1a2e963ad456a13bf6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-701cce1a2e963ad456a13bf6.body:
(A disinterested benefit without expectation of payment) It is the property of a great and good mind to covet, not the fruit of good deeds, but good deeds themselves, and to seek for a good man even after having met with bad men.
Seneca

advice-05984e772c5104b16aa82929.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-05984e772c5104b16aa82929.body:
(Taking the first steps in giving and returning gratitude) He who does not repay a benefit, sins more, but he who does not bestow one, sins earlier.
Seneca

advice-ee3bae3b5d63d70a1854c41b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ee3bae3b5d63d70a1854c41b.body:
(Not ceasing to give benefits because of ingratitude) Whatever may have been the result of your former benefits, persevere in bestowing others upon other men; they will be all the better placed in the hands of the ungrateful, whom shame, or a favourable opportunity, or imitation of others may some day cause to be grateful.
Seneca

advice-92db2da24a6ae417ffe11d73.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-92db2da24a6ae417ffe11d73.body:
(Not ceasing to give benefits because of ingratitude) Do not grow weary, perform your duty, and act as becomes a good man.
Seneca

advice-ce2718e66a2a06a5cc0371c0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ce2718e66a2a06a5cc0371c0.body:
(Kindness softens even wild animals) Even wild beasts feel kindness, nor is there any animal so savage that good treatment will not tame it and win love from it.
Seneca

advice-55215470c2e79e0166f3e28d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-55215470c2e79e0166f3e28d.body:
(Not ceasing to give benefits because of ingratitude) He who is quick to believe that he has thrown away his benefits, does really throw them away; but he who presses on and adds new benefits to his former ones, forces out gratitude even from a hard and forgetful breast.
Seneca

advice-6182dde6f6a41fb3548df18e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6182dde6f6a41fb3548df18e.body:
(Repeated benefits awaken gratitude) In the face of many kindnesses, your friend will not dare to raise his eyes; let him see you whithersoever he turns himself to escape from his remembrance of you; encircle him with your benefits.
Seneca

advice-c5f840abf51c83080306beaa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c5f840abf51c83080306beaa.body:
(The giver should forget, the recipient remember the benefit) Do thou teach me how I may bestow more good things, and be more grateful to those who have earned my gratitude, and how the minds of both parties may vie with one another, the giver in forgetting, the receiver in remembering his debt.
Seneca

advice-0ac69d603b5fabbfeebc18cf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0ac69d603b5fabbfeebc18cf.body:
(Goodwill as the essence of a benefit) A benefit is not to be felt and handled, it is a thing which exists only in the mind.
Seneca

advice-de8838b103549d84cdcb16df.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-de8838b103549d84cdcb16df.body:
(A benefit: the joy of freely helping another) It is the art of doing a kindness which both bestows pleasure and gains it by bestowing it, and which does its office by natural and spontaneous impulse.
Seneca

advice-89411aba3c9954270bd77790.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-89411aba3c9954270bd77790.body:
(Giving life's necessities first) We must begin with what is necessary, for those things which support life affect the mind very differently from, those which adorn and improve it.
Seneca

advice-34133c3678017b6ac193fa1d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-34133c3678017b6ac193fa1d.body:
(A lasting gift preserves memory of its giver) If we have a free choice as to what to give, we should above all choose lasting presents, in order that our gift may endure as long as possible; for few are so grateful as to think of what they have received, even when they do not see it.
Seneca

advice-2094f8e770cf590aac3eadf2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2094f8e770cf590aac3eadf2.body:
(A lasting gift preserves memory of its giver) As we never ought to remind men of what we have given them, we ought all the more to choose presents that will be permanent; for the things themselves will prevent the remembrance of the giver from fading away.
Seneca

advice-dffd881cc316d4ad8c40f128.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dffd881cc316d4ad8c40f128.body:
(A lasting gift preserves memory of its giver) Few remain grateful after the present is gone: many more remember their presents only while they make use of them.
Seneca

advice-3a8e52b10bb4bb454cd450ab.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3a8e52b10bb4bb454cd450ab.body:
(A lasting gift preserves memory of its giver) If possible, I should like my present not to be consumed; let it remain in existence, let it stick to my friend and share his life.
Seneca

advice-b4197201d450b3cdb646f00f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b4197201d450b3cdb646f00f.body:
(A fitting gift: person, place, and time) Common sense must guide our benefits; we must consider the time and the place, and the character of the receiver, which are the weights in the scale, which cause our gifts to be well or ill received.
Seneca

advice-32f99189e8dfb60d99c3ec1d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-32f99189e8dfb60d99c3ec1d.body:
(A gift's rarity matters more than price alone) Let us make presents of things which are rare and scarce rather than costly, things which even a rich man will be glad of, just as common fruits, such as we tire of after a few days, please us if they have ripened before the usual season.
Seneca

advice-037be9764244b87b0264e759.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-037be9764244b87b0264e759.body:
(Personal attention in choosing a gift) Let each man have some peculiarity about his gift which may make him consider himself more highly favoured than the rest.
Seneca

advice-fb231d5adb8ad20069e1ef2a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fb231d5adb8ad20069e1ef2a.body:
(Thoughtful generosity without extravagance) Since no impulse of the human mind can be approved of, even though it springs from a right feeling, unless it be made into a virtue by discretion, I forbid generosity to degenerate into extravagance.
Seneca

advice-ee13ab9954a15e2b2d9a8a71.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ee13ab9954a15e2b2d9a8a71.body:
(Thoughtful generosity without extravagance) That is not a benefit, to which the best part of a benefit, that it be bestowed with judgment, is wanting: a really great sum of money, if it be given neither with discernment nor with good will, is no more a benefit than if it remained hoarded.
Seneca

advice-c66048d235e48b51bdc6ca93.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c66048d235e48b51bdc6ca93.body:
(Helping before the humiliating need to ask) We ought, therefore, to divine every man's wishes, and when we have discovered them, to set him free from the hard necessity of asking; you may be sure that a benefit which comes unasked will be delightful and will not be forgotten.
Seneca

advice-deb18551bf59cbb776377710.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-deb18551bf59cbb776377710.body:
(Prompt and cheerful help expresses goodwill) One who gives so readily must needs give with good will; he therefore gives cheerfully and shows his disposition in his countenance.
Seneca

advice-4617eb5c27af2f7270f15d8b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4617eb5c27af2f7270f15d8b.body:
(Prompt and cheerful help expresses goodwill) It is possible to look forward with anxious disquietude even to good things, and, seeing that most benefits consist in a release from some form of misery, a man destroys the value of the benefit which he confers, if he has the power to relieve us, and yet allows us to suffer or to lack pleasure longer than we need.
Seneca

advice-29cf03bb989d02ad53ccbbe1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-29cf03bb989d02ad53ccbbe1.body:
(Prompt and cheerful help expresses goodwill) Kindness always eager to do good, and one who acts by love naturally acts at once; he who does us good, but does it tardily and with long delays, does not do so from the heart.
Seneca

advice-fb5cd37b1846197008bda7fa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fb5cd37b1846197008bda7fa.body:
