(Helping without reproach or humiliation) To reproach a man at the very moment that you are doing him a service is sheer madness; it is to mix insult with your favours.
Seneca

advice-f0d41f4eb286913118acc0dd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f0d41f4eb286913118acc0dd.body:
(Helping without reproach or humiliation) Even if there be some subject upon which you wish to warn your friend, choose some other time for doing so.
Seneca

advice-615abe6d6c0a4be603c730e1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-615abe6d6c0a4be603c730e1.body:
(Care for the recipient of a benefit inspires gratitude) If you wish those whom you lay under an obligation to be grateful to you, you must not merely confer benefits upon them, but you must also love them.
Seneca

advice-6b42095977f9250c410f19e1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6b42095977f9250c410f19e1.body:
(Giving with regard for consequences to the recipient) We ought to look at the end of our benefits as well as the beginning, and not merely to give what men are glad to receive, but what they will hereafter be glad to have received.
Seneca

advice-fb257fa6a97c7669f5af65b3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fb257fa6a97c7669f5af65b3.body:
(Refusing a request that would harm the requester) It is a cruel kindness to allow one's self to be won over into granting that which injures those who beg for it.
Seneca

advice-a6e613fac7b11c5ec0ac7e98.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a6e613fac7b11c5ec0ac7e98.body:
(Refusing a request that would harm the requester) Just as it is the noblest of acts to save men from harm against their will, so it is but hatred, under the mask of civility, to grant what is harmful to those who ask for it.
Seneca

advice-7fe4b7755741a969edd8bbf3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7fe4b7755741a969edd8bbf3.body:
(Giving with regard for consequences to the recipient) Let us confer benefits of such a kind, that the more they are made use of the better they please, and which never can turn into injuries.
Seneca

advice-ed517918ebd61fd91d069ea5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ed517918ebd61fd91d069ea5.body:
(Fairly valuing a gift without reproaching its recipient) I ought not to make a small benefit appear a great one, nor allow great benefits to be regarded as small; for although it destroys all feeling of gratitude to treat what you give like a creditor, yet you do not reproach a man, but merely set off your gift to the best advantage by letting him know what it is worth.
Seneca

advice-61d7776c5add5a41b82d3e20.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-61d7776c5add5a41b82d3e20.body:
(Thoughtful generosity without extravagance) Every man must consider what his resources and powers are, so that we may not give either more or less than we are able.
Seneca

advice-ff84362ee1d98a581376a309.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ff84362ee1d98a581376a309.body:
(A fitting gift: person, place, and time) Nothing is by itself a becoming gift for any one: all depends upon who gives it, to whom he gives it, when, for what reason, where, and so forth, without which details it is impossible to argue about it.
Seneca

advice-a293658aa636e7babaf4c4d3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a293658aa636e7babaf4c4d3.body:
(A Cynic's actions should match his professed disdain for wealth) Your cynic has publicly proclaimed his hatred of money, and assumed the character of one who despises it: let him act up to his professions.
Seneca

advice-fa0ef5bda99d36dad3af0fac.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fa0ef5bda99d36dad3af0fac.body:
(Returning a benefit freely, not demanding it as a debt) We blame usurers equally when they press harshly for payment, and when they delay and make difficulties about taking back the money which they have lent; in the same way, it is just as right that a benefit should be returned, as it is wrong to ask any one to return it.
Seneca

advice-d1620606770e4d975de8d6c5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d1620606770e4d975de8d6c5.body:
(Returning a benefit freely, not demanding it as a debt) The best man is he who gives readily, never asks for any return, and is delighted when the return is made, because, having really and truly forgotten what he gave, he receives it as though it were a present.
Seneca

advice-61d9a8cab3b48b1d73c4adee.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-61d9a8cab3b48b1d73c4adee.body:
(An accepted gift binds one to its giver through gratitude) Nothing is more wretched for a modest and honourable man than to feel it to be his duty to love one whom it does not please him to love.
Seneca

advice-70afcb8e6f88ccf866c1e17d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-70afcb8e6f88ccf866c1e17d.body:
(A gift imposed on the recipient creates no debt of gratitude) If you are free, if it lies with you to decide whether you will or not, then you will turn over in your own mind whether you will take a gift from a man or not; but if your position makes it impossible for you to choose, then be assured that you do not receive a gift, you merely obey orders.
Seneca

advice-86bd83ef50232d98b8d212ed.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-86bd83ef50232d98b8d212ed.body:
(A good outcome without goodwill is not a benefit) You see that the actual thing itself is not of much importance, because it is not regarded as a benefit at all, if you do good when you intended to do evil; in such a case the benefit is done by chance, the man did harm.
Seneca

advice-3203498df32a744422eae4e3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3203498df32a744422eae4e3.body:
(Not accepting a gift that would harm the giver) A man may be a worthy person for me to receive a benefit from, but it will hurt him to give it.
Seneca

advice-c85afae9c468821742a146fa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c85afae9c468821742a146fa.body:
(Gratefully accepting a gift already rewards the giver) When we have decided to accept, let us accept with cheerfulness, showing pleasure, and letting the giver see it, so that he may at once receive some return for his goodness: for as it is a good reason for rejoicing to see our friend happy, it is a better one to have made him so.
Seneca

advice-4baaaa68ac4fb36abf18e6f3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4baaaa68ac4fb36abf18e6f3.body:
(Gratefully accepting a gift already rewards the giver) Let us, therefore, show how acceptable a gift is by loudly expressing our gratitude for it; and let us do so, not only in the hearing of the giver, but everywhere.
Seneca

advice-76582dbe087822fb2c190b5c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-76582dbe087822fb2c190b5c.body:
(Gratefully accepting a gift already rewards the giver) He who receives a benefit with gratitude, repays the first instalment of it.
Seneca

advice-08772800e375bc7029351722.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-08772800e375bc7029351722.body:
(Gratefully accepting a gift already rewards the giver) No words need be used; if we only feel as we ought, our thankfulness will be shown in our countenances.
Seneca

advice-aed68dfcdb8eafa6a7b3b035.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-aed68dfcdb8eafa6a7b3b035.body:
(Readiness to reciprocate while receiving help) He who intends to be grateful, let him think how he shall repay a kindness while he is receiving it.
Seneca

advice-4867e7b1cbb71fa1eb0913c0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4867e7b1cbb71fa1eb0913c0.body:
(Gratefully accepting a gift already rewards the giver) A man steers well who reaches the port for which he started: a dart hurled by a steady hand performs its duty if it hits the mark; one who bestows a benefit wishes it to be received with gratitude; he gets what he wanted if it be well received.
Seneca

advice-ff5ceddd937a174c1e547ef7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ff5ceddd937a174c1e547ef7.body:
(Gratitude is possible without means to return a gift) True; but a benefit is in an evil plight if we cannot be grateful for it even when we are empty-handed.
Seneca

advice-3ae8ff9c922d668189f3df89.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3ae8ff9c922d668189f3df89.body:
(Gratefully accepting a gift already rewards the giver) A man bestows a benefit upon me: I receive it just as he wished it to be received: then he gets at once what he wanted, and the only thing which he wanted, and therefore I have proved myself grateful.
Seneca

advice-153d27b577ce28b2ad623d1e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-153d27b577ce28b2ad623d1e.body:
(Denying, concealing, and failing to return a benefit) The man is ungrateful who denies that he has received a benefit; who pretends that he has not received it; who does not return it.
Seneca

advice-f3297ee0adfaa735cb04176d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f3297ee0adfaa735cb04176d.body:
(Remembering a benefit as the foundation of gratitude) It is clear that if forgetfulness of a benefit steals over a man, he cannot have often thought about repaying it.
Seneca

advice-d44f91db1e86354ea0a8e0ca.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d44f91db1e86354ea0a8e0ca.body:
(Remembering a benefit as the foundation of gratitude) In short, repayment requires gratitude, time, opportunity, and the help of fortune; whereas, he who remembers a benefit is grateful for it, and that too without expenditure.
Seneca

advice-d416fefaa30a23140944a7d3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d416fefaa30a23140944a7d3.body:
(Remembering a benefit as the foundation of gratitude) Since gratitude demands neither labour, wealth, nor good fortune, he who fails to render it has no excuse behind which to shelter himself; for he who places a benefit so far away that it is out of his sight, never could have meant to be grateful for it.
Seneca

advice-f5d29c41a743f14874a0c870.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f5d29c41a743f14874a0c870.body:
(Envy is incompatible with joyful gratitude) Now no one can at the same time be both jealous and grateful, because those who are jealous are querulous and sad, while the grateful are joyous.
Seneca

advice-dc24bd97f2f9f63f4f9ea76e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dc24bd97f2f9f63f4f9ea76e.body:
(Past benefits can no longer be undone) Present good is not yet altogether complete, some mischance may interrupt it; the future is in suspense, and uncertain; but what is past is laid up in safety.
Seneca

advice-81ce71da551c78f82c806e1e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-81ce71da551c78f82c806e1e.body:
(Gratitude is more than formally repaying a debt) No law defines an ungrateful person, often, indeed, one who repays what he has received is ungrateful, and one who has not returned it is grateful.
Seneca

advice-a092ce67a774f6cd7457ceb0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a092ce67a774f6cd7457ceb0.body:
(Lasting joy from remembering another's kindness) On the other hand, he who takes pleasure in receiving a benefit, enjoys an unvarying and continuous happiness, which he derives from consideration, not of the thing given, but of the intention of the giver.
Seneca

advice-ebc99cfad8f5bfff7370ff95.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ebc99cfad8f5bfff7370ff95.body:
(Lasting joy from remembering another's kindness) A benefit gives perpetual joy to a grateful man, but pleases an ungrateful one only for a moment.
Seneca

advice-dc700a2da1c8199bbaabd199.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dc700a2da1c8199bbaabd199.body:
(Virtue is accessible regardless of birth and rank) The path of virtue is closed to no one, it lies open to all; it admits and invites all, whether they be free-born men, slaves or freed-men, kings or exiles; it requires no qualifications of family or of property, it is satisfied with a mere man.
Seneca

advice-6c574192bbb3a980e4992d21.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6c574192bbb3a980e4992d21.body:
(Virtue and beneficence are accessible even to slaves) A slave can be just, brave, magnanimous; he can therefore bestow a benefit, for this is also the part of a virtuous man.
Seneca

advice-4f65307ecee7e553b2de8218.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4f65307ecee7e553b2de8218.body:
(Virtue and beneficence are accessible even to slaves) Consider, rather, whether an example of virtue in a slave be not all the greater because it is rarer than in free men, and whether it be not all the more gratifying that, although to be commanded is odious, and all submission to authority is irksome, yet in some particular cases love for a master has been more powerful than men's general dislike to servitude.
Seneca

advice-c4d38cd8bd8f7e2bf6601830.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c4d38cd8bd8f7e2bf6601830.body:
(Nobility of character matters more than ancestry) All men descend from the same original stock; no one is better born than another, except in so far as his disposition is nobler and better suited for the performance of good actions.
Seneca

advice-827e3d22d5571f7e2170ca6c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-827e3d22d5571f7e2170ca6c.body:
(Nobility of character matters more than ancestry) Be not deceived when men who are reckoning up their genealogy, wherever an illustrious name is wanting, foist in that of a god in its place.
Seneca

advice-1b66f77310256ad9815a41f8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1b66f77310256ad9815a41f8.body:
(Birth is only the beginning, not the greatest benefit) Consider what the fact of my birth is in itself; you will see that it is a small matter, the outcome of which is dubious, and that it may lead equally to good or to evil; no doubt it is the first step to everything, but because it is the first, it is not on that account more important than all the others.
Seneca

advice-e4403949130828110e7b37be.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e4403949130828110e7b37be.body:
(A son can surpass his father in beneficence) A father gives life to his son; there is something better than life; therefore a father may be outdone, because there is something better than the benefit which he has bestowed.
Seneca

advice-4669aded51930c64e84ec0c5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4669aded51930c64e84ec0c5.body:
(A son can surpass his father in beneficence) Still further, he who has given any one his life, if he be more than once saved from peril of death by him, has received a greater benefit than he bestowed.
Seneca

advice-72c523706e5c484c1c899a7b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-72c523706e5c484c1c899a7b.body:
(Virtue for its own sake, without calculating profit) Some men are found who act honourably from commercial motives, and who do not care for unrewarded virtue, though it can confer no glory if it brings any profit.
Seneca

advice-620eb3ff8aceea9af207d4f1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-620eb3ff8aceea9af207d4f1.body:
(A disinterested benefit without expectation of payment) To take thought, not where your benefit will be best bestowed, but where it may be most profitably placed at interest, from whence you will most easily get it back, is not bestowal of benefits, but usury.
Seneca

advice-4cd2bee6107c9940d71c9074.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4cd2bee6107c9940d71c9074.body:
(A reasoned basis for beneficence) Nothing ought to be done without a reason: a benefit is not truly so, if it be bestowed without a reason, since reason accompanies all honorable action.
Seneca

advice-805e67ec12b43236b1f06d13.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-805e67ec12b43236b1f06d13.body:
(The consciousness of a good deed as its reward) The same is true with benefits; when you ask what return I get for them, I answer, the consciousness of a good action.
Seneca

advice-2e8c0dca94e6e5d675ca683d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2e8c0dca94e6e5d675ca683d.body:
(A disinterested benefit without expectation of payment) The true love of giving calls us away from all this, forcibly leads us to put up with loss, and foregoes its own interest, deriving its greatest pleasure from the mere act of doing good.
Seneca

advice-5f08af9073e19c89f82835ef.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5f08af9073e19c89f82835ef.body:
(The benefactor's joy and affection for the recipient) I should not lie if I were to affirm that every one takes pleasure in the benefits which he has bestowed, that everyone loves best to see the man whom he has most largely benefited.
Seneca

advice-b1eff929812563ac3013b644.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b1eff929812563ac3013b644.body:
(The universal recognition of moral goodness) No one has ever so far rebelled against the laws of nature and put off human feeling as to act basely for mere amusement.
Seneca

advice-7c5e416c525a639e0d461519.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7c5e416c525a639e0d461519.body:
(The universal recognition of moral goodness) Nature bestows upon us all this immense advantage, that the light of virtue shines into the minds of all alike; even those who do not follow her, behold her.
Seneca

advice-917a6174604ca722991af3dc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-917a6174604ca722991af3dc.body:
(Gratitude sustains human solidarity) A proof that gratitude is desirable for itself lies in the fact that ingratitude is to be avoided for itself, because no vice more powerfully rends asunder and destroys the union of the human race.
Seneca

advice-88839def8419fd962524f386.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-88839def8419fd962524f386.body:
(Appreciation forced by fear is not gratitude) In fine, I call every man ungrateful who is merely made grateful by fear.
Seneca

advice-f89a243a407c19cfea21b94e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f89a243a407c19cfea21b94e.body:
(Beneficent gods inspire love rather than fear) No sane man fears the gods; for it is madness to fear what is beneficial, and no man loves those whom he fears.
Seneca

advice-7841aafb52a4e27109250e1e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7841aafb52a4e27109250e1e.body:
(The moral beauty of gratitude as its own purpose) A grateful mind is attracted only by a sense of the beauty of its purpose.
Seneca

advice-584b872dffc44710cb14bdff.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-584b872dffc44710cb14bdff.body:
(Gratitude persists even when it cannot be expressed) A man who is silent may, nevertheless, be eloquent; his hands may be folded or even bound, and he may yet be strong; just as a pilot is a pilot even when upon dry land, because his knowledge is complete, and there is nothing wanting to it, though there may be obstacles which prevent his making use of it.
Seneca

advice-daba6422a6788a7a6fa75e27.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-daba6422a6788a7a6fa75e27.body:
(Gratitude persists even when it cannot be expressed) In the same way, a man is grateful who only wishes to be so, and who has no one but himself who can bear witness to his frame of mind.
Seneca

advice-9944269715ade37e11ea612d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9944269715ade37e11ea612d.body:
(True gratitude despite mistaken public opinion) I will go even further than this: a man sometimes is grateful when he appears to be ungrateful, when ill-judging report has declared him to be so.
Seneca

advice-67277e9307d8388bda130b51.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-67277e9307d8388bda130b51.body:
(Gratitude before death, without hope of future advantage) Nothing then remains for us to hope for; yet when on the very threshold, we wish to depart from human life as full of gratitude as possible.
Seneca

advice-1b415e488c127072b0d992de.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1b415e488c127072b0d992de.body:
(Virtue requires willingness to part with money) Virtue will not admit a covetous lover; men must approach her with open purse.
Seneca

advice-25343a7bf211b3bf7bfd23e8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-25343a7bf211b3bf7bfd23e8.body:
(Natural dispositions toward different passions) One man is naturally prone to avarice, another is the slave of wine, a third of lust; or, if not yet enslaved by these passions, he is so fashioned by nature that this is the direction in which his character would probably lead him.
Seneca

advice-821247eab0b31ef61ddc7c2e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-821247eab0b31ef61ddc7c2e.body:
(Not depriving the good of help for fear of helping the bad) It is better to benefit the bad as well, for the sake of benefiting the good, than to stint the good for fear of benefiting the bad.
Seneca

advice-4d456cdbf1d4930c4d4473b6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4d456cdbf1d4930c4d4473b6.body:
(A benefit presupposes sufficiently significant help) A benefit is a useful service, yet all useful service is not a benefit; for some are so trifling as not to claim the title of benefits.
Seneca

advice-f112bfd834d4fd14e1ab098a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f112bfd834d4fd14e1ab098a.body:
(Gratitude to parents for worthy children) If a man has begotten great men, he deserves to receive benefits, whatever he himself may be: he has given us worthy men.
Seneca

advice-719f5040127f3ddca836fcb8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-719f5040127f3ddca836fcb8.body:
(The sage considers uncertainty and possible obstacles) The wise man considers both sides: he knows how great is the power of errors, how uncertain human affairs are, how many obstacles there are to the success of plans.
Seneca

advice-cafa8cb64e9b1765878afaca.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cafa8cb64e9b1765878afaca.body:
(Gratitude is possible without means to return a gift) It is my duty to show a grateful mind, but in some cases my own poverty, in others the prosperity of the friend to whom I owe some return, will not permit me to give it.
Seneca

advice-2ffb39e0daf8ceed49b8b5d3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2ffb39e0daf8ceed49b8b5d3.body:
(Goodwill deserves praise regardless of fortune) All men do not strive for a good object with the same strength, resources, and good fortune, upon which depend at all events the issues of the most admirable projects, though we ought to praise the will itself which makes an effort in the right direction.
Seneca

advice-bf2821f8c57d52671417b007.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bf2821f8c57d52671417b007.body:
(A contest of benefits: willingness to reciprocate matters most) To be conquered, which you consider disgraceful, cannot happen to a good man; for he will never surrender, never give up the contest, to the last day of his life he will stand prepared and in that posture he will die, testifying that though he has received much, yet that he had the will to repay as much as he had received.
Seneca

advice-ef31d91f325264225f05b7d3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ef31d91f325264225f05b7d3.body:
(A contest of benefits: willingness to reciprocate matters most) No one, therefore, can be conquered in a contest of benefits, if he knows how to owe a debt, if he wishes to make a return for what he has received, and raises himself to the same level with his friend in spirit, though he cannot do so in material gifts.
Seneca

advice-6e940786a23c69ed715669ec.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6e940786a23c69ed715669ec.body:
(A contest of benefits: willingness to reciprocate matters most) No one, therefore, is worsted by benefits, because each man's gratitude is to be measured by his will.
Seneca

advice-bdc78e769c692dbf9d8b174c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bdc78e769c692dbf9d8b174c.body:
(A thought experiment: in giving to oneself, giver and recipient coincide) Imagine yourself to be ungrateful, the benefit bestowed upon you is not lost, he who gave it has it; suppose that you are unwilling to receive it, it still belongs to you before it is returned.
Seneca

advice-72cd2b688c60bbff3f4c74d7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-72cd2b688c60bbff3f4c74d7.body:
(A benefit requires two people: giver and recipient) A benefit is a voluntary act, but to do good to oneself is an instinctive one.
Seneca

advice-f49cb34b26c6e7e2752ddd54.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f49cb34b26c6e7e2752ddd54.body:
(A benefit requires two people: giver and recipient) No one bestows a benefit upon himself any more than he bestows hospitality upon himself; no one gives himself anything, any more than he lends himself anything.
Seneca

advice-a8e5101338ffde86a5ac1013.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a8e5101338ffde86a5ac1013.body:
(A benefit requires two people: giver and recipient) An act which always requires two persons cannot take place within the mind of one.
Seneca

advice-eff5bc7a58f9b17129448014.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-eff5bc7a58f9b17129448014.body:
(A benefit requires two people: giver and recipient) The man who returns a kindness ought to expend something, just as he who repays expends money; but the man who returns a kindness to himself expends nothing, just as he who receives a benefit from himself gains nothing.
Seneca

advice-08d272284fa3d6331056f46a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-08d272284fa3d6331056f46a.body:
(A benefit requires two people: giver and recipient) A benefit and gratitude for it must pass to and fro between two persons; their interchange cannot take place within one man.
Seneca

advice-7fdf1ef0a9f401986ead3c21.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7fdf1ef0a9f401986ead3c21.body:
(A benefit requires two people: giver and recipient) A benefit is received at one time, and is returned at another; (but when a man bestows a benefit upon himself, he both receives it and returns it at the same time).
Seneca

advice-6a2d47cca2aaa368f1ccfaec.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6a2d47cca2aaa368f1ccfaec.body:
(Beneficence puts another's good above one's own interest) In a benefit, too, what we commend and admire is, that a man has for the time being forgotten his own interests, in order that he may do good to another; that he has deprived himself of something, in order to bestow it upon another.
Seneca

advice-563c4946ee4b4d633b80ecfc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-563c4946ee4b4d633b80ecfc.body:
(A vicious mind turns external gifts into harm) Just as the stomach, when disordered by disease and secreting bile, changes all the food which it receives, and turns every kind of sustenance into a source of pain, so whatever you entrust to an ill-regulated mind becomes to it a burden, an annoyance, and a source of misery.
Seneca

advice-a150e1d033563b3bc9dae374.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a150e1d033563b3bc9dae374.body:
(A vicious mind turns external gifts into harm) Nothing, therefore, can reach bad men which would do them good; nay, nothing which would not do them harm.
Seneca

advice-c45846d0a2d4a40c99f57edd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c45846d0a2d4a40c99f57edd.body:
(Ingratitude in public and private life) We are ungrateful in public matters; and if every man asks himself, you will find that there is no one who has not some private ingratitude to complain of.
Seneca

advice-48faba60be6ffb9f9533cb39.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-48faba60be6ffb9f9533cb39.body:
(Life's value is determined by its use) Reflect that length of time is not the greatest of blessings; make the best of your time, however short it may be; even if the day of your death be postponed, your happiness will not be increased, for life is merely made longer, not pleasanter, by delay.
Seneca

advice-6e9f39b0142622f993613bc7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6e9f39b0142622f993613bc7.body:
(A son's welfare also affects his father) The good health, the happiness, and the inheritance of a son are connected with his father; his father will be more happy if he keeps his son safe, and more unhappy if he loses him.
Seneca

advice-7a060207356ff9d6ca9d71b3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7a060207356ff9d6ca9d71b3.body:
(Goodwill as the essence of a benefit) True, but we are not now discussing whether you have done me any good or not, but whether you have bestowed a benefit upon me; for animals, stones, and herbs can do one good, but do not bestow benefits, which can only be given by one who wishes well to the receiver.
Seneca

advice-cb86c83142fb8bee5483cc65.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cb86c83142fb8bee5483cc65.body:
(A son's obligation of gratitude does not automatically pass to his father) No return for a benefit ought to be demanded from the father of the receiver; if he does you any kindness in return for it, he should be regarded as, a righteous man, but not as a grateful one.
Seneca

advice-f257f14139a0ab7e489c955a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f257f14139a0ab7e489c955a.body:
(A helpful benefit against the recipient's wishes) We must not consider whether a man is grieved at receiving a benefit, but whether he ought to rejoice: a coin is not bad because it is refused by a savage who is unacquainted with its proper stamp.
Seneca

advice-bc4527404bf32e35e83da478.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bc4527404bf32e35e83da478.body:
(A helpful benefit against the recipient's wishes) A man receives a benefit even though he hates what is done, provided that it does him good, and that the giver bestowed it in order to do him good.
Seneca

advice-58228d19e26a2a1b0e9be994.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-58228d19e26a2a1b0e9be994.body:
(Asking for help in return only in extreme need) In the next place, when I bestow a benefit upon a good man, I do so with the intention of never demanding repayment, except in case of absolute necessity.
Seneca

advice-6a622ff3779b4c7bf5678ba6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6a622ff3779b4c7bf5678ba6.body:
(Among sages, reminders of gratitude are unnecessary) If we lived among wise men, it would be our duty to wait in silence until our benefits were returned.
Seneca

advice-a0c4c1a42b4e835f46e06557.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a0c4c1a42b4e835f46e06557.body:
(Advice awakens dormant gratitude) Very few men are led by their own reason: those who come next to the best are those who return to the right path in consequence of advice; and these we must not deprive of their guide.
Seneca

advice-337a270bb1e4c3231c0a6c12.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-337a270bb1e4c3231c0a6c12.body:
(Advice awakens dormant gratitude) Similarly men's minds contain a good feeling, which, however, lies torpid, either through luxury and disuse, or through ignorance of its duties.
Seneca

advice-c59f96c541fc6bfd2f327bb3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c59f96c541fc6bfd2f327bb3.body:
(The past cannot be changed: a benefit remains a fact) Let Nature struggle as hard as she please, she cannot give herself retrospective action.
Seneca

advice-d15c31d60520a6654bc02f48.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d15c31d60520a6654bc02f48.body:
(Compelled help creates no obligation of gratitude) That a man who does us good by acting under compulsion does not thereby lay us under any obligation, is so clear, that no words are needed to prove it.
Seneca

advice-8afed555f0f89a8dd1ed5e0e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8afed555f0f89a8dd1ed5e0e.body:
(A benefit requires conscious goodwill) Some men may receive benefits without knowing it, but no man can bestow them without knowing it.
Seneca

advice-270a27ab841df1c8514ba00c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-270a27ab841df1c8514ba00c.body:
(Intention distinguishes a benefit from a wrong) The same reason makes it possible for men to do us good without conferring benefits upon us, or to harm us without doing us wrong, because it is intention which distinguishes our friends from our enemies.
Seneca

advice-406e98883bed04e518c357de.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-406e98883bed04e518c357de.body:
(Goodwill as the essence of a benefit) Nothing can be a benefit which does not proceed from good will, and which is not meant as such by the giver.
Seneca

advice-192efe5ace810f017090d8a7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-192efe5ace810f017090d8a7.body:
(A benefit combines goodwill with actual help) That you should have wished to confer a benefit upon me is not sufficient to render me grateful; but that you should have wished not to do so is enough to set me free from any obligation to you.
Seneca

advice-d7a08011995e6d98deda8310.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d7a08011995e6d98deda8310.body:
(A benefit combines goodwill with actual help) A mere wish does not constitute a benefit; and just as the best and heartiest wish is not a benefit when fortune prevents its being carried into effect, neither is what fortune bestows upon us a benefit, unless good wishes preceded it.
Seneca

advice-2e1b38f7ab543d4b2c3c49d9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2e1b38f7ab543d4b2c3c49d9.body:
(A benefit combines goodwill with actual help) It is not enough to wish a man well, without doing him good; nor is it enough to do him good without wishing him well.
Seneca

advice-b9ccbdb38f1e773c06d64fd8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b9ccbdb38f1e773c06d64fd8.body:
(A benefit combines goodwill with actual help) Suppose that some one wished to give me a present, but did not give it; I have his good will, but I do not have his benefit, which consists of subject matter and goodwill together.
Seneca

advice-d55476b46d03702efe7227cd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d55476b46d03702efe7227cd.body:
(Humanity can understand the nature that produced it) Among her noblest products nature has none of which she can boast more than man, and assuredly no other which can comprehend her boast.
Seneca

advice-a368ed54e696bcfd39c94cbf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a368ed54e696bcfd39c94cbf.body:
(Ceasing one's own wrongdoing is not yet conferring a benefit) You do not bestow a benefit upon a man by ceasing to wrong him, nor can it ever be a piece of good service to anyone to remove from him a burden which you yourself imposed on him.
Seneca

advice-71c378e95a14fe1d8018c857.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-71c378e95a14fe1d8018c857.body:
(The wish to repay a friend must not wish him harm) Just utter your wishes in the hearing of him to whom you wish to do good.
Seneca

advice-1583a16f47cab5925910222b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1583a16f47cab5925910222b.body:
(A friend's safety is better than danger from which he is rescued) To escape from fear, however great it may be, can never be so pleasant as to live in sound unassailable safety.
Seneca

advice-5da32369aae8164432ef0ac5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5da32369aae8164432ef0ac5.body:
(Sincere advice to influential friends rather than flattery) Tell them, not what they wish to hear, but what they will wish that they always had heard; though their ears be stopped by flatteries, yet sometimes truth may penetrate them; give them useful advice.
Seneca

advice-52500e592834cb3efa536058.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-52500e592834cb3efa536058.body:
(The value and rarity of true friendship) You do not know how great is the value of friendship, if you do not understand how much you give to him to whom you give a friend, a commodity which is scarce not only in men's houses, but in whole centuries, and which is nowhere scarcer than in the places where it is thought to be most plentiful.
Seneca

advice-61049318c69cb3017234e4e4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-61049318c69cb3017234e4e4.body:
(Being useful to a friend in every circumstance) As you can bear yourself wisely both in doubtful, in prosperous, and in adverse circumstances, by showing prudence in doubtful cases, courage in misfortune, and self-restraint in good fortune, so in all circumstances you can make yourself useful to your friend.
Seneca

advice-ec79b887a20e075018ca7875.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ec79b887a20e075018ca7875.body:
(The wish to repay a friend must not wish him harm) Do not desert him in adversity, but do not wish that it may befall him: the various incidents of human life will afford you many opportunities of proving your loyalty to him without wishing him evil.
Seneca

advice-b3e9575bf8491b5e8984578d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b3e9575bf8491b5e8984578d.body:
(Thanking a friend rather than merely escaping a debt) In returning a kindness it makes a great difference whether you are eager to bestow a benefit, or merely to free yourself from a debt.
Seneca

advice-be40c0632fd6835bc3395f30.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-be40c0632fd6835bc3395f30.body:
(Thanking a friend rather than merely escaping a debt) He who wishes to return a benefit will study his friend's interests, and will hope that a suitable occasion will arise; he who only wishes to free himself from an obligation will be eager to do so by any means whatever, which shows very bad feeling.
Seneca

advice-15ce6a68dee75f0ce46e0c0c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-15ce6a68dee75f0ce46e0c0c.body:
(Ceasing one's own wrongdoing is not yet conferring a benefit) To put out a fire which you yourself have lighted, will not even gain acquittal for you, let alone credit.
Seneca

advice-b1985e38ceb4516e0891ee3b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b1985e38ceb4516e0891ee3b.body:
(Repaying at the right time without wishing the benefactor harm) Not to speak of the graver guilt which you incur by returning evil for good, you distinctly do wrong in not waiting for the fitting time for each action, for it is as wrong to anticipate this as it is not to take it when it comes.
Seneca

advice-76b93dc4413c781a7e537b86.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-76b93dc4413c781a7e537b86.body:
(Thanking a friend rather than merely escaping a debt) Let us remember that this anxiety to seize the first opportunity of setting ourselves free shows ingratitude; for no one repays with good will that which he is unwilling to owe, and his eagerness to get it out of his hands shows that he regards it as a burden rather than as a favour.
Seneca

advice-37f514f3cc2c3a15ce3ce203.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-37f514f3cc2c3a15ce3ce203.body:
(Thanking a friend rather than merely escaping a debt) He who thinks too much about repaying a benefit must suppose that his friend thinks too much about receiving repayment.
Seneca

advice-31d98be00c6dbe26d716ea6e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-31d98be00c6dbe26d716ea6e.body:
(The sage possesses everything in spirit, legally only his property) There is nothing to prevent a thing belonging to a wise man, and yet being the property of its legal owner.
Seneca

advice-a6e8c623be18ccd15eb09352.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a6e8c623be18ccd15eb09352.body:
(Ownership and the separate right to use property) You see, therefore, that it is possible for a man to receive a present by accepting what is his own.
Seneca

advice-25fe722160909a2b09cb2a3e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-25fe722160909a2b09cb2a3e.body:
(The sage possesses everything in spirit, legally only his property) Although the wise man possesses everything, yet I can give him what I individually possess; for though, king-like, he in his mind possesses everything, yet the ownership of all things is divided among various individuals, so that he can both receive a present and owe one; can buy, or hire things.
Seneca

advice-a99c3617978732d40baf9b44.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a99c3617978732d40baf9b44.body:
(The sage possesses everything in spirit, legally only his property) In the same way the wise man in his mind possesses everything, in actual right and ownership he possesses only his own property.
Seneca

advice-70a20b5e72047e5da22fff1f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-70a20b5e72047e5da22fff1f.body:
(The sage possesses everything in spirit, legally only his property) When, then, we consider that the mind of the truly wise man has power over all things and pervades all things, we cannot help declaring that everything is his, although, in the estimation of our common law, it may chance that he may be rated as possessing no property whatever.
Seneca

advice-f5507f7708a21d59eeb7759c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f5507f7708a21d59eeb7759c.body:
(The sage possesses everything in spirit, legally only his property) It is possible, then, to give something to the wise man, although all things belong to the wise man.
Seneca

advice-1d957d6b85740cffa80afff5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1d957d6b85740cffa80afff5.body:
(Persisting in attempts to repay kindness) He who watches each opportunity as it passes, and tries to avail himself of one after another, does more to show his gratitude than he whom the first opportunity enabled to be grateful without any trouble whatever.
Seneca

advice-e68bd1522c2461b00795e35a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e68bd1522c2461b00795e35a.body:
(Persisting in attempts to repay kindness) You say that you have done all in your power to repay your debt; this ought to be enough for your friend, but not enough for you.
Seneca

advice-5edac98141dfbb02fb84ed49.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5edac98141dfbb02fb84ed49.body:
(The Stoic distinction between perfect and ordinary beneficence) Benefits are of two kinds: one, the perfect and true benefit, which can only be bestowed by one wise man upon another; the other, the common vulgar form which ignorant men like ourselves interchange.
Seneca

advice-6fe77f727829f7ea9ac984ac.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6fe77f727829f7ea9ac984ac.body:
(Repaying a debt even to a morally corrupted benefactor) I will repay a good man when it is convenient; I will repay a bad man when he asks me to do so.
Seneca

advice-9bc617cf45a67704c04f658b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9bc617cf45a67704c04f658b.body:
(The imprint of philosophy and virtue never vanishes completely) Men do not change from the best to the worst; even in becoming bad, he would necessarily retain some traces of goodness; virtue is never so utterly quenched as not to imprint on the mind marks which no degradation can efface.
Seneca

advice-f8c8063ead90a2f986df9239.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f8c8063ead90a2f986df9239.body:
(The imprint of philosophy and virtue never vanishes completely) No one who has ever applied himself to philosophy ever becomes completely wicked; his mind becomes so deeply coloured with it, that its tints can never be entirely spoiled and blackened.
Seneca

advice-9d10fbd4952a00d5e2aaa6c1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9d10fbd4952a00d5e2aaa6c1.body:
(Repaying a debt even to a morally corrupted benefactor) If you owe anything, seek for some one to whom you may repay it, and if no one demands it, dun your own self; whether the man be good or bad is no concern of yours; repay him, and then blame him.
Seneca

advice-63dccc724c6a7111790867d4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-63dccc724c6a7111790867d4.body:
(Gently reminding someone of an unreturned benefit) Men ought sometimes to be reminded of their debts, though with modesty, not in the tone of one demanding a legal right.
Seneca

advice-e2f4523739bf3ac4ab925287.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e2f4523739bf3ac4ab925287.body:
(Examining one's own gratitude before judging others) Consider within yourself, whether you have always shown gratitude to those to whom you owe it, whether no one's kindness has ever been wasted upon you, whether you constantly bear in mind all the benefits which you have received.
Seneca

advice-e42744c15058f62a327b6fd2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e42744c15058f62a327b6fd2.body:
(Patience with an ungrateful friend helps him improve) You will make your friend a better man by bearing with him, you will in all cases make him a worse one by reproaching him.
Seneca

advice-d5427f32763e0511ec02e114.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d5427f32763e0511ec02e114.body:
(Publicly branding someone ungrateful destroys shame) No man fears to be that which all men see that he is; when his fault is made public, he loses his sense of shame.
Seneca

advice-06572c84404a0c7c1d7396ea.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-06572c84404a0c7c1d7396ea.body:
(Not ceasing to give benefits because of ingratitude) Bad men are overcome by unwearying goodness, nor does any one receive kindness in so harsh and hostile a spirit as not to love good men even while he does them wrong, when they lay him under the additional obligation of requiring no return for their kindness.
Seneca

advice-967be9824b3042f7cb505269.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-967be9824b3042f7cb505269.body:
(Not ceasing to give benefits because of ingratitude) It is no proof of a great mind to give and to throw away one's bounty; the true test of a great mind is to throw away one's bounty and still to give.
Seneca

advice-d307821529a67599ab990031.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d307821529a67599ab990031.body:
We are made to work together. When we resent other people and turn away from them, we act against our own nature.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-99e0436b8c24bf3f2e9254a9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-99e0436b8c24bf3f2e9254a9.body:
(On fate within the order of nature) That which is from fortune is not separated from nature or without an interweaving and involution with the things which are ordered by providence.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-17dd1f62695d3d554fec5973.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-17dd1f62695d3d554fec5973.body:
(On limited life and clarity of mind) Thou must now at last perceive of what universe thou art now a part, and of what administrator of the universe thy existence is an efflux, and that a limit of time is fixed for thee, which if thou dost not use for clearing away the clouds from thy mind, it will go and thou wilt go, and it will never return.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1a8e53522a1e1c4bd4c1c00f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1a8e53522a1e1c4bd4c1c00f.body:
(On attentive and just work) Every moment think steadily as a Roman and a man to do what thou hast in hand with perfect and simple dignity, and feeling of affection, and freedom, and justice, and to give thyself relief from all other thoughts.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-8ab9ce0aae5c09f114b2e805.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8ab9ce0aae5c09f114b2e805.body:
(On acting as if for the last time) And thou wilt give thyself relief if thou dost every act of thy life as if it were the last, laying aside all carelessness and passionate aversion from the commands of reason, and all hypocrisy, and self-love, and discontent with the portion which has been given to thee.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-74bb838ded244b6a43f7cb1d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-74bb838ded244b6a43f7cb1d.body:
(On making time to learn) Give thyself time to learn something new and good, and cease to be whirled around.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9756286ceca14a2465bdb795.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9756286ceca14a2465bdb795.body:
(On observing one's own mind) Through not observing what is in the mind of another a man has seldom been seen to be unhappy; but those who do not observe the movements of their own minds must of necessity be unhappy.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f20fc658f0d5349914b89dd2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f20fc658f0d5349914b89dd2.body:
(On the human being as part of nature) This thou must always bear in mind, what is the nature of the whole, and what is my nature, and how this is related to that, and what kind of a part it is of what kind of a whole, and that there is no one who hinders thee from always doing and saying the things which are according to the nature of which thou art a part.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-75addcedef864cd86aa4d24f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-75addcedef864cd86aa4d24f.body:
(On acting as if for the last time) Since it is possible that thou mayest depart from life this very moment, regulate every act and thought accordingly.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-efb6d919f4e3d1946693f79c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-efb6d919f4e3d1946693f79c.body:
(On death and divine providence) But to go away from among men, if there are gods, is not a thing to be afraid of, for the gods will not involve thee in evil; but if indeed they do not exist, or if they have no concern about human affairs, what is it to me to live in a universe devoid of gods or devoid of providence?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-82a0ce4c24892004ec46f9ec.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-82a0ce4c24892004ec46f9ec.body:
(On the transience of human things) How quickly all things disappear,—in the universe the bodies themselves, but in time the remembrance of them. What is the nature of all sensible things, and particularly those which attract with the bait of pleasure or terrify by pain, or are noised abroad by vapory fame; how worthless, and contemptible, and sordid, and perishable, and dead they are,—all this it is the part of the intellectual faculty to observe.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d08761dcbf9a08e41433090b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d08761dcbf9a08e41433090b.body:
(On human kinship and understanding ignorance) For the things from the gods merit veneration for their excellence; and the things from men should be dear to us by reason of kinship; and sometimes even, in a manner, they move our pity by reason of men’s ignorance of good and bad; this defect being not less than that which deprives us of the power of distinguishing things that are white and black.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-439f7d8eb810c67155976e5e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-439f7d8eb810c67155976e5e.body:
(On the present as the only life available) Though thou shouldest be going to live three thousand years, and as many times ten thousand years, still remember that no man loses any other life than this which he now lives, nor lives any other than this which he now loses.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-ddae1e41b0bed776c550ddf0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ddae1e41b0bed776c550ddf0.body:
(On the present as the only life available) For the present is the same to all, though that which perishes is not the same; and so that which is lost appears to be a mere moment.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1595739d44e9313d6848bed5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1595739d44e9313d6848bed5.body:
(On the soul opposing nature's common order) The soul of man does violence to itself, first of all, when it becomes an abscess, and, as it were, a tumor on the universe, so far as it can.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-37ed77e597312667bbe8b478.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-37ed77e597312667bbe8b478.body:
(On the soul submitting to pleasure and pain) In the third place, the soul does violence to itself when it is overpowered by pleasure or by pain.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-53b16fbbca0d568c5d789fb9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-53b16fbbca0d568c5d789fb9.body:
(On the transience of human things) Of human life the time is a point, and the substance is in a flux, and the perception dull, and the composition of the whole body subject to putrefaction, and the soul a whirl, and fortune hard to divine, and fame a thing devoid of judgment.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-4fb8c5e4c6478f3a9df7f3d8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4fb8c5e4c6478f3a9df7f3d8.body:
(On the transience of human things) And, to say all in a word, everything which belongs to the body is a stream, and what belongs to the soul is a dream and vapor, and life is a warfare and a stranger’s sojourn, and after—fame is oblivion.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d0904c34ffda2031954c82ed.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d0904c34ffda2031954c82ed.body:
(On limited life and clarity of mind) We ought to consider not only that our life is daily wasting away and a smaller part of it is left, but another thing also must be taken into the account, that if a man should live longer, it is quite uncertain whether the understanding will still continue sufficient for the comprehension of things, and retain the power of contemplation which strives to acquire the knowledge of the divine and the human.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-93811628fff31ea6c0e6092b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-93811628fff31ea6c0e6092b.body:
(On limited life and clarity of mind) We must make haste, then, not only because we are daily nearer to death, but also because the conception of things and the understanding of them cease first.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-8283ca741609c711905832ff.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8283ca741609c711905832ff.body:
(On beauty visible to one who understands nature) We ought to observe also that even the things which follow after the things which are produced according to nature contain something pleasing and attractive.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-92eb56961305e1e54fb7bee2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-92eb56961305e1e54fb7bee2.body:
(On beauty visible to one who understands nature) And the ears of corn bending down, and the lion’s eyebrows, and the foam which flows from the mouth of wild boars, and many other things,—though they are far from being beautiful if a man should examine them severally,—still, because they are consequent upon the things which are formed by nature, help to adorn them, and they please the mind; so that if a man should have a feeling and deeper insight with respect to the things which are produced in the universe, there is hardly one of those which follow by way of consequence which will not seem to him to be in a manner disposed so as to give pleasure.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-42e14f2bc6b15009c6a0a590.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-42e14f2bc6b15009c6a0a590.body:
(On beauty visible to one who understands nature) And so he will see even the real gaping jaws of wild beasts with no less pleasure than those which painters and sculptors show by imitation; and in an old woman and an old man he will be able to see a certain maturity and comeliness; and the attractive loveliness of young persons he will be able to look on with chaste eyes; and many such things will present themselves, not pleasing to every man, but to him only who has become truly familiar with Nature and her works.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-e11e72f2ad13a0107f6a4b1b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e11e72f2ad13a0107f6a4b1b.body:
(On death as the end of life's voyage) Thou hast embarked, thou hast made the voyage, thou art come to shore; get out.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3526cbbe83e2d6ff85104d9e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3526cbbe83e2d6ff85104d9e.body:
(On attending to others for the common good) Do not waste the remainder of thy life in thoughts about others, when thou dost not refer thy thoughts to some object of common utility.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-4af7196d125cc134a61772e9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4af7196d125cc134a61772e9.body:
(On attentive and just work) Labor not unwillingly, nor without regard to the common interest, nor without due consideration, nor with distraction; nor let studied ornament set off thy thoughts, and be not either a man of many words, or busy about too many things.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-ba91058ea822449de2394684.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ba91058ea822449de2394684.body:
(On inner reason and the ruler's duty) And further, let the deity which is in thee be the guardian of a living being, manly and of ripe age, and engaged in matter political, and a Roman, and a ruler, who has taken his post like a man waiting for the signal which summons him from life, and ready to go, having need neither of oath nor of any man’s testimony.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-e60f9ef8efa3b43e50874d92.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e60f9ef8efa3b43e50874d92.body:
(On moral self-reliance) Be cheerful also, and seek not external help nor the tranquillity which others give.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9987861b0b71a1b4e75bd6d9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9987861b0b71a1b4e75bd6d9.body:
(On moral self-reliance) A man then must stand erect, not be kept erect by others.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-0bca1ce7bdb593fb536d5584.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0bca1ce7bdb593fb536d5584.body:
(On cleansing the mind of vice) In the mind of one who is chastened and purified thou wilt find no corrupt matter, nor impurity, nor any sore skinned over.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3baf616c8bb734e730c45744.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3baf616c8bb734e730c45744.body:
(On the mind that forms judgments) Reverence the faculty which produces opinion. On this faculty it entirely depends whether there shall exist in thy ruling part any opinion inconsistent with nature and the constitution of the rational animal.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-0541bba1b3f5c98a50252e7c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0541bba1b3f5c98a50252e7c.body:
(On the fragility of posthumous fame) Short then is the time which every man lives, and small the nook of the earth where he lives; and short too the longest posthumous fame, and even this only continued by a succession of poor human beings, who will very soon die, and who know not even themselves, much less him who died long ago.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c43e40ed27cdbc822731e9b6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c43e40ed27cdbc822731e9b6.body:
(On attentive and just work) If thou workest at that which is before thee, following right reason seriously, vigorously, calmly, without allowing anything else to distract thee, but keeping thy divine part pure, as if thou shouldst be bound to give it back immediately; if thou holdest to this, expecting nothing, fearing nothing, but satisfied with thy present activity according to nature, and with heroic truth in every word and sound which thou utterest, thou wilt live happy. And there is no man who is able to prevent this.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-328b67e4891b9d27d38f60b3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-328b67e4891b9d27d38f60b3.body:
(On readiness to apply philosophical principles) As physicians have always their instruments and knives ready for cases which suddenly require their skill, so do thou have principles ready for the understanding of things divine and human, and for doing everything, even the smallest, with a recollection of the bond which unites the divine and human to one another.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-6bf4efefee25fa630461fc99.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6bf4efefee25fa630461fc99.body:
(On turning from postponed reading to self-improvement) Hasten then to the end which thou hast before thee, and, throwing away idle hopes, come to thy own aid, if thou carest at all for thyself, while it is in thy power.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-dc5a5d447f3d39f1257319fe.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dc5a5d447f3d39f1257319fe.body:
(On the body, desires, and reason) Body, soul, intelligence: to the body belong sensations, to the soul appetites, to the intelligence principles.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a2ad006d78fdc1ed8c4a95d7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a2ad006d78fdc1ed8c4a95d7.body:
(On reason adapting to circumstances) That which rules within, when it is according to nature, is so affected with respect to the events which happen, that it always easily adapts itself to that which is possible and is presented to it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-5a7c87d7d8a7f8f051199118.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5a7c87d7d8a7f8f051199118.body:
(On purpose and skillful action) Let no act be done without a purpose, nor otherwise than according to the perfect principles of art.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-6ee4509cdcf94752388d1d53.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6ee4509cdcf94752388d1d53.body:
(On finding peace within oneself) For nowhere either with more quiet or more freedom from trouble does a man retire than into his own soul, particularly when he has within him such thoughts that by looking into them he is immediately in perfect tranquillity; and I affirm that tranquillity is nothing else than the good ordering of the mind.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a988ed5f3467a27a3ecb7f70.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a988ed5f3467a27a3ecb7f70.body:
(On changes in the world and human judgments) The universe is transformation: life is opinion.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-28282d74cfa13805f5623fb7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-28282d74cfa13805f5623fb7.body:
(On shared reason and world citizenship) If our intellectual part is common, the reason also, in respect of which we are rational beings, is common: if this is so, common also is the reason which commands us what to do, and what not to do; if this is so, there is a common law also; if this is so, we are fellow-citizens; if this is so, we are members of some political community; if this is so, the world is in a manner a state. For of what other common political community will any one say that the whole human race are members?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-bb09bf285182f9f0a177c6d3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bb09bf285182f9f0a177c6d3.body:
(On death as the natural dissolution of elements) Death is such as generation is, a mystery of nature; composition out of the same elements, and a decomposition into the same; and altogether not a thing of which any man should be ashamed, for it is not contrary to [the nature of] a reasonable animal, and not contrary to the reason of our constitution.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d88736279ec574f1afca247e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d88736279ec574f1afca247e.body:
(On the judgment that makes an event harmful) Take away thy opinion, and then there is taken away the complaint, “I have been harmed.” Take away the complaint, “I have been harmed,” and the harm is taken away.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d07fd34827586cea45091fc2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d07fd34827586cea45091fc2.body:
(On moral harm and our judgments) That which does not make a man worse than he was, also does not make his life worse, nor does it harm him either from without or from within.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-de4d085ad21f4bf74b0c799e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-de4d085ad21f4bf74b0c799e.body:
(On fate within the order of nature) Consider that everything which happens, happens justly, and if thou observest carefully, thou wilt find it to be so.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-7238ec82d0efc03a24269807.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7238ec82d0efc03a24269807.body:
(On independence from an offender's opinion) Do not have such an opinion of things as he has who does thee wrong, or such as he wishes thee to have, but look at them as they are in truth.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-985de3ee2d8695f63bf38fad.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-985de3ee2d8695f63bf38fad.body:
(On the common good and revising one's opinions) A man should always have these two rules in readiness; the one to do only whatever the reason of the ruling and legislating faculty may suggest for the use of men; the other, to change thy opinion, if there is any one at hand who sets thee right and moves thee from any opinion.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3884153c89c9a0770f5751ac.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3884153c89c9a0770f5751ac.body:
(On returning to the nature that produced us) Thou shalt disappear in that which produced thee; but rather thou shalt be received back into its seminal principle by transmutation.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-001df903baea75034a5cbe84.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-001df903baea75034a5cbe84.body:
(On changing character through loyalty to reason) Within ten days thou wilt seem a god to those to whom thou art now a beast and an ape, if thou wilt return to thy principles and the worship of reason.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c7da2e0ecb36e1ea83266048.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c7da2e0ecb36e1ea83266048.body:
(On practicing virtue now) Do not act as if thou wert going to live ten thousand years.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3b29088ebe3e563982967519.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3b29088ebe3e563982967519.body:
(On practicing virtue now) While thou livest, while it is in thy power, be good.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-fb0cdaaee2773b443ba70879.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fb0cdaaee2773b443ba70879.body:
(On the fragility of posthumous fame) He who has a vehement desire for posthumous fame does not consider that every one of those who remember him will himself also die very soon; then again also they who have succeeded them, until the whole remembrance shall have been extinguished as it is transmitted through men who foolishly admire and perish.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-25c8b90f85fb48fe9c1566a0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-25c8b90f85fb48fe9c1566a0.body:
(On beauty independent of praise) That which is really beautiful has no need of anything; not more than law, not more than truth, not more than benevolence or modesty.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-8481b84f57f2a90386223793.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8481b84f57f2a90386223793.body:
(On the Stoic account of the transformation of souls) For as here the mutation of these bodies after a certain continuance, whatever it may be, and their dissolution make room for other dead bodies, so the souls which are removed into the air after subsisting for some time are transmuted and diffused, and assume a fiery nature by being received into the seminal intelligence of the universe, and in this way make room for the fresh souls which come to dwell there.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9b0271872a2ba7f57e6ff1d4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9b0271872a2ba7f57e6ff1d4.body:
(On justice and examining impressions) Do not be whirled about, but in every movement have respect to justice, and on the occasion of every impression maintain the faculty of comprehension [or understanding].
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a2423f0db7c1a0bb1379b8a1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a2423f0db7c1a0bb1379b8a1.body:
(On addressing nature as a whole) Everything is fruit to me which thy seasons bring, O Nature: from thee are all things, in thee are all things, to thee all things return.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-5b7a53302f7b401dcab6249f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5b7a53302f7b401dcab6249f.body:
(On discarding needless thoughts and actions) Now a man should take away not only unnecessary acts, but also unnecessary thoughts, for thus superfluous acts will not follow after.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d91fe30566af768130b60d94.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d91fe30566af768130b60d94.body:
(On virtuous living and accepting one's lot) Try how the life of the good man suits thee, the life of him who is satisfied with his portion out of the whole, and satisfied with his own just acts and benevolent disposition.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-37700933a311ee14871143fe.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-37700933a311ee14871143fe.body:
(On the transience of human things) In a word, thy life is short.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-136bb5bf7b2f17f22956c252.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-136bb5bf7b2f17f22956c252.body:
(On using the present wisely and justly) Thou must turn to profit the present by the aid of reason and justice.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f0cda0e6a5128970d7cb4ade.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f0cda0e6a5128970d7cb4ade.body:
(On understanding the world's structure and course) If he is a stranger to the universe who does not know what is in it, no less is he a stranger who does not know what is going on in it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-0f6ef5f966d4fc4985d540d8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0f6ef5f966d4fc4985d540d8.body:
(On devotion to one's craft and personal independence) Love the art, poor as it may be, which thou hast learned, and be content with it; and pass through the rest of life like one who has intrusted to the gods with his whole soul all that he has, making thyself neither the tyrant nor the slave of any man.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9a92664cfdffb5cc91e23d37.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9a92664cfdffb5cc91e23d37.body:
(On the short life of memories and those remembering) Everything is only for a day, both that which remembers and that which is remembered.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-efec30804b8704429bbc0bfb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-efec30804b8704429bbc0bfb.body:
(On natural change in things) Observe constantly that all things take place by change, and accustom thyself to consider that the nature of the universe loves nothing so much as to change the things which are and to make new things like them.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-e04416e1b678bef1a22ef8bf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e04416e1b678bef1a22ef8bf.body:
(On practicing virtue now) Thou wilt soon die, and thou art not yet simple, nor free from perturbations, nor without suspicion of being hurt by external things, nor kindly disposed towards all; nor dost thou yet place wisdom only in acting justly.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1f7551aaf3d343cef6f2cb44.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1f7551aaf3d343cef6f2cb44.body:
(On other people's motives and aims) Examine men’s ruling principles, even those of the wise, what kind of things they avoid, and what kind they pursue.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f5686e4cedc5e1bbac143335.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f5686e4cedc5e1bbac143335.body:
(On moral harm and our judgments) What is evil to thee does not subsist in the ruling principle of another; nor yet in any turning and mutation of thy corporeal covering.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3d5d4593b308bc2df546f4a2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3d5d4593b308bc2df546f4a2.body:
(On the world as one interconnected organism) Constantly regard the universe as one living being, having one substance and one soul; and observe how all things have reference to one perception, the perception of this one living being; and how all things act with one movement; and how all things are the co-operating causes of all things which exist; observe too the continuous spinning of the thread and the contexture of the web.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-42f3aca9acbc9cdd2fef8f8a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-42f3aca9acbc9cdd2fef8f8a.body:
(On natural change in things) It is no evil for things to undergo change, and no good for things to subsist in consequence of change.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-247a4c01e530d18602534d2e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-247a4c01e530d18602534d2e.body:
(On time as an unceasing succession of events) Time is like a river made up of the events which happen, and a violent stream; for as soon as a thing has been seen, it is carried away, and another comes in its place, and this will be carried away too.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-ee8d44822b1f70377d8a06da.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ee8d44822b1f70377d8a06da.body:
(On the ordinary nature of illness, death, and others' actions) Everything which happens is as familiar and well known as the rose in spring and the fruit in summer; for such is disease, and death, and calumny, and treachery, and whatever else delights fools or vexes them.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1aaa5172db2900dbf351c0b9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1aaa5172db2900dbf351c0b9.body:
(On death's inevitability regardless of lifespan) If any god told thee that thou shalt die to-morrow, or certainly on the day after to-morrow, thou wouldst not care much whether it was on the third day or on the morrow, unless thou wast in the highest degree mean- spirited; for how small is the difference. So think it no great thing to die after as many years as thou canst name rather than to-morrow.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-fee63f11183c60046ba8718f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fee63f11183c60046ba8718f.body:
(On the mortality of people and states) Think continually how many physicians are dead after often contracting their eyebrows over the sick; and how many astrologers after predicting with great pretensions the deaths of others; and how many philosophers after endless discourses on death or immortality; how many heroes after killing thousands; and how many tyrants who have used their power over men’s lives with terrible insolence, as if they were immortal; and how many cities are entirely dead, so to speak, Helice and Pompeii and Herculaneum, and others innumerable.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b022986f6b8cf125f9e3e3b3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b022986f6b8cf125f9e3e3b3.body:
(On the mortality of people and states) One man after burying another has been laid out dead, and another buries him; and all this in a short time.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-dc9441c061e04d6ba5508558.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dc9441c061e04d6ba5508558.body:
(On the transience of human things) To conclude, always observe how ephemeral and worthless human things are, and what was yesterday a little mucus, to-morrow will be a mummy or ashes.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-957e89cd74fc110359c8182d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-957e89cd74fc110359c8182d.body:
(On ending life's journey peacefully) Pass then through this little space of time conformably to nature, and end thy journey in content, just as an olive falls off when it is ripe, blessing nature who produced it, and thanking the tree on which it grew.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-08bbc0ec3c2e479cdeab59ef.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-08bbc0ec3c2e479cdeab59ef.body:
(On adversity that does not take away virtue) And does a thing seem to thee to be a deviation from man’s nature, when it is not contrary to the will of man’s nature?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d05f952f7cfab633f3c98ba9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d05f952f7cfab633f3c98ba9.body:
(On adversity that does not take away virtue) Will then this which has happened prevent thee from being just, magnanimous, temperate, prudent, secure against inconsiderate opinions and falsehood; will it prevent thee from having modesty, freedom, and everything else, by the presence of which man’s nature obtains all that is its own?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-67d4dad30b187a4dcf1b40d7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-67d4dad30b187a4dcf1b40d7.body:
(On death's inevitability regardless of lifespan) It is a vulgar, but still a useful help towards contempt of death, to pass in review those who have tenaciously stuck to life.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-8d0d0aa6ebe352fc8c09d94f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8d0d0aa6ebe352fc8c09d94f.body:
(On the direct path of rational action) Always run to the short way; and the short way is the natural: accordingly say and do everything in conformity with the soundest reason.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f159b5600673179d3deb8ec9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f159b5600673179d3deb8ec9.body:
(On waking up and the duty to act) In the morning when thou risest unwillingly, let this thought be present,—I am rising to the work of a human being.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1889418698cc6489dddf96e3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1889418698cc6489dddf96e3.body:
(On self-love through doing human work) So thou lovest not thyself, for if thou didst, thou wouldst love thy nature and her will.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b3ff32ecb2c09fe8ad181306.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b3ff32ecb2c09fe8ad181306.body:
(On freeing oneself from troubling impressions) How easy it is to repel and to wipe away every impression which is troublesome or unsuitable, and immediately to be in all tranquillity.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-6c858218414db66db62f05e5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6c858218414db66db62f05e5.body:
(On doing right despite others' disapproval) Judge every word and deed which are according to nature to be fit for thee; and be not diverted by the blame which follows from any people nor by their words, but if a thing is good to be done or said, do not consider it unworthy of thee.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f0684fbb55758b666847ba9a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f0684fbb55758b666847ba9a.body:
(On qualities that depend on choice) Show those qualities then which are altogether in thy power, sincerity, gravity, endurance of labor, aversion to pleasure, contentment with thy portion and with few things, benevolence, frankness, no love of superfluity, freedom from trifling, magnanimity.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1302e033a7f5b9ae1eee23e0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1302e033a7f5b9ae1eee23e0.body:
(On qualities that depend on choice) Dost thou not see how many qualities thou art immediately able to exhibit, in which there is no excuse of natural incapacity and unfitness, and yet thou still remainest voluntarily below the mark? or art thou compelled through being defectively furnished by nature to murmur, and to be stingy, and to flatter, and to find fault with thy poor body, and to try to please men, and to make great display, and to be so restless in thy mind?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-e53047a912fc4c32836eb14b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e53047a912fc4c32836eb14b.body:
(On training the mind despite slowness) Only if in truth thou canst be charged with being rather slow and dull of comprehension, thou must exert thyself about this also, not neglecting it nor yet taking pleasure in thy dulness.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-e10d50394d3fffab9f7a2912.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e10d50394d3fffab9f7a2912.body:
(On the common good as the universe's health) Let the perfecting and accomplishment of the things which the common nature judges to be good, be judged by thee to be of the same kind as thy health.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9044598f48faa0c6f304f208.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9044598f48faa0c6f304f208.body:
(On the harmony of nature and its parts) Neither does the nature of anything, whatever it may be, cause anything which is not suitable to that which is directed by it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-395a2aeff6998b543b81b12f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-395a2aeff6998b543b81b12f.body:
(On returning to philosophy after mistakes) Be not disgusted, nor discouraged, nor dissatisfied, if thou dost not succeed in doing everything according to right principles, but when thou hast failed, return back again, and be content if the greater part of what thou dost is consistent with man’s nature, and love this to which thou returnest; and do not return to philosophy as if she were a master, but act like those who have sore eyes and apply a bit of sponge and egg, or as another applies a plaster, or drenching with water. For thus thou wilt not fail to obey reason, and thou wilt repose in it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-34af6fd2e4e0449d875a58ca.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-34af6fd2e4e0449d875a58ca.body:
(On wisdom as a source of calm) For what is more agreeable than wisdom itself, when thou thinkest of the security and the happy course of all things which depend on the faculty of understanding and knowledge?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f9eee976ceb6272c63c4e776.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f9eee976ceb6272c63c4e776.body:
(On the difficulty of understanding the world) Things are in such a kind of envelopment that they have seemed to philosophers, not a few nor those common philosophers, altogether unintelligible; nay even to the Stoics themselves they seem difficult to understand.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b4202c8213592bd0ffe21525.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b4202c8213592bd0ffe21525.body:
(On death and divine providence) But on the contrary it is a man’s duty to comfort himself, and to wait for the natural dissolution, and not to be vexed at the delay, but to rest in these principles only: the one, that nothing will happen to me which is not conformable to the nature of the universe; and the other, that it is in my power never to act contrary to my god and daemon: for there is no man who will compel me to this.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-ba1c1f0ac39c3c383363bbd8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ba1c1f0ac39c3c383363bbd8.body:
(On transformations of form and matter in nature) I am composed of the formal and the material; and neither of them will perish into non-existence, as neither of them came into existence out of non-existence.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a8d691add864cbb3b80895ca.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a8d691add864cbb3b80895ca.body:
(On transformations of form and matter in nature) Every part of me then will be reduced by change into some part of the universe, and that again will change into another part of the universe, and so on forever.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-cd4c65c2df7252fa0646169f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cd4c65c2df7252fa0646169f.body:
(On the self-sufficiency of reason and philosophy) Reason and the reasoning art [philosophy] are powers which are sufficient for themselves and for their own works.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-0639eae3c53726f65c387d3f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0639eae3c53726f65c387d3f.body:
(On reason as humanity's distinction among living beings) But the things which have life are superior to those which have not life, and of those which have life the superior are those which have reason.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-91ec1cc4bca12ba2b6f299fd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-91ec1cc4bca12ba2b6f299fd.body:
(On the natural capacity to endure adversity) Nothing happens to any man which he is not formed by nature to bear.
Marcus Aurelius
