advice-82193b69077d89a26c344a09.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-82193b69077d89a26c344a09.body:
(On the unwise person's endurance as a challenge to wisdom) It is a shame then that ignorance and conceit should be stronger than wisdom.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f60126af6528b3d78b260eae.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f60126af6528b3d78b260eae.body:
(On the mind that forms judgments) Things themselves touch not the soul, not in the least degree; nor have they admission to the soul, nor can they turn or move the soul: but the soul turns and moves itself alone, and whatever judgments it may think proper to make, such it makes for itself the things which present themselves to it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2c5d7774a463177e6e0862f0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2c5d7774a463177e6e0862f0.body:
(On human kinship and understanding ignorance) In one respect man is the nearest thing to me, so far as I must do good to men and endure them.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-8788cbbd6e47b58f8bb563d9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8788cbbd6e47b58f8bb563d9.body:
(On divine reason in the world and in us) Reverence that which is best in the universe; and this is that which makes use of all things and directs all things. And in like manner also reverence that which is best in thyself; and this is of the same kind as that.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9a1be891144cbc5d38b737c7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9a1be891144cbc5d38b737c7.body:
(On the connection between personal and common good) That which does no harm to the state, does no harm to the citizen. In the case of every appearance of harm apply this rule: if the state is not harmed by this, neither am I harmed.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-e938cb03e7dac0fe64bbc166.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e938cb03e7dac0fe64bbc166.body:
(On natural change in things) Often think of the rapidity with which things pass by and disappear, both the things which are and the things which are produced. For substance is like a river in a continual flow, and the activities of things are in constant change, and the causes work in infinite varieties; and there is hardly anything which stands still.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-010a3a7a62ef415571950b7e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-010a3a7a62ef415571950b7e.body:
(On the human being as part of nature) Think of the universal substance, of which thou hast a very small portion; and of universal time, of which a short and indivisible interval has been assigned to thee; and of that which is fixed by destiny, and how small a part of it thou art.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-18f80d6fc1b87c90fe10a184.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-18f80d6fc1b87c90fe10a184.body:
(On virtuous living and accepting one's lot) I now have what the universal nature wills me to have; and I do what my nature now wills me to do.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-98c67af80fa8663cde249909.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-98c67af80fa8663cde249909.body:
(On the soul submitting to pleasure and pain) Let the part of thy soul which leads and governs be undisturbed by the movements in the flesh, whether of pleasure or of pain; and let it not unite with them, but let it circumscribe itself and limit those affects to their parts.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-8d2c1a73cafda79368d4d41a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8d2c1a73cafda79368d4d41a.body:
(On divine reason in the world and in us) And he does live with the gods who constantly shows to them that his own soul is satisfied with that which is assigned to him, and that it does all that the daemon wishes, which Zeus hath given to every man for his guardian and guide, a portion of himself.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-cddf6d5a4b892748c230e47a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cddf6d5a4b892748c230e47a.body:
(On the transience of human things) Soon, very soon, thou wilt be ashes, or a skeleton, and either a name or not even a name; but name is sound and echo.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b75646bb39d30a92b8691361.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b75646bb39d30a92b8691361.body:
(On the direct path of rational action) Thou canst pass thy life in an equable flow of happiness, if thou canst go by the right way, and think and act in the right way.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-662ff03294431a914a754953.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-662ff03294431a914a754953.body:
(On the connection between personal and common good) If this is neither my own badness, nor an effect of my own badness, and the common weal is not injured, why am I troubled about it, and what is the harm to the common weal?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-e24f8c74c7d3c9746b77db12.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e24f8c74c7d3c9746b77db12.body:
(On well-being created by one's own character) I was once a fortunate man, but I lost it, I know not how.—But fortunate means that a man has assigned to himself a good fortune: and a good fortune is good disposition of the soul, good emotions, good actions.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9f53b78e85571a3d7b732704.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9f53b78e85571a3d7b732704.body:
(On fate within the order of nature) The substance of the universe is obedient and compliant; and the reason which governs it has in itself no cause for doing evil, for it has no malice, nor does it do evil to anything, nor is anything harmed by it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a24d629ad107a208b5fe79d3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a24d629ad107a208b5fe79d3.body:
(On attentive and just work) Let it make no difference to thee whether thou art cold or warm, if thou art doing thy duty; and whether thou art drowsy or satisfied with sleep; and whether ill-spoken of or praised; and whether dying or doing something else.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-ce46e4be13be6fa4771c016f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ce46e4be13be6fa4771c016f.body:
(On ending life's journey peacefully) For it is one of the acts of life, this act by which we die: it is sufficient then in this act also to do well what we have in hand.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-e81669c3b5073420db57d2c2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e81669c3b5073420db57d2c2.body:
(On examining the nature and value of things) Look within. Let neither the peculiar quality of anything nor its value escape thee.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9bc0f875ffd8fffd31c551ff.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9bc0f875ffd8fffd31c551ff.body:
(On natural change in things) All existing things soon change, and they will either be reduced to vapor, if indeed all substance is one, or they will be dispersed.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-437445877ac29461084084f4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-437445877ac29461084084f4.body:
(On reason aware of its own actions) The reason which governs knows what its own disposition is, and what it does, and on what material it works.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-e498913cd50424699c6c4d14.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e498913cd50424699c6c4d14.body:
(On remaining good despite others' wrongdoing) The best way of avenging thyself is not to become like [the wrong- doer].
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f3db29123fd325617dba3fdb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f3db29123fd325617dba3fdb.body:
(On cooperation and human community) Take pleasure in one thing and rest in it, in passing from one social act to another social act, thinking of God.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c54d494eb053a199a3d7a66a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c54d494eb053a199a3d7a66a.body:
(On the mind that forms judgments) The ruling principle is that which rouses and turns itself, and while it makes itself such as it is and such as it wills to be, it also makes everything which happens appear to itself to be such as it wills.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3929bc033bb3b57a17b73fad.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3929bc033bb3b57a17b73fad.body:
(On fate within the order of nature) In conformity to the nature of the universe every single thing is accomplished; for certainly it is not in conformity to any other nature that each thing is accomplished, either a nature which externally comprehends this, or a nature which is comprehended within this nature, or a nature external and independent of this.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-603dcdd53e1a8b7b932970f4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-603dcdd53e1a8b7b932970f4.body:
(On restoring inner balance) When thou hast been compelled by circumstances to be disturbed in a manner, quickly return to thyself, and do not continue out of tune longer than the compulsion lasts; for thou wilt have more mastery over the harmony by continually recurring to it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-89873bf335a8d7d7918e2808.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-89873bf335a8d7d7918e2808.body:
(On philosophy as a refuge from court life) Let the court and philosophy now be to thee stepmother and mother: return to philosophy frequently and repose in her, through whom what thou meetest with in the court appears to thee tolerable, and thou appearest tolerable in the court.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-683e9b113945a7a8927325fd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-683e9b113945a7a8927325fd.body:
(On natural change in things) Motions and changes are continually renewing the world, just as the uninterrupted course of time is always renewing the infinite duration of ages.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b6d75119f7e58d8f95c0aed6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b6d75119f7e58d8f95c0aed6.body:
(On returning to the nature that produced us) For such as it is to have once drawn in the air and to have given it back, which we do every moment, just the same is it with the whole respiratory power, which thou didst receive at thy birth yesterday and the day before, to give it back to the element from which thou didst first draw it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-7c2ca67ad4fe0fe0d22d8008.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7c2ca67ad4fe0fe0d22d8008.body:
(On divine reason in the world and in us) But to reverence and honor thy own mind will make thee content with thyself, and in harmony with society, and in agreement with the gods, that is, praising all that they give and have ordered.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b1265228d5ab64437a2aaa11.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b1265228d5ab64437a2aaa11.body:
(On moral progress rather than bodily movement) Above, below, all around are the movements of the elements. But the motion of virtue is in none of these: it is something more divine, and advancing by a way hardly observed, it goes happily on its road.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-cd0d5b088160ebc47b643cbd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cd0d5b088160ebc47b643cbd.body:
(On the fragility of posthumous fame) How strangely men act! They will not praise those who are living at the same time and living with themselves; but to be themselves praised by posterity, by those whom they have never seen or ever will see, this they set much value on.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b19e6c738954acb227b3adde.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b19e6c738954acb227b3adde.body:
(On what is achievable and trust in one's abilities) If a thing is difficult to be accomplished by thyself, do not think that it is impossible for man: but if anything is possible for man and conformable to his nature, think that this can be attained by thyself too.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-6307247e3b56efb12785f94f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6307247e3b56efb12785f94f.body:
(On the common good and revising one's opinions) If any man is able to convince me and show me that I do not think or act rightly, I will gladly change; for I seek the truth, by which no man was ever injured.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3820579721403c9e54e71a5c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3820579721403c9e54e71a5c.body:
(On duty amid external things and misguided people) I do my duty: other things trouble me not; for they are either things without life, or things without reason, or things that have rambled and know not the way.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-880eaac10653ec7aeb984000.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-880eaac10653ec7aeb984000.body:
(On responsible treatment of non-rational creatures) As to the animals which have no reason, and generally all things and objects, do thou, since thou hast reason and they have none, make use of them with a generous and liberal spirit.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c8ddd1baf765322418607697.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c8ddd1baf765322418607697.body:
(On cooperation and human community) But towards human beings, as they have reason, behave in a social spirit.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-6b118c9021b5ce566865c95e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6b118c9021b5ce566865c95e.body:
(On the world as one interconnected organism) Consider how many things in the same indivisible time take place in each of us,—things which concern the body and things which concern the soul: and so thou wilt not wonder if many more things, or rather all things which come into existence in that which is the one and all, which we call Cosmos, exist in it at the same time.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-eed6da60eb46dbcdb72c5d90.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-eed6da60eb46dbcdb72c5d90.body:
(On human kinship and understanding ignorance) How cruel it is not to allow men to strive after the things which appear to them to be suitable to their nature and profitable!
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d63a0875368fb255500b68a8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d63a0875368fb255500b68a8.body:
(On death as the end of awareness or a change) Death is a cessation of the impressions through the senses, and of the pulling of the strings which move the appetites, and of the discursive movements of the thoughts, and of the service to the flesh.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2b6cd399336d738709f93025.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2b6cd399336d738709f93025.body:
(On keeping the spirit strong while the body endures) It is a shame for the soul to be first to give way in this life, when thy body does not give way.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d1801d4d36b9d5dc44cf2702.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d1801d4d36b9d5dc44cf2702.body:
(On preserving simplicity and goodness in power) Keep thyself then simple, good, pure, serious, free from affectation, a friend of justice, a worshipper of the gods, kind, affectionate, strenuous in all proper acts.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9f04e2791f59e1863d2a102a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9f04e2791f59e1863d2a102a.body:
(On waking anxieties compared to dreams) Return to thy sober senses and call thyself back; and when thou hast roused thyself from sleep and hast perceived that they were only dreams which troubled thee, now in thy waking hours look at these [the things about thee] as thou didst look at those [the dreams].
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b611216868a359a5686f3b76.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b611216868a359a5686f3b76.body:
(On the distinction between body and soul) I consist of a little body and a soul.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-091b87fa1bbb16b91513dad3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-091b87fa1bbb16b91513dad3.body:
(On one's proper work and natural purpose) Neither the labor which the hand does nor that of the foot is contrary to nature, so long as the foot does the foot’s work and the hand the hand’s.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-4b05b8c0128469eb086e4a41.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4b05b8c0128469eb086e4a41.body:
(On devotion to one's craft and personal independence) Dost thou not see how the handicraftsmen accommodate themselves up to a certain point to those who are not skilled in their craft,—nevertheless they cling to the reason [the principles] of their art, and do not endure to depart from it? Is it not strange if the architect and the physician shall have more respect to the reason [the principles] of their own arts than man to his own reason, which is common to him and the gods?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f27b1fb67d660b59d0914ef8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f27b1fb67d660b59d0914ef8.body:
(On the smallness of earth and the present before infinity) Asia, Europe, are corners of the universe; all the sea a drop in the universe; Athos a little clod of the universe: all the present time is a point in eternity.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-931da586df02a4e6ea44d25c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-931da586df02a4e6ea44d25c.body:
(On the recurring patterns of human events) He who has seen present things has seen all, both everything which has taken place from all eternity and everything which will be for time without end; for all things are of one kin and of one form.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-fd24144251af6bef15beda8f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fd24144251af6bef15beda8f.body:
(On the world as one interconnected organism) Frequently consider the connection of all things in the universe and their relation to one another. For in a manner all things are implicated with one another, and all in this way are friendly to one another; for one thing comes in order after another, and this is by virtue of the active movement and mutual conspiration and the unity of the substance.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-6706a8a868b0e28ce9a733bb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6706a8a868b0e28ce9a733bb.body:
(On virtuous living and accepting one's lot) Adapt thyself to the things with which thy lot has been cast: and the men among whom thou hast received thy portion, love them, but do it truly [sincerely].
Marcus Aurelius

advice-02530f4119377bd5c748cddd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-02530f4119377bd5c748cddd.body:
(On inner nature as a creative principle) Every instrument, tool, vessel, if it does that for which it has been made, is well, and yet he who made it is not there. But in the things which are held together by nature there is within, and there abides in, them the power which made them; wherefore the more is it fit to reverence this power, and to think, that, if thou dost live and act according to its will, everything in thee is in conformity to intelligence.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-fada7e15fc8a35bcad7984b8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fada7e15fc8a35bcad7984b8.body:
(On good and evil within the sphere of choice) But if we judge only those things which are in our power to be good or bad, there remains no reason either for finding fault with God or standing in a hostile attitude to man.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-22811a9dc9db38086d955195.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-22811a9dc9db38086d955195.body:
(On the common good as the universe's health) Whatever happens to every man, this is for the interest of the universal: this might be sufficient.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-4a1147f43d6f88fc7f69c957.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4a1147f43d6f88fc7f69c957.body:
(On the recurring patterns of human events) As it happens to thee in the amphitheatre and such places, that the continual sight of the same things, and the uniformity make the spectacle wearisome, so it is in the whole of life; for all things above, below, are the same and from the same.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-ca7badef5cc6164820067a24.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ca7badef5cc6164820067a24.body:
(On remaining good despite others' wrongdoing) One thing here is worth a great deal, to pass thy life in truth and justice, with a benevolent disposition even to liars and unjust men.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d71862c2879bcf592e1e9e92.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d71862c2879bcf592e1e9e92.body:
(On examples of virtue in people around us) For nothing delights so much as the examples of the virtues, when they are exhibited in the morals of those who live with us and present themselves in abundance, as far as is possible.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9dd061514c3f4c382d4c737d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9dd061514c3f4c382d4c737d.body:
(On virtuous living and accepting one's lot) Be not dissatisfied then that thou must live only so many years and not more; for as thou art satisfied with the amount of substance which has been assigned to thee, so be content with the time.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-4c95fffc6b8ae8c614da2b19.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4c95fffc6b8ae8c614da2b19.body:
(On one's own actions as the true good) He who loves fame considers another man’s activity to be his own good; and he who loves pleasure, his own sensations; but he who has understanding considers his own acts to be his own good.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-ede4d38a7472e606df0043c1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ede4d38a7472e606df0043c1.body:
(On the freedom to withhold a troubling judgment) It is in our power to have no opinion about a thing, and not to be disturbed in our soul; for things themselves have no natural power to form our judgments.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-32443775c4e8424b754c3f81.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-32443775c4e8424b754c3f81.body:
(On listening carefully to another person) Accustom thyself to attend carefully to what is said by another, and as much as it is possible, be in the speaker’s mind.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-ce75e7d65837ca1db4b1a5fd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ce75e7d65837ca1db4b1a5fd.body:
(On the connection between personal and common good) That which is not good for the swarm, neither is it good for the bee.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-54b9ea2903d5167fa0037caa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-54b9ea2903d5167fa0037caa.body:
(On mistaken judgment as a source of distortion) Dost thou think that a false opinion has less power than the bile in the jaundiced or the poison in him who is bitten by a mad dog?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-5e1ce5997eaf7c64329ae76a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5e1ce5997eaf7c64329ae76a.body:
(On the human being as part of nature) No man will hinder thee from living according to the reason of thy own nature: nothing will happen to thee contrary to the reason of the universal nature.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9a69dd866243b9139660ad61.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9a69dd866243b9139660ad61.body:
(On the transience of human things) How soon will time cover all things, and how many it has covered already.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-bb47625e02211cf0f0360923.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bb47625e02211cf0f0360923.body:
(On the mind that forms judgments) I can have that opinion about anything which I ought to have.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-72f962b3b0b11c0fee41a884.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-72f962b3b0b11c0fee41a884.body:
(On returning to sound judgments) The things which are external to my mind have no relation at all to my mind.—Let this be the state of thy affects, and thou standest erect.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-219e8df0c39b03954c73599e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-219e8df0c39b03954c73599e.body:
(On returning to sound judgments) To recover thy life is in thy power.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-eb813fc7d20085729b2702e0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-eb813fc7d20085729b2702e0.body:
(On returning to sound judgments) Look at things again as thou didst use to look at them; for in this consists the recovery of thy life.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-64d2bcd8ddf483218d60aafb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-64d2bcd8ddf483218d60aafb.body:
(On attention to words and actions) In discourse thou must attend to what is said, and in every movement thou must observe what is doing.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-6d14e0e53c3395ec16dad2de.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6d14e0e53c3395ec16dad2de.body:
(On accepting help in fulfilling one's duty) Be not ashamed to be helped; for it is thy business to do thy duty like a soldier in the assault on a town.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-212845dfe9a1eba59d405cce.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-212845dfe9a1eba59d405cce.body:
(On anxiety about the future and reliance on reason) Let not future things disturb thee, for thou wilt come to them, if it shall be necessary, having with thee the same reason which now thou usest for present things.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-08deff4f39aca69309513558.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-08deff4f39aca69309513558.body:
(On the direct path of rational action) To the rational animal the same act is according to nature and according to reason.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-fcb5bcfbf18aca35e9a7b807.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fcb5bcfbf18aca35e9a7b807.body:
(On cooperation and human community) Just as it is with the members in those bodies which are united in one, so it is with rational beings which exist separate, for they have been constituted for one co-operation.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c89c7a4b462fcfad78b04ccb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c89c7a4b462fcfad78b04ccb.body:
(On remaining good despite others' wrongdoing) Whatever any one does or says, I must be good; just as if the gold, or the emerald, or the purple were always saying this, Whatever any one does or says, I must be emerald and keep my color.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a6757243c5316c7f02715e4a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a6757243c5316c7f02715e4a.body:
(On reason preserving inner peace) The ruling faculty does not disturb itself; I mean, does not frighten itself or cause itself pain.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-6c60baa8120de6ebfacf91c7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6c60baa8120de6ebfacf91c7.body:
(On reason preserving inner peace) The leading principle in itself wants nothing, unless it makes a want for itself; and therefore it is both free from perturbation and unimpeded, if it does not disturb and impede itself.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-7c040088296f0cb5c1e90394.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7c040088296f0cb5c1e90394.body:
(On the world as one interconnected organism) Through the universal substance as through a furious torrent all bodies are carried, being by their nature united with and co-operating with the whole, as the parts of our body with one another.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c5b91799a9941e67385b5a7d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c5b91799a9941e67385b5a7d.body:
(On practicing virtue now) One thing only troubles me, lest I should do something which the constitution of man does not allow, or in the way which it does not allow, or what it does not allow now.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-4303fee735a858ac758a427b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4303fee735a858ac758a427b.body:
(On remaining good despite others' wrongdoing) It is peculiar to man to love even those who do wrong.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2522b9ee7c8f22fc8f180fd7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2522b9ee7c8f22fc8f180fd7.body:
(On natural change in things) Nature which governs the whole will soon change all things which thou seest, and out of their substance will make other things, and again other things from the substance of them, in order that the world may be ever new.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-dd8bcfd0d7ff217da438b648.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dd8bcfd0d7ff217da438b648.body:
(On human kinship and understanding ignorance) When a man has done thee any wrong, immediately consider with what opinion about good or evil he has done wrong.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-7c6d1d095a0a408b1b3d91c3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7c6d1d095a0a408b1b3d91c3.body:
(On appreciating what one already has) Think not so much of what thou hast not as of what thou hast: but of the things which thou hast select the best, and then reflect how eagerly they would have been sought, if thou hadst them not.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1a530dd3e5a5c7e48cdb9ea4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1a530dd3e5a5c7e48cdb9ea4.body:
(On justice as a condition of inner peace) The rational principle which rules has this nature, that it is content with itself when it does what is just, and so secures tranquillity.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-02ca73bbc4ae7171382357cb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-02ca73bbc4ae7171382357cb.body:
(On clear understanding of what happens) Understand well what happens either to thee or to another.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-78ada3108a0025b5813aec94.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-78ada3108a0025b5813aec94.body:
(On another's wrongdoing that need not become our own) Let the wrong which is done by a man stay there where the wrong was done.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-22bfa0bd1fe5e013ad7efc9e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-22bfa0bd1fe5e013ad7efc9e.body:
(On external things that are neither good nor evil) Adorn thyself with simplicity and modesty, and with indifference towards the things which lie between virtue and vice.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-ddf2ee20a17a0d005c233001.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ddf2ee20a17a0d005c233001.body:
(On death as the end of awareness or a change) About death: whether it is a dispersion, or a resolution into atoms, or annihilation, it is either extinction or change.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-937398400e91da0b48bf0049.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-937398400e91da0b48bf0049.body:
(On pain that does not destroy reason or dignity) About pain: the pain which is intolerable carries us off; but that which lasts a long time is tolerable; and the mind maintains its own tranquillity by retiring into itself, and the ruling faculty is not made worse.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-67ca04d148b5ab5b3b5b7245.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-67ca04d148b5ab5b3b5b7245.body:
(On contemplating the cosmos to clear one's thoughts) Look around at the courses of the stars, as if thou wert going along with them; and constantly consider the changes of the elements into one another, for such thoughts purge away the filth of the terrene life.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-dbd597c65616cc451775e622.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dbd597c65616cc451775e622.body:
(On justice and examining impressions) Everywhere and at all times it is in thy power piously to acquiesce in thy present condition, and to behave justly to those who are about thee, and to exert thy skill upon thy present thoughts, that nothing shall steal into them without being well examined.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a3df27ca9849f0450e9547dd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a3df27ca9849f0450e9547dd.body:
(On one's duty rather than tracking others' motives) Do not look around thee to discover other men’s ruling principles, but look straight to this, to what nature leads thee, both the universal nature through the things which happen to thee, and thy own nature through the acts which must be done by thee.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-edafa436a417418b08d0f85d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-edafa436a417418b08d0f85d.body:
(On living after mentally accepting death) Consider thyself to be dead, and to have completed thy life up to the present time; and live according to nature the remainder which is allowed thee.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1d87273415e4c531b960e9f9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1d87273415e4c531b960e9f9.body:
(On reason as an inner source of goodness) Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if thou wilt ever dig.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f15db170f6e4fe7a39dbd51f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f15db170f6e4fe7a39dbd51f.body:
(On readiness for unexpected adversity) The art of life is more like the wrestler’s art than the dancer’s, in respect of this, that it should stand ready and firm to meet onsets which are sudden and unexpected.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1c968a92034cca29f5b5e2a4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1c968a92034cca29f5b5e2a4.body:
(On examining the value of others' approval) Constantly observe who those are whose approbation thou wishest to have, and what ruling principles they possess.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-69aebe1d7abf2572d26fba97.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-69aebe1d7abf2572d26fba97.body:
(On pain that does not destroy reason or dignity) In every pain let this thought be present, that there is no dishonor in it, nor does it make the governing intelligence worse, for it does not damage the intelligence either so far as the intelligence is rational or so far as it is social.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-0797c36c13b3b312d6c83a92.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0797c36c13b3b312d6c83a92.body:
(On remaining good despite others' wrongdoing) Take care not to feel towards the inhuman as they feel towards men.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b0a5866d705ed554571c3d68.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b0a5866d705ed554571c3d68.body:
(On virtue accessible without scholarly sophistication) And because thou hast despaired of becoming a dialectician and skilled in the knowledge of nature, do not for this reason renounce the hope of being both free and modest, and social and obedient to God.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c2cc5e7b29435dbab1bc1df1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c2cc5e7b29435dbab1bc1df1.body:
(On pain that does not destroy reason or dignity) It is in thy power to live free from all compulsion in the greatest tranquillity of mind, even if all the world cry out against thee as much as they choose, and even if wild beasts tear in pieces the members of this kneaded matter which has grown around thee.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-7518c9b1a6675eb3a30a59d5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7518c9b1a6675eb3a30a59d5.body:
(On acting as if for the last time) The perfection of moral character consists in this, in passing every day as the last, and in being neither violently excited nor torpid nor playing the hypocrite.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-26255565760ba3a643f5655b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-26255565760ba3a643f5655b.body:
(On the gods' patience with humanity as an example) The gods who are immortal are not vexed because during so long a time they must tolerate continually men such as they are and so many of them bad; and besides this, they also take care of them in all ways.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-774a4b677601b897790784dd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-774a4b677601b897790784dd.body:
(On correcting one's vices rather than fleeing others') It is a ridiculous thing for a man not to fly from his own badness, which is indeed possible, but to fly from other men’s badness, which is impossible.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9a3873db1104c2341d850084.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9a3873db1104c2341d850084.body:
(On good actions benefiting the person who performs them) No man is tired of receiving what is useful.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2777aa6faabf093582ac77c0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2777aa6faabf093582ac77c0.body:
(On good actions benefiting the person who performs them) But it is useful to act according to nature.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-bb3aeb2cbfa469a88c5876bd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bb3aeb2cbfa469a88c5876bd.body:
(The universe's creation by universal nature) The nature of the All moved to make the universe.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a7e2e00b67c76caabde44402.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a7e2e00b67c76caabde44402.body:
(On the transience of human things) A little time and I am dead, and all is gone.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d053cf02bfbd46c7d2aa4096.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d053cf02bfbd46c7d2aa4096.body:
(On shared reason and world citizenship) What more do I seek, if what I am now doing is the work of an intelligent living being, and a social being, and one who is under the same law with God?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-cd1a00206ec0d01a1c4df6b9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cd1a00206ec0d01a1c4df6b9.body:
(On attentive and just work) In the next place, having fixed thy eyes steadily on thy business look at it, and at the same time remembering that it is thy duty to be a good man, and what man’s nature demands, do that without turning aside; and speak as it seems to thee most just, only let it be with a good disposition and with modesty and without hypocrisy.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-5c1baee2625880fdd479ab3e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5c1baee2625880fdd479ab3e.body:
(On natural change in things) The nature of the universal has this work to do,—to remove to that place the things which are in this, to change them, to take them away hence, and to carry them there.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-5e8ae27ee7f52b6f0832909b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5e8ae27ee7f52b6f0832909b.body:
(On natural change in things) All things are change, yet we need not fear anything new.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a4a53814d942c5ba0fa9be88.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a4a53814d942c5ba0fa9be88.body:
(Rational life: truth, community, and acceptance) Every nature is contented with itself when it goes on its way well; and a rational nature goes on its way well when in its thoughts it assents to nothing false or uncertain, and when it directs its movements to social acts only, and when it confines its desires and aversions to the things which are in its power, and when it is satisfied with everything that is assigned to it by the common nature.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-09f2a4b66c3c18be5b45ef01.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-09f2a4b66c3c18be5b45ef01.body:
(Giving up complaints about court life) Let no man any longer hear thee finding fault with the court life or with thy own.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-15c1beac2275c68ae80526d3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-15c1beac2275c68ae80526d3.body:
(Regret over neglecting something useful) Repentance is a kind of self-reproof for having neglected something useful; but that which is good must be something useful, and the perfect good man should look after it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-8c4b182e2dce8f550bcfc629.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8c4b182e2dce8f550bcfc629.body:
(Pleasure and moral goodness) Pleasure then is neither good nor useful.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1030b7834e07464685047f92.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1030b7834e07464685047f92.body:
(On waking up and the duty to act) When thou risest from sleep with reluctance, remember that it is according to thy constitution and according to human nature to perform social acts, but sleeping is common also to irrational animals.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-8dabe1d89be0fc5dbc200164.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8dabe1d89be0fc5dbc200164.body:
(Physics, ethics, and logic in examining impressions) Constantly and, if it be possible, on the occasion of every impression on the soul, apply to it the principles of Physic, of Ethic, and of Dialectic.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-37fef175e0a65e0389e42fc3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-37fef175e0a65e0389e42fc3.body:
(On human kinship and understanding ignorance) Whatever man thou meetest with, immediately say to thyself: What opinions has this man about good and bad? For if with respect to pleasure and pain and the causes of each, and with respect to fame and ignominy, death and life, he has such and such opinions, it will seem nothing wonderful or strange to me if he does such and such things; and I shall bear in mind that he is compelled to do so.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-0105f9670e80615e61bcc263.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0105f9670e80615e61bcc263.body:
(On the common good and revising one's opinions) Remember that to change thy opinion and to follow him who corrects thy error is as consistent with freedom as it is to persist in thy error.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-025e1084706caf848646f4ba.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-025e1084706caf848646f4ba.body:
(The natural ending of every process) Nature has had regard in everything no less to the end than to the beginning and the continuance, just like the man who throws up a ball.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1b979eee3047886d882a0533.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1b979eee3047886d882a0533.body:
(On attention to words and actions) Attend to the matter which is before thee, whether it is an opinion or an act or a word.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-911c33c3c32a961f120a5a52.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-911c33c3c32a961f120a5a52.body:
(On death as the end of awareness or a change) Remember this then, that this little compound, thyself, must either be dissolved, or thy poor breath must be extinguished, or be removed and placed elsewhere.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-5059a7ce19fbfd54dcf78ab4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5059a7ce19fbfd54dcf78ab4.body:
(On one's proper work and natural purpose) It is satisfaction to a man to do the proper works of a man.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a22ceff8c0daff568d293857.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a22ceff8c0daff568d293857.body:
(Rational life: truth, community, and acceptance) Now it is a proper work of a man to be benevolent to his own kind, to despise the movements of the senses, to form a just judgment of plausible appearances, and to take a survey of the nature of the universe and of the things which happen in it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3fe6703cd5d48873dd084e19.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3fe6703cd5d48873dd084e19.body:
(On pain that does not destroy reason or dignity) Pain is either an evil to the body—then let the body say what it thinks of it—or to the soul; but it is in the power of the soul to maintain its own serenity and tranquillity, and not to think that pain is an evil. For every judgment and movement and desire and aversion is within, and no evil ascends so high.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-333cc9da55c53e8053eeca7e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-333cc9da55c53e8053eeca7e.body:
(On the mind that forms judgments) Wipe out thy imaginations by often saying to thyself: Now it is in my power to let no badness be in this soul, nor desire, nor any perturbation at all; but looking at all things I see what is their nature, and I use each according to its value.—Remember this power which thou hast from nature.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-0c41458adcfdc413ae5f0bf8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0c41458adcfdc413ae5f0bf8.body:
(Plain and appropriate speech) Speak both in the senate and to every man, whoever he may be, appropriately, not with any affectation: use plain discourse.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a982f1f5d707d3b10f460816.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a982f1f5d707d3b10f460816.body:
(Separation from others as severance from the whole) If thou didst ever see a hand cut off, or a foot, or a head, lying anywhere apart from the rest of the body, such does a man make himself, as far as he can, who is not content with what happens, and separates himself from others, or does anything unsocial.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-0ad33facc5c7ed52cbd9e5dc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0ad33facc5c7ed52cbd9e5dc.body:
(Facing only the present difficulty) Do not disturb thyself by thinking of the whole of thy life.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-39d83e5bb8ae9b30e34da344.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-39d83e5bb8ae9b30e34da344.body:
(Facing only the present difficulty) In the next place remember that neither the future nor the past pains thee, but only the present.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-8d139a6c29d7f15aaf1e71a6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8d139a6c29d7f15aaf1e71a6.body:
(Justice and moderation in pleasures) In the constitution of the rational animal I see no virtue which is opposed to justice; but I see a virtue which is opposed to love of pleasure, and that is temperance.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d3bfb78ce546128092ce3f0b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d3bfb78ce546128092ce3f0b.body:
(On reason preserving inner peace) Let then the reason itself not trouble itself.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b547a5a318d1d671991efe55.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b547a5a318d1d671991efe55.body:
(The distinction between bodily harm and moral evil) Hindrance to the perceptions of sense is an evil to the animal nature.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1ed7675a8cc42bd9d14534c9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1ed7675a8cc42bd9d14534c9.body:
(Rational choice and external coercion) The things however which are proper to the understanding no other man is used to impede, for neither fire, nor iron, nor tyrant, nor abuse, touches it in any way.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-095fa85eaff50f540ab8ab29.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-095fa85eaff50f540ab8ab29.body:
(Not causing oneself mental pain) It is not fit that I should give myself pain, for I have never intentionally given pain even to another.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d4fb1a09aaaf3b58ed4ea14f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d4fb1a09aaaf3b58ed4ea14f.body:
(A sound mind accepting people and events) Different things delight different people; but it is my delight to keep the ruling faculty sound without turning away either from any man or from any of the things which happen to men, but looking at and receiving all with welcome eyes and using everything according to its value.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3b9240c907b04ce45b8b5c8a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3b9240c907b04ce45b8b5c8a.body:
(On the fragility of posthumous fame) See that thou secure this present time to thyself: for those who rather pursue posthumous fame do not consider that the men of after time will be exactly such as these whom they cannot bear now; and both are mortal.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-bc8659a6a7d7f918aaf85602.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bc8659a6a7d7f918aaf85602.body:
(On the natural capacity to endure adversity) Nothing can happen to any man which is not a human accident, nor to an ox which is not according to the nature of an ox, nor to a vine which is not according to the nature of a vine, nor to a stone which is not proper to a stone.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-5eb85eff1c9f8372554a6eae.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5eb85eff1c9f8372554a6eae.body:
(On the judgment that makes an event harmful) If thou art pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs thee, but thy own judgment about it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-11c1c96667781daefb1f5315.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-11c1c96667781daefb1f5315.body:
(On returning to sound judgments) But if anything in thy own disposition gives thee pain, who hinders thee from correcting thy opinion?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f575ffee9f97cbc65807afa9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f575ffee9f97cbc65807afa9.body:
(Rational choice and external coercion) Remember that the ruling faculty is invincible, when self-collected it is satisfied with itself, if it does nothing which it does not choose to do, even if it resist from mere obstinacy.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-ba77559a70236edfbe26e8f4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ba77559a70236edfbe26e8f4.body:
(Facts without added judgments or fears) Say nothing more to thyself than what the first appearances report.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-7c37fb4e33e379244df80d9d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7c37fb4e33e379244df80d9d.body:
(Composure without bustle or inner conflict) Neither in thy actions be sluggish nor in thy conversation without method, nor wandering in thy thoughts, nor let there be in thy soul inward contention nor external effusion, nor in life be so busy as to have no leisure.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-48c0e5b260626edd7ca7a6a2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-48c0e5b260626edd7ca7a6a2.body:
(On understanding the world's structure and course) He who does not know what the world is, does not know where he is.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d9a23dfe604c4cfa958dcac3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d9a23dfe604c4cfa958dcac3.body:
(On divine reason in the world and in us) No longer let thy breathing only act in concert with the air which surrounds thee, but let thy intelligence also now be in harmony with the intelligence which embraces all things.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-88c778fefcc32bd28743bc92.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-88c778fefcc32bd28743bc92.body:
(One's own choice independent of another's will) To my own free will the free will of my neighbor is just as indifferent as his poor breath and flesh.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-0f4544eb7f9dfe634c7de69d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0f4544eb7f9dfe634c7de69d.body:
(On death as the end of awareness or a change) He who fears death either fears the loss of sensation or a different kind of sensation.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-8b7584a19fa919ca6184708e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8b7584a19fa919ca6184708e.body:
(On cooperation and human community) Men exist for the sake of one another.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-165e297c9d442a106fc15512.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-165e297c9d442a106fc15512.body:
(The mind's purposefulness in caution and inquiry) The mind indeed, both when it exercises caution and when it is employed about inquiry, moves straight onward not the less, and to its object.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-56f15d5c5a24d832ba54053e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-56f15d5c5a24d832ba54053e.body:
(Mutual understanding of thoughts) Enter into every man’s ruling faculty; and also let every other man enter into thine.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-eb68772f2563fd2b909c2386.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-eb68772f2563fd2b909c2386.body:
(On cooperation and human community) For since the universal nature has made rational animals for the sake of one another to help one another according to their deserts, but in no way to injure one another, he who transgresses her will is clearly guilty of impiety towards the highest divinity.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f1f28b539517cf0f5a19e2ba.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f1f28b539517cf0f5a19e2ba.body:
(Nature as the foundation of truth) And further, this universal nature is named truth, and is the prime cause of all things that are true.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-76852e732f7eccee6d311788.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-76852e732f7eccee6d311788.body:
(Stoic piety and judgments of pain and pleasure) And indeed he who pursues pleasure as good, and avoids pain as evil, is guilty of impiety.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-aecf221c1bd42345d00703ca.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-aecf221c1bd42345d00703ca.body:
(Stoic piety and judgments of pain and pleasure) And further, he who is afraid of pain will sometimes also be afraid of some of the things which will happen in the world, and even this is impiety.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f8db6e339dc93174f0f55d63.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f8db6e339dc93174f0f55d63.body:
(Stoic piety and judgments of pain and pleasure) And he who pursues pleasure will not abstain from injustice, and this is plainly impiety.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9478fbe8f7041693eb158d67.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9478fbe8f7041693eb158d67.body:
(Stoic piety and judgments of pain and pleasure) With respect to pain, then, and pleasure, or death and life, or honor and dishonor, which the universal nature employs equally, whoever is not equally affected is manifestly acting impiously.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f3f8e3622438e52bd6e96bf9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f3f8e3622438e52bd6e96bf9.body:
(On death as the natural dissolution of elements) Do not despise death, but be well content with it, since this too is one of those things which nature wills.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c80221bffd3f3cafe6e96b63.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c80221bffd3f3cafe6e96b63.body:
(Death; the envelope is the body that the soul leaves) As thou now waitest for the time when the child shall come out of thy wife’s womb, so be ready for the time when thy soul shall fall out of this envelope.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-6cdba4fea2b7ee06ca6556b5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6cdba4fea2b7ee06ca6556b5.body:
(Consolation before death: leaving an imperfect society) But if thou requirest also a vulgar kind of comfort which shall reach thy heart, thou wilt be made best reconciled to death by observing the objects from which thou art going to be removed, and the morals of those with whom thy soul will no longer be mingled.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-8115dea6ddd8de9861a5e013.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8115dea6ddd8de9861a5e013.body:
(Consolation before death: leaving an imperfect society) For it is no way right to be offended with men, but it is thy duty to care for them and to bear with them gently; and yet to remember that thy departure will not be from men who have the same principles as thyself.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-0ddd8cbf118e376048d9872d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0ddd8cbf118e376048d9872d.body:
(The mind's mastery of desires and impressions) Wipe out imagination: check desire: extinguish appetite: keep the ruling faculty in its own power.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2f034f7283623d52bf05b517.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2f034f7283623d52bf05b517.body:
(On shared reason and world citizenship) Among the animals which have not reason one life is distributed; but among reasonable animals one intelligent soul is distributed: just as there is one earth of all things which are of an earthy nature, and we see by one light, and breathe one air, all of us that have the faculty of vision and all that have life.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-912526989715b8a55b2e6ad3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-912526989715b8a55b2e6ad3.body:
(On cooperation and human community) Sooner, then, will one find anything earthy which comes in contact with no earthy thing, than a man altogether separated from other men.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c960cbd26ff01ea046075688.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c960cbd26ff01ea046075688.body:
(Reason's fruitfulness for the person and society) Reason produces fruit both for all and for itself, and there are produced from it other things of the same kind as reason itself.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9b2f6231a4cbd33a000b28a8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9b2f6231a4cbd33a000b28a8.body:
(Gently correcting others' errors) If thou art able, correct by teaching those who do wrong; but if thou canst not, remember that indulgence is given to thee for this purpose.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-893161fe0def8869f18c9b73.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-893161fe0def8869f18c9b73.body:
(On the judgment that makes an event harmful) To-day I have got out of all trouble, or rather I have cast out all trouble, for it was not outside, but within and in my opinions.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-06ca39ab77f6decd460fe5ea.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-06ca39ab77f6decd460fe5ea.body:
(On the recurring patterns of human events) All things are the same, familiar in experience, and ephemeral in time, and worthless in the matter.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1a784124b891b71fe0ac44b1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1a784124b891b71fe0ac44b1.body:
(Moral goodness in action rather than what one undergoes) Not in passivity but in activity lie the evil and the good of the rational social animal, just as his virtue and his vice lie not in passivity but in activity.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f10258adb63853f4f91fed50.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f10258adb63853f4f91fed50.body:
(On examining the value of others' approval) Penetrate inwards into men’s leading principles, and thou wilt see what judges thou art afraid of, and what kind of judges they are of themselves.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-0ab71f45e2c79b3f7ea429b3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0ab71f45e2c79b3f7ea429b3.body:
(On natural change in things) All things are changing: and thou thyself art in continuous mutation and in a manner in continuous destruction, and the whole universe too.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f35a9157dc672f5de7224aa6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f35a9157dc672f5de7224aa6.body:
(On another's wrongdoing that need not become our own) It is thy duty to leave another man’s wrongful act there where it is.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3d021da17c9e9b6b40bb6354.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3d021da17c9e9b6b40bb6354.body:
(Life's successive stages as natural endings) Termination of activity, cessation from movement and opinion, and in a sense their death, is no evil.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b0ff3d3bb8ccba6ca521a808.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b0ff3d3bb8ccba6ca521a808.body:
(Life's successive stages as natural endings) Turn thy thoughts now to the consideration of thy life, thy life as a child, as a youth, thy manhood, thy old age, for in these also every change was a death.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-102f099884e573bdc43f595b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-102f099884e573bdc43f595b.body:
(On cooperation and human community) As thou thyself art a component part of a social system, so let every act of thine be a component part of social life.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-e1ec83611ed33095a9e70c92.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e1ec83611ed33095a9e70c92.body:
(Separation from others as severance from the whole) Whatever act of thine then has no reference either immediately or remotely to a social end, this tears asunder thy life, and does not allow it to be one, and it is of the nature of a mutiny, just as when in a popular assembly a man acting by himself stands apart from the general agreement.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3ddd69ecb090a8d1d82354bb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3ddd69ecb090a8d1d82354bb.body:
(A thing's form, matter, and duration) Examine into the quality of the form of an object, and detach it altogether from its material part, and then contemplate it; then determine the time, the longest which a thing of this peculiar form is naturally made to endure.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1643ae65c2453c6dfae1365e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1643ae65c2453c6dfae1365e.body:
(Dissatisfaction with reason acting according to nature) Thou hast endured infinite troubles through not being contented with thy ruling faculty when it does the things which it is constituted by nature to do.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2b678b77e309349d326cd6b2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2b678b77e309349d326cd6b2.body:
(On examining the value of others' approval) When another blames thee or hates thee, or when men say about thee anything injurious, approach their poor souls, penetrate within, and see what kind of men they are.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-080976b5fb644a387b1c1053.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-080976b5fb644a387b1c1053.body:
(On natural change in things) Soon will the earth cover us all: then the earth, too, will change, and the things also which result from change will continue to change forever, and these again forever.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-357756efdadf901e172a9836.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-357756efdadf901e172a9836.body:
(Philosophy's simplicity and modesty) Simple and modest is the work of philosophy.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-895064a7f90468482dd0f642.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-895064a7f90468482dd0f642.body:
(A view of human life from above) Look down from above on the countless herds of men and their countless solemnities, and the infinitely varied voyagings in storms and calms, and the differences among those who are born, who live together, and die.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-37c1c933e7afc1ce65b44281.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-37c1c933e7afc1ce65b44281.body:
(On the fragility of posthumous fame) And consider, too, the life lived by others in olden time, and the life of those who will live after thee, and the life now lived among barbarous nations, and how many know not even thy name, and how many will soon forget it, and how they who perhaps now are praising thee will very soon blame thee, and that neither a posthumous name is of any value, nor reputation, nor anything else.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2653ef55badd3c3180138f0b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2653ef55badd3c3180138f0b.body:
(Calm about external events and justice in one's actions) Let there be freedom from perturbations with respect to the things which come from the external cause; and let there be justice in the things done by virtue of the internal cause, that is, let there be movement and action terminating in this, in social acts, for this is according to thy nature.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-5f1c19032032a2e22cd899e6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5f1c19032032a2e22cd899e6.body:
(On contemplating the cosmos to clear one's thoughts) Thou canst remove out of the way many useless things among those which disturb thee, for they lie entirely in thy opinion; and thou wilt then gain for thyself ample space by comprehending the whole universe in thy mind, and by contemplating the eternity of time, and observing the rapid change of every several thing, how short is the time from birth to dissolution, and the illimitable time before birth as well as the equally boundless time after dissolution!
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2df8765f6f616a498e648b24.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2df8765f6f616a498e648b24.body:
(On the transience of human things) All that thou seest will quickly perish, and those who have been spectators of its dissolution will very soon perish too.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-e1c6d21653f4b15973ed77aa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e1c6d21653f4b15973ed77aa.body:
(On natural change in things) Loss is nothing else than change. But the universal nature delights in change, and in obedience to her all things are now done well, and from eternity have been done in like form, and will be such to time without end.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-4b594a1fe76becad66ed5c34.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4b594a1fe76becad66ed5c34.body:
(On another's wrongdoing that need not become our own) If any man has done wrong, the harm is his own.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-4178eb74d56cb9005f081a44.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4178eb74d56cb9005f081a44.body:
(A rational cosmos or a combination of atoms) Either all things proceed from one intelligent source and come together as in one body, and the part ought not to find fault with what is done for the benefit of the whole; or there are only atoms, and nothing else than mixture and dispersion.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-1c145ef566e5e333501fcfb8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1c145ef566e5e333501fcfb8.body:
(Virtues as a response to others' wrongdoing) It is useful to perceive this, too, immediately when the occasion arises, what virtue nature has given to man to oppose to every wrongful act.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-affae32ea8842c4cd9c20b68.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-affae32ea8842c4cd9c20b68.body:
(The hierarchy of natural, animal, and rational needs) Observe what thy nature requires, so far as thou art governed by nature only: then do it and accept it, if thy nature, so far as thou art a living being, shall not be made worse by it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a1891698d7b2cbd04344844c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a1891698d7b2cbd04344844c.body:
(The hierarchy of natural, animal, and rational needs) And next thou must observe what thy nature requires so far as thou art a living being.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-dd9ad4e6943d59b2a0eaf575.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dd9ad4e6943d59b2a0eaf575.body:
(On the natural capacity to endure adversity) If, then, it happens to thee in such way as thou art formed by nature to bear it, do not complain, but bear it as thou art formed by nature to bear it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b9977360056022d541b2185b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b9977360056022d541b2185b.body:
(On the natural capacity to endure adversity) Remember, however, that thou art formed by nature to bear everything, with respect to which it depends on thy own opinion to make it endurable and tolerable, by thinking that it is either thy interest or thy duty to do this.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c4b1ed72eff77f4f4cb333ad.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c4b1ed72eff77f4f4cb333ad.body:
(Gently correcting others' errors) If a man is mistaken, instruct him kindly and show him his error.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-815f84e38e1974c3f6b628de.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-815f84e38e1974c3f6b628de.body:
(Names of virtues as demands on one's character) When thou hast assumed these names, good, modest, true, rational, a man of equanimity, and magnanimous, take care that thou dost not change these names; and if thou shouldst lose them, quickly return to them.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-60a992671bb61ed06403a819.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-60a992671bb61ed06403a819.body:
(The meaning of rationality, equanimity, and magnanimity) And remember that the term Rational was intended to signify a discriminating attention to every several thing, and freedom from negligence; and that Equanimity is the voluntary acceptance of the things which are assigned to thee by the common nature; and that Magnanimity is the elevation of the intelligent part above the pleasurable or painful sensations of the flesh, and above that poor thing called fame, and death, and all such things.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-09d92f420dcc53bc2d0b8beb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-09d92f420dcc53bc2d0b8beb.body:
(Combining action, contemplation, and quiet confidence) But it is thy duty so to look on and so to do everything, that at the same time the power of dealing with circumstances is perfected, and the contemplative faculty is exercised, and the confidence which comes from the knowledge of each several thing is maintained without showing it, but yet not concealed.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-df8419980f206afbd04ea256.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-df8419980f206afbd04ea256.body:
(On wisdom as a source of calm) He who follows reason in all things is both tranquil and active at the same time, and also cheerful and collected.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-6fa1349957a1919eec3576f7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6fa1349957a1919eec3576f7.body:
(One's own choice independent of another's will) Inquire of thyself as soon as thou wakest from sleep whether it will make any difference to thee if another does what is just and right.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c8120eacecc7e10874141fa7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c8120eacecc7e10874141fa7.body:
(On addressing nature as a whole) To her who gives and takes back all, to nature, the man who is instructed and modest says, Give what thou wilt; take back what thou wilt.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a70ac4d3c721ceb6f2abaf41.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a70ac4d3c721ceb6f2abaf41.body:
(On the transience of human things) Short is the little which remains to thee of life.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-dc7aae93b7762b57b133223b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dc7aae93b7762b57b133223b.body:
(A personal example of living according to nature) Let men see, let them know a real man who lives according to nature.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-063383a0970998550e23c0b6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-063383a0970998550e23c0b6.body:
(On practicing virtue now) No longer talk at all about the kind of man that a good man ought to be, but be such.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-455f677b8e8ca5d325561c6a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-455f677b8e8ca5d325561c6a.body:
(On the smallness of earth and the present before infinity) Constantly contemplate the whole of time and the whole of substance, and consider that all individual things as to substance are a grain of a fig, and as to time the turning of a gimlet.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9b3ebf7607150a74097c0a02.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9b3ebf7607150a74097c0a02.body:
(On natural change in things) Look at everything that exists, and observe that it is already in dissolution and in change, and as it were putrefaction or dispersion, or that everything is so constituted by nature as to die.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a9250ce58339b8a3ac326f8e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a9250ce58339b8a3ac326f8e.body:
(On fate within the order of nature) That is for the good of each thing, which the universal nature brings to each.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-5eb1a0dc18d70950e3c1daf0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5eb1a0dc18d70950e3c1daf0.body:
(A change of place does not change the nature of things) Let this always be plain to thee, that this piece of land is like any other; and that all things here are the same with things on the top of a mountain, or on the sea-shore, or wherever thou choosest to be.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-87efdb22f5ca574c5c244d0f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-87efdb22f5ca574c5c244d0f.body:
(On the recurring patterns of human events) Constantly consider how all things such as they now are, in time past also were; and consider that they will be the same again.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-91d58af460fe8b7493b712f4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-91d58af460fe8b7493b712f4.body:
(Protesting the inevitable as futile resistance) Imagine every man who is grieved at anything or discontented to be like a pig which is sacrificed and kicks and screams.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2b3131abb326dbb95331a263.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2b3131abb326dbb95331a263.body:
(Assessing one's activities in the face of death) Severally on the occasion of everything that thou doest, pause and ask thyself if death is a dreadful thing because it deprives thee of this.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d213e0323372503348e7fa61.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d213e0323372503348e7fa61.body:
(Understanding others' errors by acknowledging one's own) When thou art offended at any man’s fault, forthwith turn to thyself and reflect in what like manner thou dost err thyself; for example, in thinking that money is a good thing, or pleasure, or a bit of reputation, and the like.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2c1dfe4a04304ff185df1bae.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2c1dfe4a04304ff185df1bae.body:
(On good actions benefiting the person who performs them) Thou wilt not cease to lament till thy mind is in such a condition that, what luxury is to those who enjoy pleasure, such shall be to thee, in the matter which is subjected and presented to thee, the doing of the things which are conformable to man’s constitution; for a man ought to consider as an enjoyment everything which it is in his power to do according to his own nature.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-dbd860601c39eaca1d9490b4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dbd860601c39eaca1d9490b4.body:
(On reason adapting to circumstances) But intelligence and reason are able to go through everything that opposes them, and in such manner as they are formed by nature and as they choose.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-26dedf48a69f9c28438150e8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-26dedf48a69f9c28438150e8.body:
(On readiness to apply philosophical principles) To him who is penetrated by true principles even the briefest precept is sufficient, and any common precept, to remind him that he should be free from grief and fear.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-e55488cf1a2bb30b21a60007.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e55488cf1a2bb30b21a60007.body:
(On the mortality of people and states) A little time, and thou shalt close thy eyes; and him who has attended thee to thy grave another will soon lament.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-14b985771dfc0e1aa489dad4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-14b985771dfc0e1aa489dad4.body:
(Consolation before death: leaving an imperfect society) There is no man so fortunate that there shall not be by him when he is dying some who are pleased with what is going to happen.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-822433626f7919ee4052c9dd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-822433626f7919ee4052c9dd.body:
(The hidden mind as the person's driving force) Remember that this which pulls the strings is the thing which is hidden within: this is the power of persuasion, this is life, this, if one may so say, is man.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f1101d0356fa8f00375f5fc2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f1101d0356fa8f00375f5fc2.body:
(Breaking attractive things into simple parts) In all things, then, except virtue and the acts of virtue, remember to apply thyself to their several parts, and by this division to come to value them little: and apply this rule also to thy whole life.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3b2678f224fc9d52a9baa587.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3b2678f224fc9d52a9baa587.body:
(Reasoned readiness for death; a polemic against Christians) What a soul that is which is ready, if at any moment it must be separated from the body, and ready either to be extinguished or dispersed or continue to exist; but so that this readiness comes from a man’s own judgment, not from mere obstinacy, as with the Christians, but considerately and with dignity and in a way to persuade another, without tragic show.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-7ee9cf290c7ad60128bdf02f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7ee9cf290c7ad60128bdf02f.body:
(Tragedy as practice in accepting life's events) At first tragedies were brought on the stage as means of reminding men of the things which happen to them, and that it is according to nature for things to happen so, and that, if you are delighted with what is shown on the stage, you should not be troubled with that which takes place on the larger stage.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-5239006691db3de00ba9cadc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5239006691db3de00ba9cadc.body:
(Philosophy in one's present circumstances) How plain does it appear that there is not another condition of life so well suited for philosophizing as this in which thou now happenest to be.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2bd87c95067efbc5e76ab6dd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2bd87c95067efbc5e76ab6dd.body:
(Separation from others as severance from the whole) Now as to a branch, another cuts it off; but a man by his own act separates himself from his neighbor when he hates him and turns away from him, and he does not know that he has at the same time cut himself off from the whole social system.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-30d658037c70174688bb37f5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-30d658037c70174688bb37f5.body:
(On remaining good despite others' wrongdoing) As those who try to stand in thy way when thou art proceeding according to right reason will not be able to turn thee aside from thy proper action, so neither let them drive thee from thy benevolent feelings towards them, but be on thy guard equally in both matters, not only in the matter of steady judgment and action, but also in the matter of gentleness to those who try to hinder or otherwise trouble thee.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-881a64aa2d929f87386c97b2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-881a64aa2d929f87386c97b2.body:
(Nature as the model for art and craft) There is no nature which is inferior to art, for the arts imitate the natures of things.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b8f0af3f3d5116e1cd188bb3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b8f0af3f3d5116e1cd188bb3.body:
(Subordinating the lesser to the greater in art and nature) Now all arts do the inferior things for the sake of the superior; therefore the universal nature does so too.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3e33f33c533fc813872c0c2f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3e33f33c533fc813872c0c2f.body:
(How desire and fear bring troubling objects closer) If the things do not come to thee, the pursuits and avoidances of which disturb thee, still in a manner thou goest to them.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2b2d99465f4fef75255e99e8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2b2d99465f4fef75255e99e8.body:
(The soul as a sphere: composure and inner light) The spherical form of the soul maintains its figure when it is neither extended towards any object, nor contracted inwards, nor dispersed nor sinks down, but is illuminated by light, by which it sees the truth,—the truth of all things and the truth that is in itself.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2ebdb1e0dc17516e02317695.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2ebdb1e0dc17516e02317695.body:
(On the connection between personal and common good) For what evil is it to thee, if thou art now doing what is agreeable to thy own nature, and art satisfied with that which at this moment is suitable to the nature of the universe, since thou art a human being placed at thy post in order that what is for the common advantage may be done in some way?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9b7a6bc6733c0de231af8e2c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9b7a6bc6733c0de231af8e2c.body:
(The contradictions of vanity and flattery) Men despise one another and flatter one another; and men wish to raise themselves above one another, and crouch before one another.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f6592a3c429717d2e748294f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f6592a3c429717d2e748294f.body:
(Genuine honesty visible without assurances) The man who is honest and good ought to be exactly like a man who smells strong, so that the bystander as soon as he comes near him must smell whether he choose or not.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-4f56d79e27904e734a989a0f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4f56d79e27904e734a989a0f.body:
(On external things that are neither good nor evil) As to living in the best way, this power is in the soul, if it be indifferent to things which are indifferent.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-cb2ed8dbd4280e277e6924ca.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cb2ed8dbd4280e277e6924ca.body:
(A thing's form, matter, and duration) Consider whence each thing is come, and of what it consists, and into what it changes, and what kind of a thing it will be when it has changed, and that it will sustain no harm.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2233b678f1385bba617eeb8f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2233b678f1385bba617eeb8f.body:
(Error as an involuntary source of injustice) For as every soul is unwillingly deprived of the truth, so also is it unwillingly deprived of the power of behaving to each man according to his deserts.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-37a158a8941a4e1002e157e5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-37a158a8941a4e1002e157e5.body:
(Gently correcting others' errors) For what will the most violent man do to thee, if thou continuest to be of a kind disposition towards him, and if, as opportunity offers, thou gently admonishest him and calmly correctest his errors at the very time when he is trying to do thee harm, saying, Not so, my child: we are constituted by nature for something else: I shall certainly not be injured, but thou art injuring thyself, my child.—And show him with gentle tact and by general principles that this is so, and that even bees do not do as he does, nor any animals which are formed by nature to be gregarious.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2353698aebac572e4f630556.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2353698aebac572e4f630556.body:
(Gentleness as strength, anger as weakness) And let this truth be present to thee in the excitement of anger, that to be moved by passion is not manly, but that mildness and gentleness, as they are more agreeable to human nature, so also are they more manly; and he who possesses these qualities possesses strength, nerves, and courage, and not the man who is subject to fits of passion and discontent.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-319bd12939e91c799e28e997.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-319bd12939e91c799e28e997.body:
(Gentleness as strength, anger as weakness) For in the same degree in which a man’s mind is nearer to freedom from all passion, in the same degree also is it nearer to strength: and as the sense of pain is a characteristic of weakness, so also is anger.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f266638f6c1db5de55ff8884.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f266638f6c1db5de55ff8884.body:
(Gentleness as strength, anger as weakness) For he who yields to pain and he who yields to anger, both are wounded and both submit.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b6d06383767984ba15f7ffdd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b6d06383767984ba15f7ffdd.body:
(Anger, fear, and vices as departures from nature) For the movement towards injustice and intemperance and to anger and grief and fear is nothing else than the act of one who deviates from nature.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f0eb802a00f80d902408122d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f0eb802a00f80d902408122d.body:
(A common social purpose as the basis of consistent character) He who has not one and always the same object in life, cannot be one and the same all through his life.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-56b494f8b2a18552eb972efb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-56b494f8b2a18552eb972efb.body:
(Learning first before teaching others) Neither in writing nor in reading wilt thou be able to lay down rules for others before thou shalt have first learned to obey rules thyself.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-f2305642b8e6f5979a63cd09.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f2305642b8e6f5979a63cd09.body:
(Piety and justice available in the present) All those things at which thou wishest to arrive by a circuitous road thou canst have now, if thou dost not refuse them to thyself.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d63ea69e40602e2f9333e675.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d63ea69e40602e2f9333e675.body:
(The distinction between bodily harm and moral evil) And let neither another man’s wickedness hinder thee, nor opinion nor voice, nor yet the sensations of the poor flesh which has grown about thee; for the passive part will look to this.
Marcus Aurelius
