advice-984401c2cf19ddf0962b52a9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-984401c2cf19ddf0962b52a9.body:
(Approaching death and remaining true to inner reason) If, then, whatever the time may be when thou shalt be near to thy departure, neglecting everything else thou shalt respect only thy ruling faculty and the divinity within thee, and if thou shalt be afraid not because thou must some time cease to live, but if thou shalt fear never to have begun to live according to nature,—then thou wilt be a man worthy of the universe which hast produced thee, and thou wilt cease to be a stranger in thy native land, and to wonder at things which happen daily as if they were something unexpected, and not to be dependent on this or that.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-30f7824137c7d706296cc333.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-30f7824137c7d706296cc333.body:
(On examining the value of others' approval) I have often wondered how it is that every man loves himself more than all the rest of men, but yet sets less value on his own opinion of himself than on the opinion of others.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-ae6e0c1d1be75dc42896879e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ae6e0c1d1be75dc42896879e.body:
(Concealing thoughts out of fear of others' opinions) If then a god or a wise teacher should present himself to a man and bid him to think of nothing and to design nothing which he would not express as soon as he conceived it, he could not endure it even for a single day.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-d2e5b771c70e1e6abc75ff5f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d2e5b771c70e1e6abc75ff5f.body:
(On what is achievable and trust in one's abilities) Practise thyself even in the things which thou despairest of accomplishing.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-eac276f4572db42a3f854f55.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-eac276f4572db42a3f854f55.body:
(Readiness for death and life's brevity) Consider in what condition both in body and soul a man should be when he is overtaken by death; and consider the shortness of life, the boundless abyss of time past and future, the feebleness of all matter.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-bde031c574c01608fd69b796.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bde031c574c01608fd69b796.body:
(A thing's form, matter, and duration) See what things are in themselves, dividing them into matter, form, and purpose.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-3bc97f999b1b2d808eedeb2b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3bc97f999b1b2d808eedeb2b.body:
(Aligning actions and will with divine order) What a power man has to do nothing except what God will approve, and to accept all that God may give him.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-ca8403acee27fadb7d3de16a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ca8403acee27fadb7d3de16a.body:
(Error as an involuntary source of injustice) With respect to that which happens conformably to nature, we ought to blame neither gods, for they do nothing wrong either voluntarily or involuntarily, nor men, for they do nothing wrong except involuntarily.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-5ff3106272466b42025bc78a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5ff3106272466b42025bc78a.body:
(On the recurring patterns of human events) How ridiculous and what a stranger he is who is surprised at anything which happens in life.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-993593cbc33b93f06ba299ff.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-993593cbc33b93f06ba299ff.body:
(Necessity, providence, or unguided chance) Either there is a fatal necessity and invincible order, or a kind providence, or a confusion without a purpose and without a director.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c31dcf586d0e6f7cc1154403.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c31dcf586d0e6f7cc1154403.body:
(Realistic expectations of a bad character) Consider that he who would not have the bad man do wrong, is like the man who would not have the fig-tree bear juice in the figs, and infants cry, and the horse neigh, and whatever else must of necessity be.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-12e2b73fa2b231f93add8aec.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-12e2b73fa2b231f93add8aec.body:
(A thing's form, matter, and duration) In everything always observe what the thing is which produces for thee an appearance, and resolve it by dividing it into the formal, the material, the purpose, and the time within which it must end.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-a231b16c693c4910f60b9c90.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a231b16c693c4910f60b9c90.body:
(The hidden mind as the person's driving force) Perceive at last that thou hast in thee something better and more divine than the things which cause the various effects, and as it were pull thee by the strings.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-6f551e38e6b546d31112cd0c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6f551e38e6b546d31112cd0c.body:
(On observing one's own mind) What is there now in my mind,—is it fear, or suspicion, or desire, or anything of the kind?
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2af31e56526fe5f34f57cb4f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2af31e56526fe5f34f57cb4f.body:
(On purpose and skillful action) First, do nothing inconsiderately, nor without a purpose.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-758a9b99a0b6aa63f85c82b5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-758a9b99a0b6aa63f85c82b5.body:
(On natural change in things) Consider that before long thou wilt be nobody and nowhere, nor will any of the things exist which thou now seest, nor any of those who are now living. For all things are formed by nature to change and be turned and to perish, in order that other things in continuous succession may exist.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2c55b00d736748621f0959b0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2c55b00d736748621f0959b0.body:
(On the mind that forms judgments) Consider that everything is opinion, and opinion is in thy power.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-2ff8b4b56057d76ca8563ca3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2ff8b4b56057d76ca8563ca3.body:
(On the freedom to withhold a troubling judgment) Take away then, when thou choosest, thy opinion, and like a mariner who has doubled the promontory, thou wilt find calm, everything stable, and a waveless bay.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-fdcf54eb8cdb7721586fcd60.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fdcf54eb8cdb7721586fcd60.body:
(The natural ending of every process) Any one activity, whatever it may be, when it has ceased at its proper time, suffers no evil because it has ceased; nor he who has done this act, does he suffer any evil for this reason, that the act has ceased. In like manner then the whole which consists of all the acts, which is our life, if it cease at its proper time, suffers no evil for this reason, that it has ceased; nor he who has terminated this series at the proper time, has he been ill dealt with.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-8c0dec5deb798be395bf8fb2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8c0dec5deb798be395bf8fb2.body:
(Natural death without moral harm) Therefore the termination of life for every man is no evil, because neither is it shameful, since it is both independent of the will and not opposed to the general interest, but it is good, since it is seasonable, and profitable to and congruent with the universal.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-b79905e695ef9370470c79b6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b79905e695ef9370470c79b6.body:
(A thing's form, matter, and duration) Second, consider what every being is from the seed to the time of its receiving a soul, and from the reception of a soul to the giving back of the same, and of what things every being is compounded, and into what things it is resolved.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-18ce5f6c9546a4ac7bd6d695.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-18ce5f6c9546a4ac7bd6d695.body:
(On the world as one interconnected organism) When thou art troubled about anything, thou hast forgotten this, that all things happen according to the universal nature; and forgotten this, that a man’s wrongful act is nothing to thee; and further thou hast forgotten this, that everything which happens, always happened so and will happen so, and now happens so everywhere; forgotten this too, how close is the kinship between a man and the whole human race, for it is a community, not of a little blood or seed, but of intelligence.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-4bf1c3a1a070355b40a8e12d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4bf1c3a1a070355b40a8e12d.body:
(Arguing for belief in gods by analogy with the soul) To those who ask, Where hast thou seen the gods, or how dost thou comprehend that they exist and so worshippest them, I answer, in the first place, they may be seen even with the eyes; in the second place, neither have I seen even my own soul, and yet I honor it.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-de5f98c67b96285be54a61e8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-de5f98c67b96285be54a61e8.body:
(Understanding things, justice, and truthfulness) The safety of life is this, to examine everything all through, what it is itself, that is its material, what the formal part; with all thy soul to do justice and to say the truth.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-9ff634c145cd9ba1c7b955f1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9ff634c145cd9ba1c7b955f1.body:
(On divine reason in the world and in us) There is one intelligent soul, though it seems to be divided.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-4a1ea69d5f773ba1c2d16577.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4a1ea69d5f773ba1c2d16577.body:
(On the smallness of earth and the present before infinity) How small a part of the boundless and unfathomable time is assigned to every man, for it is very soon swallowed up in the eternal!
Marcus Aurelius

advice-c757356c603c8b4beb7c4a3f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c757356c603c8b4beb7c4a3f.body:
(Human smallness before time and the moral task) Reflecting on all this, consider nothing to be great, except to act as thy nature leads thee, and to endure that which the common nature brings.
Marcus Aurelius

advice-7425b8246f1bbf4cacc84865.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7425b8246f1bbf4cacc84865.body:
The gods put the most important thing in our hands: the right use of our impressions and judgments. They did not give us control over everything else.
Epictetus

advice-53b7dc56667d62905114c085.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-53b7dc56667d62905114c085.body:
(On what depends on our own choice) We must make the best use that we can of the things which are in our power, and use the rest according to their nature.
Epictetus

advice-dec445a99d994990de34a80b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dec445a99d994990de34a80b.body:
(On freedom of choice under external coercion) You may fetter my leg, but my will not even Zeus himself can overpower.
Epictetus

advice-299aeaf1fcc353e32a3e28d4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-299aeaf1fcc353e32a3e28d4.body:
(Rufus on choosing between death and exile) If you choose death as the heavier misfortune, how great is the folly of your choice?
Epictetus

advice-db4bb2ef846eea9cef154762.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-db4bb2ef846eea9cef154762.body:
(On reason as a guide to human conduct) In short, if we observe, we shall find that the animal man is pained by nothing so much as by that which is irrational; and, on the contrary, attracted to nothing so much as to that which is rational.
Epictetus

advice-be93aca85ece55cf89fa3ef0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-be93aca85ece55cf89fa3ef0.body:
(On shared basic concepts and rational moral choice) For this reason, particularly, we need discipline, in order to learn how to adapt the preconception of the rational and the irrational to the several things conformably to nature.
Epictetus

advice-fbf8f8a2f269a46b7828e7b4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fbf8f8a2f269a46b7828e7b4.body:
(On gradually developing endurance and courage) Now a bull is not made suddenly, nor a brave man; but we must discipline ourselves in the winter for the summer campaign, and not rashly run upon that which does not concern us.
Epictetus

advice-240de4ec63a616baad0fb3e7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-240de4ec63a616baad0fb3e7.body:
(On the cost of compromising moral choice) Only consider at what price you sell your own will: if for no other reason, at least for this, that you sell it not for a small sum.
Epictetus

advice-bf5174edab3b84a15483350e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bf5174edab3b84a15483350e.body:
(On integrity, modesty, and self-respect) Since then it is of necessity that every man uses everything according to the opinion which he has about it, those, the few, who think that they are formed for fidelity and modesty and a sure use of appearances have no mean or ignoble thoughts about themselves; but with the many it is quite the contrary.
Epictetus

advice-b08561fe376184b527a5590e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b08561fe376184b527a5590e.body:
(On desire and avoidance within our control) He who is making progress, having learned from philosophers that desire means the desire of good things, and aversion means aversion from bad things; having learned too that happiness and tranquillity are not attainable by man otherwise than by not failing to obtain what he desires, and not falling into that which he would avoid; such a man takes from himself desire altogether and defers it, but he employs his aversion only on things which are dependent on his will. For if he attempts to avoid anything independent of his will, he knows that sometimes he will fall in with something which he wishes to avoid, and he will be unhappy.
Epictetus

advice-080ecb83b7c43359e79d66fd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-080ecb83b7c43359e79d66fd.body:
(On tragedy as a lesson in inner independence) But if a man must learn by fiction that no external things which are independent of the will concern us, for my part I should like this fiction, by the aid of which I should live happily and undisturbed.
Epictetus

advice-ddfaf9cc4c2d88952530214b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ddfaf9cc4c2d88952530214b.body:
(On gratitude to God for reason and truth) Because the gods have given the vine, or wheat, we sacrifice to them: but because they have produced in the human mind that fruit by which they designed to show us the truth which relates to happiness, shall we not thank God for this?
Epictetus

advice-48deace7e9f7e87c5f95d072.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-48deace7e9f7e87c5f95d072.body:
(On stubbornly denying evidence and accepting contradictions) Now there are two kinds of hardening, one of the understanding, the other of the sense of shame, when a man is resolved not to assent to what is manifest nor to desist from contradictions.
Epictetus

advice-c5c0731370de4aa598abaefb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c5c0731370de4aa598abaefb.body:
(On mistaking a dulled conscience for strength) And indeed with regard to the soul, if a man be in such a state as not to apprehend anything, or understand at all, we think that he is in a bad condition: but if the sense of shame and modesty are deadened, this we call even power (or strength).
Epictetus

advice-a0623650a9a7cb1ad2cfb8a7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a0623650a9a7cb1ad2cfb8a7.body:
(On God as nature’s designer in Stoic thought) From everything which is or happens in the world, it is easy to praise Providence, if a man possesses these two qualities, the faculty of seeing what belongs and happens to all persons and things, and a grateful disposition.
Epictetus

advice-e8c62d982bc3a1a86a96bd59.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e8c62d982bc3a1a86a96bd59.body:
(On God as nature’s designer in Stoic thought) And, indeed, from the very structure of things which have attained their completion, we are accustomed to show that the work is certainly the act of some artificer, and that it has not been constructed without a purpose.
Epictetus

advice-79ee7b904b0f73aa4b640cea.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-79ee7b904b0f73aa4b640cea.body:
(On God as nature’s designer in Stoic thought) And the existence of male and female, and the desire of each for conjunction, and the power of using the parts which are constructed, do not even these declare the workman?
Epictetus

advice-9597e7dc35597470d74f0eb0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9597e7dc35597470d74f0eb0.body:
(On reason as humanity’s distinction from other animals) In those animals then whose constitution is adapted only to use, use alone is enough; but in an animal (man), which has also the power of understanding the use, unless there be the due exercise of the understanding he will never attain his proper end.
Epictetus

advice-96394c387113f6fbd7facb9a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-96394c387113f6fbd7facb9a.body:
(On reason as humanity’s distinction from other animals) For this reason it is shameful for man to begin and to end where irrational animals do; but rather he ought to begin where they begin, and to end where nature ends in us; and nature ends in contemplation and understanding, and in a way of life conformable to nature.
Epictetus

advice-ff3df065bb376cfcf1a51210.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ff3df065bb376cfcf1a51210.body:
(On God as nature’s designer in Stoic thought) But when there is no need to take a journey, and where a man is, there he has the works (of God) before him, will you not desire to see and understand them?
Epictetus

advice-fef704bce0258134a39aa1bd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fef704bce0258134a39aa1bd.body:
(On logic and its use in life) The handling of sophistical and hypothetical arguments, and of those which derive their conclusions from questioning, and in a word the handling of all such arguments, relates to the duties of life, though the many do not know this truth.
Epictetus

advice-1dd8b7577b75549b4f9ef9f2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1dd8b7577b75549b4f9ef9f2.body:
(On logic and its use in life) In as many ways as we can change things which are equivalent to one another, in just so many ways we can change the forms of arguments (ἐπιχειρήματα) and enthymemes (ἐνθυμήματα) in argumentation.
Epictetus

advice-ee55d724178f7f371bc29f1a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ee55d724178f7f371bc29f1a.body:
(On self-reliance and dependence on others’ support) And shall it be necessary for one among us who is a philosopher to travel into foreign parts, and trust to and rely on others, and not to take care of himself, and shall he be inferior to irrational animals and more cowardly, each of which being self-sufficient, neither fails to get its proper food, nor to find a suitable way of living, and one conformable to nature?
Epictetus

advice-81528494f6e39f3f21bcf559.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-81528494f6e39f3f21bcf559.body:
(On dependence on bodily needs and powerful patrons) But we think about ourselves as if we were only stomachs, and intestines, and shameful parts; we fear, we desire; we flatter those who are able to help us in these matters, and we fear them also.
Epictetus

advice-ac7003813690428da43a93a6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ac7003813690428da43a93a6.body:
(On working diligently on one’s own character) If we applied ourselves as busily to our own work as the old men at Rome do to those matters about which they are employed, perhaps we also might accomplish something.
Epictetus

advice-d7c5826d49c07a9c7e8b26ad.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d7c5826d49c07a9c7e8b26ad.body:
(On harmonizing the mind with unchangeable circumstances) Remembering then this disposition of things, we ought to go to be instructed, not that we may change the constitution of things⁠—for we have not the power to do it, nor is it better that we should have the power⁠—but in order that, as the things around us are what they are and by nature exist, we may maintain our minds in harmony with the things which happen.
Epictetus

advice-b870188dafe2aa5d4dc7b579.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b870188dafe2aa5d4dc7b579.body:
(On meeting solitude and company with equanimity) But you ought when you are alone to call this condition by the name of tranquillity and freedom, and to think yourself like to the gods; and when you are with many, you ought not to call it crowd, nor trouble, nor uneasiness, but festival and assembly, and so accept all contentedly.
Epictetus

advice-ca20d2d521c2ac6699259447.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ca20d2d521c2ac6699259447.body:
(On God as nature’s designer in Stoic thought) And will you be vexed and discontented with the things established by Zeus, which he with the Moirae (fates) who were present and spinning the thread of your generation, defined and put in order?
Epictetus

advice-cad71466ac1dbf479a511069.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cad71466ac1dbf479a511069.body:
(On a person as part of the cosmos) Know you not how small a part you are compared with the whole.
Epictetus

advice-5cc5f8b088d77ca7e95dcf06.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5cc5f8b088d77ca7e95dcf06.body:
(On one’s life as material for moral practice) For as the carpenter’s material is wood, and that of the statuary is copper, so the matter of the art of living is each man’s life.
Epictetus

advice-bc14cefbc2bed9645e9cb4fc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bc14cefbc2bed9645e9cb4fc.body:
(On patience: moral growth resembles ripening fruit) If you say to me now that you want a fig, I will answer to you that it requires time: let it flower first, then put forth fruit, and then ripen.
Epictetus

advice-f412a47f4d410819a2e3996f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f412a47f4d410819a2e3996f.body:
(On gratitude to God for reason and truth) But now I am a rational creature, and I ought to praise God: this is my work; I do it, nor will I desert this post so long as I am allowed to keep it; and I exhort you to join in this same song.
Epictetus

advice-38a9c265dedd6d548a55fb96.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-38a9c265dedd6d548a55fb96.body:
(On staying composed when others act badly) Man, you ought not to be affected contrary to nature by the bad things of another.
Epictetus

advice-cc5a431f3d14e5649cab3004.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cc5a431f3d14e5649cab3004.body:
(On attachment to possessions and anger at thieves) Do not admire your clothes, and then you will not be angry with the thief.
Epictetus

advice-aed519044f22c04c59d64b92.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-aed519044f22c04c59d64b92.body:
(On attachment to possessions and anger at thieves) The thief does not know wherein man’s good consists, but he thinks that it consists in having fine clothes, the very thing which you also think.
Epictetus

advice-24cbf1c62eca0a4eca37cc06.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-24cbf1c62eca0a4eca37cc06.body:
(On pride in real or imagined superiority) If a man possesses any superiority, or thinks that he does when he does not, such a man, if he is uninstructed, will of necessity be puffed up through it.
Epictetus

advice-9414a00a432feefe8a2741f6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9414a00a432feefe8a2741f6.body:
(On inner freedom limited by our own judgments) It is not possible that what is by nature free can be disturbed by anything else, or hindered by any other thing than by itself.
Epictetus

advice-61166f3233382ccc6a04a3e6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-61166f3233382ccc6a04a3e6.body:
(On correctly handling impressions in the mind) For this reason it is the chief and the first work of a philosopher to examine appearances, and to distinguish them, and to admit none without examination.
Epictetus

advice-19725958b3b982b5fb66abfa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-19725958b3b982b5fb66abfa.body:
(On one’s role in life and craving recognition) When a man holds his proper station in life, he does not gape after things beyond it.
Epictetus

advice-38353378a0ddc1148297bbac.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-38353378a0ddc1148297bbac.body:
(On desire and avoidance within our control) I am satisfied if I desire and avoid conformably to nature, if I employ movements towards and from an object as I am by nature formed to do, and purpose and design and assent.
Epictetus

advice-d1d981d05fe5fe3282885986.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d1d981d05fe5fe3282885986.body:
(On shared basic concepts and rational moral choice) Precognitions are common to all men, and precognition is not contradictory to precognition.
Epictetus

advice-58889190a82ca16271a2ed64.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-58889190a82ca16271a2ed64.body:
(On shared basic concepts and rational moral choice) Education is the learning how to adapt the natural precognitions to the particular things conformably to nature; and then to distinguish that of things some are in our power, but others are not: in our power are will and all acts which depend on the will; things not in our power are the body, the parts of the body, possessions, parents, brothers, children, country, and generally all with whom we live in society.
Epictetus

advice-6ad43a20cb806da43d8c6592.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6ad43a20cb806da43d8c6592.body:
(On difficulties as training for character) It is circumstances (difficulties) which show what men are.
Epictetus

advice-c37ea3fdef6be5585e40bef1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c37ea3fdef6be5585e40bef1.body:
(On difficulties as training for character) In my opinion no man has had a more profitable difficulty than you have had, if you choose to make use of it as an athlete would deal with a young antagonist.
Epictetus

advice-cd1e78a0be8559929c10ab28.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cd1e78a0be8559929c10ab28.body:
(On one’s own and others’ belongings: travel luggage) You take what is your own, your bottle and your wallet; and now if you think of what is your own, you will never claim what belongs to others.
Epictetus

advice-6ac4c82b12eb8c5ca3b11ce0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6ac4c82b12eb8c5ca3b11ce0.body:
(On inner possessions: integrity and moral choice) Keep by every means what is your own; do not desire what belongs to others.
Epictetus

advice-7db6b6fba1c2349a746bdd50.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7db6b6fba1c2349a746bdd50.body:
(On rational living taking precedence over logical rules) But much before this law is the law of life, that we must act conformably to nature.
Epictetus

advice-fc0e00f45a3e3bff2fe9b068.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fc0e00f45a3e3bff2fe9b068.body:
(On moving from theoretical learning to action) First then philosophers exercise us in theory (contemplation of things), which is easier; and then next they lead us to the more difficult things; for in theory, there is nothing which draws us away from following what is taught; but in the matters of life, many are the things which distract us.
Epictetus

advice-dc11dc0a9acfda95ff915132.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dc11dc0a9acfda95ff915132.body:
(On parental anger and learning the art of living) Do you think then that by means of your anger I shall learn the art of life?
Epictetus

advice-2a4c3824d3bdfda04c9ca2d0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2a4c3824d3bdfda04c9ca2d0.body:
(On accepting correction of one’s own errors) In theory it is easy to convince an ignorant person; but in the affairs of real life no one offers himself to be convinced, and we hate the man who has convinced us.
Epictetus

advice-51360114e4c960052d5cb24c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-51360114e4c960052d5cb24c.body:
(On countering a habit with its opposite) If it is habit which annoys us, we must try to seek aid against habit.
Epictetus

advice-1a54ae4b5cf4f5955e1dc268.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1a54ae4b5cf4f5955e1dc268.body:
(On countering a habit with its opposite) Oppose to one habit the contrary habit: to sophistry oppose reason, and the exercise and discipline of reason; against persuasive (deceitful) appearances we ought to have manifest precognitions (προλήψεις) cleared of all impurities and ready to hand.
Epictetus

advice-92343976ebda60c2b0f53628.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-92343976ebda60c2b0f53628.body:
(On death’s inevitability and the fear of it) When death appears an evil, we ought to have this rule in readiness, that it is fit to avoid evil things, and that death is a necessary thing.
Epictetus

advice-7f4286fd025e9c78ad8b7325.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7f4286fd025e9c78ad8b7325.body:
(On death’s inevitability and the fear of it) Tell me where I can escape death: discover for me the country, show me the men to whom I must go, whom death does not visit.
Epictetus

advice-16f6fe3084232735fcc387bb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-16f6fe3084232735fcc387bb.body:
(On assenting to what appears to be true) It is not possible then to assent to that which appears not to be true.
Epictetus

advice-d667eaf6575248d50568ba4f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d667eaf6575248d50568ba4f.body:
(On mistaken judgments behind conduct and anger) Whoever then clearly remembers this, that to man the measure of every act is the appearance (the opinion)⁠—whether the thing appears good or bad: if good, he is free from blame; if bad, himself suffers the penalty, for it is impossible that he who is deceived can be one person, and he who suffers another person⁠—whoever remembers this will not be angry with any man, will not be vexed at any man, will not revile or blame any man, nor hate nor quarrel with any man.
Epictetus

advice-dfe2e3e362bacd7d650cdbdc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dfe2e3e362bacd7d650cdbdc.body:
(On verifying truth instead of acting by guesswork) In all cases where it is our interest to know what is true in any matter, never will any man among us do anything by guess.
Epictetus

advice-8b52957df2ad2c2dc4b42988.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8b52957df2ad2c2dc4b42988.body:
(On good and evil in moral choice) The being (nature) of the Good is a certain Will; the being of the Bad is a certain kind of Will.
Epictetus

advice-f806f8e432f6dfbb0075a98f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f806f8e432f6dfbb0075a98f.body:
(On a tyrant’s power over body, not choice) Do I fear the master of things which are not in my power?
Epictetus

advice-6f5282e77d0affb924e274ac.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6f5282e77d0affb924e274ac.body:
(On what depends on our own choice) I have learned to see that everything which happens, if it be independent of my will, is nothing to me.
Epictetus

advice-c2b9d5c4068e63e31660cc0a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c2b9d5c4068e63e31660cc0a.body:
(On patience with someone unwilling to reconsider) Do you also then, when you are not able to make a man change his mind, be assured that he is a child, and clap your hands with him; and if you do not choose to do this, keep silent.
Epictetus

advice-fa2b45301d68e4a657ab2391.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fa2b45301d68e4a657ab2391.body:
(On careful choices and courage before circumstances) For if the bad consists in a bad exercise of the will, caution ought only to be used where things are dependent on the will.
Epictetus

advice-583c52efad1f18f9eec2e365.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-583c52efad1f18f9eec2e365.body:
(On careful choices and courage before circumstances) But if things independent of the will and not in our power are nothing to us, with respect to these we must employ confidence; and thus we shall both be cautious and confident, and indeed confident because of our caution.
Epictetus

advice-bd554fd15591e4792bfdbef8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bd554fd15591e4792bfdbef8.body:
(On careful choices and courage before circumstances) But where there is death, or exile or pain or infamy, there we attempt to run away, there we are struck with terror.
Epictetus

advice-8327eed64e2075659e8c4cc3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8327eed64e2075659e8c4cc3.body:
(On careful choices and courage before circumstances) Therefore as we may expect it to happen with those who err in the greatest matters, we convert natural confidence (that is, according to nature) into audacity, desperation, rashness, shamelessness; and we convert natural caution and modesty into cowardice and meanness, which are full of fear and confusion.
Epictetus

advice-d2c325371fbcc540e21be72f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d2c325371fbcc540e21be72f.body:
(On careful choices and courage before circumstances) For if a man should transfer caution to those things in which the will may be exercised and the acts of the will, he will immediately by willing to be cautious have also the power of avoiding what he chooses: but if he transfer it to the things which are not in his power and will, and attempt to avoid the things which are in the power of others, he will of necessity fear, he will be unstable, he will be disturbed.
Epictetus

advice-49b50fd0d09a134cf410ebd8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-49b50fd0d09a134cf410ebd8.body:
(On death’s inevitability and the fear of it) For death or pain is not formidable, but the fear of pain or death.
Epictetus

advice-4477b93ee29280a09b4d1cee.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4477b93ee29280a09b4d1cee.body:
(On careful choices and courage before circumstances) Confidence (courage) then ought to be employed against death, and caution against the fear of death.
Epictetus

advice-3a66eca7f89c0eee3efeda55.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3a66eca7f89c0eee3efeda55.body:
(On desire and avoidance within our control) Only show that you know this, how never to be disappointed in your desire and how never to fall into that which you would avoid.
Epictetus

advice-40542cf66652864c4cc3bd8d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-40542cf66652864c4cc3bd8d.body:
(On trials of character as service to God) Let others labor at forensic causes, problems and syllogisms: do you labor at thinking about death, chains, the rack, exile; and do all this with confidence and reliance on him who has called you to these sufferings, who has judged you worthy of the place in which being stationed you will show what things the rational governing power can do when it takes its stand against the forces which are not within the power of our will.
Epictetus

advice-008bddaa60cea11d22589619.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-008bddaa60cea11d22589619.body:
(On careful choices and courage before circumstances) And thus this paradox will no longer appear either impossible or a paradox: that a man ought to be at the same time cautious and courageous⁠—courageous towards the things which do not depend on the will, and cautious in things which are within the power of the will.
Epictetus

advice-5d38d01229b52f90ab10d1f5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5d38d01229b52f90ab10d1f5.body:
(On freedom of choice under external coercion) For if you wish to maintain a will conformable to nature, you have every security, every facility, you have no troubles.
Epictetus

advice-1e58e02750ddad01b040b378.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1e58e02750ddad01b040b378.body:
(On freedom of choice under external coercion) If you choose not to be restrained or compelled, who shall compel you to desire what you think that you ought not to desire? who shall compel you to avoid what you do not think fit to avoid?
Epictetus

advice-265ad469fdcf3530ad276026.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-265ad469fdcf3530ad276026.body:
(On circumstances as material for moral choice) When then you have received the material, work on it.
Epictetus

advice-34246a0858886bcdcba92770.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-34246a0858886bcdcba92770.body:
(On a person as part of human society) Do you not know, that as a foot is no longer a foot if it is detached from the body, so you are no longer a man if you are separated from other men.
Epictetus

advice-21f473ae2c6ed34daf6a7dba.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-21f473ae2c6ed34daf6a7dba.body:
(On an external object and judgments about it) The hypothetical proposition is indifferent: the judgment about it is not indifferent, but it is either knowledge or opinion or error.
Epictetus

advice-30a5e381362dc03dc722a6b9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-30a5e381362dc03dc722a6b9.body:
(On inner possessions: integrity and moral choice) Always remember what is your own, and what belongs to another; and you will not be disturbed.
Epictetus

advice-8df36444e5febc7ba08de4bb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8df36444e5febc7ba08de4bb.body:
(On inner freedom limited by our own judgments) For who can compel you to have any opinion which you do not choose?
Epictetus

advice-e7cf4328be53e8151040c09f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e7cf4328be53e8151040c09f.body:
(On freedom of choice under external coercion) A tribunal and a prison are each a place, one high and the other low; but the will can be maintained equal, if you choose to maintain it equal in each.
Epictetus

advice-ca067c5cdc5b16ce553a8660.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ca067c5cdc5b16ce553a8660.body:
(On approaching ancient divination without a preferred answer) We ought to come (to divination) without desire or aversion, as the wayfarer asks of the man whom he meets which of two roads leads (to his journey’s end), without any desire for that which leads to the right rather than to the left, for he has no wish to go by any road except the road which leads (to his end).
Epictetus

advice-5e69398b308cb75601682fff.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5e69398b308cb75601682fff.body:
(On divine reason as the source of goodness) It is consistent then that where the nature of God is, there also the nature of the good should be.
Epictetus

advice-06dd92099f10a60dddcb98f8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-06dd92099f10a60dddcb98f8.body:
(On what depends on our own choice) When anything shall be reported to you which is of a nature to disturb, have this principle in readiness: that the news is about nothing which is within the power of your will.
Epictetus

advice-c0a360c894c0c8ee016c3a30.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c0a360c894c0c8ee016c3a30.body:
(On divine reason as the source of goodness) Will you not then seek the nature of good in the rational animal? for if it is not there, you will not choose to say that it exists in any other thing (plant or animal).
Epictetus

advice-660b839483c45b5053d726d2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-660b839483c45b5053d726d2.body:
(On divine reason within humans in Stoic thought) Wretch, you are carrying about a god with you, and you know it not.
Epictetus

advice-ad4937d86890f03e47e27e86.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ad4937d86890f03e47e27e86.body:
(On divine reason within humans in Stoic thought) And if an image of God were present, you would not dare to do any of the things which you are doing: but when God himself is present within and sees all and hears all, you are not ashamed of thinking such things and doing such things, ignorant as you are of your own nature and subject to the anger of God.
Epictetus

advice-dc6b12ada2527e9e50039fdf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dc6b12ada2527e9e50039fdf.body:
(On reason as humanity’s distinction from other animals) It is no common (easy) thing to do this only: to fulfil the promise of a man’s nature.
Epictetus

advice-4a5b8d58d9a9480113bafb71.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4a5b8d58d9a9480113bafb71.body:
(On building skills and habits through repeated actions) Each man is improved and preserved by corresponding acts: the carpenter by acts of carpentry, the grammarian by acts of grammar.
Epictetus

advice-b4233d835a66a6df4aafe6d7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b4233d835a66a6df4aafe6d7.body:
(On moving from theoretical learning to action) For this reason philosophers admonish us not to be satisfied with learning only, but also to add study, and then practice.
Epictetus

advice-f07879cdaa73d83dd26f6bbf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f07879cdaa73d83dd26f6bbf.body:
(On moving from theoretical learning to action) If then we shall not also put in practice right opinions, we shall be nothing more than the expositors of the opinions of others.
Epictetus

advice-09b7d2a92c7de57fc0fe4104.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-09b7d2a92c7de57fc0fe4104.body:
(On freedom of choice under external coercion) In the first place, you are a man and this is one who has nothing superior to the faculty of the will, but all other things subjected to it; and the faculty itself he possesses unenslaved and free from subjection.
Epictetus

advice-9346b8e596195481676adfa2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9346b8e596195481676adfa2.body:
(On reasonable choices when the future is unknown) But now because we do not know the future, it is our duty to stick to the things which are in their nature more suitable for our choice, for we were made among other things for this.
Epictetus

advice-e19604e5d46dedc868c942db.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e19604e5d46dedc868c942db.body:
(On duties connected with one’s role in life) Next to this, if you are a senator of any state, remember that you are a senator; if a youth, that you are a youth; if an old man, that you are an old man.
Epictetus

advice-897c2c15f730c2807b39004f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-897c2c15f730c2807b39004f.body:
(On the harm vice causes its own agent) No man is bad without suffering some loss and damage.
Epictetus

advice-c85c2e6392c42b4af7daacf8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c85c2e6392c42b4af7daacf8.body:
(On recognizing ignorance as the beginning of philosophy) The beginning of philosophy, to him at least who enters on it in the right way and by the door, is a consciousness of his own weakness and inability about necessary things.
Epictetus

advice-42203665039132b422a58203.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-42203665039132b422a58203.body:
(On explaining the truth clearly and patiently) Do you also show the illiterate man the truth, and you will see that he follows.
Epictetus

advice-6aa19cbce373c18c5cd7476b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6aa19cbce373c18c5cd7476b.body:
(On one’s role in life and craving recognition) For this reason a lute player when he is singing by himself has no anxiety, but when he enters the theatre, he is anxious even if he has a good voice and plays well on the lute; for he not only wishes to sing well, but also to obtain applause: but this is not in his power.
Epictetus

advice-d76e79292df4dcb1fa73a2b4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d76e79292df4dcb1fa73a2b4.body:
(On difficult training and the mastery it produces) And the discipline of a smith when he is learning is very disagreeable to one who chances to be present and is a stranger to the art: but the work shows the use of the art.
Epictetus

advice-d0aea128f7a1ee24c9ef5c1b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d0aea128f7a1ee24c9ef5c1b.body:
(On difficult training and the mastery it produces) But you will see this much more in music; for if you are present while a person is learning, the discipline will appear most disagreeable; and yet the results of music are pleasing and delightful to those who know nothing of music.
Epictetus

advice-a1034f8da5d80d2721b8f63e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a1034f8da5d80d2721b8f63e.body:
(On difficult training and the mastery it produces) We see then that the carpenter (τέκτων) when he has learned certain things becomes a carpenter; the pilot by learning certain things becomes a pilot.
Epictetus

advice-288fdfe4e8c4c4e4117094ef.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-288fdfe4e8c4c4e4117094ef.body:
(On God as nature’s designer in Stoic thought) The philosophers say that we ought first to learn that there is a God and that he provides for all things; also that it is not possible to conceal from him our acts, or even our intentions and thoughts.
Epictetus

advice-d853105656b803491c638634.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d853105656b803491c638634.body:
(On imitating divine moral qualities) The next thing is to learn what is the nature of the Gods; for such as they are discovered to be, he, who would please and obey them, must try with all his power to be like them.
Epictetus

advice-ebf08d2036b53444bd4efacc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ebf08d2036b53444bd4efacc.body:
(On imitating divine moral qualities) If the divine is faithful, man also must be faithful; if it is free, man also must be free; if beneficent, man also must be beneficent; if magnanimous, man also must be magnanimous; as being then an imitator of God he must do and say everything consistently with this fact.
Epictetus

advice-bef1de999d7d70fbc03680f4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bef1de999d7d70fbc03680f4.body:
(On sound resolutions rather than blind stubbornness) We ought to keep not to all our determinations, but to those which are right; for if you are now persuaded that it is night, do not change your mind, if you think fit, but persist and say, we ought to abide by our determinations.
Epictetus

advice-4783779e8ec219181862a99e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4783779e8ec219181862a99e.body:
(On building skills and habits through repeated actions) Why then do you still wonder, if in the matters which a man has learned, there he surpasses others, and in those in which he has not been disciplined, there he is the same with the many.
Epictetus

advice-eae091f4c9824f53cee575e8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-eae091f4c9824f53cee575e8.body:
(On the quality of actions rather than outcomes) Give me a man who cares how he shall do anything, not for the obtaining of a thing, but who cares about his own energy.
Epictetus

advice-d306864b9738f63785bd33ec.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d306864b9738f63785bd33ec.body:
(On fear as an obstacle to inner peace) But if we had feared not death or banishment, but fear itself, we should have studied not to fall into those things which appear to us evils.
Epictetus

advice-b831efbb900ec4e3a0fa5d3e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b831efbb900ec4e3a0fa5d3e.body:
(On testing convictions through actual mental challenges) Let some disturbing appearance come on us, and you will know what we have been studying and in what we have been exercising ourselves.
Epictetus

advice-3b55ead5d79e544274c4bc89.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3b55ead5d79e544274c4bc89.body:
(On tragedy as a lesson in inner independence) See how tragedy is made when common things happen to silly men.
Epictetus

advice-8c052f1c7cd26f7a33876167.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8c052f1c7cd26f7a33876167.body:
(On fighting vices as though they were mythical bandits) From yourself, from your thoughts cast away instead of Procrustes and Sciron, sadness, fear, desire, envy, malevolence, avarice, effeminacy, intemperance.
Epictetus

advice-ec12b0e244f5602632e4fee5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ec12b0e244f5602632e4fee5.body:
(On building skills and habits through repeated actions) It is ridiculous then to think that a person wishes to learn one thing, and will learn another; or further, that a man will make proficiency in that which he does not learn.
Epictetus

advice-fc5b2e90b9bc4d6e7ffed408.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fc5b2e90b9bc4d6e7ffed408.body:
(On building skills and habits through repeated actions) Every habit and faculty is maintained and increased by the corresponding actions: the habit of walking by walking, the habit of running by running.
Epictetus

advice-67fc20dd5674b02a0c34564e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-67fc20dd5674b02a0c34564e.body:
(On building skills and habits through repeated actions) If you would be a good reader, read; if a writer, write.
Epictetus

advice-c9bdf80c1a77dfe77de5acba.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c9bdf80c1a77dfe77de5acba.body:
(On building skills and habits through repeated actions) Generally then if you would make anything a habit, do it; if you would not make it a habit, do not do it, but accustom yourself to do something else in place of it.
Epictetus

advice-f06476f5f9f1a93d5225b5f2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f06476f5f9f1a93d5225b5f2.body:
(On reason restraining the craving for wealth) For when you have once desired money, if reason be applied to lead to a perception of the evil, the desire is stopped, and the ruling faculty of our mind is restored to the original authority.
Epictetus

advice-678d43260f2f73db02834784.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-678d43260f2f73db02834784.body:
(On anger as a habit that can be weakened) If then you wish not to be of an angry temper, do not feed the habit: throw nothing on it which will increase it: at first keep quiet, and count the days on which you have not been angry.
Epictetus

advice-9d5edacbc0a021b7e6264047.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9d5edacbc0a021b7e6264047.body:
(On conscience and inner purity before God) Be willing at length to be approved by yourself, be willing to appear beautiful to God, desire to be in purity with your own pure self and with God.
Epictetus

advice-49b5f67939cef17442a26071.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-49b5f67939cef17442a26071.body:
(On divine help amid a storm of mental impressions) Remember God: call on him as a helper and protector, as men at sea call on the Dioscuri in a storm.
Epictetus

advice-6475d52834af89d287464e16.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6475d52834af89d287464e16.body:
(On fear as an obstacle to inner peace) For take away the fear of death, and suppose as many thunders and lightnings as you please, and you will know what calm and serenity there is in the ruling faculty.
Epictetus

advice-bd7e1d4cbcdf1a665bc42faa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bd7e1d4cbcdf1a665bc42faa.body:
(On external advantages that do not determine moral worth) The good then are the virtues and the things which partake of the virtues: the bad are the vices, and the things which partake of them; and the indifferent are the things which lie between the virtues and the vices: wealth, health, life, death, pleasure, pain.
Epictetus

advice-c61ef0151660f1c36659bb78.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c61ef0151660f1c36659bb78.body:
(On moving from theoretical learning to action) As we call a statue Phidiac, which is fashioned according to the art of Phidias; so show me a man who is fashioned according to the doctrines which he utters.
Epictetus

advice-119e8ed7efcd4c8715a15284.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-119e8ed7efcd4c8715a15284.body:
(On testing convictions through actual mental challenges) Show me a man who is sick and happy, in danger and happy, dying and happy, in exile and happy, in disgrace and happy.
Epictetus

advice-35227c9ffea54cc947011bc9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-35227c9ffea54cc947011bc9.body:
(On imitating divine moral qualities) Let any of you show me a human soul ready to think as God does, and not to blame either God or man, ready not to be disappointed about anything, not to consider himself damaged by anything, not to be angry, not to be envious, not to be jealous; and why should I not say it direct? desirous from a man to become a god, and in this poor mortal body thinking of his fellowship with Zeus.
Epictetus

advice-fed110729fae8f17900a7012.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fed110729fae8f17900a7012.body:
(On correctly handling impressions in the mind) Neither wealth is in our power, nor health, nor reputation, nor in a word anything else except the right use of appearances.
Epictetus

advice-0d99bb9429014d7ec86d0523.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0d99bb9429014d7ec86d0523.body:
(On stubbornly denying evidence and accepting contradictions) The propositions which are true and evident are of necessity used even by those who contradict them: and a man might perhaps consider it to be the greatest proof of a thing being evident that it is found to be necessary even for him who denies it to make use of it at the same time.
Epictetus

advice-9308bb8d6472191c46a7a48a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9308bb8d6472191c46a7a48a.body:
(On defending rational ways of discovering truth) What a shame is this: when a man has received from nature measures and rules for the knowing of truth, and does not strive to add to these measures and rules and to improve them, but just the contrary, endeavors to take away and destroy whatever enables us to discern the truth?
Epictetus

advice-4441c6e4c10b59334e50bdb2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4441c6e4c10b59334e50bdb2.body:
(On admitting one’s faults and avoiding self-deception) Some things men readily confess, and other things they do not.
Epictetus

advice-3be41ae4d242605bb3b47e81.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3be41ae4d242605bb3b47e81.body:
(On friendship grounded in understanding what is good) What a man applies himself to earnestly, that he naturally loves.
Epictetus

advice-1fb67e51cbd6f592b0b2ade3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1fb67e51cbd6f592b0b2ade3.body:
(On friendship grounded in understanding what is good) To love then is only in the power of the wise.
Epictetus

advice-dfa14bb9a6b000600fee7465.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dfa14bb9a6b000600fee7465.body:
(On aligning personal good with friendship and duty) For this reason if a man put in the same place his interest, sanctity, goodness, and country, and parents, and friends, all these are secured: but if he puts in one place his interest, in another his friends, and his country and his kinsmen and justice itself, all these give way being borne down by the weight of interest.
Epictetus

advice-2c96b5e525b5d3142743b201.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2c96b5e525b5d3142743b201.body:
(On where a person locates their true good) For where the I and the Mine are placed, to that place of necessity the animal inclines: if in the flesh, there is the ruling power: if in the will, it is there: and if it is in externals, it is there.
Epictetus

advice-b66535b295db2d7aa44d83b8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b66535b295db2d7aa44d83b8.body:
(On aligning personal good with friendship and duty) If then I am there where my will is, then only shall I be a friend such as I ought to be, and son, and father; for this will be my interest, to maintain the character of fidelity, of modesty, of patience, of abstinence, of active cooperation, of observing my relations (towards all).
Epictetus

advice-500d576b996d93b1c77d0135.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-500d576b996d93b1c77d0135.body:
(On testing friendship when personal interests conflict) And now when you see brothers to be friends appearing to have one mind, do not conclude from this anything about their friendship, not even if they swear it and say that it is impossible for them to be separated from one another.
Epictetus

advice-8fe316fe932abfc36d36f550.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8fe316fe932abfc36d36f550.body:
(On clear and beautiful handwriting) Every man will read a book with more pleasure, or even with more ease, if it is written in fairer characters.
Epictetus

advice-b9250159280f0cdbbc9e2ad5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b9250159280f0cdbbc9e2ad5.body:
(On gratitude for life and nature’s gifts) But indeed for the power of seeing and hearing, and indeed for life itself, and for the things which contribute to support it, for the fruits which are dry, and for wine and oil give thanks to God.
Epictetus

advice-135a458cee9cec47b75b764a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-135a458cee9cec47b75b764a.body:
(On good and evil in moral choice) Therefore this (the will) is alone vice or alone virtue.
Epictetus

advice-6f3426052ddd944ae294723b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6f3426052ddd944ae294723b.body:
(On moral choice as the highest human faculty) There is a certain value in the power of speaking, but it is not so great as the power of the will.
Epictetus

advice-9e1f31fa976cfb2ac79ae2d2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9e1f31fa976cfb2ac79ae2d2.body:
(On eloquence as a faculty subordinate to moral choice) But to take away the faculty of speaking and to say that there is no such faculty in reality, is the act not only of an ungrateful man towards those who gave it, but also of a cowardly man: for such a person seems to me to fear, if there is any faculty of this kind, that we shall not be able to despise it.
Epictetus

advice-c6332bd9d1dfd3c5072c9ade.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c6332bd9d1dfd3c5072c9ade.body:
(On moral choice as the highest human faculty) But this is the great matter; to leave to each thing the power (faculty) which it has, and leaving to it this power to see what is the worth of the power, and to learn what is the most excellent of all things, and to pursue this always, to be diligent about this, considering all other things of secondary value compared with this, but yet, as far as we can, not neglecting all those other things.
Epictetus

advice-0e8e078f0ede1ff0ef2c49d9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0e8e078f0ede1ff0ef2c49d9.body:
(On attentive listeners who inspire others to speak) As the grass which is suitable, when it is presented to a sheep, moves its inclination to eat, but if you present to it a stone or bread, it will not be moved to eat; so there are in us certain natural inclinations also to speak, when the hearer shall appear to be somebody, when he himself shall excite us: but when he shall sit by us like a stone or like grass, how can he excite a man’s desire (to speak)?
Epictetus

advice-6b2763c28140232f598a7375.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6b2763c28140232f598a7375.body:
(On error as a mismatch between intention and outcome) Every error comprehends contradiction: for since he who errs does not wish to err, but to be right, it is plain that he does not do what he wishes.
Epictetus

advice-18f71deceb648ab46c992751.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-18f71deceb648ab46c992751.body:
(On error as a mismatch between intention and outcome) But every rational soul is by nature offended at contradiction, and so long as it does not understand this contradiction, it is not hindered from doing contradictory things: but when it does understand the contradiction, it must of necessity avoid the contradiction and avoid it as much as a man must dissent from the false when he sees that a thing is false; but so long as this falsehood does not appear to him, he assents to it as to truth.
Epictetus

advice-b7559bca321bee3a184765b5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b7559bca321bee3a184765b5.body:
(On error as a mismatch between intention and outcome) Show the rational governing faculty a contradiction, and it will withdraw from it; but if you do not show it, rather blame yourself than him who is not persuaded.
Epictetus

advice-09d78c9e012809e3a1e5b042.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-09d78c9e012809e3a1e5b042.body:
(On genuine beauty appropriate to a being’s nature) And you will judge of this matter thus: Since we see a dog naturally formed for one thing, and a horse for another, and for another still, as an example, a nightingale, we may generally and not improperly declare each of them to be beautiful then when it is most excellent according to its nature; but since the nature of each is different, each of them seems to me to be beautiful in a different way.
Epictetus

advice-c2ec086e6fb5522e9bc2da56.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c2ec086e6fb5522e9bc2da56.body:
(On genuine beauty appropriate to a being’s nature) That then which makes a dog beautiful, makes a horse ugly; and that which makes a horse beautiful, makes a dog ugly, if it is true that their natures are different.
Epictetus

advice-9813b1b58c3daeb3e222b039.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9813b1b58c3daeb3e222b039.body:
(On genuine beauty appropriate to a being’s nature) In the first place, know who you are and then adorn yourself appropriately.
Epictetus

advice-c62c87cd3d6b2b1e98f938a5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c62c87cd3d6b2b1e98f938a5.body:
(On reason as humanity’s distinction from other animals) You are a human being; and this is a mortal animal which has the power of using appearances rationally.
Epictetus

advice-5729bfcd841be7a8d0ad2dc4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5729bfcd841be7a8d0ad2dc4.body:
(On ancient ideas of cleanliness and appropriate appearance) A man should be cleanly as a man, a woman as a woman, a child as a child.
Epictetus

advice-0a5289bd11b4010c255d2381.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0a5289bd11b4010c255d2381.body:
(On tranquility before leisure and advanced studies) To those who are happy it is appropriate to light a fire, to dine; if they choose, both to sing and to dance.
Epictetus

advice-47396684dc86af5f2416620d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-47396684dc86af5f2416620d.body:
(On one’s own mind as material for moral practice) The material for the wise and good man is his own ruling faculty: and the body is the material for the physician and the aliptes (the man who oils persons); the land is the matter for the husbandman.
Epictetus

advice-ffd9bafd45d0e463701e34f8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ffd9bafd45d0e463701e34f8.body:
(On correctly handling impressions in the mind) The business of the wise and good man is to use appearances conformably to nature: and as it is the nature of every soul to assent to the truth, to dissent from the false, and to remain in suspense as to that which is uncertain; so it is its nature to be moved towards the desire of the good, and to aversion from the evil; and with respect to that which is neither good nor bad it feels indifferent.
Epictetus

advice-66b8361149b63eb07ea5ce7e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-66b8361149b63eb07ea5ce7e.body:
(On actions guided by impressions of what is good) When the good appears, it immediately attracts to itself; the evil repels from itself.
Epictetus

advice-cce4690b28a901c83e3e232b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cce4690b28a901c83e3e232b.body:
(On aligning personal good with friendship and duty) But if we place the good in a right determination of the will, the very observance of the relations of life is good, and accordingly he who gives up any external things, obtains that which is good.
Epictetus

advice-cf14ebe93f802fb76ed40b48.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cf14ebe93f802fb76ed40b48.body:
(On death’s inevitability and the fear of it) Death is a thing independent of the will.
Epictetus

advice-c94114358033a24a2dd1a512.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c94114358033a24a2dd1a512.body:
(On the public example set by influential people) You ought then to know when you enter the theatre that you enter as a rule and example to the rest how they ought to look at the acting.
Epictetus

advice-b0e89afe9b85cdf8c1e835b7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b0e89afe9b85cdf8c1e835b7.body:
(On hostility toward those who obstruct people’s desires) Because every man hates that which is a hindrance to him.
Epictetus

advice-79187c6f05dd1f413ac1ddc4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-79187c6f05dd1f413ac1ddc4.body:
(On moral character as the basis of conduct) For if your ruling power cannot be maintained in a state conformable to nature, it is possible that your land can, that you will be able to increase your money, you will take care of your father in his old age, frequent the public place, hold magisterial office: being bad you will do badly anything else that you have to do.
Epictetus

advice-2941684aaad9e29f73df765f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2941684aaad9e29f73df765f.body:
(On freedom of choice under external coercion) For I wish to be surprised by disease or death when I am looking after nothing else than my own will, that I may be free from perturbation, that I may be free from hindrance, free from compulsion, and in a state of liberty.
Epictetus

advice-7973f2948d51ac719544e0f0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7973f2948d51ac719544e0f0.body:
(On working diligently on one’s own character) But see if any man among us when he is intent upon this, the keeping himself in a state conformable to nature and living so always, does not make progress.
Epictetus

advice-239affa57867f66f1ef338f4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-239affa57867f66f1ef338f4.body:
(On steadfastness: competing only in one’s moral choices) The good man is invincible, for he does not enter the contest where he is not stronger.
Epictetus

advice-1acb80e488dab332b61f36d9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1acb80e488dab332b61f36d9.body:
(On an unprepared pupil: the soft-cheese comparison) It is not easy to exhort weak young men; for neither is it easy to hold (soft) cheese with a hook.
Epictetus

advice-32fcca9c146a257b65a753fe.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-32fcca9c146a257b65a753fe.body:
(Debating Epicureans about the source of mental pleasure) On what then shall we depend for this pleasure of the soul? for if it shall depend on things of the soul, the substance (nature) of the good is discovered; for good cannot be one thing, and that at which we are rationally delighted another thing; nor if that which precedes is not good, can that which comes after be good, for in order that the thing which comes after may be good, that which precedes must be good.
Epictetus

advice-818decbd87b052700ef6d646.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-818decbd87b052700ef6d646.body:
(On duties connected with one’s role in life) You live in a chief city: it is your duty to be a magistrate, to judge justly, to abstain from that which belongs to others; no woman ought to seem beautiful to you except your own wife, and no youth, no vessel of silver, no vessel of gold (except your own).
Epictetus

advice-fcca3fc4bd81ec4593752dcf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fcca3fc4bd81ec4593752dcf.body:
(On human purpose: function matters more than bodily material) The substance of the hand is the flesh; but the work of the hand is the principal part (that which precedes and leads the rest).
Epictetus

advice-2bcd1abf61ed0b8093dbea88.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2bcd1abf61ed0b8093dbea88.body:
(On explaining the truth clearly and patiently) Govern us as rational animals: show us what is profitable to us, and we will follow it: show us what is unprofitable, and we will turn away from it.
Epictetus

advice-e8ecd4332d3dfeee0d9e1c56.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e8ecd4332d3dfeee0d9e1c56.body:
(On correctly handling impressions in the mind) As we exercise ourselves against sophistical questions, so we ought to exercise ourselves daily against appearances; for these appearances also propose questions to us.
Epictetus

advice-10f5eac44aa5f6e55dfe3af2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-10f5eac44aa5f6e55dfe3af2.body:
(On the Stoic account of distress through judgments) Affliction is a thing which depends on the will: it is an evil.
Epictetus

advice-d5722b043006ece26657fec0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d5722b043006ece26657fec0.body:
(On dialogue as mutual examination of beliefs) Learn my opinions, show me yours, and then say that you have visited me.
Epictetus

advice-75fec36cb7b103d2050d3617.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-75fec36cb7b103d2050d3617.body:
(On dialogue as mutual examination of beliefs) Let us examine one another: if I have any bad opinion, take it away; if you have any, show it.
Epictetus

advice-25d3fdb1024448503b76fd45.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-25d3fdb1024448503b76fd45.body:
(On costly possessions and impoverished moral judgments) You have utensils of gold; but your discourse, your opinions, your assents, your movements (pursuits), your desires are of earthen ware.
Epictetus

advice-819c6b0038a1a578456da123.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-819c6b0038a1a578456da123.body:
(On limiting desires instead of remaining insatiable) Your desire is insatiable; mine is satisfied.
Epictetus

advice-f3ad89fe4d0e602c7e2d2c52.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f3ad89fe4d0e602c7e2d2c52.body:
(On limiting desires instead of remaining insatiable) And do you part with your desires: do not desire many things and you will have what you want.
Epictetus

advice-99855e59f8894917b09ae7b9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-99855e59f8894917b09ae7b9.body:
(On keeping moral principles ready for everyday use) When the need of each opinion comes, we ought to have it in readiness: on the occasion of breakfast, such opinions as relate to breakfast; in the bath, those that concern the bath; in bed, those that concern bed.
Epictetus

advice-fd8d37744bf68c1b05fcd97f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fd8d37744bf68c1b05fcd97f.body:
(On a patient’s endurance in an ancient medical example) Now is the time for thirst, bear it well.
Epictetus

advice-c8e7c62ca0d4544f713fcdce.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c8e7c62ca0d4544f713fcdce.body:
(On a patient’s endurance in an ancient medical example) The physician will hinder you from drinking, but he cannot prevent you from bearing thirst well; and he will hinder you from eating, but he cannot prevent you from bearing hunger well.
Epictetus

advice-1d23b2e1ec602d6a03b56824.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1d23b2e1ec602d6a03b56824.body:
(On a patient’s endurance in an ancient medical example) If you bear a fever well, you have all that belongs to a man in a fever.
Epictetus

advice-5fb19b22616e06bec1c72112.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5fb19b22616e06bec1c72112.body:
(On external advantages that do not determine moral worth) Whoever thinks any other thing to be good except those things which depend on the will, let him envy, let him desire, let him flatter, let him be perturbed; whoever considers anything else to be evil, let him grieve, let him lament, let him weep, let him be unhappy.
Epictetus

advice-11c0e8549a20f53ced499e34.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-11c0e8549a20f53ced499e34.body:
(On moral training without showy feats) We ought not to make our exercises consist in means contrary to nature and adapted to cause admiration, for if we do so, we who call ourselves philosophers shall not differ at all from jugglers.
Epictetus

advice-17ab2034b7ea63f2416cd0ce.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-17ab2034b7ea63f2416cd0ce.body:
(On desire and avoidance within our control) For since it is not possible to have your desire not disappointed and your aversion free from falling into that which you would avoid, without great and constant practice, you must know that if you allow your desire and aversion to turn to things which are not within the power of the will, you will neither have your desire capable of attaining your object, nor your aversion free from the power of avoiding that which you would avoid.
Epictetus

advice-0067eedc673f5f2bbe2c9423.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0067eedc673f5f2bbe2c9423.body:
(On countering a habit with its opposite) And since strong habit leads (prevails), and we are accustomed to employ desire and aversion only to things which are not within the power of our will, we ought to oppose to this habit a contrary habit, and where there is great slipperiness in the appearances, there to oppose the habit of exercise.
Epictetus

advice-696c1173a908db9c17e2bdf6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-696c1173a908db9c17e2bdf6.body:
(On temporary abstinence as training against craving pleasure) I am rather inclined to pleasure: I will incline to the contrary side above measure for the sake of exercise.
Epictetus

advice-fa960735e4af4541526a3263.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fa960735e4af4541526a3263.body:
(On handling impressions that provoke fear of pain) I am averse to pain: I will rub and exercise against this the appearances which are presented to me for the purpose of withdrawing my aversion from every such thing.
Epictetus

advice-5a1b9dd3205d681e28c95686.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5a1b9dd3205d681e28c95686.body:
(On anger as a habit that can be weakened) Practice, man, if you are irritable, to endure if you are abused, not to be vexed if you are treated with dishonor.
Epictetus

advice-cae25a8948c71ee544fd66a3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cae25a8948c71ee544fd66a3.body:
(On testing convictions through actual mental challenges) Then at last, if occasion presents itself, for the purpose of trying yourself at a proper time you will descend into the arena to know if appearances overpower you as they did formerly.
Epictetus

advice-6019d5972ad1597c68a8cea2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6019d5972ad1597c68a8cea2.body:
(The second Stoic practice: rational impulses toward action) After the desire and the aversion comes the second topic (matter) of the movements towards action and the withdrawals from it; that you may be obedient to reason, that you do nothing out of season or place, or contrary to any propriety of the kind.
Epictetus

advice-f4b5cefbe6a2476d57fa210b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f4b5cefbe6a2476d57fa210b.body:
(On distinguishing loneliness from simply being alone) Solitude is a certain condition of a helpless man.
Epictetus

advice-0c5d122e549d161193365491.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0c5d122e549d161193365491.body:
(On distinguishing loneliness from simply being alone) For this reason when we travel, then especially do we say that we are lonely when we fall among robbers, for it is not the sight of a human creature which removes us from solitude, but the sight of one who is faithful and modest and helpful to us.
Epictetus

advice-bf3b749a114ac0fcbcb082c6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bf3b749a114ac0fcbcb082c6.body:
(On powerful abilities being dangerous for unprepared beginners) Every great power (faculty) is dangerous to beginners.
Epictetus

advice-e626a23a96fffffb11399109.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e626a23a96fffffb11399109.body:
(On moving from theoretical learning to action) Show to them in your own example what kind of men philosophy makes, and don’t trifle.
Epictetus

advice-984619cf06c81d1db16e4f0a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-984619cf06c81d1db16e4f0a.body:
(On kindness and patience in everyday company) When you are eating, do good to those who eat with you; when you are drinking, to those who are drinking with you; by yielding to all, giving way, bearing with them, thus do them good, and do not spit on them your phlegm (bad humors).
Epictetus

advice-3ca27d98a9025e944ba1a2a6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3ca27d98a9025e944ba1a2a6.body:
(On independent thinking rather than hiding in the crowd) Man, if you are anything, both walk alone and talk to yourself, and do not hide yourself in the chorus.
Epictetus

advice-58995552acee4ad2585bf459.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-58995552acee4ad2585bf459.body:
(On self-knowledge and deliberately choosing a way of life) Examine a little at last, look around, stir yourself up, that you may know who you are.
Epictetus

advice-890824ab278b03c2e30aea96.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-890824ab278b03c2e30aea96.body:
(On purposes, circumstances, and different grounds for action) Of things that are done some are done with a final purpose (προηγουμένως), some according to occasion, others with a certain reference to circumstances, others for the purpose of complying with others, and some according to a fixed scheme of life.
Epictetus

advice-370db21a4bf433306e536db2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-370db21a4bf433306e536db2.body:
(On complacency and doubting the possibility of inner happiness) You must root out of men these two things: arrogance (pride) and distrust.
Epictetus

advice-c274306b1a832221489ebef8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c274306b1a832221489ebef8.body:
(On complacency and doubting the possibility of inner happiness) Arrogance then is the opinion that you want nothing (are deficient in nothing): but distrust is the opinion that you cannot be happy when so many circumstances surround you.
Epictetus

advice-dc12f20a6322417abdb71330.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dc12f20a6322417abdb71330.body:
(On human dignity and rational conduct) If you tell me that you can kick violently, I also will say to you that you are proud of that which is the act of an ass.
Epictetus

advice-cc43cef563f71d7dbbfa815a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cc43cef563f71d7dbbfa815a.body:
(On considering an action’s requirements and consequences) In every act consider what precedes and what follows, and then proceed to the act.
Epictetus

advice-ad6ea3e52ea67ef30a22c662.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ad6ea3e52ea67ef30a22c662.body:
(On considering an action’s requirements and consequences) If you do not consider, you will at first begin with spirit, since you have not thought at all of the things which follow; but afterwards when some consequences have shown themselves, you will basely desist (from that which you have begun).
Epictetus

advice-a906a5de3e8d51476507047a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a906a5de3e8d51476507047a.body:
(On assessing one’s abilities before undertaking a task) Man, consider first what the matter is (which you propose to do), then your own nature also, what it is able to bear.
Epictetus

advice-70f9a9947ffb80147098b08a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-70f9a9947ffb80147098b08a.body:
(On assessing one’s abilities before undertaking a task) If you are a wrestler, look at your shoulders, your thighs, your loins: for different men are naturally formed for different things.
Epictetus

advice-218d47debf8337971f64a8a0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-218d47debf8337971f64a8a0.body:
(On company shaping habits and convictions) If a man has frequent intercourse with others either for talk, or drinking together, or generally for social purposes, he must either become like them, or change them to his own fashion.
Epictetus

advice-6a1ef76a62e0462cab752d00.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6a1ef76a62e0462cab752d00.body:
(On company shaping habits and convictions) Since then the danger is so great, we must cautiously enter into such intimacies with those of the common sort, and remember that it is impossible that a man can keep company with one who is covered with soot without being partaker of the soot himself.
Epictetus

advice-27e5769f150edd9be60da7e0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-27e5769f150edd9be60da7e0.body:
(On company shaping habits and convictions) Until then the good (κομψαί) sentiments (ὑπολήψεις) are fixed in you, and you shall have acquired a certain power for your security, I advise you to be careful in your association with common persons: if you are not, every day like wax in the sun there will be melted away whatever you inscribe on your minds in the school.
Epictetus

advice-b6de36e51cf1659ad2c38d27.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b6de36e51cf1659ad2c38d27.body:
(On countering a habit with its opposite) Do you also introduce other habits than those which you have: fix your opinions and exercise yourselves in them.
Epictetus

advice-5b98f340a6d9dfa68025e26b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5b98f340a6d9dfa68025e26b.body:
(On God as nature’s designer in Stoic thought) When you make any charge against Providence, consider, and you will learn that the thing has happened according to reason.
Epictetus

advice-edb7fec470b38973bbeab51f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-edb7fec470b38973bbeab51f.body:
(On advantages corresponding to particular abilities) Remember then always and have in readiness the truth, that this is a law of nature⁠—that the superior has an advantage over the inferior in that in which he is superior⁠—and you will never be vexed.
Epictetus

advice-6b32f859bf602a73cbb9ed88.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6b32f859bf602a73cbb9ed88.body:
(On distress arising from judgments about poverty) For this reason we must not get rid of poverty, but of the opinion about poverty, and then we shall be happy.
Epictetus

advice-54830c7a2f8c83610f490d91.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-54830c7a2f8c83610f490d91.body:
(On a father’s and son’s duties during disagreement) Your father has a certain duty, and if he shall not fulfil it, he loses the character of a father, of a man of natural affection, of gentleness.
Epictetus

advice-cfe576e984b95b144a7f0ef9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cfe576e984b95b144a7f0ef9.body:
(On a father’s and son’s duties during disagreement) On the other side it is your duty to make your defense firmly, modestly, without anger: but if you do not, you also lose the character of a son, of a man of modest behavior, of generous character.
Epictetus

advice-8f97450409b4a05535a2836d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8f97450409b4a05535a2836d.body:
