(On the Stoic account of distress through judgments) If then we ourselves incline in this direction, so as, when we are unlucky, to blame ourselves and to remember that nothing else is the cause of perturbation or loss of tranquillity except our own opinion, I swear to you by all the gods that we have made progress.
Epictetus

advice-5c7dc2372b74d95e189dac05.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5c7dc2372b74d95e189dac05.body:
(A child as an image of inexperience in living) For he who is unmusical is a child in music; he who is without letters is a child in learning: he who is untaught, is a child in life.
Epictetus

advice-8ff4a796471efee6df45beb3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8ff4a796471efee6df45beb3.body:
(On making moral use of health and illness) To be healthy, and healthy in a right way, is good: to be healthy in a bad way is bad; so that it is possible to gain advantage even from sickness, I declare.
Epictetus

advice-674331c2d6aa44caa488bfe3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-674331c2d6aa44caa488bfe3.body:
(On actions guided by impressions of what is good) But to desire or to be averse from, or to move towards an object or to move from it, or to prepare yourself, or to propose to do anything, which of you can do this, unless he has received an impression of the appearance of that which is profitable or a duty?
Epictetus

advice-fc4ba0ed9de7aa9b7f8301cc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fc4ba0ed9de7aa9b7f8301cc.body:
(On choosing the Cynic vocation and its trials) Reflect more carefully, know thyself, consult the divinity, without God attempt nothing; for if he shall advise you (to do this or anything), be assured that he intends you to become great or to receive many blows.
Epictetus

advice-0c29ef580bff311f4a6b09cd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0c29ef580bff311f4a6b09cd.body:
(The Cynic here is an itinerant philosopher and guide) But in the present state of things which is like that of an army placed in battle order, is it not fit that the Cynic should without any distraction be employed only on the ministration of God, able to go about among men, not tied down to the common duties of mankind, nor entangled in the ordinary relations of life, which if he neglects, he will not maintain the character of an honorable and good man? and if he observes them he will lose the character of the messenger, and spy, and herald of God.
Epictetus

advice-e8af35d4a5e536257b9e6fa2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e8af35d4a5e536257b9e6fa2.body:
(The Cynic here is an itinerant philosopher and guide) Man, the Cynic is the father of all men; the men are his sons, the women are his daughters: he so carefully visits all, so well does he care for all.
Epictetus

advice-c60ceaabcdf2e03c74eef854.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c60ceaabcdf2e03c74eef854.body:
(The Cynic here is an itinerant philosopher and guide) It is necessary also for such a man (the Cynic) to have a certain habit of body: for if he appears to be consumptive, thin and pale, his testimony has not then the same weight.
Epictetus

advice-5336455e4cde698d71e6cba6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5336455e4cde698d71e6cba6.body:
(On self-knowledge and deliberately choosing a way of life) First say to yourself who you wish to be, then do accordingly what you are doing; for in nearly all other things we see this to be so.
Epictetus

advice-1ac57b3ccecd0c8c3f2251b3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1ac57b3ccecd0c8c3f2251b3.body:
(On human dignity and rational conduct) First of all, we must act as a man.
Epictetus

advice-eb758fb49be675343dbbc671.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-eb758fb49be675343dbbc671.body:
(On caring for moral choice rather than external acquisitions) I invite you to come and hear that things are in a bad way for you, and that you are taking care of everything except that of which you ought to take care, and that you are ignorant of the good and the bad and are unfortunate and unhappy.
Epictetus

advice-1edb524ff7491b09b75e7679.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1edb524ff7491b09b75e7679.body:
(The philosophical school as treatment for mistaken beliefs) The philosopher’s school, ye men, is a surgery: you ought not to go out of it with pleasure, but with pain.
Epictetus

advice-d68a578e043b61ac59ff65e4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d68a578e043b61ac59ff65e4.body:
(On philosophical guidance and showy public speaking) Cease, I entreat you by the gods, to spoil good words and good acts as much as you can.
Epictetus

advice-c7676817e8ad1eb3fd309aab.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c7676817e8ad1eb3fd309aab.body:
(On philosophical guidance and showy public speaking) Nothing can have more power in exhortation than when the speaker shows to the hearers that he has need of them.
Epictetus

advice-b03c59cff117f1d8be139f80.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b03c59cff117f1d8be139f80.body:
(On staying composed when others act badly) Let not that which in another is contrary to nature be an evil to you: for you are not formed by nature to be depressed with others nor to be unhappy with others, but to be happy with them.
Epictetus

advice-5ea88ee950e4d92796a08466.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5ea88ee950e4d92796a08466.body:
(On the Stoic account of distress through judgments) If a man is unhappy, remember that his unhappiness is his own fault: for God has made all men to be happy, to be free from perturbations.
Epictetus

advice-73d3266a7b761bca86b5d598.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-73d3266a7b761bca86b5d598.body:
(On limiting desires instead of remaining insatiable) And it is never possible for happiness and desire of what is not present to come together.
Epictetus

advice-d8d8b6658c654935a2dfb23d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d8d8b6658c654935a2dfb23d.body:
(On harmonizing the mind with unchangeable circumstances) To desire then things which are impossible is to have a slavish character, and is foolish: it is the part of a stranger, of a man who fights against God in the only way that he can, by his opinions.
Epictetus

advice-889a803167bcad237356bdad.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-889a803167bcad237356bdad.body:
(On where a person locates their true good) I am formed by nature for my own good: I am not formed for my own evil.
Epictetus

advice-88878593d2218bfab4c00c08.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-88878593d2218bfab4c00c08.body:
(On love mindful of mortality and temporary companionship) Do you also remind yourself in like manner, that he whom you love is mortal, and that what you love is nothing of your own: it has been given to you for the present, not that it should not be taken from you, nor has it been given to you for all time, but as a fig is given to you or a bunch of grapes at the appointed season of the year.
Epictetus

advice-405a11dad9b18679bff3444b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-405a11dad9b18679bff3444b.body:
(On human vocation within the Stoic cosmic order) Wherefore the wise and good man, remembering who he is and whence he came, and by whom he was produced, is attentive only to this, how he may fill his place with due regularity, and obediently to God.
Epictetus

advice-2b18721ee63923e0103bf343.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2b18721ee63923e0103bf343.body:
(On harmonizing the mind with unchangeable circumstances) If means of living according to nature be allowed to me, I will seek no other place than that in which I am, or other men than those among whom I am.
Epictetus

advice-68e54ac643f74f9f2a0978ed.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-68e54ac643f74f9f2a0978ed.body:
(On correctly handling impressions in the mind) Then, when the appearance (of things) pains you, for it is not in your power to prevent this, contend against it by the aid of reason, conquer it: do not allow it to gain strength nor to lead you to the consequences by raising images such as it pleases and as it pleases.
Epictetus

advice-29b151c45f175140a51eb116.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-29b151c45f175140a51eb116.body:
(Gyara is an island of exile; the theme is resilience) If you be in Gyara, do not imagine the mode of living at Rome, and how many pleasures there were for him who lived there and how many there would be for him who returned to Rome: but fix your mind on this matter, how a man who lives in Gyara ought to live in Gyara like a man of courage.
Epictetus

advice-35863e1f21df5ea83262a9cf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-35863e1f21df5ea83262a9cf.body:
(On distress arising from judgments about poverty) For it is not shameful to be without something to eat, but not to have reason sufficient for keeping away fear and sorrow.
Epictetus

advice-39eb0ffc3fbbdf4e5871eefa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-39eb0ffc3fbbdf4e5871eefa.body:
(On reviewing moral goals and returning to them) Consider as to the things which you proposed to yourself at first, which you have secured, and which you have not; and how you are pleased when you recall to memory the one, and are pained about the other; and if it is possible, recover the things wherein you failed.
Epictetus

advice-59f271496c85e70873b3cdb3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-59f271496c85e70873b3cdb3.body:
(On steadfastness: competing only in one’s moral choices) For the combat before us is not in wrestling and the Pancration, in which both the successful and the unsuccessful may have the greatest merit, or may have little, and in truth may be very fortunate or very unfortunate; but the combat is for good fortune and happiness themselves.
Epictetus

advice-eb5fb086b8f828e005d0c632.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-eb5fb086b8f828e005d0c632.body:
(On building skills and habits through repeated actions) And when you found fault with a person lately, did you not do the act of a malignant person, of a trifling babbler; did you not cherish this habit in you by adding to it the corresponding acts?
Epictetus

advice-783d18c3ad3583ee280fe941.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-783d18c3ad3583ee280fe941.body:
(On difficulties as training for character) Sufferings then of the trying character are useful to us, whether we choose or not.
Epictetus

advice-40b5365b8602f29bb398340d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-40b5365b8602f29bb398340d.body:
(On the inner slavery of vice and dependence) Not one then of the bad lives as he wishes; nor is he then free.
Epictetus

advice-0e30bb2d46bf7c0c8ef6fada.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0e30bb2d46bf7c0c8ef6fada.body:
(On the inner slavery of vice and dependence) And who chooses to live in sorrow, fear, envy, pity, desiring and failing in his desires, attempting to avoid something and falling into it?
Epictetus

advice-3e50b6f1e260a7481d3b5eb6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3e50b6f1e260a7481d3b5eb6.body:
(On defending rational ways of discovering truth) Seek, and you will find; for you have aids from nature for the discovery of truth.
Epictetus

advice-4f8b109a4d96e0309e502419.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4f8b109a4d96e0309e502419.body:
(On fear of the future and grief over the present) And what is grief to you? for fear comes from what you expect, but grief from that which is present.
Epictetus

advice-28d428fd84b034277dd7c28f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-28d428fd84b034277dd7c28f.body:
(On desire and avoidance within our control) For of the things which are within the power of the will, as being good and present, you have a proper and regulated desire: but of the things which are not in the power of the will you do not desire any one, and so you do not allow any place to that which is irrational, and impatient, and above measure hasty.
Epictetus

advice-62195beae3e323457aaa9000.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-62195beae3e323457aaa9000.body:
(On human vocation within the Stoic cosmic order) I have placed my movements towards action (ὁρμήν) in obedience to God.
Epictetus

advice-1cd8b4a940b773a541ed3f59.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1cd8b4a940b773a541ed3f59.body:
(On human vocation within the Stoic cosmic order) Did not he (God) introduce you here, did he not show you the light, did he not give you fellow workers, and perceptions and reason? and as whom did he introduce you here? did he not introduce you as subject to death, and as one to live on the earth with a little flesh, and to observe his administration, and to join with him in the spectacle and the festival for a short time?
Epictetus

advice-c6e53f3771585bb9559a9979.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c6e53f3771585bb9559a9979.body:
(On a person as part of human society) But because we say that the nature of man is tame (gentle) and social and faithful, you will not say that this is a paradox?
Epictetus

advice-07dc5ff2de9acc60d3a2f6d8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-07dc5ff2de9acc60d3a2f6d8.body:
(On the inner slavery of vice and dependence) The man who is not under restraint is free, to whom things are exactly in that state in which he wishes them to be; but he who can be restrained or compelled or hindered, or thrown into any circumstances against his will, is a slave.
Epictetus

advice-e278fc8db40782c21edbf1ca.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e278fc8db40782c21edbf1ca.body:
(On inner readiness developed through practical action) But keep yourself strong and fit for the uses of life and initiated by being exercised in action.
Epictetus

advice-ef20d8cc25d87e281a0969b0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ef20d8cc25d87e281a0969b0.body:
(On passion preventing obedience to one’s rational judgment) And indeed when a man is compelled by love to do something contrary to his opinion (judgment), and at the same time sees the better, but has not the strength to follow it, one might consider him still more worthy of excuse as being held by a certain violent and in a manner a divine power.
Epictetus

advice-7da00f0d27378748667e1727.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7da00f0d27378748667e1727.body:
(On Socrates facing execution: the actor comparison) For the good actor also preserves his character by stopping when he ought to stop, better than when he goes on acting beyond the proper time.
Epictetus

advice-c094d9e76a99ee3904238a04.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c094d9e76a99ee3904238a04.body:
(Choosing moral growth over former habits and approval) Choose then which of the two you will have, to be equally loved by those by whom you were formerly loved, being the same with your former self; or, being superior, not to obtain from your friends the same that you did before.
Epictetus

advice-c760907f0469235778a43421.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c760907f0469235778a43421.body:
(Choosing moral growth over former habits and approval) For no man is able to make progress (improvement), when he is wavering between opposite things; but if you have preferred this (one thing) to all things, if you choose to attend to this only, to work out this only, give up everything else.
Epictetus

advice-f912669fbe91f9a22794d620.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f912669fbe91f9a22794d620.body:
(Choosing moral growth over former habits and approval) Choose then whether you will be a hard drinker and pleasant to your former associates or a sober man and disagreeable to them.
Epictetus

advice-b84202fb87e9c0fe354eba34.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b84202fb87e9c0fe354eba34.body:
(On correctly handling impressions in the mind) Attend therefore to the appearances of things, and watch over them; for that which you have to preserve is no small matter, but it is modesty and fidelity and constancy, freedom from the affects, a state of mind undisturbed, freedom from fear, tranquillity, in a word: liberty.
Epictetus

advice-1e828be80e5bbbbd40890971.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1e828be80e5bbbbd40890971.body:
(On inner possessions: integrity and moral choice) Preserve that which is your own good in every thing; and as to every other thing, as it is permitted, and so far as to behave consistently with reason in respect to them, content with this only.
Epictetus

advice-5471ffd769f5e19f4c0b7924.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5471ffd769f5e19f4c0b7924.body:
(On dependence even on books, leisure, and quiet conditions) Remember that not only the desire of power and of riches makes us mean and subject to others, but even the desire of tranquillity, and of leisure, and of travelling abroad, and of learning.
Epictetus

advice-298325e1030556ca42218000.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-298325e1030556ca42218000.body:
(On dependence even on books, leisure, and quiet conditions) For as salutations and power are things external and independent of the will, so is a book.
Epictetus

advice-701edc794c80277a03a150a5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-701edc794c80277a03a150a5.body:
(On inner tranquility independent of circumstances) But a tranquil and happy life contains nothing so sure as continuity and freedom from obstacle.
Epictetus

advice-6c3c3feb8f082605b4d857fa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6c3c3feb8f082605b4d857fa.body:
(On what depends on our own choice) In short remember this, that what you shall prize which is beyond your will, so far you have destroyed your will.
Epictetus

advice-f25ba294fbf02e62b56b854f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f25ba294fbf02e62b56b854f.body:
(On meeting solitude and company with equanimity) If you fall into a crowd, call it a celebration of games, a panegyris, a festival: try to enjoy the festival with other men.
Epictetus

advice-7acd3d86a11e00e905397e84.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7acd3d86a11e00e905397e84.body:
(On what depends on our own choice) Do you only bear in mind the general rules: what is mine? what is not mine? what is given (permitted) to me? what does God will that I should do now? what does he not will?
Epictetus

advice-c3549ae9a7828502dc91549e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c3549ae9a7828502dc91549e.body:
(On moving from theoretical learning to action) If you see anything which you have learned and inquired about occurring to you in your course of life (or opportunely applied by you to the acts of life), be delighted at it.
Epictetus

advice-23cf202287049eb807786576.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-23cf202287049eb807786576.body:
(On working diligently on one’s own character) If you have laid aside or have lessened bad disposition and a habit of reviling; if you have done so with rash temper, obscene words, hastiness, sluggishness; if you are not moved by what you formerly were, and not in the same way as you once were, you can celebrate a festival daily, today because you have behaved well in one act, and tomorrow because you have behaved well in another.
Epictetus

advice-21e6309b5602ad98487b6d8d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-21e6309b5602ad98487b6d8d.body:
(On resolving conflicts peacefully and preventing quarrels) The wise and good man neither himself fights with any person, nor does he allow another, so far as he can prevent it.
Epictetus

advice-29903cf7d7a0a12d722aa1b7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-29903cf7d7a0a12d722aa1b7.body:
(On moral harm depending on one’s own judgments) Then do we not choose to make secure the only means of safety which are offered to us, and do we not choose to withdraw ourselves from that which is perishable and servile and to labor at the things which are imperishable and by nature free; and do we not remember that no man either hurts another or does good to another, but that a man’s opinion about each thing, is that which hurts him, is that which overturns him; this is fighting, this is civil discord, this is war?
Epictetus

advice-487fcdf3bed611317245fa5d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-487fcdf3bed611317245fa5d.body:
(On hostility toward those who obstruct people’s desires) Now this is the nature of every man to seek the good, to avoid the bad; to consider him who deprives us of the one and involves us in the other an enemy and treacherous, even if he be a brother, or a son, or a father.
Epictetus

advice-f56fe44f8152ca25570f4292.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f56fe44f8152ca25570f4292.body:
(On distress arising from judgments about poverty) I am poor, but I have a right opinion about poverty.
Epictetus

advice-f1de0dbeab1d0ec8c7288316.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f1de0dbeab1d0ec8c7288316.body:
(On public office and the price of obtaining it) I am not in power (not a magistrate); but others are: and I have the opinion which I ought to have about having and not having power.
Epictetus

advice-0de0f505738f7a40a51a8185.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0de0f505738f7a40a51a8185.body:
(On public office and the price of obtaining it) But if they exercise power, and you do not, will you not choose to tell yourself the truth, that you do nothing for the sake of this (power), and they do all?
Epictetus

advice-2bff4aa3e258e0c48de8e1c7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2bff4aa3e258e0c48de8e1c7.body:
(On a tyrant’s power over body, not choice) If then any man neither wishing to die, nor to live by all means but only as it may be permitted, approaches the tyrant, what hinders him from approaching the tyrant without fear?
Epictetus

advice-89bbf32c2b20643dc4026966.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-89bbf32c2b20643dc4026966.body:
(On what depends on our own choice) And besides this being naturally noble, magnanimous, and free, man sees that of the things which surround him some are free from hindrance and in his power, and the other things are subject to hindrance and in the power of others; that the things which are free from hindrance are in the power of the will; and those which are subject to hindrance are the things which are not in the power of the will.
Epictetus

advice-a03d6cf5c1b83ea9b7877fad.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a03d6cf5c1b83ea9b7877fad.body:
(On the inner slavery of vice and dependence) But if he thinks that his good and his interest are in externals and in things which are not in the power of his will, he must of necessity be hindered, be impeded, be a slave to those who have the power over the things which he admires (desires) and fears; and he must of necessity be impious because he thinks that he is harmed by God, and he must be unjust because he always claims more than belongs to him; and he must of necessity be abject and mean.
Epictetus

advice-2b0bcafd797850c72499f98b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2b0bcafd797850c72499f98b.body:
(On distress arising from judgments about poverty) Come and you will know what poverty is when it has found one who can act well the part of a poor man.
Epictetus

advice-eeb3766013d2e266a6a36aa6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-eeb3766013d2e266a6a36aa6.body:
(On a tyrant’s power over body, not choice) Make trial of your power, and you will know how far it reaches.
Epictetus

advice-6931880d8980aa2e292940ac.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6931880d8980aa2e292940ac.body:
(On judging actions by convictions rather than appearances) Never praise nor blame a man because of the things which are common (to all, or to most), and do not ascribe to him any skill or want of skill; and thus you will be free from rashness and from malevolence.
Epictetus

advice-ba81bf984970d66f98bc97d4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ba81bf984970d66f98bc97d4.body:
(On judging actions by convictions rather than appearances) By no means: but the acts which proceed from right opinions are done well; and those which proceed from bad opinions are done ill.
Epictetus

advice-9bfbd6962a639fb9a9d850fa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9bfbd6962a639fb9a9d850fa.body:
(On judging actions by convictions rather than appearances) But do you, until you know the opinion from which a man does each thing, neither praise nor blame the act.
Epictetus

advice-b4a2f86863c7580cc46937bf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b4a2f86863c7580cc46937bf.body:
(On quietly developing as a philosopher without public labels) First strive that it be not known what you are: be a philosopher to yourself (or, philosophize to yourself) a short time.
Epictetus

advice-6c25e41be2cf1e5680e0999c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6c25e41be2cf1e5680e0999c.body:
(On patience: moral growth resembles ripening fruit) Fruit grows thus: the seed must be buried for some time, hid, grow slowly in order that it may come to perfection.
Epictetus

advice-90858c9ece240a22cef28401.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-90858c9ece240a22cef28401.body:
(On the inner slavery of vice and dependence) And how much would these persons give, these very men who are rich, and in possession of power, and live with handsome women, to be able to despise riches, and power, and these very women whom they love and enjoy?
Epictetus

advice-3ba418d8dc641a3fde171f9d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3ba418d8dc641a3fde171f9d.body:
(On restoring inner freedom through moral choice) Fight with yourself, restore yourself to decency, to modesty, to liberty.
Epictetus

advice-bff23acc05f0f6a90dc5763c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bff23acc05f0f6a90dc5763c.body:
(On restoring inner freedom through moral choice) There is no need to kill any man, nor to put him in chains, nor to treat him with contumely nor to enter the Forum (go to the courts of law), but it is only necessary for you to speak to yourself who will be most easily persuaded, with whom no man has more power of persuasion than yourself.
Epictetus

advice-1a1292d1a2c314ee9ebededa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1a1292d1a2c314ee9ebededa.body:
(On restoring inner freedom through moral choice) You must exercise the Will, and the thing is done, it is set right: as on the other hand, only fall a-nodding (be careless), and the thing is lost: for from within comes ruin and from within comes help.
Epictetus

advice-e28294596d59b27f600ef784.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e28294596d59b27f600ef784.body:
(On restoring inner freedom through moral choice) From a shameless man you will become a modest man, from a disorderly you will become an orderly man, from a faithless you will become a faithful man, from a man of unbridled habits a sober man.
Epictetus

advice-6daccfb43983bc7691512a68.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6daccfb43983bc7691512a68.body:
(On what depends on our own choice) The difficulties of all men are about external things; their helplessness is about externals.
Epictetus

advice-035d69d0ce6ab6b680212e3f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-035d69d0ce6ab6b680212e3f.body:
(On desire and avoidance within our control) Then I shall say to him: if you do not choose to desire that which you will fail to obtain, nor to attempt to avoid that into which you will fall, desire nothing which belongs to (which is in the power of) others, nor try to avoid any of the things which are not in your power.
Epictetus

advice-ab7cafda0ed53dea214cefd5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ab7cafda0ed53dea214cefd5.body:
(On good and evil in moral choice) And the nature of good and of evil, is it not in the things which are within the power of the will?
Epictetus

advice-c62499c94e7c66be58642063.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c62499c94e7c66be58642063.body:
(On good actions in which death might find us) I for my part would wish to be found doing something which belongs to a man: beneficent, suitable to the general interest, noble.
Epictetus

advice-9054d66e73b156752f2fc14b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9054d66e73b156752f2fc14b.body:
(On public office and the price of obtaining it) If you wish to be a consul, you must keep awake, run about, kiss hands, waste yourself with exhaustion at other men’s doors, say and do many things unworthy of a free man, send gifts to many, daily presents to some.
Epictetus

advice-1f00d65db4368427b3a09285.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1f00d65db4368427b3a09285.body:
(On the effort required for inner tranquility) In order then to secure freedom from passions (ἀπαφείας), tranquillity, to sleep well when you do sleep, to be really awake when you are awake, to fear nothing, to be anxious about nothing, will you spend nothing and give no labor?
Epictetus

advice-1dbf757958280c918b4a21ed.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1dbf757958280c918b4a21ed.body:
(On moral harm depending on one’s own judgments) Neither can any man deprive me of the good, nor involve me in the bad against my will.
Epictetus

advice-d47acc431ac04de34bbec290.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d47acc431ac04de34bbec290.body:
(On bodily and mental purity in Stoic thought) Some persons raise a question whether the social feeling is contained in the nature of man; and yet I think that these same persons would have no doubt that love of purity is certainly contained in it, and that if man is distinguished from other animals by anything, he is distinguished by this.
Epictetus

advice-0dc339a0abcef5f74f6db931.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0dc339a0abcef5f74f6db931.body:
(On bodily and mental purity in Stoic thought) For since the Gods by their nature are pure and free from corruption, so far as men approach them by reason, so far do they cling to purity and to a love (habit) of purity.
Epictetus

advice-26ae3fee58fcd30dc1244b58.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-26ae3fee58fcd30dc1244b58.body:
(On purity of soul as sound moral judgment) The first then and highest purity is that which is in the soul; and we say the same of impurity.
Epictetus

advice-c014e2b660e04c2d34bd242f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c014e2b660e04c2d34bd242f.body:
(Acts of mind: desires, intentions, and assent to impressions) Now the acts of the soul are movement towards an object or movement from it, desire, aversion, preparation, design (purpose), assent.
Epictetus

advice-acb1db3332da8471304b2d16.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-acb1db3332da8471304b2d16.body:
(On purity of soul as sound moral judgment) Consequently the impurity of the soul is the soul’s bad opinions; and the purification of the soul is the planting in it of proper opinions; and the soul is pure which has proper opinions, for the soul alone in her own acts is free from perturbation and pollution.
Epictetus

advice-8c328ab620b43b1779b36afe.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8c328ab620b43b1779b36afe.body:
(On sustained attention to one’s judgments and actions) When you have remitted your attention for a short time, do not imagine this: that you will recover it when you choose.
Epictetus

advice-f9ca8209b28f723895ddf90c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f9ca8209b28f723895ddf90c.body:
(On sustained attention to one’s judgments and actions) For will you do it (anything in life) worse by using attention, and better by not attending at all?
Epictetus

advice-aa2a422f9af5e0b5eadd29e3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-aa2a422f9af5e0b5eadd29e3.body:
(On sustained attention to one’s judgments and actions) Do you not see that when you have let your mind loose, it is no longer in your power to recall it, either to propriety, or to modesty, or to moderation: but you do everything that comes into your mind in obedience to your inclinations.
Epictetus

advice-5f354c68e691e232b4d8ed65.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5f354c68e691e232b4d8ed65.body:
(On trusting someone willing to share our difficulties) Who will not willingly receive a man who is ready to bear a share, as we may say, of the difficulty of his circumstances, and by this very act to ease the burden, by taking a part of it.
Epictetus

advice-35340663695f04e0244c4b25.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-35340663695f04e0244c4b25.body:
(On trust and the integrity of a confidant) You must remember then among general principles that secret discourses (discourses about secret matters) require fidelity and corresponding opinions.
Epictetus

advice-402618dd213aeb8feb4d45f7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-402618dd213aeb8feb4d45f7.body:
(On what depends on our own choice) Of things some are in our power, and others are not.
Epictetus

advice-2d3c45f03311fda570db4c90.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2d3c45f03311fda570db4c90.body:
(On what depends on our own choice) Not in our power are the body, property, reputation, offices (magisterial power), and in a word, whatever are not our own acts.
Epictetus

advice-0cbb888f28f6052c78fa7c75.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0cbb888f28f6052c78fa7c75.body:
(On what depends on our own choice) And the things in our power are by nature free, not subject to restraint or hindrance; but the things not in our power are weak, slavish, subject to restraint, in the power of others.
Epictetus

advice-16f38edcc0b2dd2bb2ea459d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-16f38edcc0b2dd2bb2ea459d.body:
(On desire and avoidance within our control) Remember that desire contains in it the profession (hope) of obtaining that which you desire; and the profession (hope) in aversion (turning from a thing) is that you will not fall into that which you attempt to avoid; and he who fails in his desire is unfortunate; and he who falls into that which he would avoid is unhappy.
Epictetus

advice-7e3ec3b23becda3ff48f3bae.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7e3ec3b23becda3ff48f3bae.body:
(On desire and avoidance within our control) If then you attempt to avoid only the things contrary to nature which are within your power you will not be involved in any of the things which you would avoid.
Epictetus

advice-fdadfca1449766492d2e3c28.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fdadfca1449766492d2e3c28.body:
(On desire and avoidance within our control) But if you attempt to avoid disease, or death, or poverty, you will be unhappy.
Epictetus

advice-bb10d59ecf982c9aac1c604e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bb10d59ecf982c9aac1c604e.body:
(On desire and avoidance within our control) Take away then aversion from all things which are not in our power, and transfer it to the things contrary to nature which are in our power.
Epictetus

advice-eb98ca4d4e284541fd7c8f99.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-eb98ca4d4e284541fd7c8f99.body:
(On attachment mindful of fragile and temporary possessions) If you love an earthen vessel, say it is an earthen vessel which you love; for when it has been broken you will not be disturbed.
Epictetus

advice-2d807254de254e3c4b8efce5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2d807254de254e3c4b8efce5.body:
(On love mindful of mortality and temporary companionship) If you are kissing your child or wife, say that it is a human being whom you are kissing, for when the wife or child dies you will not be disturbed.
Epictetus

advice-ed653d3d344a26f175f86be7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ed653d3d344a26f175f86be7.body:
(On considering an action’s requirements and consequences) When you are going to take in hand any act remind yourself what kind of an act it is.
Epictetus

advice-b29e2d5ee4b16c0100ee9af6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b29e2d5ee4b16c0100ee9af6.body:
(On anticipating everyday interruptions while keeping composure) If you are going to bathe, place before yourself what happens in the bath; some splashing the water, others pushing against one another, others abusing one another, and some stealing; and thus with more safety you will undertake the matter, if you say to yourself, I now intend to bathe, and to maintain my will in a manner conformable to nature.
Epictetus

advice-36fc34417e80e98fc95518af.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-36fc34417e80e98fc95518af.body:
(On moral progress from blame toward understanding) It is the act of an ill-instructed man to blame others for his own bad condition; it is the act of one who has begun to be instructed, to lay the blame on himself; and of one whose instruction is completed, neither to blame another, nor himself.
Epictetus

advice-cd7f849d7bb5e150beb98abd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cd7f849d7bb5e150beb98abd.body:
(On correctly handling impressions in the mind) Consequently when in the use of appearances you are conformable to nature, then be elated, for then you will be elated at something good which is your own.
Epictetus

advice-7ce95e72007547282e74d5b5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7ce95e72007547282e74d5b5.body:
(On harmonizing the mind with unchangeable circumstances) Seek not that the things which happen should happen as you wish; but wish the things which happen to be as they are, and you will have a tranquil flow of life.
Epictetus

advice-1aeed0db99336a1332003068.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1aeed0db99336a1332003068.body:
(On bodily limitations and freedom of moral choice) Disease is an impediment to the body, but not to the will, unless the will itself chooses.
Epictetus

advice-ad7ec2e480dacd8c668db8b7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ad7ec2e480dacd8c668db8b7.body:
(On bodily limitations and freedom of moral choice) Lameness is an impediment to the leg, but not to the will.
Epictetus

advice-e06d1452bb5881c4fbb91004.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e06d1452bb5881c4fbb91004.body:
(On difficulties as training for character) On the occasion of every accident (event) that befalls you, remember to turn to yourself and inquire what power you have for turning it to use.
Epictetus

advice-408efd6db5626ca24498cf0c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-408efd6db5626ca24498cf0c.body:
(On self-control when attracted to physical beauty) If you see a fair man or a fair woman, you will find that the power to resist is temperance (continence).
Epictetus

advice-a4da8ae0bdb42bdf3a820b7a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a4da8ae0bdb42bdf3a820b7a.body:
(On Stoic asceticism in an ancient slaveholding household) If you intend to improve, throw away such thoughts as these: if I neglect my affairs, I shall not have the means of living: unless I chastise my slave, he will be bad. For it is better to die of hunger and so to be released from grief and fear than to live in abundance with perturbation; and it is better for your slave to be bad than for you to be unhappy.
Epictetus

advice-2c23056de8e1b1bde8d789dd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2c23056de8e1b1bde8d789dd.body:
(On being willing to appear foolish for moral growth) If you would improve, submit to be considered without sense and foolish with respect to externals.
Epictetus

advice-70bc01b83307fc11903e7867.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-70bc01b83307fc11903e7867.body:
(On being willing to appear foolish for moral growth) Wish to be considered to know nothing; and if you shall seem to some to be a person of importance, distrust yourself.
Epictetus

advice-0ba73a1b46c2c82d951bcf9a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0ba73a1b46c2c82d951bcf9a.body:
(On moral choice as the highest human faculty) For you should know that it is not easy both to keep your will in a condition conformable to nature and (to secure) external things: but if a man is careful about the one, it is an absolute necessity that he will neglect the other.
Epictetus

advice-bf25792e059b1e0b06489393.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bf25792e059b1e0b06489393.body:
(On love mindful of mortality and temporary companionship) If you would have your children and your wife and your friends to live for ever, you are silly; for you would have the things which are not in your power to be in your power, and the things which belong to others to be yours.
Epictetus

advice-52f7eaa141c45d6066fd1de2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-52f7eaa141c45d6066fd1de2.body:
(On the inner slavery of vice and dependence) Whoever then wishes to be free let him neither wish for anything nor avoid anything which depends on others: if he does not observe this rule, he must be a slave.
Epictetus

advice-108077820263cb72fbd79c41.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-108077820263cb72fbd79c41.body:
(On compassion without surrendering judgment to another’s grief) When you see a person weeping in sorrow either when a child goes abroad or when he is dead, or when the man has lost his property, take care that the appearance do not hurry you away with it, as if he were suffering in external things.
Epictetus

advice-657981c7c2b4c76901d3b9cd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-657981c7c2b4c76901d3b9cd.body:
(Life as a play: God assigns, humans perform roles) Remember that thou art an actor in a play, of such a kind as the teacher (author) may choose; if short, of a short one; if long, of a long one: if he wishes you to act the part of a poor man, see that you act the part naturally; if the part of a lame man, of a magistrate, of a private person, (do the same). For this is your duty, to act well the part that is given to you; but to select the part, belongs to another.
Epictetus

advice-69c54425436aae0598d34703.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-69c54425436aae0598d34703.body:
(On omens: external events do not determine moral choice) When a raven has croaked inauspiciously, let not the appearance hurry you away with it; but straightway make a distinction in your mind and say, None of these things is signified to me, but either to my poor body, or to my small property, or to my reputation, or to my children, or to my wife: but to me all significations are auspicious if I choose. For whatever of these things results, it is in my power to derive benefit from it.
Epictetus

advice-306b50a40a05cbb5e00da165.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-306b50a40a05cbb5e00da165.body:
(On steadfastness: competing only in one’s moral choices) You can be invincible, if you enter into no contest in which it is not in your power to conquer.
Epictetus

advice-c4489a356fd872741f43e7b9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c4489a356fd872741f43e7b9.body:
(On outward honor that does not prove happiness) Take care then when you observe a man honored before others or possessed of great power or highly esteemed for any reason, not to suppose him happy, and be not carried away by the appearance.
Epictetus

advice-f92d1460b722857229e3b5d4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f92d1460b722857229e3b5d4.body:
(On good and evil in moral choice) For if the nature of the good is in our power, neither envy nor jealousy will have a place in us.
Epictetus

advice-487e9cb8f30ab5d075cf74ab.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-487e9cb8f30ab5d075cf74ab.body:
(On the Stoic account of distress through judgments) When then a man irritates you, you must know that it is your own opinion which has irritated you.
Epictetus

advice-53618961c4e01fec19371521.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-53618961c4e01fec19371521.body:
(On pausing before responding to irritation) For if you once gain time and delay, you will more easily master yourself.
Epictetus

advice-ca64145706d7fe762a91f19a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ca64145706d7fe762a91f19a.body:
(On remembering death and life’s finite duration) Let death and exile and every other thing which appears dreadful be daily before your eyes; but most of all death: and you will never think of anything mean nor will you desire anything extravagantly.
Epictetus

advice-271888dd52f284dc5e0f53c0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-271888dd52f284dc5e0f53c0.body:
(On one’s role in life and craving recognition) If it should ever happen to you to be turned to externals in order to please some person, you must know that you have lost your purpose in life.
Epictetus

advice-5d4be0c6149dcdf8c63f3c38.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5d4be0c6149dcdf8c63f3c38.body:
(On quietly developing as a philosopher without public labels) Be satisfied then in everything with being a philosopher; and if you wish to seem also to any person to be a philosopher, appear so to yourself, and you will be able to do this.
Epictetus

advice-8ede2a8f1d3ad0addcceabd4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8ede2a8f1d3ad0addcceabd4.body:
(On worth independent of office and recognition) And how will you be nobody nowhere, when you ought to be somebody in those things only which are in your power, in which indeed it is permitted to you to be a man of the greatest worth?
Epictetus

advice-274c3b7b85a797682317a885.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-274c3b7b85a797682317a885.body:
(On acquiring wealth without sacrificing integrity) If I can acquire money and also keep myself modest and faithful and magnanimous, point out the way, and I will acquire it.
Epictetus

advice-0df858116c85d21905d8ce94.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0df858116c85d21905d8ce94.body:
(On judging our losses as we judge others’ losses) We may learn the wish (will) of nature from the things in which we do not differ from one another: for instance, when your neighbor’s slave has broken his cup, or anything else, we are ready to say forthwith, that it is one of the things which happen.
Epictetus

advice-f530d256a71396d434b612a9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f530d256a71396d434b612a9.body:
(On judging our losses as we judge others’ losses) You must know then that when your cup also is broken, you ought to think as you did when your neighbor’s cup was broken.
Epictetus

advice-84c7e71388761bfb95bf6d46.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-84c7e71388761bfb95bf6d46.body:
(On the Stoic denial of evil’s independent nature) As a mark is not set up for the purpose of missing the aim, so neither does the nature of evil exist in the world.
Epictetus

advice-8a443ffc7a58b5243264097e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8a443ffc7a58b5243264097e.body:
(On considering an action’s requirements and consequences) In every act observe the things which come first, and those which follow it; and so proceed to the act.
Epictetus

advice-5c660e3b9496ed7029e19793.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5c660e3b9496ed7029e19793.body:
(On consistently choosing a moral way of life) You must be one man, either good or bad.
Epictetus

advice-3ef2a12c644afe6db285991b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3ef2a12c644afe6db285991b.body:
(On consistently choosing a moral way of life) You must either exercise your skill on internal things or on external things; that is you must either maintain the position of a philosopher or that of a common person.
Epictetus

advice-5d7a3a1ea780d1a79de275af.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5d7a3a1ea780d1a79de275af.body:
(On duty toward a brother who acts unjustly) Maintain then your own position towards him, and do not examine what he is doing, but what you must do that your will shall be conformable to nature.
Epictetus

advice-a1cc3d4531f77d071683e5c1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a1cc3d4531f77d071683e5c1.body:
(On moral harm depending on one’s own judgments) For another will not damage you, unless you choose: but you will be damaged then when you shall think that you are damaged.
Epictetus

advice-346d78173f50de74c8d66ce7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-346d78173f50de74c8d66ce7.body:
(On external advantages that do not determine moral worth) For if you think that any of the things which are not in our power is good or bad, it is absolutely necessary that, when you do not obtain what you wish, and when you fall into those things which you do not wish, you will find fault and hate those who are the cause of them; for every animal is formed by nature to this, to fly from and to turn from the things which appear harmful and the things which are the cause of the harm, but to follow and admire the things which are useful and the causes of the useful.
Epictetus

advice-8608862938b6636d32d18408.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8608862938b6636d32d18408.body:
(On approaching ancient divination without a preferred answer) But having determined in your mind that everything which shall turn out (result) is indifferent, and does not concern you, and whatever it may be, for it will be in your power to use it well, and no man will hinder this, come then with confidence to the gods as your advisers.
Epictetus

advice-1f6d83ed257b0031b77f3b98.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1f6d83ed257b0031b77f3b98.body:
(On consistently choosing a moral way of life) Immediately prescribe some character and some form to yourself, which you shall observe both when you are alone and when you meet with men.
Epictetus

advice-72213c0e43db75435e41f3b5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-72213c0e43db75435e41f3b5.body:
(On worthwhile conversation and appropriate silence) If then you are able, bring over by your conversation, the conversation of your associates, to that which is proper; but if you should happen to be confined to the company of strangers, be silent.
Epictetus

advice-393a173f0955b8afb04947a1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-393a173f0955b8afb04947a1.body:
(On ancient rules of continence and premarital relations) As to pleasure with women, abstain as far as you can before marriage; but if you do indulge in it, do it in the way which is conformable to custom.
Epictetus

advice-88e3bb9614b69cccb4013fdf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-88e3bb9614b69cccb4013fdf.body:
(On answering slander with self-deprecating humor) If a man has reported to you, that a certain person speaks ill of you, do not make any defence (answer) to what has been told you; but reply, The man did not know the rest of my faults, for he would not have mentioned these only.
Epictetus

advice-bb37db80a9c59efaf169d28b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bb37db80a9c59efaf169d28b.body:
(On worthwhile conversation and appropriate silence) It is a dangerous habit also to approach obscene talk.
Epictetus

advice-67a6320505a3a049d07fa956.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-67a6320505a3a049d07fa956.body:
(On weighing pleasure together with subsequent regret) Then think of both times, of the time when you will enjoy the pleasure, and of the time after the enjoyment of the pleasure, when you will repent and will reproach yourself.
Epictetus

advice-478e703892c25861b48580d1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-478e703892c25861b48580d1.body:
(On following a sound decision despite others’ disapproval) When you have decided that a thing ought to be done, and are doing it, never avoid being seen doing it, though the many shall form an unfavorable opinion about it.
Epictetus

advice-924622bcfd09b0c74cfc39dd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-924622bcfd09b0c74cfc39dd.body:
(On sustained attention to one’s judgments and actions) In walking about, as you take care not to step on a nail, or to sprain your foot, so take care not to damage your own ruling faculty; and if we observe this rule in every act, we shall undertake this act with more security.
Epictetus

advice-4723d4d31eb142c703965344.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4723d4d31eb142c703965344.body:
(On bodily needs as the measure of possessions) The measure of possession (property) is to every man the body, as the foot is of the shoe.
Epictetus

advice-3fd34a7be44e35f24223d5d2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3fd34a7be44e35f24223d5d2.body:
(On bodily needs as the measure of possessions) As also in the matter of the shoe, if you go beyond the (necessities of the) foot, the shoe is gilded, then of a purple color, then embroidered; for there is no limit to that which has once passed the true measure.
Epictetus

advice-b234bdf5aa008de6045d90a7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b234bdf5aa008de6045d90a7.body:
(On excessive bodily preoccupation at the mind’s expense) It is a mark of a mean capacity to spend much time on the things which concern the body, such as much exercise, much eating, much drinking, much easing of the body, much copulation.
Epictetus

advice-b201a4fb3b6d47b9b92b8585.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b201a4fb3b6d47b9b92b8585.body:
(On mistaken judgments behind conduct and anger) When any person treats you ill or speaks ill of you, remember that he does this or says this because he thinks that it is his duty.
Epictetus

advice-70b8e90ed15ba0321dfdf65d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-70b8e90ed15ba0321dfdf65d.body:
(Two handles represent different perspectives on a relative’s conduct) Everything has two handles, the one by which it may be borne, the other by which it may not. If your brother acts unjustly, do not lay hold of the act by that handle wherein he acts unjustly, for this is the handle which cannot be borne; but lay hold of the other, that he is your brother, that he was nurtured with you, and you will lay hold of the thing by that handle by which it can be borne.
Epictetus

advice-99b4a657f57a102821a89396.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-99b4a657f57a102821a89396.body:
(On moving from theoretical learning to action) On no occasion call yourself a philosopher, and do not speak much among the uninstructed about theorems (philosophical rules, precepts); but do that which follows from them.
Epictetus

advice-c9fd3a1bb0199bccfbf62a8f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c9fd3a1bb0199bccfbf62a8f.body:
(On consistently choosing a moral way of life) Whatever things (rules) are proposed to you (for the conduct of life) abide by them, as if they were laws, as if you would be guilty of impiety if you transgressed any of them.
Epictetus

advice-171a23756ae8b43cee3411ea.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-171a23756ae8b43cee3411ea.body:
(On maturity: not postponing work on one’s character) You are no longer a youth, but already a full-grown man.
Epictetus

advice-a5213391032dee98b4d7bc41.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a5213391032dee98b4d7bc41.body:
(On maturity: not postponing work on one’s character) If, then, you are negligent and slothful, and are continually making procrastination after procrastination, and proposal (intention) after proposal, and fixing day after day, after which you will attend to yourself, you will not know that you are not making improvement, but you will continue ignorant (uninstructed) both while you live and till you die.
Epictetus

advice-b0da4546050a7e11edf3380a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b0da4546050a7e11edf3380a.body:
(On maturity: not postponing work on one’s character) Immediately then think it right to live as a full-grown man, and one who is making proficiency, and let everything which appears to you to be the best be to you a law which must not be transgressed.
Epictetus

advice-9b3ad5d3546a5a588276e0c3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9b3ad5d3546a5a588276e0c3.body:
Pleasure is easily mistaken for goodness. That is why we often choose what feels pleasant and avoid pain without asking what is truly good.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book III, chapter VI, paragraph 5 (Chase edition)

advice-5ccd54b1adc1976635e2dafc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5ccd54b1adc1976635e2dafc.body:
(On the limits of close friendship) To be a friend to many people, in the way of the perfect Friendship, is not possible; just as you cannot be in love with many at once: it is, so to speak, a state of excess which naturally has but one object; and besides, it is not an easy thing for one man to be very much pleased with many people at the same time, nor perhaps to find many really good.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book VIII, chapter VII, paragraph 5 (Chase edition)

advice-4069e5e8972c77d2e7d9c96f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4069e5e8972c77d2e7d9c96f.body:
(On friendship for advantage or pleasure) So then they whose motive to Friendship is utility love their friends for what is good to themselves; they whose motive is pleasure do so for what is pleasurable to themselves; that is to say, not in so far as the friend beloved is but in so far as he is useful or pleasurable.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book VIII, chapter IV, paragraph 3 (Chase edition)

advice-bf16b16cc942c6eb7d66058a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bf16b16cc942c6eb7d66058a.body:
(On educating moral feelings) And to like and dislike what one ought is judged to be most important for the formation of good moral character: because these feelings extend all one’s life through, giving a bias towards and exerting an influence on the side of Virtue and Happiness, since men choose what is pleasant and avoid what is painful.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book X, chapter I, paragraph 1 (Chase edition)

advice-b5696166308b655dff8ebec4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b5696166308b655dff8ebec4.body:
(On justice as a good for others) And for this same reason Justice alone of all the Virtues is thought to be a good to others, because it has immediate relation to some other person, inasmuch as the Just man does what is advantageous to another, either to his ruler or fellow-subject.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book V, chapter II, paragraph 9 (Chase edition)

advice-e1ff22ab1d53d1473d7c5384.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e1ff22ab1d53d1473d7c5384.body:
(On courage in the face of danger) Now the Brave man cannot be frighted from his propriety (but of course only so far as he is man); fear such things indeed he will, but he will stand up against them as he ought and as right reason may direct, with a view to what is honourable, because this is the end of the virtue.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book III, chapter X, paragraph 2 (Chase edition)

advice-fc9d74e6e8525ed625c1a022.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fc9d74e6e8525ed625c1a022.body:
(On honour as recognition of virtue) And besides, men seem to pursue honour, that they may believe themselves to be good: for instance, they seek to be honoured by the wise, and by those among whom they are known, and for virtue: clearly then, in the opinion at least of these men, virtue is higher than honour.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book I, chapter III, paragraph 4 (Chase edition)

advice-108b1f184d19c77594a2c3f0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-108b1f184d19c77594a2c3f0.body:
(On human self-sufficiency within relationships) Now by sufficient for Self, we mean not for a single individual living a solitary life, but for his parents also and children and wife, and, in general, friends and countrymen; for man is by nature adapted to a social existence.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book I, chapter IV, paragraph 6 (Chase edition)

advice-18d92c417e508eff5aa6cff8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-18d92c417e508eff5aa6cff8.body:
(On the judgments of a good person) For the good man judges in every instance correctly, and in every instance the notion conveyed to his mind is the true one.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book III, chapter VI, paragraph 3 (Chase edition)

advice-0da3a6342e1d7c272fe32734.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0da3a6342e1d7c272fe32734.body:
(On the changeable friendships of youth) The young are also much given up to Love; this passion being, in great measure, a matter of impulse and based on pleasure: for which cause they conceive Friendships and quickly drop them, changing often in the same day: but these wish for society and intimate intercourse with their friends, since they thus attain the object of their Friendship.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book VIII, chapter IV, paragraph 8 (Chase edition)

advice-b506a657bead767549a77a53.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b506a657bead767549a77a53.body:
(On friendship based on mutual advantage) The Friendship based on motives of profit is thought to be most of all formed out of contrary elements: the poor man, for instance, is thus a friend of the rich, and the ignorant of the man of information; that is to say, a man desiring that of which he is, as it happens, in want, gives something else in exchange for it.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book VIII, chapter VIII, paragraph 13 (Chase edition)

advice-c0a1d9e1bbd5cc65c4a08b8f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c0a1d9e1bbd5cc65c4a08b8f.body:
(On a friend as a second self) But the good man is to his friend as to himself, friend being but a name for a second Self; therefore as his own existence is choice-worthy to each so too, or similarly at least, is his friend’s existence.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IX, chapter IX, paragraph 14 (Chase edition)

advice-990008b48dc72cc2db9469d1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-990008b48dc72cc2db9469d1.body:
(On how virtue is acquired) The formation of a virtuous character some ascribe to Nature, some to Custom, and some to Teaching.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book X, chapter VIII, paragraph 4 (Chase edition)

advice-64766fc6d11c4273debb9498.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-64766fc6d11c4273debb9498.body:
(On mildness and measured anger) For the notion represented by the term Meek man is the being imperturbable, and not being led away by passion, but being angry in that manner, and at those things, and for that length of time, which Reason may direct.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IV, chapter VII, paragraph 2 (Chase edition)

advice-e02cb31004563788898af783.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e02cb31004563788898af783.body:
(On people who harbour resentment) The Bitter-tempered are hard to reconcile and keep their anger for a long while, because they repress the feeling: but when they have revenged themselves then comes a lull; for the vengeance destroys their anger by producing pleasure in lieu of pain.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IV, chapter VII, paragraph 6 (Chase edition)

advice-1d6a1435b74b7f395cf55f48.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1d6a1435b74b7f395cf55f48.body:
(On friends who share our prosperity) On the other hand, the advantages of friends in our prosperity are the pleasurable intercourse and the consciousness that they are pleased at our good fortune.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IX, chapter XI, paragraph 6 (Chase edition)

advice-c9aaafa2520728397d542c9c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c9aaafa2520728397d542c9c.body:
(On virtuous and vicious self-love) And so the good man ought to be Self-loving: because by doing what is noble he will have advantage himself and will do good to others: but the bad man ought not to be, because he will harm himself and his neighbours by following low and evil passions.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IX, chapter VIII, paragraph 10 (Chase edition)

advice-609a7776755374f8cedef058.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-609a7776755374f8cedef058.body:
(On boasting and its motives) Now the Braggart is such not by his power but by his purpose, that is to say, in virtue of his moral state, and because he is a man of a certain kind; just as there are liars who take pleasure in falsehood for its own sake while others lie from a desire of glory or gain.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IV, chapter IX, paragraph 9 (Chase edition)

advice-facd85205012229516068aa5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-facd85205012229516068aa5.body:
(On friendship in adversity and prosperity) To have friends is more necessary in adversity, and therefore in this case useful ones are wanted; and to have them in prosperity is more honourable, and this is why the prosperous want good men for friends, it being preferable to confer benefits on, and to live with, these.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IX, chapter XI, paragraph 2 (Chase edition)

advice-2e764649b28b631977fb7488.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2e764649b28b631977fb7488.body:
(On the remorse of a wrongdoer) And though it is impossible actually to have at the same time the sensations of pain and pleasure; yet after a little time the man is sorry for having been pleased, and he could wish that those objects had not given him pleasure; for the wicked are full of remorse.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IX, chapter IV, paragraph 9 (Chase edition)

advice-1e5f5e86acd9bec3d5d0eb20.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1e5f5e86acd9bec3d5d0eb20.body:
(On exercising virtue rather than merely possessing it) And as at the Olympic games it is not the finest and strongest men who are crowned, but they who enter the lists, for out of these the prize-men are selected; so too in life, of the honourable and the good, it is they who act who rightly win the prizes.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book I, chapter VI, paragraph 7 (Chase edition)

advice-6a0037bb6fad4b6fa74e3a25.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6a0037bb6fad4b6fa74e3a25.body:
(On magnanimity and justified self-worth) Well then, he is thought to be Great-minded who values himself highly and at the same time justly, because he that does so without grounds is foolish, and no virtuous character is foolish or senseless.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IV, chapter IV, paragraph 2 (Chase edition)

advice-adb1c686dc1b5db3b938aaed.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-adb1c686dc1b5db3b938aaed.body:
(On the meaning of a happy life) So far as name goes, there is a pretty general agreement: for HAPPINESS both the multitude and the refined few call it, and “living well” and “doing well” they conceive to be the same with “being happy;” but about the Nature of this Happiness, men dispute, and the multitude do not in their account of it agree with the wise.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book I, chapter II, paragraph 2 (Chase edition)

advice-6b2b1e20be5ce172c4ddb399.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6b2b1e20be5ce172c4ddb399.body:
(On virtue as human excellence) Virtue, must be a state whereby Man comes to be good and whereby he will perform well his proper work.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book II, chapter V, paragraph 2 (Chase edition)

advice-0d4b27a2183570c1de71758c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0d4b27a2183570c1de71758c.body:
(On recognising one's own inclinations) We ought also to take into consideration our own natural bias; which varies in each man’s case, and will be ascertained from the pleasure and pain arising in us.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book II, chapter IX, paragraph 6 (Chase edition)

advice-50c55487ec5e2b364e072a70.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-50c55487ec5e2b364e072a70.body:
(On friendship based on mutual advantage) Now it is the nature of utility not to be permanent but constantly varying: so, of course, when the motive which made them friends is vanished, the Friendship likewise dissolves; since it existed only relatively to those circumstances.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book VIII, chapter IV, paragraph 4 (Chase edition)

advice-382a4ac913f47fd949c7f9ed.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-382a4ac913f47fd949c7f9ed.body:
(On happiness as activity of the soul) And by Human Excellence we mean not that of man’s body but that of his soul; for we call Happiness a working of the Soul.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book I, chapter XI, paragraph 3 (Chase edition)

advice-42dbdd84f42c3aebb1a65077.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-42dbdd84f42c3aebb1a65077.body:
(On vanity and ignorance of oneself) But the Vain are foolish and self-ignorant, and that palpably: because they attempt honourable things, as though they were worthy, and then they are detected.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IV, chapter V, paragraph 3 (Chase edition)

advice-1c4da687b0130359493a3c7a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1c4da687b0130359493a3c7a.body:
(On one's obligations to a former friend) Surely he ought to bear in mind the intimacy of past times, and just as we think ourselves bound to do favours for our friends in preference to strangers, so to those who have been friends and are so no longer we should allow somewhat on the score of previous Friendship, whenever the cause of severance is not excessive depravity on their part.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IX, chapter III, paragraph 10 (Chase edition)

advice-8d7f8c5085a00ba8aa532bfa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8d7f8c5085a00ba8aa532bfa.body:
(On virtue as a mean between extremes) And so, viewing it in respect of its essence and definition, Virtue is a mean state; but in reference to the chief good and to excellence it is the highest state possible.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book II, chapter VI, paragraph 3 (Chase edition)

advice-8fd388277f1d8a2257095be5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8fd388277f1d8a2257095be5.body:
(On personal well-being within family and community) And yet it is just possible that the good of the individual cannot be secured independently of connection with a family or a community.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book VI, chapter VIII, paragraph 6 (Chase edition)

advice-a2fe9e0a8d62654a4169e749.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a2fe9e0a8d62654a4169e749.body:
(On the limits of close friendship) To be sure, in the way merely of society, a man may be a friend to many without being necessarily over-complaisant, but being truly good: but one cannot be a friend to many because of their virtue, and for the persons’ own sake; in fact, it is a matter for contentment to find even a few such.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IX, chapter X, paragraph 8 (Chase edition)

advice-a0423cae53e3ffd13c0cc79a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a0423cae53e3ffd13c0cc79a.body:
(On unstable friendship between bad people) The bad, on the contrary, have no principle of stability: in fact, they do not even continue like themselves: only they come to be friends for a short time from taking delight in one another’s wickedness.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book VIII, chapter VIII, paragraph 12 (Chase edition)

advice-85303325a1c42c0c190a6513.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-85303325a1c42c0c190a6513.body:
(On practical wisdom in choosing actions) And so, in a general way of speaking, the man who is good at deliberation will be Practically Wise.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book VI, chapter V, paragraph 2 (Chase edition)

advice-94e98372078af9c51db6605c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-94e98372078af9c51db6605c.body:
(On courage in the face of danger) But a man is to be Brave, not on compulsion, but from a sense of honour.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book III, chapter XI, paragraph 11 (Chase edition)

advice-2d1d04722be6605d495e8d9f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2d1d04722be6605d495e8d9f.body:
(On the material needs of contemplation) So Happiness must be a kind of Contemplative Speculation; but since it is Man we are speaking of he will need likewise External Prosperity, because his Nature is not by itself sufficient for Speculation, but there must be health of body, and nourishment, and tendance of all kinds.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book X, chapter VII, paragraph 1 (Chase edition)

advice-13c3946798a098b024d5c821.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-13c3946798a098b024d5c821.body:
(On living virtuously with modest means) However, it must not be thought, because without external goods a man cannot enjoy high Happiness, that therefore he will require many and great goods in order to be happy: for neither Self-sufficiency, nor Action, stand in Excess, and it is quite possible to act nobly without being ruler of sea and land, since even with moderate means a man may act in accordance with Virtue.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book X, chapter VII, paragraph 2 (Chase edition)

advice-ac23d800986797e2b5349a83.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ac23d800986797e2b5349a83.body:
(On exercising virtue rather than merely possessing it) For the state or habit may possibly exist in a subject without effecting any good, as, for instance, in him who is asleep, or in any other way inactive; but the working cannot so, for it will of necessity act, and act well.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book I, chapter VI, paragraph 7 (Chase edition)

advice-f4e70169026840a238edb448.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f4e70169026840a238edb448.body:
(On knowing general rules and particular circumstances) Since then Practical Wisdom is apt to act, one ought to have both kinds of knowledge, or, if only one, the knowledge of details rather than of Principles.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book VI, chapter VIII, paragraph 2 (Chase edition)

advice-854d44048882a961aebcbfb7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-854d44048882a961aebcbfb7.body:
(On responding well to pleasure and pain) Virtue then is assumed to be that habit which is such, in relation to pleasures and pains, as to effect the best results, and Vice the contrary.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book II, chapter II, paragraph 8 (Chase edition)

advice-74e47ac0d3be1b62c8813c6a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-74e47ac0d3be1b62c8813c6a.body:
(On how virtue is acquired) So too then is it with the Virtues: for by acting in the various relations in which we are thrown with our fellow men, we come to be, some just, some unjust: and by acting in dangerous positions and being habituated to feel fear or confidence, we come to be, some brave, others cowards.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book II, chapter I, paragraph 6 (Chase edition)

advice-569ed40e2c2e3fb4751afe3c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-569ed40e2c2e3fb4751afe3c.body:
(On the pleasure of being aware of life) Now to perceive that one lives is a thing pleasant in itself, life being a thing naturally good, and the perceiving of the presence in ourselves of things naturally good being pleasant.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IX, chapter IX, paragraph 12 (Chase edition)

advice-8cf4d2557d8c4fe89fdab69e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8cf4d2557d8c4fe89fdab69e.body:
(On friendship as a bond of community) Furthermore, Friendship seems to be the bond of Social Communities, and legislators seem to be more anxious to secure it than Justice even.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book VIII, chapter I, paragraph 4 (Chase edition)

advice-f662aa5e14a3c5353124e541.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f662aa5e14a3c5353124e541.body:
(On the self-controlled person and the obstinate person) The man of Self-Control does not change by reason of passion and lust, yet when occasion so requires he will be easy of persuasion: but the obstinate man changes not at the call of Reason, though many of this class take up certain desires and are led by their pleasures.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book VII, chapter VIII, paragraph 3 (Chase edition)

advice-64c4b1f53274fb59a4eb9ba3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-64c4b1f53274fb59a4eb9ba3.body:
(On benefactors and the lasting worth of kindness) Now the benefactor’s work abides (for the honourable is enduring), but the advantage of him who has received the kindness passes away.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IX, chapter VII, paragraph 8 (Chase edition)

advice-9f6fc77d2869409772f8657f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9f6fc77d2869409772f8657f.body:
(On happiness as the final goal of action) So then Happiness is manifestly something final and self-sufficient, being the end of all things which are and may be done.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book I, chapter IV, paragraph 7 (Chase edition)

advice-ff6b34ebf332fad4bba03705.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ff6b34ebf332fad4bba03705.body:
(On human dignity in severe misfortune) But still, even in these, nobleness shines through when a man bears contentedly many and great mischances not from insensibility to pain but because he is noble and high-spirited.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book I, chapter VIII, paragraph 9 (Chase edition)

advice-42419b57bb93aecc941bfa02.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-42419b57bb93aecc941bfa02.body:
(On excessive anger and the desire for revenge) To Meekness we oppose the excess rather than the defect, because it is of more common occurrence: for human nature is more disposed to take than to forgo revenge.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IV, chapter VII, paragraph 8 (Chase edition)

advice-4553f34fd3aa18985952188a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4553f34fd3aa18985952188a.body:
(On shameful actions and moral character) In truth, to be such a man as to do anything disgraceful is the part of a faulty character.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IV, chapter XI, paragraph 2 (Chase edition)

advice-802a339f3f79755645dc8874.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-802a339f3f79755645dc8874.body:
(On wishing a friend well for their own sake) I mean, people define a friend to be “one who intends and does what is good (or what he believes to be good) to another for that other’s sake,” or “one who wishes his friend to be and to live for that friend’s own sake” (which is the feeling of mothers towards their children, and of friends who have come into collision).
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IX, chapter IV, paragraph 2 (Chase edition)

advice-60e0ba0b09c1035078d748c7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-60e0ba0b09c1035078d748c7.body:
(On courage and reckless boldness) The rash again are precipitate, and, being eager before danger, when actually in it fall away, while the Brave are quick and sharp in action, but before are quiet and composed.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book III, chapter X, paragraph 9 (Chase edition)

advice-b86cd6ec70804e8022ccd0ab.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b86cd6ec70804e8022ccd0ab.body:
(On generosity in the use of wealth) And the Liberal are liked almost best of all virtuous characters, because they are profitable to others, and this their profitableness consists in their giving.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IV, chapter I, paragraph 8 (Chase edition)

advice-bb0c4e6426452d84be523042.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bb0c4e6426452d84be523042.body:
(On a person who undervalues their merits) The Small-minded man, for instance, being really worthy of good deprives himself of his deserts, and seems to have somewhat faulty from not having a sufficiently high estimate of his own desert, in fact from self-ignorance: because, but for this, he would have grasped after what he really is entitled to, and that is good.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IV, chapter V, paragraph 2 (Chase edition)

advice-1034c2916cd58969788075c9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1034c2916cd58969788075c9.body:
(On pleasure mistaken for goodness) But in all cases we must guard most carefully against what is pleasant, and pleasure itself, because we are not impartial judges of it.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book II, chapter IX, paragraph 7 (Chase edition)

advice-9087cf7813d904f792e23a05.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9087cf7813d904f792e23a05.body:
(On accepting sympathy and help from friends) One should perhaps be cautious not to present the appearance of sullenness in declining the sympathy or help of friends, for this happens occasionally.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book IX, chapter XI, paragraph 9 (Chase edition)

advice-6f7268b2642c03e82bd383a8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6f7268b2642c03e82bd383a8.body:
(On appropriate precision in different subjects) And in the same spirit should each person receive what we say: for the man of education will seek exactness so far in each subject as the nature of the thing admits, it being plainly much the same absurdity to put up with a mathematician who tries to persuade instead of proving, and to demand strict demonstrative reasoning of a Rhetorician.
Aristotle

sources.author: Aristotle
sources.reference: Book I, chapter I, paragraph 9 (Chase edition)
