(On laws being just through their usefulness for coexistence) When, without any fresh circumstances arising, a thing which has been declared just in practice does not agree with the impressions of reason, that is a proof that the thing was not really just. In the same way, when in consequence of new circumstances, a thing which has been pronounced just does not any longer appear to agree with utility, the thing which was just, inasmuch as it was useful to the social relations and intercourse of mankind, ceases to be just the moment when it ceases to be useful.
Epicurus

advice-2e34331264afc65617be24d9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2e34331264afc65617be24d9.body:
(On friendship and safe relations with other people) He who desires to live tranquilly without having any thing to fear from other men, ought to make himself friends; those whom he cannot make friends of, he should, at least, avoid rendering enemies; and if that is not in his power, he should, as far as possible, avoid all intercourse with them, and keep them aloof, as far as it is for his interest to do so.
Epicurus

advice-ff13e687cab0370e3d57a62a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ff13e687cab0370e3d57a62a.body:
(Security and mutual trust within a community of friends) The happiest men are they who have arrived at the point of having nothing to fear from those who surround them. Such men live with one another most agreeably, having the firmest grounds of confidence in one another, enjoying the advantages of friendship in all their fulness, and not lamenting, as a pitiable circumstance, the premature death of their friends.
Epicurus

advice-955b90a44d2533f9a3be3e33.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-955b90a44d2533f9a3be3e33.body:
To fear death as the greatest evil is to claim knowledge no one possesses: we do not know what death will bring.
Socrates

advice-a499bc07ee76f4778bd05961.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a499bc07ee76f4778bd05961.body:
(Justice and moral conduct) Let us, then, take the argument as our guide, which has revealed to us that the best way of life is to practise justice and every virtue in life and death.
Socrates

advice-8cea6e879e1831ceff78a228.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8cea6e879e1831ceff78a228.body:
(The nature and unity of virtue) But we shall never know the certain truth until, before asking how virtue is given, we enquire into the actual nature of virtue.
Socrates

advice-2fddff02f39ec87a06f1024a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2fddff02f39ec87a06f1024a.body:
(Socrates on moral steadfastness in the face of a death sentence) Wherefore, O judges, be of good cheer about death, and know of a certainty, that no evil can happen to a good man, either in life or after death.
Socrates

advice-0e2f6a75974f64db818576d6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0e2f6a75974f64db818576d6.body:
(A person who understands justice and the majority’s opinion) Then, my friend, we must not regard what the many say of us: but what he, the one man who has understanding of just and unjust, will say, and what the truth will say.
Socrates

advice-88b8ce458aa1b4c064c4af93.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-88b8ce458aa1b4c064c4af93.body:
(Truthful speech and fair judgment) Never mind the manner, which may or may not be good; but think only of the truth of my words, and give heed to that: let the speaker speak truly and the judge decide justly.
Socrates

advice-02c02012040ccfa927762300.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-02c02012040ccfa927762300.body:
(The value of refutation in seeking truth) And if you refute me, I shall not be angry with you as you are with me, but I shall inscribe you as the greatest of benefactors on the tablets of my soul.
Socrates

advice-ba63354b1cd0d50851cc1e5f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ba63354b1cd0d50851cc1e5f.body:
(A tyrant and a morally superior person) But when the tyrant is rude and uneducated, he may be expected to fear any one who is his superior in virtue, and will never be able to be perfectly friendly with him.
Socrates

advice-3aa038d4e00d1f3a7a688675.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3aa038d4e00d1f3a7a688675.body:
(Knowledge and true opinion) And the only right guides are knowledge and true opinion—these are the guides of man; for things which happen by chance are not under the guidance of man: but the guides of man are true opinion and knowledge.
Socrates

advice-80c84cc79d192b18cad6d2ff.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-80c84cc79d192b18cad6d2ff.body:
(Knowledge and true opinion) And yet that knowledge differs from true opinion is no matter of conjecture with me.
Socrates

advice-6c7953a1174eaf03e852fe79.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6c7953a1174eaf03e852fe79.body:
(Wealth, wisdom, and virtue) I tell you that virtue is not given by money, but that from virtue comes money and every other good of man, public as well as private.
Socrates

advice-9618dda1648cdf0a545b9e95.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9618dda1648cdf0a545b9e95.body:
(Correcting one’s own faults) If you think that by killing men you can prevent some one from censuring your evil lives, you are mistaken; that is not a way of escape which is either possible or honourable; the easiest and the noblest way is not to be disabling others, but to be improving yourselves.
Socrates

advice-ac579c3b1eef742d4eee2800.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ac579c3b1eef742d4eee2800.body:
(An examined life and the search for truth) Renouncing the honours at which the world aims, I desire only to know the truth, and to live as well as I can, and, when I die, to die as well as I can.
Socrates

advice-0ee09ecbc21ef239b7ea6554.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0ee09ecbc21ef239b7ea6554.body:
(Life as a moral contest) And, in return for your exhortation of me, I exhort you also to take part in the great combat, which is the combat of life, and greater than every other earthly conflict.
Socrates

advice-525c18bcd2be8183fbf705ed.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-525c18bcd2be8183fbf705ed.body:
(Injustice as a disease of the soul) For I certainly think that I and you and every man do really believe, that to do is a greater evil than to suffer injustice: and not to be punished than to be punished.
Socrates

advice-896b8f36fcaaa62715562962.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-896b8f36fcaaa62715562962.body:
(Care of the soul and the order of goods) For I do nothing but go about persuading you all, old and young alike, not to take thought for your persons or your properties, but first and chiefly to care about the greatest improvement of the soul.
Socrates

advice-fbd6b402c8953c204374060f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fbd6b402c8953c204374060f.body:
(Socrates on moral steadfastness in the face of a death sentence) The difficulty, my friends, is not to avoid death, but to avoid unrighteousness; for that runs faster than death.
Socrates

advice-3f71307421a2ad559ba30684.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3f71307421a2ad559ba30684.body:
(Rejecting revenge and tolerating mistakes) Then we ought not to retaliate or render evil for evil to any one, whatever evil we may have suffered from him.
Socrates

advice-11b60191d542129532a60754.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-11b60191d542129532a60754.body:
(Injustice as a disease of the soul) Yes; for happiness surely does not consist in being delivered from evils, but in never having had them.
Socrates

advice-03fe5fc6c7fc797bb3feddd7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-03fe5fc6c7fc797bb3feddd7.body:
(Inner harmony and consistency) And yet, my friend, I would rather that my lyre should be inharmonious, and that there should be no music in the chorus which I provided; aye, or that the whole world should be at odds with me, and oppose me, rather than that I myself should be at odds with myself, and contradict myself.
Socrates

advice-6f147642b41fa6ac29c0c0d6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6f147642b41fa6ac29c0c0d6.body:
(Socrates on moral steadfastness in the face of a death sentence) I thought at the time that I ought not to do anything common or mean when in danger: nor do I now repent of the style of my defence; I would rather die having spoken after my manner, than speak in your manner and live.
Socrates

advice-fe3b29e31f8dca2f0430932e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fe3b29e31f8dca2f0430932e.body:
(The corrective purpose of punishment) Now the proper office of punishment is twofold: he who is rightly punished ought either to become better and profit by it, or he ought to be made an example to his fellows, that they may see what he suffers, and fear and become better.
Socrates

advice-37b3694dd87e8d8763370338.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-37b3694dd87e8d8763370338.body:
(Insults and physical blows do not destroy virtue) And never mind if some one despises you as a fool, and insults you, if he has a mind; let him strike you, by Zeus, and do you be of good cheer, and do not mind the insulting blow, for you will never come to any harm in the practice of virtue, if you are a really good and true man.
Socrates

advice-bfeef2d9aca49a6d86e29bb3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bfeef2d9aca49a6d86e29bb3.body:
(A judge’s experience and moral knowledge) Therefore, the judge should not be young; he should have learned to know evil, not from his own soul, but from late and long observation of the nature of evil in others: knowledge should be his guide, not personal experience.
Socrates

advice-4deee96bf3c8a62fb4c9ede6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4deee96bf3c8a62fb4c9ede6.body:
(Early learning without compulsion) Then, my good friend, do not use compulsion, but let early education be a sort of amusement; you will then be better able to find out the natural bent.
Socrates

advice-9c9f9fce96c1890788b47e39.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9c9f9fce96c1890788b47e39.body:
(Wealth, poverty, and moderate desires) Wealth, and poverty; the one is the parent of luxury and indolence, and the other of meanness and viciousness, and both of discontent.
Socrates

advice-ede67b676d1712ed94eca4bc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ede67b676d1712ed94eca4bc.body:
(Sharing the grief of characters in poetry) Few persons ever reflect, as I should imagine, that from the evil of other men something of evil is communicated to themselves.
Socrates

advice-25875833d19454e28b3f4ef4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-25875833d19454e28b3f4ef4.body:
(The parallel between soul and state) I mean, that there appear to be as many forms of the soul as there are distinct forms of the State.
Socrates

advice-a823c85099a2e1573341cc65.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a823c85099a2e1573341cc65.body:
(The common good and the order of the state) At present, I take it, we are fashioning the happy State, not piecemeal, or with a view of making a few happy citizens, but as a whole; and by-and-by we will proceed to view the opposite kind of State.
Socrates

advice-e635a16f44e1264efc216512.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e635a16f44e1264efc216512.body:
(The distinction between good and pleasure) Why, my friend, the inference is that the good is not the same as the pleasant, or the evil the same as the painful; there is a cessation of pleasure and pain at the same moment; but not of good and evil, for they are different.
Socrates

advice-abfbf0ae4e0f54be57d6aff2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-abfbf0ae4e0f54be57d6aff2.body:
(Knowledge of the good as a basis for moral judgment) I am sure, that he who does not know how the beautiful and the just are likewise good will be but a sorry guardian of them; and I suspect that no one who is ignorant of the good will have a true knowledge of them.
Socrates

advice-f24ffc6ba6ee97074b82e096.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f24ffc6ba6ee97074b82e096.body:
(Free and frank speech) Speak out, my good friend, freely and fairly as you did at first and ought to do again, and tell me your entire mind.
Socrates

advice-c9a512a89e07d87ffe84693c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c9a512a89e07d87ffe84693c.body:
(A shared search for truth about the virtuous life) And if I am to carry on the enquiry by myself, I will first of all remark that not only I but all of us should have an ambition to know what is true and what is false in this matter, for the discovery of the truth is a common good.
Socrates

advice-6af0093fe3b028ca0ea13efe.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6af0093fe3b028ca0ea13efe.body:
(Death and the fate of consciousness) Let us reflect in another way, and we shall see that there is great reason to hope that death is a good; for one of two things—either death is a state of nothingness and utter unconsciousness, or, as men say, there is a change and migration of the soul from this world to another.
Socrates

advice-c437ba68d279f5d9e76d47d7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c437ba68d279f5d9e76d47d7.body:
(Happiness and the condition of the soul) For, indeed, we are at issue about matters which to know is honourable and not to know disgraceful; to know or not to know happiness and misery—that is the chief of them.
Socrates

advice-03513791803b7537fc14dfd2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-03513791803b7537fc14dfd2.body:
(Moral preparation for political activity) When we have practised virtue together, we will apply ourselves to politics, if that seems desirable, or we will advise about whatever else may seem good to us, for we shall be better able to judge then.
Socrates

advice-2482d3417f86018f4d9c34fd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2482d3417f86018f4d9c34fd.body:
(The distinction between fear and reverence) I should not say that where there is fear there is also reverence; for I am sure that many persons fear poverty and disease, and the like evils, but I do not perceive that they reverence the objects of their fear.
Socrates

advice-147dc4089f000b33ecc918f8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-147dc4089f000b33ecc918f8.body:
(Disagreement about what is just) But, as you say, people regard the same things, some as just and others as unjust,—about these they dispute; and so there arise wars and fightings among them.
Socrates

advice-ddb1d417fe33f3e2d1df3b5b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ddb1d417fe33f3e2d1df3b5b.body:
(Human needs as the origin of society) A State, arises, as I conceive, out of the needs of mankind; no one is self-sufficing, but all of us have many wants.
Socrates

advice-56b7b8c11204eefff95362d6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-56b7b8c11204eefff95362d6.body:
(Precision in understanding the highest good) When little things are elaborated with an infinity of pains, in order that they may appear in their full beauty and utmost clearness, how ridiculous that we should not think the highest truths worthy of attaining the highest accuracy!
Socrates

advice-a92ba0c26237c240edae50ce.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a92ba0c26237c240edae50ce.body:
(Training spiritedness: courage or brutality) Yet surely, this ferocity only comes from spirit, which, if rightly educated, would give courage, but, if too much intensified, is liable to become hard and brutal.
Socrates

advice-44daa60f193348c50cf2b89d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-44daa60f193348c50cf2b89d.body:
(Persistence and care in philosophical inquiry) Still, as we are near the spot at which we may see the truth in the clearest manner with our own eyes, let us not faint by the way.
Socrates

advice-389f857d9c3db9c0e60b40fe.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-389f857d9c3db9c0e60b40fe.body:
(Payment for a capable teacher) Although, if a man were really able to instruct mankind, to receive money for giving instruction would, in my opinion, be an honour to him.
Socrates

advice-5d516b15e4817d95ca772f8c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5d516b15e4817d95ca772f8c.body:
(The moral responsibility of rulers) And yet in that very class there may arise good men, and worthy of all admiration they are, for where there is great power to do wrong, to live and to die justly is a hard thing, and greatly to be praised, and few there are who attain to this.
Socrates

advice-edf93091248354bc443f4d93.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-edf93091248354bc443f4d93.body:
(The higher aim of studying musical harmony: knowledge of truth) At the same time, we must not lose sight of our own higher object.
Socrates

advice-80f4a9818d99e35c0ad3f5f0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-80f4a9818d99e35c0ad3f5f0.body:
(Socrates on the supposed wisdom of influential people) So I left him, saying to myself, as I went away: Well, although I do not suppose that either of us knows anything really beautiful and good, I am better off than he is,—for he knows nothing, and thinks that he knows; I neither know nor think that I know.
Socrates

advice-4c6d39b782dd022c96be96f5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4c6d39b782dd022c96be96f5.body:
(Intellectual ability without moral education) You are aware, that quick intelligence, memory, sagacity, cleverness, and similar qualities, do not often grow together, and that persons who possess them and are at the same time high-spirited and magnanimous are not so constituted by nature as to live orderly and in a peaceful and settled manner; they are driven any way by their impulses, and all solid principle goes out of them.
Socrates

advice-91629bfb0c8326552b430bf8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-91629bfb0c8326552b430bf8.body:
(A writer or lawgiver who does not understand justice) For not to know the nature of justice and injustice, and good and evil, and not to be able to distinguish the dream from the reality, cannot in truth be otherwise than disgraceful to him, even though he have the applause of the whole world.
Socrates

advice-7ef1f87578ecb06beef5ac3c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7ef1f87578ecb06beef5ac3c.body:
(Striving for the true art of speaking) But even to fail in an honourable object is honourable.
Socrates

advice-cb5abd40bfec7fbca2135ebd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cb5abd40bfec7fbca2135ebd.body:
(Clarifying the subject before discussion) But people imagine that they know about the nature of things, when they don't know about them, and, not having come to an understanding at first because they think that they know, they end, as might be expected, in contradicting one another and themselves.
Socrates

advice-10d498f97abb86e000f6973a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-10d498f97abb86e000f6973a.body:
(Doubt about the literal truth of myths) The wise are doubtful, and I should not be singular if, like them, I too doubted.
Socrates

advice-cd6757ada8f94537bb8cd14c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cd6757ada8f94537bb8cd14c.body:
(Discussing the merits and faults of Lysias’s speech) The worst of authors will say something which is to the point.
Socrates

advice-530238e84b27631c02b4270f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-530238e84b27631c02b4270f.body:
(Persistence and care in philosophical inquiry) Better a little which is well done, than a great deal imperfectly.
Socrates

advice-c72cf3025329624ed335647f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c72cf3025329624ed335647f.body:
(An apparent victory in debate without establishing truth) Like a good-for-nothing cock, without having won the victory, we walk away from the argument and crow.
Socrates

advice-c1053a03a07ed025af695903.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c1053a03a07ed025af695903.body:
(The starting concepts of an inquiry into the good) Let us be very careful in laying the foundation.
Socrates

advice-4b2c8a035cb6b8cb6f35b9b0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4b2c8a035cb6b8cb6f35b9b0.body:
(Precision in understanding the highest good) Nothing imperfect is the measure of anything, although persons are too apt to be contented and think that they need search no further.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Republic, Book VI, Stephanus 504B–504C, paragraph 293 (Jowett); complete clause excerpt

advice-1f96a34e8cfa3a845d52ce6d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1f96a34e8cfa3a845d52ce6d.body:
(Socrates on the supposed wisdom of influential people) I found that the men most in repute were all but the most foolish; and that others less esteemed were really wiser and better.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Apology, Stephanus 21–22, dialogue paragraph 8 (Jowett 1892); complete clause excerpt

advice-ae56b2b5a2f66f1b7d0f36c8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ae56b2b5a2f66f1b7d0f36c8.body:
(Justice and moral conduct) He is good who has a good soul.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Republic, Book III, Stephanus 409C–409D, paragraph 420 (Jowett); complete clause excerpt

advice-b9414be38f0f273bfba6250a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b9414be38f0f273bfba6250a.body:
(The nature and unity of virtue) The argument seems to have reached a height from which, as from some tower of speculation, a man may look down and see that virtue is one, but that the forms of vice are innumerable.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Republic, Book IV, Stephanus 445C–445C, paragraph 453 (Jowett); complete clause excerpt

advice-31e1c1ff6e1ac5ea298febe4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-31e1c1ff6e1ac5ea298febe4.body:
(Human needs as the origin of society) The true creator is necessity, who is the mother of our invention.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Republic, Book II, Stephanus 369C–369C, paragraph 72 (Jowett); complete clause excerpt

advice-744e3ecb48821c5a801c5bf0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-744e3ecb48821c5a801c5bf0.body:
(The difference between practical skill and oratory) As to the arts generally, they are for the most part concerned with doing, and require little or no speaking; in painting, and statuary, and many other arts, the work may proceed in silence.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Gorgias, Stephanus 450, dialogue paragraph 84 (Jowett 1892); complete clause excerpt

advice-986bd92e93dfa2a7fea2e136.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-986bd92e93dfa2a7fea2e136.body:
(Learning, experience, and wise guidance) I am a lover of knowledge, and the men who dwell in the city are my teachers, and not the trees or the country.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Phaedrus, dialogue paragraph 37 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1636); complete clause excerpt

advice-22d77b39fe91329585a91465.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-22d77b39fe91329585a91465.body:
(Clarifying the subject before discussion) All good counsel begins in the same way; a man should know what he is advising about, or his counsel will all come to nought.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Phaedrus, dialogue paragraph 72 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1636); complete clause excerpt

advice-a9a18f949f477a8f1ef55b9e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a9a18f949f477a8f1ef55b9e.body:
(Truthfulness and the rejection of falsehood) To think truly is noble and to be deceived is base.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Theaetetus, dialogue paragraph 713 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1726); complete clause excerpt

advice-6a53736a5f8cfebab2f1003a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6a53736a5f8cfebab2f1003a.body:
(Philosophical dialogue as help in bringing forth thought) The triumph of my art is in thoroughly examining whether the thought which the mind of the young man brings forth is a false idol or a noble and true birth.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Theaetetus, dialogue paragraph 143 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1726); complete clause excerpt

advice-0b6b5a046ef68271e8e28842.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0b6b5a046ef68271e8e28842.body:
(Philosophical dialogue as help in bringing forth thought) And therefore I am not myself at all wise, nor have I anything to show which is the invention or birth of my own soul, but those who converse with me profit.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Theaetetus, dialogue paragraph 143 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1726); complete clause excerpt

advice-e7ade11de7ebf259bc6d9034.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e7ade11de7ebf259bc6d9034.body:
(Truthfulness and the rejection of falsehood) It would be wrong for me to admit falsehood, or to stifle the truth.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Theaetetus, dialogue paragraph 143 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1726); complete clause excerpt

advice-f2e99370f588f95528a20a25.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f2e99370f588f95528a20a25.body:
(Wonder as the beginning of philosophy) Wonder is the feeling of a philosopher, and philosophy begins in wonder.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Theaetetus, dialogue paragraph 207 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1726); complete clause excerpt

advice-3390519304a474d10bee46b3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3390519304a474d10bee46b3.body:
(Self-knowledge before other people’s affairs) I must first know myself, as the Delphian inscription says; to be curious about that which is not my concern, while I am still in ignorance of my own self, would be ridiculous.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Phaedrus, dialogue paragraph 33 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1636); complete clause excerpt

advice-f0a567a068eddd5115186e14.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f0a567a068eddd5115186e14.body:
(The ability to listen and learn from others) The words of the wise are not to be set aside; for there is probably something in them.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Phaedrus, dialogue paragraph 159 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1636); complete clause excerpt

advice-290069a64baaa8091fbce473.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-290069a64baaa8091fbce473.body:
(Clearly defining concepts in speech) The speaker should define his several notions and so make his meaning clear.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Phaedrus, dialogue paragraph 261 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1636); complete clause excerpt

advice-d2778bdbb4ce569c1fc9a4a1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d2778bdbb4ce569c1fc9a4a1.body:
(Socrates’s prayer for inner beauty) Beloved Pan, and all ye other gods who haunt this place, give me beauty in the inward soul; and may the outward and inward man be at one. May I reckon the wise to be the wealthy, and may I have such a quantity of gold as a temperate man and he only can bear and carry.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Phaedrus, dialogue paragraph 407 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1636); complete clause excerpt

advice-de240b489e4437ee50e35d0d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-de240b489e4437ee50e35d0d.body:
(An examined life and the search for truth) The unexamined life is not worth living.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Apology, Stephanus 37–38, dialogue paragraph 69 (Jowett 1892); complete clause excerpt

advice-1435d3256152c2f4d8db82d2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1435d3256152c2f4d8db82d2.body:
(The moral responsibility of rulers) Now the worst part of the punishment is that he who refuses to rule is liable to be ruled by one who is worse than himself.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Republic, Book I, Stephanus 347B–347E, paragraph 318 (Jowett); complete clause excerpt

advice-bf9297323839cb3cc320d771.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bf9297323839cb3cc320d771.body:
(Early learning without compulsion) You know also that the beginning is the most important part of any work, especially in the case of a young and tender thing; for that is the time at which the character is being formed and the desired impression is more readily taken.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Republic, Book II, Stephanus 377A–377B, paragraph 235 (Jowett); complete clause excerpt

advice-8a8dfff2bb8b8d3472a69a16.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8a8dfff2bb8b8d3472a69a16.body:
(Early learning without compulsion) It would seem, Adeimantus, that the direction in which education starts a man, will determine his future life.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Republic, Book IV, Stephanus 425B–425C, paragraph 82 (Jowett); complete clause excerpt

advice-e15e1a201de81be12b7e6f9a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e15e1a201de81be12b7e6f9a.body:
(Early learning without compulsion) Knowledge which is acquired under compulsion obtains no hold on the mind.
Socrates

sources.author: Socrates
sources.reference: Republic, Book VII, Stephanus 536D–536E, paragraph 317 (Jowett); complete clause excerpt

advice-66ea8015b85728414977657a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-66ea8015b85728414977657a.body:
(Knowledge as nourishment for the soul) Surely, knowledge is the food of the soul.
Socrates

advice-5107750d9d44db46dcc5f447.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5107750d9d44db46dcc5f447.body:
(The risk of uncritically absorbing a sophist’s teaching) But you cannot buy the wares of knowledge and carry them away in another vessel; when you have paid for them you must receive them into the soul and go your way, either greatly harmed or greatly benefited; and therefore we should deliberate and take counsel with our elders; for we are still young—too young to determine such a matter.
Socrates

advice-d0f67b0a5173e1eb330560e7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d0f67b0a5173e1eb330560e7.body:
(Learning at any age) Even at your age, and with all your wisdom, if any one were to teach you what you did not know before, you would become better no doubt.
Socrates

advice-f57ce5f4c0ee34e20ac5893a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f57ce5f4c0ee34e20ac5893a.body:
(Philosophical dialogue as help in bringing forth thought) For discussion is one thing, and making an oration is quite another, in my humble opinion.
Socrates

advice-83dde4c2fb564d7f043ac555.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-83dde4c2fb564d7f043ac555.body:
(Philosophical dialogue as help in bringing forth thought) Leaving the poets, and keeping to ourselves, let us try the mettle of one another and make proof of the truth in conversation.
Socrates

advice-98e33d36c4639ba58734a43d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-98e33d36c4639ba58734a43d.body:
(Philosophical dialogue as help in bringing forth thought) Do not imagine, Protagoras, that I have any other interest in asking questions of you but that of clearing up my own difficulties.
Socrates

advice-cd4589d9e34ae898b6b10b68.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cd4589d9e34ae898b6b10b68.body:
(Wrongdoing through ignorance and the possibility of reform) Then, no man voluntarily pursues evil, or that which he thinks to be evil. To prefer evil to good is not in human nature; and when a man is compelled to choose one of two evils, no one will choose the greater when he may have the less.
Socrates

advice-7f51c839b72efdc813c02df4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7f51c839b72efdc813c02df4.body:
(Learning, experience, and wise guidance) I think that I ought certainly to hear first what my elders have to say, and to learn of them, and if I have anything to add, then I may venture to give my opinion to them as well as to you.
Socrates

advice-4e00d2aa58e9f9f1cc00d3ba.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4e00d2aa58e9f9f1cc00d3ba.body:
(Family and the upbringing of children) For children are your riches; and upon their turning out well or ill depends the whole order of their father's house.
Socrates

advice-f0580b6a09f2dfde1b7b768c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f0580b6a09f2dfde1b7b768c.body:
(Examining courage as a part of virtue) I would not have us begin, my friend, with enquiring about the whole of virtue; for that may be more than we can accomplish; let us first consider whether we have a sufficient knowledge of a part; the enquiry will thus probably be made easier to us.
Socrates

advice-2c202a7d52a33fe053df42ea.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2c202a7d52a33fe053df42ea.body:
(Examining courage as a part of virtue) Some have courage in pleasures, and some in pains: some in desires, and some in fears, and some are cowards under the same conditions, as I should imagine.
Socrates

advice-dc54a677b3093b7c37cb46f6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dc54a677b3093b7c37cb46f6.body:
(Examining courage as a part of virtue) And yet I cannot say that every kind of endurance is, in my opinion, to be deemed courage.
Socrates

advice-8c0e7b6b12459440bc67781c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8c0e7b6b12459440bc67781c.body:
(Persistence and care in philosophical inquiry) We too must endure and persevere in the enquiry, and then courage will not laugh at our faint-heartedness in searching for courage; which after all may, very likely, be endurance.
Socrates

advice-29f1a6dc2455b4e7016daebc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-29f1a6dc2455b4e7016daebc.body:
(Discussing Nicias’s definition of courage) Let us ask him just to explain what he means, and if he has reason on his side we will agree with him; if not, we will instruct him.
Socrates

advice-4c060d12a55883cb9e361d8a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4c060d12a55883cb9e361d8a.body:
(The nature and unity of virtue) For I say that justice, temperance, and the like, are all of them parts of virtue as well as courage.
Socrates

advice-01bf4bcc862ddb49a63b3272.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-01bf4bcc862ddb49a63b3272.body:
(Cultivating courage and overcoming fear) Fear is not of the present, nor of the past, but is of future and expected evil.
Socrates

advice-3c0594465832d17c7791343e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3c0594465832d17c7791343e.body:
(Learning, experience, and wise guidance) Indeed, Lysimachus, I should be very wrong in refusing to aid in the improvement of anybody.
Socrates

advice-a775d252f0b9b71ab06eae97.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a775d252f0b9b71ab06eae97.body:
(Learning, experience, and wise guidance) I maintain, my friends, that every one of us should seek out the best teacher whom he can find, first for ourselves, who are greatly in need of one, and then for the youth, regardless of expense or anything.
Socrates

advice-3476410e629c98858c3835ae.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3476410e629c98858c3835ae.body:
(Moderation, self-knowledge, and wisdom) Then once more, Charmides, fix your attention, and look within; consider the effect which temperance has upon yourself, and the nature of that which has the effect.
Socrates

advice-8640f716ad9ce44725ac084f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8640f716ad9ce44725ac084f.body:
(Clarifying the subject before discussion) Now I have no objection to your giving names any signification which you please, if you will only tell me what you mean by them.
Socrates

advice-b3d993fc20168d648da5d104.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b3d993fc20168d648da5d104.body:
(Philosophical dialogue as help in bringing forth thought) The fact is that I enquire with you into the truth of that which is advanced from time to time, just because I do not know; and when I have enquired, I will say whether I agree with you or not.
Socrates

advice-82db026f210d5d852fc5e8ed.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-82db026f210d5d852fc5e8ed.body:
(The value of refutation in seeking truth) Then, be cheerful, sweet sir, and give your opinion in answer to the question which I asked, never minding whether Critias or Socrates is the person refuted; attend only to the argument, and see what will come of the refutation.
Socrates

advice-6aeec4a9c87efaea7c5bcf0d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6aeec4a9c87efaea7c5bcf0d.body:
(Examining one’s own thought) I dare say that what I am saying is nonsense; and yet if a man has any feeling of what is due to himself, he cannot let the thought which comes into his mind pass away unheeded and unexamined.
Socrates

advice-a5e20d41baec1a292106ce48.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a5e20d41baec1a292106ce48.body:
(Moderation, self-knowledge, and wisdom) The more wise and temperate you are, the happier you will be.
Socrates

advice-80cd68f71f3887380a3fe8c1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-80cd68f71f3887380a3fe8c1.body:
(Explaining the prohibition on taking one’s own life) Do not lose heart, and the day may come when you will understand.
Socrates

advice-2eb74dca043ba7ecd7d89937.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2eb74dca043ba7ecd7d89937.body:
(Apparent courage from fear of a greater evil) Then all but the philosophers are courageous only from fear, and because they are afraid; and yet that a man should be courageous from fear, and because he is a coward, is surely a strange thing.
Socrates

advice-85fc560a5e5f19c0bb8cf76a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-85fc560a5e5f19c0bb8cf76a.body:
(True virtue and trading one passion for another) Yet the exchange of one fear or pleasure or pain for another fear or pleasure or pain, and of the greater for the less, as if they were coins, is not the exchange of virtue.
Socrates

advice-8b73d814ad3f4a045bc35b10.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8b73d814ad3f4a045bc35b10.body:
(Bodily feelings can distort the appearance of truth) The evil is that when the feeling of pleasure or pain is most intense, every soul of man imagines the objects of this intense feeling to be then plainest and truest: but this is not so.
Socrates

advice-e339e4140a6f339374b7e1d0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e339e4140a6f339374b7e1d0.body:
(Freeing the soul from the rule of bodily pleasures) The soul of a philosopher will reason in quite another way; she will not ask philosophy to release her in order that when released she may deliver herself up again to the thraldom of pleasures and pains, doing a work only to be undone again, weaving instead of unweaving her Penelope's web.
Socrates

advice-74492cf7dc69574a77010776.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-74492cf7dc69574a77010776.body:
(Examining arguments for the soul’s immortality) I dare say, my friend, that you may be right, but I should like to know in what respect the argument is insufficient.
Socrates

advice-c8472276888e4dc61b1cf3a2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c8472276888e4dc61b1cf3a2.body:
(Simmias and Cebes question the proof of the soul’s immortality) But perhaps, before we answer him, we had better also hear what Cebes has to say that we may gain time for reflection, and when they have both spoken, we may either assent to them, if there is truth in what they say, or if not, we will maintain our position.
Socrates

advice-de6e21abf0d6a601e4109d3b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-de6e21abf0d6a601e4109d3b.body:
(Distrust of arguments after disappointment with them) For as there are misanthropists or haters of men, there are also misologists or haters of ideas, and both spring from the same cause, which is ignorance of the world.
Socrates

advice-6ac919a13a41083b5be105a8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6ac919a13a41083b5be105a8.body:
(Distrust of arguments after disappointment with them) Let us then, in the first place, be careful of allowing or of admitting into our souls the notion that there is no health or soundness in any arguments at all.
Socrates

advice-0b781d9da3cfbaad421448df.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0b781d9da3cfbaad421448df.body:
(An apparent victory in debate without establishing truth) Now the partisan, when he is engaged in a dispute, cares nothing about the rights of the question, but is anxious only to convince his hearers of his own assertions.
Socrates

advice-b452623330444db5c1fdbad6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b452623330444db5c1fdbad6.body:
(The value of refutation in seeking truth) And I would ask you to be thinking of the truth and not of Socrates: agree with me, if I seem to you to be speaking the truth; or if not, withstand me might and main, that I may not deceive you as well as myself in my enthusiasm, and like the bee, leave my sting in you before I die.
Socrates

advice-933ad965fcf6df32b9ae8037.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-933ad965fcf6df32b9ae8037.body:
(Examining arguments for the soul’s immortality) I may add that first principles, even if they appear certain, should be carefully considered; and when they are satisfactorily ascertained, then, with a sort of hesitating confidence in human reason, you may, I think, follow the course of the argument; and if that be plain and clear, there will be no need for any further enquiry.
Socrates

advice-33de927855f4115416be933a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-33de927855f4115416be933a.body:
(Burial of the body: Socrates distinguishes himself from his remains) For false words are not only evil in themselves, but they infect the soul with evil.
Socrates

advice-8f313e0a15e49bddf8236124.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8f313e0a15e49bddf8236124.body:
The soul seeks to turn away from evil and find the highest good. Once we find that good, we should remain faithful to it for the rest of our lives.
Plato

advice-9372cc742bee9a0130d612a6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9372cc742bee9a0130d612a6.body:
(Reason, wisdom, and mere learning) But without reason there never has been, or is, or will be a wise and understanding soul; it is of a different nature.
Plato

advice-367898a2e058d46159123844.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-367898a2e058d46159123844.body:
(Wealth, poverty, and moderate desires) And in this case also the war is against two enemies—wealth and poverty; one of whom corrupts the soul of man with luxury, while the other drives him by pain into utter shamelessness.
Plato

advice-d514a6d75c77c57160f33802.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d514a6d75c77c57160f33802.body:
(Youth without flattery or deprivation) The condition of youth which is free from flattery, and at the same time not in need of the necessaries of life, is the best and most harmonious of all, being in accord and agreement with our nature, and making life to be most entirely free from sorrow.
Plato

advice-7b003d603660801360bd8063.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7b003d603660801360bd8063.body:
(Training the body and the soul) And we may say that the use of exercise and motion in the earliest years of life greatly contributes to create a part of virtue in the soul.
Plato

advice-670ec1563cec86a8b59aba05.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-670ec1563cec86a8b59aba05.body:
(Training the body and the soul) For there ought to be no bye-work interfering with the greater work of providing the necessary exercise and nourishment for the body, and instruction and education for the soul.
Plato

advice-df3c2c1245abc921756a3dd6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-df3c2c1245abc921756a3dd6.body:
(Peace and civic concord) But war, whether external or civil, is not the best, and the need of either is to be deprecated; but peace with one another, and good will, are best.
Plato

advice-d5250ab2c0766c6d5c4cac53.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d5250ab2c0766c6d5c4cac53.body:
(The moral education of children’s feelings) Pleasure and pain I maintain to be the first perceptions of children, and I say that they are the forms under which virtue and vice are originally present to them.
Plato

advice-940c1e025fac20f6142b5449.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-940c1e025fac20f6142b5449.body:
(Wealth, wisdom, and virtue) Our statement, then, is true, that the very rich are not good, and, if they are not good, they are not happy.
Plato

advice-52b315f4fc72ec8fe081e5b5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-52b315f4fc72ec8fe081e5b5.body:
(Self-love that distorts judgment) Wherefore let every man avoid excess of self-love, and condescend to follow a better man than himself, not allowing any false shame to stand in the way.
Plato

advice-b9b2f8018c08a276e4c4f708.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b9b2f8018c08a276e4c4f708.body:
(Training the body and the soul) Education has two branches—one of gymnastic, which is concerned with the body, and the other of music, which is designed for the improvement of the soul.
Plato

advice-dca74198c1511ae36af6287f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dca74198c1511ae36af6287f.body:
(Care of the soul and the order of goods) And the right way is to place the goods of the soul first and highest in the scale, always assuming temperance to be the condition of them; and to assign the second place to the goods of the body; and the third place to money and property.
Plato

advice-967c0f226c0acfa7535e6e23.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-967c0f226c0acfa7535e6e23.body:
(Clarifying the subject before discussion) All those who are ready at a moment's notice to praise or censure any practice which is matter of discussion, seem to me to proceed in a wrong way.
Plato

advice-4bb444512c11288768340124.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4bb444512c11288768340124.body:
(Proportionate distribution of civic honors) For to unequals equals become unequal, if they are not harmonised by measure; and both by reason of equality, and by reason of inequality, cities are filled with seditions.
Plato

advice-de4153c1421907cb29e25384.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-de4153c1421907cb29e25384.body:
(Truth as a standard for artistic imitation) Then, if such be our principles, we must assert that imitation is not to be judged of by pleasure and false opinion; and this is true of all equality, for the equal is not equal or the symmetrical symmetrical, because somebody thinks or likes something, but they are to be judged of by the standard of truth, and by no other whatever.
Plato

advice-249c49187a3f48bff5f221f1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-249c49187a3f48bff5f221f1.body:
(Wealth, wisdom, and virtue) But if, in any of the laws which have been ordained, health has been preferred to temperance, or wealth to health and temperate habits, that law must clearly be wrong.
Plato

advice-f497e5dc239c05072664b949.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f497e5dc239c05072664b949.body:
(Anger, mockery, and quarrels) And in such cases almost all men take to saying something ridiculous about their opponent, and there is no man who is in the habit of laughing at another who does not miss virtue and earnestness altogether, or lose the better half of greatness.
Plato

advice-e58c9989f83c05ef9d868582.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e58c9989f83c05ef9d868582.body:
(The part in relation to the good of the whole) For every physician and every skilled artist does all things for the sake of the whole, directing his effort towards the common good, executing the part for the sake of the whole, and not the whole for the sake of the part.
Plato

advice-9a6be4a10c18b230dbc58edf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9a6be4a10c18b230dbc58edf.body:
(Educating a virtuous citizen) For we are not speaking of education in this narrower sense, but of that other education in virtue from youth upwards, which makes a man eagerly pursue the ideal perfection of citizenship, and teaches him how rightly to rule and how to obey.
Plato

advice-613aee75f994b7b72d7ddaa4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-613aee75f994b7b72d7ddaa4.body:
(Moderation as a basis for public honor) For no man ought to have pre-eminent honour in a state because he surpasses others in wealth, any more than because he is swift of foot or fair or strong, unless he have some virtue in him; nor even if he have virtue, unless he have this particular virtue of temperance.
Plato

advice-8d7811ec0ee0f519f73ee7dc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8d7811ec0ee0f519f73ee7dc.body:
(Wrongdoing through ignorance and the possibility of reform) As to the actions of those who do evil, but whose evil is curable, in the first place, let us remember that the unjust man is not unjust of his own free will.
Plato

advice-ccff6b8bf32c28c40d7da717.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ccff6b8bf32c28c40d7da717.body:
(The education of future guardians of the state) Furthermore, to write down the times at which, and during which, they ought to receive the several kinds of instruction, would be a vain thing; for the learners themselves do not know what is learned to advantage until the knowledge which is the result of learning has found a place in the soul of each.
Plato

advice-8d06f14f4df0d76d75691ecb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8d06f14f4df0d76d75691ecb.body:
(The moral education of children’s feelings) Now I mean by education that training which is given by suitable habits to the first instincts of virtue in children;—when pleasure, and friendship, and pain, and hatred, are rightly implanted in souls not yet capable of understanding the nature of them, and who find them, after they have attained reason, to be in harmony with her.
Plato

advice-d7dfebb9fb2b09062a1be70a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d7dfebb9fb2b09062a1be70a.body:
(Moderation in desires and pleasures) For, in the first place, moderation is the appointment of nature, and deters men from all frenzy and madness of love, and from all adulteries and immoderate use of meats and drinks, and makes them good friends to their own wives.
Plato

advice-c0d5872312e3980d211e244e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c0d5872312e3980d211e244e.body:
(Pleasure in a virtuous life) And so the one class of lives exceeds the other class in pleasure; the temperate and courageous and wise and healthy exceed the cowardly and foolish and intemperate and diseased lives; and generally speaking, that which has any virtue, whether of body or soul, is pleasanter than the vicious life, and far superior in beauty and rectitude and excellence and reputation, and causes him who lives accordingly to be infinitely happier than the opposite.
Plato

advice-e33f5d287dfb6d4c62202ab9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e33f5d287dfb6d4c62202ab9.body:
(Cultivating courage and overcoming fear) But if fear has such a power we ought to infer from these facts, that every soul which from youth upward has been familiar with fears, will be made more liable to fear (compare Republic), and every one will allow that this is the way to form a habit of cowardice and not of courage.
Plato

advice-ed452cfa0f6bbe91079e7d55.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ed452cfa0f6bbe91079e7d55.body:
(External goods and knowing how to use them) For I plainly declare that evils as they are termed are goods to the unjust, and only evils to the just, and that goods are truly good to the good, but evil to the evil.
Plato

advice-045c2c3e6e3462b07348668b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-045c2c3e6e3462b07348668b.body:
(The divine and human virtue) Injustice and insolence and folly are the destruction of us, and justice and temperance and wisdom are our salvation; and the place of these latter is in the life of the Gods, although some vestige of them may occasionally be discerned among mankind.
Plato

advice-4d1542c41770fa6dace1df68.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4d1542c41770fa6dace1df68.body:
(Music and the education of taste) But the pleasure must not be that of chance persons; the fairest music is that which delights the best and best educated, and especially that which delights the one man who is pre-eminent in virtue and education.
Plato

advice-6deee6be20ac273937222eca.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6deee6be20ac273937222eca.body:
(Anger, mockery, and quarrels) For the speaker gratifies his anger, which is an ungracious element of his nature; and nursing up his wrath by the entertainment of evil thoughts, and exacerbating that part of his soul which was formerly civilised by education, he lives in a state of savageness and moroseness, and pays a bitter penalty for his anger.
Plato

advice-a8cd89cbce3faa5401dbbf84.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a8cd89cbce3faa5401dbbf84.body:
(The relation between pleasure and pain) And each one of us has in his bosom two counsellors, both foolish and also antagonistic; of which we call the one pleasure, and the other pain.
Plato

advice-997db3e4adc926669e057d9e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-997db3e4adc926669e057d9e.body:
(Foresight before trouble occurs) Truly there is no great wisdom in knowing, and no great difficulty in telling, after the evil has happened; but to have foreseen the remedy at the time would have taken a much wiser head than ours.
Plato

advice-8e71c0a9faa19e40f0aaa528.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8e71c0a9faa19e40f0aaa528.body:
(Family and the upbringing of children) The best way of training the young is to train yourself at the same time; not to admonish them, but to be always carrying out your own admonitions in practice.
Plato

advice-73f424861a6e98f741ee8c20.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-73f424861a6e98f741ee8c20.body:
(Hospitality and the treatment of strangers) And for this reason, he who has a spark of caution in him, will do his best to pass through life without sinning against the stranger.
Plato

advice-ed9b2e1a713f76454653e7e2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ed9b2e1a713f76454653e7e2.body:
(The need for laws in shared life) And the reason of this is that no man's nature is able to know what is best for human society; or knowing, always able and willing to do what is best.
Plato

advice-39cf069820f02b7d817d0df9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-39cf069820f02b7d817d0df9.body:
(Shame, conscience, and self-respect) And there is the fear of an evil reputation; we are afraid of being thought evil, because we do or say some dishonourable thing, which fear we and all men term shame.
Plato

advice-b9a5328b404b4dc812874930.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b9a5328b404b4dc812874930.body:
(Desires as a basis of character) For every one of us is made pretty much what he is by the bent of his desires and the nature of his soul.
Plato

advice-1c3884429c5fd947f2cb5ae5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1c3884429c5fd947f2cb5ae5.body:
(Early learning without compulsion) The soul of the child in his play should be guided to the love of that sort of excellence in which when he grows up to manhood he will have to be perfected.
Plato

advice-ddec2c06631fe80d458316e3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ddec2c06631fe80d458316e3.body:
(Knowledge and true opinion) As to wisdom and true and fixed opinions, happy is the man who acquires them, even when declining in years; and we may say that he who possesses them, and the blessings which are contained in them, is a perfect man.
Plato

advice-036ffb610f37fd9249dbdd67.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-036ffb610f37fd9249dbdd67.body:
(Peace and civic concord) And therefore, as we say, every one of us should live the life of peace as long and as well as he can.
Plato

advice-4baed9845600f4635695fe87.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4baed9845600f4635695fe87.body:
(Wealth, wisdom, and virtue) On the other hand, the utterly bad is in general profligate, and therefore very poor; while he who spends on noble objects, and acquires wealth by just means only, can hardly be remarkable for riches, any more than he can be very poor.
Plato

advice-70cf70648ecaa6c6360003f0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-70cf70648ecaa6c6360003f0.body:
(Truthfulness and the rejection of falsehood) Truth is the beginning of every good thing, both to Gods and men; and he who would be blessed and happy, should be from the first a partaker of the truth, that he may live a true man as long as possible, for then he can be trusted; but he is not to be trusted who loves voluntary falsehood, and he who loves involuntary falsehood is a fool.
Plato

advice-a783c30418e1254be6f8782e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a783c30418e1254be6f8782e.body:
(A calm conversation with a young person who denies the gods) Our address to these lost and perverted natures should not be spoken in passion; let us suppose ourselves to select some one of them, and gently reason with him, smothering our anger: O my son, we will say to him, you are young, and the advance of time will make you reverse many of the opinions which you now hold.
Plato

advice-93c562ab43c7ee23e8e1d91b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-93c562ab43c7ee23e8e1d91b.body:
(Intellectual ability without moral education) For entire ignorance is not so terrible or extreme an evil, and is far from being the greatest of all; too much cleverness and too much learning, accompanied with an ill bringing up, are far more fatal.
Plato

advice-f47de5fc4628cb395929d8a6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f47de5fc4628cb395929d8a6.body:
(Striving for virtue without envy) Let every man, then, freely strive for the prize of virtue, and let there be no envy.
Plato

advice-0aca5d8c1e0867fa1f3b2367.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0aca5d8c1e0867fa1f3b2367.body:
(Inner harmony and consistency) Concerning all things honourable and just, let us then endeavour to ascertain how far we are consistent with ourselves, and how far we are inconsistent, and how far the many, from whom at any rate we should profess a desire to differ, agree and disagree among themselves.
Plato

advice-962643d26688aabbc7ed1f48.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-962643d26688aabbc7ed1f48.body:
(Courage in battle and fear of dishonor) For there are two things which give victory—confidence before enemies, and fear of disgrace before friends.
Plato

advice-0c38bcc89478c92ecfa5f175.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0c38bcc89478c92ecfa5f175.body:
(Reason and the senses as supports of life) The soul, besides other things, contains mind, and the head, besides other things, contains sight and hearing; and the mind, mingling with the noblest of the senses, and becoming one with them, may be truly called the salvation of all.
Plato

advice-0aaab23e2dc413bcc9927d36.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0aaab23e2dc413bcc9927d36.body:
(Inquiry into the nature of the cosmos) Men say that we ought not to enquire into the supreme God and the nature of the universe, nor busy ourselves in searching out the causes of things, and that such enquiries are impious; whereas the very opposite is the truth.
Plato

advice-a4df65b0d7d83f4b1dbec5bd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a4df65b0d7d83f4b1dbec5bd.body:
(Moderation in desires and pleasures) When opinion by the help of reason leads us to the best, the conquering principle is called temperance; but when desire, which is devoid of reason, rules in us and drags us to pleasure, that power of misrule is called excess.
Plato

advice-aaa1dd344d1aa0a2fd264c7f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-aaa1dd344d1aa0a2fd264c7f.body:
(True friendship and how it is tested) For fate which has ordained that there shall be no friendship among the evil has also ordained that there shall ever be friendship among the good.
Plato

advice-88a27ca7f0e8325b823b3aee.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-88a27ca7f0e8325b823b3aee.body:
(Love, desires, and character) Every one chooses his love from the ranks of beauty according to his character, and this he makes his god, and fashions and adorns as a sort of image which he is to fall down and worship.
Plato

advice-4d8f70f5d5cb65921df18fa0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4d8f70f5d5cb65921df18fa0.body:
(Philosophical dialogue as help in bringing forth thought) But nobler far is the serious pursuit of the dialectician, who, finding a congenial soul, by the help of science sows and plants therein words which are able to help themselves and him who planted them, and are not unfruitful, but have in them a seed which others brought up in different soils render immortal, making the possessors of it happy to the utmost extent of human happiness.
Plato

advice-aedb651fbac2cab87e40e8af.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-aedb651fbac2cab87e40e8af.body:
(Living beings’ desire for the good) And no one can deny that all percipient beings desire and hunt after good, and are eager to catch and have the good about them, and care not for the attainment of anything which is not accompanied by good.
Plato

advice-5cbc146466027461679ac5a7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5cbc146466027461679ac5a7.body:
(The distinction between good and pleasure) Philebus was saying that enjoyment and pleasure and delight, and the class of feelings akin to them, are a good to every living being, whereas I contend, that not these, but wisdom and intelligence and memory, and their kindred, right opinion and true reasoning, are better and more desirable than pleasure for all who are able to partake of them, and that to all such who are or ever will be they are the most advantageous of all things.
Plato

advice-26184e0f27531903e1b1c605.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-26184e0f27531903e1b1c605.body:
(The relation between pleasure and pain) And the argument implies that there are combinations of pleasure and pain in lamentations, and in tragedy and comedy, not only on the stage, but on the greater stage of human life; and so in endless other cases.
Plato

advice-49c7f5cd34ff66960c731991.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-49c7f5cd34ff66960c731991.body:
(Beauty as measure and proportion) And now the power of the good has retired into the region of the beautiful; for measure and symmetry are beauty and virtue all the world over.
Plato

advice-2c3e1ed579c6dde8335ced77.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2c3e1ed579c6dde8335ced77.body:
(A good life combining knowledge and pleasure) Unless truth enter into the composition, nothing can truly be created or subsist.
Plato

advice-ae06339a2818d61e814367d9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ae06339a2818d61e814367d9.body:
(Analysis of the soul’s nature in the art of speaking) The method which proceeds without analysis is like the groping of a blind man.
Plato

advice-d76f585bffeb34de0108fc3d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d76f585bffeb34de0108fc3d.body:
(Striving for the true art of speaking) All the great arts require discussion and high speculation about the truths of nature; hence come loftiness of thought and completeness of execution.
Plato

advice-1fce4aaaebd6ed35a7df61a3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1fce4aaaebd6ed35a7df61a3.body:
(Thinking as an inner dialogue) I speak of what I scarcely understand; but the soul when thinking appears to me to be just talking—asking questions of herself and answering them, affirming and denying.
Plato

advice-9e306a2467394282017c744b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9e306a2467394282017c744b.body:
(The beauty of invisible wisdom) For sight is the most piercing of our bodily senses; though not by that is wisdom seen; her loveliness would have been transporting if there had been a visible image of her, and the other ideas, if they had visible counterparts, would be equally lovely.
Plato

advice-05eb4f180bc5577ffd15ec0d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-05eb4f180bc5577ffd15ec0d.body:
(The mixture of amusement and envy when watching comedy) And the greater the obscurity of the case the more desirable is the examination of it, because the difficulty in detecting other cases of mixed pleasures and pains will be less.
Plato

advice-362083132bc96d8e5f3d334e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-362083132bc96d8e5f3d334e.body:
(Wealth, poverty, and moderate desires) Dear Cleinias, the class of men is small—they must have been rarely gifted by nature, and trained by education—who, when assailed by wants and desires, are able to hold out and observe moderation, and when they might make a great deal of money are sober in their wishes, and prefer a moderate to a large gain.
Plato

advice-bc33c794ee908cd0973550f6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bc33c794ee908cd0973550f6.body:
(Careful consideration of a legal dispute) The point in dispute between the parties should be made clear; and time, and deliberation, and repeated examination, greatly tend to clear up doubts.
Plato

advice-a8a148b30af5f3a594b9162c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a8a148b30af5f3a594b9162c.body:
(A discussion partner’s right to disagree) But if you do not agree with me, there is no reason why you should not argue on the other side.
Plato

advice-5aa5689512f17eb43a412457.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5aa5689512f17eb43a412457.body:
(True friendship and how it is tested) Dear is the like in virtue to the like, and the equal to the equal; dear also, though unlike, is he who has abundance to him who is in want.
Plato

advice-0f1f6d0f7951cebe188d6966.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0f1f6d0f7951cebe188d6966.body:
(Educating a virtuous citizen) Neither must we cast a slight upon education, which is the first and fairest thing that the best of men can ever have, and which, though liable to take a wrong direction, is capable of reformation.
Plato

advice-577540a0c1f514c75b44fe86.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-577540a0c1f514c75b44fe86.body:
(Deliberating on laws concerning music) Then we will allow time for reflection, and decide when we have given the subject sufficient consideration.
Plato

advice-ac0732d220dbec4938e0e169.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ac0732d220dbec4938e0e169.body:
(Shaping a life in accordance with the soul’s character) As the shipwright first lays down the lines of the keel, and thus, as it were, draws the ship in outline, so do I seek to distinguish the patterns of life, and lay down their keels according to the nature of different men's souls; seeking truly to consider by what means, and in what ways, we may go through the voyage of life best.
Plato

advice-2e8a469d80830b4ed0cf6b55.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2e8a469d80830b4ed0cf6b55.body:
(Effort and willingness to become better) For there is no great inclination or readiness on the part of mankind to be made as good, or as quickly good, as possible.
Plato

advice-b9945a147bd7e9229088850e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b9945a147bd7e9229088850e.body:
(Music and the education of taste) And the sound of the voice which reaches and educates the soul, we have ventured to term music.
Plato

advice-8693affef192fb00d9605811.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8693affef192fb00d9605811.body:
(Testing character in the safer setting of a banquet) I might mention numberless cases, in which the advantage would be manifest of getting to know a character in sport, and without paying dearly for experience.
Plato

advice-15b4d14f10a4c7ff8de36b19.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-15b4d14f10a4c7ff8de36b19.body:
(Greed and the pursuit of wealth) But from an insatiable love of gold and silver, every man will stoop to any art or contrivance, seemly or unseemly, in the hope of becoming rich; and will make no objection to performing any action, holy, or unholy and utterly base; if only like a beast he have the power of eating and drinking all kinds of things, and procuring for himself in every sort of way the gratification of his lusts.
Plato

advice-af9824a68c0783ae8d1a12d9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-af9824a68c0783ae8d1a12d9.body:
(The rule of passions over the soul) When anger and fear, and pleasure and pain, and jealousies and desires, tyrannize over the soul, whether they do any harm or not—I call all this injustice.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book IX, paragraph 83 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-fdd8e36ebc602131a0329da2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fdd8e36ebc602131a0329da2.body:
(Reasoned persuasion instead of compulsion) Reason is beautiful and gentle, and not violent.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book I, paragraph 177 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-3428da62ee0091bd13a1189e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3428da62ee0091bd13a1189e.body:
(Cultivating courage and overcoming fear) The habit of courage and fearlessness is to be trained amid fears.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book I, paragraph 248 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-4a8341cc6245204b69d0956f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4a8341cc6245204b69d0956f.body:
(The relation between pleasure and pain) Pleasure cannot be rightly tested apart from pain.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Philebus, dialogue paragraph 332 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1744); complete clause excerpt

advice-bc7249c74a2acc9f2b86b280.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bc7249c74a2acc9f2b86b280.body:
(The relation between pleasure and pain) The negation of pain will not be the same with pleasure.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Philebus, dialogue paragraph 674 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1744); complete clause excerpt

advice-ef879cd347a9cef758635f41.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ef879cd347a9cef758635f41.body:
(A single moral aim for law and education) The beginning of virtue is not to make mistakes by guessing many things, but to look steadily at one thing, and on this to fix all our aims.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book XII, paragraph 54 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-1c46f5db484db37aa959bb21.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1c46f5db484db37aa959bb21.body:
(Practice, effort, and perseverance) Any one who would be good at anything must practise that thing from his youth upwards, both in sport and earnest, in its several branches.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book I, paragraph 162 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-bd3bfd47aa6139002a83fec8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bd3bfd47aa6139002a83fec8.body:
(Care of the soul and the order of goods) Of all the things which a man has, next to the Gods, his soul is the most divine and most truly his own.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 1 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-1d0f921c1807de401e693118.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1d0f921c1807de401e693118.body:
(Responsibility for one’s own mistakes) Again, when a man thinks that others are to be blamed, and not himself, for the errors which he has committed from time to time, and the many and great evils which befell him in consequence, and is always fancying himself to be exempt and innocent, he is under the idea that he is honouring his soul; whereas the very reverse is the fact, for he is really injuring her.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 1 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-254cb127fdca29de22704cbe.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-254cb127fdca29de22704cbe.body:
(Wealth, wisdom, and virtue) All the gold which is under or upon the earth is not enough to give in exchange for virtue.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 1 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-344dab4166ee72b417abecf9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-344dab4166ee72b417abecf9.body:
(Following a better moral example) Speaking generally, our glory is to follow the better and improve the inferior, which is susceptible of improvement, as far as this is possible.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 2 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-d7d1245067a39c0992007f73.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d7d1245067a39c0992007f73.body:
(Family and the upbringing of children) Let parents, then, bequeath to their children not a heap of riches, but the spirit of reverence.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 2 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-beeb13be7edbce6cec595de6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-beeb13be7edbce6cec595de6.body:
(Giving, help, and gratitude) And he who deems the services which his friends and acquaintances do for him, greater and more important than they themselves deem them, and his own favours to them less than theirs to him, will have their good-will in the intercourse of life.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 2 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-cbad582ab91e3a41e571989f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cbad582ab91e3a41e571989f.body:
(Justice and moral conduct) Worthy of honour is he who does no injustice, and of more than twofold honour, if he not only does no injustice himself, but hinders others from doing any.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 4 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-b1818d846dc34da530b144e0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b1818d846dc34da530b144e0.body:
(Striving for virtue without envy) The envious, who thinks that he ought to get the better by defaming others, is less energetic himself in the pursuit of true virtue, and reduces his rivals to despair by his unjust slanders of them.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 4 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-242c723ef413712498a00da3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-242c723ef413712498a00da3.body:
(Combining courage and gentleness) Now every man should be valiant, but he should also be gentle.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 4 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-4aa1e11333bca069814d466c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4aa1e11333bca069814d466c.body:
(Wrongdoing through ignorance and the possibility of reform) The unrighteous and vicious are always to be pitied in any case; and one can afford to forgive as well as pity him who is curable, and refrain and calm one's anger.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 4 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-816b1194a1ea24e3e19b07da.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-816b1194a1ea24e3e19b07da.body:
(Self-love that distorts judgment) Whereas the excessive love of self is in reality the source to each man of all offences; for the lover is blinded about the beloved, so that he judges wrongly of the just, the good, and the honourable, and thinks that he ought always to prefer himself to the truth.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 5 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-301ac43c08cdf1dd46bdc9bf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-301ac43c08cdf1dd46bdc9bf.body:
(Justice and moral conduct) But he who would be a great man ought to regard, not himself or his interests, but what is just, whether the just act be his own or that of another.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 5 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-0812cfc7bb5898230f049a2f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0812cfc7bb5898230f049a2f.body:
(Self-love that distorts judgment) Through a similar error men are induced to fancy that their own ignorance is wisdom, and thus we who may be truly said to know nothing, think that we know all things; and because we will not let others act for us in what we do not know, we are compelled to act amiss ourselves.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 5 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-4c4f2f5c7af5cf1f3cc82a87.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4c4f2f5c7af5cf1f3cc82a87.body:
(Repeating moral precepts to counter forgetting) For when a stream is flowing out, there should be water flowing in too; and recollection flows in while wisdom is departing.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 5 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-590b0442f849e0e553c86f12.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-590b0442f849e0e553c86f12.body:
(The relation between pleasure and pain) Pleasures and pains and desires are a part of human nature, and on them every mortal being must of necessity hang and depend with the most eager interest.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Laws, Book V, paragraph 6 (Jowett / Gutenberg #1750); complete clause excerpt

advice-0d3b5a64f6b80791342c256b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0d3b5a64f6b80791342c256b.body:
(A written text cannot answer a question) I cannot help feeling, Phaedrus, that writing is unfortunately like painting; for the creations of the painter have the attitude of life, and yet if you ask them a question they preserve a solemn silence.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Phaedrus, dialogue paragraph 363 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1636); complete clause excerpt

advice-70d4fcd85afa69b0ab0d5b8c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-70d4fcd85afa69b0ab0d5b8c.body:
(Divine ecstasy and inspiration) There is also a madness which is a divine gift, and the source of the chiefest blessings granted to men.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Phaedrus, dialogue paragraph 111 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1636); complete clause excerpt

advice-0a5d4321b393f47a6d552942.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0a5d4321b393f47a6d552942.body:
(Divine ecstasy and inspiration) But he who, having no touch of the Muses' madness in his soul, comes to the door and thinks that he will get into the temple by the help of art—he, I say, and his poetry are not admitted; the sane man disappears and is nowhere when he enters into rivalry with the madman.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Phaedrus, dialogue paragraph 112 (Jowett; Gutenberg #1636); complete clause excerpt

advice-88ec88480195ae71c20c5eb0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-88ec88480195ae71c20c5eb0.body:
(The soul’s capacity to learn) The power and capacity of learning exists in the soul already.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Republic, Book VII, Stephanus 518C–518D, paragraph 48 (Jowett); complete clause excerpt

advice-a06416b0d37e04443155bee7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a06416b0d37e04443155bee7.body:
(Parts of the soul: reason, spiritedness, and desire) The just man does not permit the several elements within him to interfere with one another, or any of them to do the work of others,—he sets in order his own inner life, and is his own master and his own law, and at peace with himself.
Plato

sources.author: Plato
sources.reference: Republic, Book IV, Stephanus 443C–444A, paragraph 421 (Jowett); complete clause excerpt

advice-53260d1dae101ae093f20cb0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-53260d1dae101ae093f20cb0.body:
Listen to the common order of the world rather than to my authority, and you will understand that all things form one whole.
Heraclitus

advice-fded002a118ce8733824b13d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fded002a118ce8733824b13d.body:
(Logos: the shared rational order of the world) Though this Word is true evermore, yet men are as unable to understand it when they hear it for the first time as before they have heard it at all. For, though all things come to pass in accordance with this Word, men seem as if they had no experience of them, when they make trial of words and deeds such as I set forth, dividing each thing according to its nature and showing how it truly is. But other men know not what they are doing when awake, even as they forget what they do in sleep.
Heraclitus

advice-354591d9209fcd41197c43e4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-354591d9209fcd41197c43e4.body:
(Hearing words does not yet mean understanding them) Fools when they do hear are like the deaf: of them does the saying bear witness that they are absent when present.
Heraclitus

advice-696aa099df94e7dfc3f6d0b5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-696aa099df94e7dfc3f6d0b5.body:
(Making sense of sensory evidence requires a soul capable of understanding) Eyes and ears are bad witnesses to men if they have souls that understand not their language.
Heraclitus

advice-a8de167af0e332352d062b07.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a8de167af0e332352d062b07.body:
(Hearing words does not yet mean understanding them) The many do not take heed of such things as those they meet with, nor do they mark them when they are taught, though they think they do.
Heraclitus

advice-127f4327a83406dc19dcdc04.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-127f4327a83406dc19dcdc04.body:
(Being ready to seek the unexpected) If you do not expect the unexpected, you will not find it; for it is hard to be sought out and difficult.
Heraclitus

advice-f84f8bfff3d8b9769528deb2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f84f8bfff3d8b9769528deb2.body:
