(Seeking truth pictured as mining for gold) Those who seek for gold dig up much earth and find a little.
Heraclitus

advice-d2ecc9597cec0ad252ae2e4c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d2ecc9597cec0ad252ae2e4c.body:
(Nature’s hiddenness and the difficulty of understanding) Nature loves to hide.
Heraclitus

advice-ab0e6b7d6fa8c0fd2f001d04.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ab0e6b7d6fa8c0fd2f001d04.body:
(Apollo gives signs through the Delphic oracle) The lord whose is the oracle at Delphoi neither utters nor hides his meaning, but shows it by a sign.
Heraclitus

advice-44e7d151a417b109b9bed7bf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-44e7d151a417b109b9bed7bf.body:
(The Sibyl: a prophetess whose voice is considered divinely inspired) And the Sibyl, with raving lips uttering things mirthless, unbedizened, and unperfumed, reaches over a thousand years with her voice, thanks to the god in her.
Heraclitus

advice-e21e1e1d3744e822fb8b2ade.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e21e1e1d3744e822fb8b2ade.body:
(The value of direct experience for knowledge) The things that can be seen, heard, and learned are what I prize the most.
Heraclitus

advice-01d1faffbbbb081e4bf25a98.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-01d1faffbbbb081e4bf25a98.body:
(The value of direct experience for knowledge) The eyes are more exact witnesses than the ears.
Heraclitus

advice-1695c955e4215099b110cb79.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1695c955e4215099b110cb79.body:
(Extensive learning alone does not bring understanding) The learning of many things teacheth not understanding, else would it have taught Hesiod and Pythagoras, and again Xenophanes and Hekataios.
Heraclitus

advice-96e301c8f146ddf95fde723c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-96e301c8f146ddf95fde723c.body:
(Extensive learning alone does not bring understanding) Pythagoras, son of Mnesarchos, practised inquiry beyond all other men, and choosing out these writings, claimed for his own wisdom what was but a knowledge of many things and an art of mischief.
Heraclitus

advice-58385ebad4f06d5c52753606.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-58385ebad4f06d5c52753606.body:
(Wisdom as something distinct from everything else) Of all whose discourses I have heard, there is not one who attains to understanding that wisdom is apart from all.
Heraclitus

advice-68dee490fee299fde1a0bd71.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-68dee490fee299fde1a0bd71.body:
(Wisdom as understanding the unified order of things) Wisdom is one thing. It is to know the thought by which all things are steered through all things.
Heraclitus

advice-4aaee587519d37f48240596c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4aaee587519d37f48240596c.body:
(The cosmic fire and transformations according to due measure) This world, which is the same for all, no one of gods or men has made; but it was ever, is now, and ever shall be an ever-living Fire, with measures kindling, and measures going out.
Heraclitus

advice-a69bf13182679f8415fa6e36.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a69bf13182679f8415fa6e36.body:
(The cosmic fire and transformations according to due measure) All things are an exchange for Fire, and Fire for all things, even as wares for gold and gold for wares.
Heraclitus

advice-75f2f41899932b7de1cb2dce.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-75f2f41899932b7de1cb2dce.body:
(The cosmic fire and transformations according to due measure) Fire is want and surfeit.
Heraclitus

advice-a18620dcada744aa67d6a995.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a18620dcada744aa67d6a995.body:
(One element’s life as another element’s transformation) Fire lives the death of air, and air lives the death of fire; water lives the death of earth, earth that of water.
Heraclitus

advice-8ee96863fcaa18a902fff4c9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8ee96863fcaa18a902fff4c9.body:
(Fire as the cosmic judge in Heraclitus’s cosmology) Fire in its advance will judge and convict all things.
Heraclitus

advice-044d3f19e3950f0b5c297324.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-044d3f19e3950f0b5c297324.body:
(The eternal cosmic principle pictured as what never sets) How can one hide from that which never sets?
Heraclitus

advice-0539436860b789c260505cc0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0539436860b789c260505cc0.body:
(The thunderbolt as an image of world-governing fire) It is the thunderbolt that steers the course of all things.
Heraclitus

advice-b81a54ed08494a09811a75a7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b81a54ed08494a09811a75a7.body:
(The Erinyes: mythical guardians of justice and measure) The sun will not overstep his measures; if he does, the Erinyes, the handmaids of Justice, will find him out.
Heraclitus

advice-37ab0eb83927f09ee228de82.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-37ab0eb83927f09ee228de82.body:
(The Bear is a constellation; bright Zeus means the clear sky) The limit of East and West is the Bear; and opposite the Bear is the boundary of bright Zeus.
Heraclitus

advice-21a05d74456cef188e039a30.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-21a05d74456cef188e039a30.body:
(The sun as the source of daylight) If there were no sun it would be night, for all the other stars could do.
Heraclitus

advice-e268670edfa5b6bbab563b19.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e268670edfa5b6bbab563b19.body:
(The sun’s renewal each day) The sun is new every day.
Heraclitus

advice-f926377c4ee408d27d4b4200.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f926377c4ee408d27d4b4200.body:
(Day and night as a unity of opposites) Hesiod is most men’s teacher. Men think he knew very many things, a man who did not know day or night! They are one.
Heraclitus

advice-25d21c6387076b8953c6f7fe.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-25d21c6387076b8953c6f7fe.body:
(One divine order in the world’s opposite states) God is day and night, winter and summer, war and peace, surfeit and hunger; but he takes various shapes, just as fire, when it is mingled with spices, is named according to the savour of each.
Heraclitus

advice-635d876869b1f1ffdcc0f5cd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-635d876869b1f1ffdcc0f5cd.body:
(Distinguishing things through the sense of smell) If all things were turned to smoke, the nostrils would distinguish them.
Heraclitus

advice-7590a24ff38d1d415369221e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7590a24ff38d1d415369221e.body:
(Souls sense smells in Hades) Souls smell in Hades.
Heraclitus

advice-dfa44987e2711a074e3f918f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dfa44987e2711a074e3f918f.body:
(Opposite states changing into one another) Cold things become warm, and what is warm cools; what is wet dries, and the parched is moisted.
Heraclitus

advice-429d34140f93c9e50b42f951.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-429d34140f93c9e50b42f951.body:
(The river as an image of continuous change) You cannot step twice into the same rivers; for fresh waters are ever flowing in upon you.
Heraclitus

advice-d0dccb46f5805da5f34fb98b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d0dccb46f5805da5f34fb98b.body:
(Strife as a condition of the world’s existence) Homer was wrong in saying: “Would that strife might perish from among gods and men!” He did not see that he was praying for the destruction of the universe; for, if his prayer were heard, all things would pass away....
Heraclitus

advice-0825787e04b4e58169f8ef67.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0825787e04b4e58169f8ef67.body:
(War as a force changing beings’ status) War is the father of all and the king of all; and some he has made gods and some men, some bond and some free.
Heraclitus

advice-ed9159c642351d957c6d0a53.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ed9159c642351d957c6d0a53.body:
(Bow and lyre: unity through opposing tensions) Men do not know how what is at variance agrees with itself. It is an attunement of opposite tensions, like that of the bow and the lyre.
Heraclitus

advice-fbcbd55daf2d9200f9f22a04.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fbcbd55daf2d9200f9f22a04.body:
(The opposite as a means of restoring balance) It is the opposite which is good for us.
Heraclitus

advice-679b2ed53b2f79c170704a51.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-679b2ed53b2f79c170704a51.body:
(The hidden harmony of things) The hidden attunement is better than the open.
Heraclitus

advice-7b303e47b2d168ce26908f04.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7b303e47b2d168ce26908f04.body:
(On verifying truth instead of acting by guesswork) Let us not conjecture at random about the greatest things.
Heraclitus

advice-af9ab10bd78e64234e7d80c0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-af9ab10bd78e64234e7d80c0.body:
(The broad knowledge needed by a seeker of wisdom) Men that love wisdom must be acquainted with very many things indeed.
Heraclitus

advice-64a331ed2b457e6cdf69f34f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-64a331ed2b457e6cdf69f34f.body:
(The fuller’s comb: a tool for working cloth) The straight and the crooked path of the fuller’s comb is one and the same.
Heraclitus

advice-a7e9b26a64151bb146a6fddb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a7e9b26a64151bb146a6fddb.body:
(Benefit and preference depend on a creature’s nature) Asses would rather have straw than gold.
Heraclitus

advice-a7407ab4650396d7a8f47c52.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a7407ab4650396d7a8f47c52.body:
(Benefit and preference depend on a creature’s nature) Oxen are happy when they find bitter vetches to eat.
Heraclitus

advice-c3c7d01fcd135582834a75ab.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c3c7d01fcd135582834a75ab.body:
(Benefit and preference depend on a creature’s nature) The sea is the purest and the impurest water. Fish can drink it, and it is good for them; to men it is undrinkable and destructive.
Heraclitus

advice-2fe0beeb91f31022db7ab85f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2fe0beeb91f31022db7ab85f.body:
(Benefit and preference depend on a creature’s nature) Swine wash in the mire, and barnyard fowls in dust.
Heraclitus

advice-c51908ebcdae2e7c85acd80a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c51908ebcdae2e7c85acd80a.body:
(The image of a herd driven to pasture) Every beast is driven to pasture with blows.
Heraclitus

advice-338166c6281d83bdb766360c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-338166c6281d83bdb766360c.body:
(The unity of opposites: good and evil) Good and ill are one.
Heraclitus

advice-71b7560c91f77c50d1fbf6a5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-71b7560c91f77c50d1fbf6a5.body:
(An ancient paradox: a physician causes pain to heal) Physicians who cut, burn, stab, and rack the sick, demand a fee for it which they do not deserve to get.
Heraclitus

advice-8e3fc19be48dadd3ffef6503.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8e3fc19be48dadd3ffef6503.body:
(Pairs here means connections between opposing qualities) Couples are things whole and things not whole, what is drawn together and what is drawn asunder, the harmonious and the discordant. The one is made up of all things, and all things issue from the one.
Heraclitus

advice-0f710674c7d106d9918762ff.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0f710674c7d106d9918762ff.body:
(Divine order and human judgments of good and evil) To God all things are fair and good and right, but men hold some things wrong and some right.
Heraclitus

advice-d1c429976dc1e76168f0059b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d1c429976dc1e76168f0059b.body:
(Strife as a condition of the world’s existence) We must know that war is common to all and strife is justice, and that all things come into being and pass away (?) through strife.
Heraclitus

advice-3289bd22eab223fa0cec6883.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3289bd22eab223fa0cec6883.body:
(An enigmatic fragment about waking, sleep, and death) All the things we see when awake are death, even as all we see in slumber are sleep.
Heraclitus

advice-7516102512bfb86fa6c89ae9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7516102512bfb86fa6c89ae9.body:
(The one wisdom: the paradox of accepting and refusing the name Zeus) The wise is one only. It is unwilling and willing to be called by the name of Zeus.
Heraclitus

advice-b5eddf9da5844b699a1c84eb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b5eddf9da5844b699a1c84eb.body:
(Greek wordplay: the words for bow and life sound alike) The bow (βιός) is called life (βίος), but its work is death.
Heraclitus

advice-e2a97a4314c3d4030de54459.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e2a97a4314c3d4030de54459.body:
(The mutual relation between mortal and immortal) Mortals are immortals and immortals are mortals, the one living the others’ death and dying the others’ life.
Heraclitus

advice-7ef1e3c69f1ccd9c8f4cbf0b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7ef1e3c69f1ccd9c8f4cbf0b.body:
(One element’s life as another element’s transformation) For it is death to souls to become water, and death to water to become earth. But water comes from earth; and from water, soul.
Heraclitus

advice-976c58f6ca90906b19037c26.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-976c58f6ca90906b19037c26.body:
(One path viewed in opposite directions) The way up and the way down is one and the same.
Heraclitus

advice-806a94f00fc24d0b0762a185.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-806a94f00fc24d0b0762a185.body:
(The circle as the unity of beginning and end) In the circumference of a circle the beginning and end are common.
Heraclitus

advice-8d7f7109c3c01fc262442f35.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8d7f7109c3c01fc262442f35.body:
(The inexhaustible depth of the soul) You will not find the boundaries of soul by travelling in any direction, so deep is the measure of it.
Heraclitus

advice-43679bda264f1731fbcfdbc2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-43679bda264f1731fbcfdbc2.body:
(Dry and moist soul: clarity and intoxication) It is pleasure to souls to become moist.
Heraclitus

advice-692a4397faddfc69cc72a2e5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-692a4397faddfc69cc72a2e5.body:
(Dry and moist soul: clarity and intoxication) A man, when he gets drunk, is led by a beardless lad, tripping, knowing not where he steps, having his soul moist.
Heraclitus

advice-26d138b894f4c16d5eed0b05.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-26d138b894f4c16d5eed0b05.body:
(Dry and moist soul: clarity and intoxication) The dry soul is the wisest and best.
Heraclitus

advice-1078dfa31dd78a83cd61d2d4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1078dfa31dd78a83cd61d2d4.body:
(Life and consciousness pictured as a light being kindled) Man is kindled and put out like a light in the night-time.
Heraclitus

advice-a6d20106ce14cb302c42c45f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a6d20106ce14cb302c42c45f.body:
(Opposites alternate: life/death, waking/sleep, youth/age; ‘quick’ means alive) And it is the same thing in us that is quick and dead, awake and asleep, young and old; the former are shifted and become the latter, and the latter in turn are shifted and become the former.
Heraclitus

advice-7ac9d71ebf422e0f51d46f89.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7ac9d71ebf422e0f51d46f89.body:
(Lifetime pictured as a child playing draughts) Time is a child playing draughts, the kingly power is a child’s.
Heraclitus

advice-79624567723d94b2fb1c2649.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-79624567723d94b2fb1c2649.body:
(On self-knowledge and deliberately choosing a way of life) I have sought for myself.
Heraclitus

advice-897a27ca0fd96a35b34dd568.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-897a27ca0fd96a35b34dd568.body:
(The river as an image of continuous change) We step and do not step into the same rivers; we are and are not.
Heraclitus

advice-97e124e5769e5fd29a53f96a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-97e124e5769e5fd29a53f96a.body:
(The weariness of remaining unchanged, pictured as serving the same masters) It is a weariness to labour for the same masters and be ruled by them.
Heraclitus

advice-e01e6a835ded0df435f448a6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e01e6a835ded0df435f448a6.body:
(Kykeon: a mixed drink that separates unless stirred) Even the posset separates if it is not stirred.
Heraclitus

advice-7a7ab75ca444ffe3b2475b70.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7a7ab75ca444ffe3b2475b70.body:
(The body’s loss of value after life departs) Corpses are more fit to be cast out than dung.
Heraclitus

advice-8a8307f990e2a6249634bccd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8a8307f990e2a6249634bccd.body:
(The succession of human generations and inevitable death) When they are born, they wish to live and to meet with their dooms—or rather to rest—and they leave children behind them to meet with their dooms in turn.
Heraclitus

advice-52af16f07994c0073a2493de.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-52af16f07994c0073a2493de.body:
(Logos: the shared rational order of the world) Thought is common to all.
Heraclitus

advice-ef75f5b8ce49e7a3e847c69d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ef75f5b8ce49e7a3e847c69d.body:
(The shared rational order as the basis of human laws) Those who speak with understanding must hold fast to what is common to all as a city holds fast to its law, and even more strongly. For all human laws are fed by the one divine law. It prevails as much as it will, and suffices for all things with something to spare.
Heraclitus

advice-9e1a0440bbf11de5d228e6c8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9e1a0440bbf11de5d228e6c8.body:
(Logos: the shared rational order of the world) So we must follow the common, yet the many live as if they had a wisdom of their own.
Heraclitus

advice-768bd84941ccf0253d6c8598.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-768bd84941ccf0253d6c8598.body:
(Wakefulness as an image of conscious living) It is not meet to act and speak like men asleep.
Heraclitus

advice-d15a9efd153e3887b4bdc1ad.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d15a9efd153e3887b4bdc1ad.body:
(The shared waking world and separate dream worlds) The waking have one common world, but the sleeping turn aside each into a world of his own.
Heraclitus

advice-77e41c4f08024aa3cc53f3b3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-77e41c4f08024aa3cc53f3b3.body:
(The limits of human wisdom before divine wisdom) The way of man has no wisdom, but that of God has.
Heraclitus

advice-ec5d3a8386bfc61a90087a67.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ec5d3a8386bfc61a90087a67.body:
(The limits of human wisdom before divine wisdom) Man is called a baby by God, even as a child by a man.
Heraclitus

advice-02548d767efdc867dd49d4c1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-02548d767efdc867dd49d4c1.body:
(The limits of human wisdom before divine wisdom) The wisest man is an ape compared to God, just as the most beautiful ape is ugly compared to man.
Heraclitus

advice-fe6247f573c0137508cb6efb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fe6247f573c0137508cb6efb.body:
(Law as protection for the city’s shared order) The people must fight for its law as for its walls.
Heraclitus

advice-ac29120e97692e9bd9c8e414.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ac29120e97692e9bd9c8e414.body:
(Posthumous fate; the precise meaning of the ‘greater portion’ is uncertain) Greater deaths win greater portions.
Heraclitus

advice-e74e47dcbc1f543a8d690ab7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e74e47dcbc1f543a8d690ab7.body:
(Ancient honours for those killed in battle) Gods and men honour those who are slain in battle.
Heraclitus

advice-5af8c6e85190bdaa29b01890.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5af8c6e85190bdaa29b01890.body:
(Restraining arrogance and destructive excess) Wantonness needs putting out, even more than a house on fire.
Heraclitus

advice-41b56e483cbf469144e06d75.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-41b56e483cbf469144e06d75.body:
(Opposites make us value health, satiety, and rest) It is not good for men to get all they wish to get. It is sickness that makes health pleasant; evil, good; hunger, plenty; weariness, rest.
Heraclitus

advice-aef8ddb7bf46952ebd417681.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-aef8ddb7bf46952ebd417681.body:
(On passion preventing obedience to one’s rational judgment) It is hard to fight with one’s heart’s desire. Whatever it wishes to get, it purchases at the cost of soul.
Heraclitus

advice-da76c965c21d1bf6ba5eb11f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-da76c965c21d1bf6ba5eb11f.body:
(Wine makes human foolishness more visible) It is best to hide folly; but it is hard in times of relaxation, over our cups.
Heraclitus

advice-392d9f27cf49da4891b37397.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-392d9f27cf49da4891b37397.body:
(Law and obedience to one person’s counsel) And it is law, too, to obey the counsel of one.
Heraclitus

advice-9e36307a1c5fe6973ae13c3b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9e36307a1c5fe6973ae13c3b.body:
(Criticism of crowds that take the majority as their standard) For what thought or wisdom have they? They follow the poets and take the crowd as their teacher, knowing not that there are many bad and few good. For even the best of them choose one thing above all others, immortal glory among mortals, while most of them are glutted like beasts.
Heraclitus

advice-4c2c3fbeb28de4433534a64c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4c2c3fbeb28de4433534a64c.body:
(The sage Bias of Priene, one of the Seven Sages) In Priene lived Bias, son of Teutamas, who is of more account than the rest.
Heraclitus

advice-8db225f946c237ba1ab5e06c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8db225f946c237ba1ab5e06c.body:
(A person’s excellence matters more than superior numbers) One is ten thousand to me, if he be the best.
Heraclitus

advice-f7175af42bb8caf5d0e26b54.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f7175af42bb8caf5d0e26b54.body:
(Fierce political invective against the Ephesians’ expulsion of Hermodorus) The Ephesians would do well to hang themselves, every grown man of them, and leave the city to beardless lads; for they have cast out Hermodoros, the best man among them, saying, “We will have none who is best among us; if there be any such, let him be so elsewhere and among others.”
Heraclitus

advice-c2f06f3baed743af5750fd9a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c2f06f3baed743af5750fd9a.body:
(Hostile reactions to what is unfamiliar) Dogs bark at every one they do not know.
Heraclitus

advice-7fb094b40bd96cdc2698620b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7fb094b40bd96cdc2698620b.body:
(The instability of a mind swayed by every word) The fool is fluttered at every word.
Heraclitus

advice-c751e8fa7931683cc3461623.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c751e8fa7931683cc3461623.body:
(Criticism of recognised authorities and false testimony) The most esteemed of them knows but fancies; yet of a truth justice shall overtake the artificers of lies and the false witnesses.
Heraclitus

advice-1177d6c41d165589bee164da.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1177d6c41d165589bee164da.body:
(Heraclitus’s polemic against Homer’s and Archilochus’s poetic authority) Homer should be turned out of the lists and whipped, and Archilochos likewise.
Heraclitus

advice-9af84c489d8e5ffcef8ce67d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9af84c489d8e5ffcef8ce67d.body:
(The likeness of days) One day is like any other.
Heraclitus

advice-92ca99406827df185f88f79c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-92ca99406827df185f88f79c.body:
(The connection between character and destiny) Man’s character is his fate.
Heraclitus

advice-5eeba7bcba354d3c73ac6848.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5eeba7bcba354d3c73ac6848.body:
(The unknown fate after death) There awaits men when they die such things as they look not for nor dream of.
Heraclitus

advice-83596e3c31839f2313b70757.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-83596e3c31839f2313b70757.body:
(Criticism of customary initiation rites in the mysteries) The mysteries practised among men are unholy mysteries.
Heraclitus

advice-cfe479514e2166d348c64c68.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cfe479514e2166d348c64c68.body:
(Criticism of prayers addressed to cult statues) And they pray to these images, as if one were to talk with a man’s house, knowing not what gods or heroes are.
Heraclitus

advice-ecbd57e320f24b475dc24d2e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ecbd57e320f24b475dc24d2e.body:
(Dionysus and Hades: a paradox of life’s and death’s unity) For if it were not to Dionysos that they made a procession and sang the shameful phallic hymn, they would be acting most shamelessly. But Hades is the same as Dionysos in whose honour they go mad and keep the feast of the wine-vat.
Heraclitus

advice-cc9571c5ce6af5e12db7474a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cc9571c5ce6af5e12db7474a.body:
(Criticism of ritual purification with animals’ blood) They vainly purify themselves by defiling themselves with blood, just as if one who had stepped into the mud were to wash his feet in mud. Any man who marked him doing thus, would deem him mad.
Heraclitus

advice-7e59f804ae76515ca811c0b1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7e59f804ae76515ca811c0b1.body:
(On self-knowledge and deliberately choosing a way of life) It is the part of all men to know themselves and to be temperate.
Heraclitus (attributed)

advice-1848945bc0592811a7a8bbfd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1848945bc0592811a7a8bbfd.body:
(On reason as a guide to human conduct) To be temperate is the greatest virtue; and it is wisdom to speak the truth and to act according to nature with understanding.
Heraclitus (attributed)

advice-2458cd4fddc1bc334ade0c8d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2458cd4fddc1bc334ade0c8d.body:
(Heraclitus compares false opinion to epilepsy, the ancient sacred disease) He was wont to say that false opinion is a sacred disease, and that vision is deceitful.
Heraclitus (attributed)

advice-1cbfd37c2a77edaffb1badec.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1cbfd37c2a77edaffb1badec.body:
Begin by honouring the immortal gods and observing the sacred customs established for their worship.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-d7fdc5dcfbec2f90a1b5f269.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d7fdc5dcfbec2f90a1b5f269.body:
(The sanctity of oaths and honouring deified heroes) Reverence the Oath, and next the Heroes, full of goodness and light.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-9734fa1fe9588195e7303a6e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9734fa1fe9588195e7303a6e.body:
(Daimons here means revered spirits in ancient Greek religion) Honour likewise the Terrestrial Dæmons by rendering them the worship lawfully due to them.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-7c1317d0e670b78a44aca452.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7c1317d0e670b78a44aca452.body:
(Respect for parents and close relatives) Honour likewise thy parents, and those most nearly related to thee.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-674d66f142fd1c80ad909418.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-674d66f142fd1c80ad909418.body:
(A virtuous friend as an example for moral learning) Of all the rest of mankind, make him thy friend who distinguishes himself by his virtue. Always give ear to his mild exhortations, and take example from his virtuous and useful actions.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-4df342bd4f9bcc91ee5cd6ce.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4df342bd4f9bcc91ee5cd6ce.body:
(Forbearance towards a friend’s minor faults) Avoid as much as possible hating thy friend for a slight fault. [And understand that] power is a near neighbour to necessity.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-deb98153098993a89f3ddd5d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-deb98153098993a89f3ddd5d.body:
(From honouring gods, parents, and friends to self-control) Know that all these things are as I have told thee; and accustom thyself to overcome and vanquish these passions:-- First gluttony, sloth, sensuality, and anger.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-ba821b099140476cfff781cd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ba821b099140476cfff781cd.body:
(On integrity, modesty, and self-respect) Do nothing evil, neither in the presence of others, nor privately; But above all things respect thyself.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-33273c105c5fe001915f90c9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-33273c105c5fe001915f90c9.body:
(Justice in words and actions) In the next place, observe justice in thy actions and in thy words.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-d008efff632534c37aa033f9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d008efff632534c37aa033f9.body:
(On reason as a guide to human conduct) And accustom not thyself to behave thyself in any thing without rule, and without reason.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-08c1108bd0a1421ab093b6c7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-08c1108bd0a1421ab093b6c7.body:
(Human mortality and the fragility of outward prosperity) But always make this reflection, that it is ordained by destiny that all men shall die. And that the goods of fortune are uncertain; and that as they may be acquired, so may they likewise be lost.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-b4dc232ae3e4e9301d4f6cd0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b4dc232ae3e4e9301d4f6cd0.body:
(Patience in adversity and improving circumstances where possible) Concerning all the calamities that men suffer by divine fortune, Support with patience thy lot, be it what it may, and never repine at it. But endeavour what thou canst to remedy it. And consider that fate does not send the greatest portion of these misfortunes to good men.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-1911148c7c59feaf8c26e8e2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1911148c7c59feaf8c26e8e2.body:
(Weighing others’ words without hasty agreement) There are among men many sorts of reasonings, good and bad; Admire them not too easily, nor reject them. But if falsehoods be advanced, hear them with mildness, and arm thyself with patience.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-fa8137c3bfa16aa6a9f84940.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fa8137c3bfa16aa6a9f84940.body:
(Independence when facing others’ persuasion and example) Observe well, on every occasion, what I am going to tell thee:-- Let no man either by his words, or by his deeds, ever seduce thee. Nor entice thee to say or to do what is not profitable for thyself.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-9371bc1896de97c04d244e59.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9371bc1896de97c04d244e59.body:
(On considering an action’s requirements and consequences) Consult and deliberate before thou act, that thou mayest not commit foolish actions. For it is the part of a miserable man to speak and to act without reflection. But do that which will not afflict thee afterwards, nor oblige thee to repentance.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-9d97f34a04b1c8dbacbb2efb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9d97f34a04b1c8dbacbb2efb.body:
(Understanding a task before acting) Never do anything which thou dost not understand. But learn all thou ought'st to know, and by that means thou wilt lead a very pleasant life.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-5a3dd05b32622670b78dc107.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5a3dd05b32622670b78dc107.body:
(Moderate food, drink, and exercise in caring for the body) in no wise neglect the health of thy body; But give it drink and meat in due measure, and also the exercise of which it has need. Now by measure I mean what will not incommode thee.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-9a79c869e072920ccab6472c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9a79c869e072920ccab6472c.body:
(A neat and simple life without luxury) Accustom thyself to a way of living that is neat and decent without luxury.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-2445926df017882b779532d3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2445926df017882b779532d3.body:
(Moderation in spending between extravagance and miserliness) Avoid all things that will occasion envy. And be not prodigal out of season, like one who knows not what is decent and honourable. Neither be covetous nor niggardly; a due measure is excellent in these things.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-4c140da5c30c4b2f99661835.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4c140da5c30c4b2f99661835.body:
(On considering an action’s requirements and consequences) Do only the things that cannot hurt thee, and deliberate before thou dost them.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-a996d10e1256934133972375.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a996d10e1256934133972375.body:
(An evening review of one’s actions and omissions) Never suffer sleep to close thy eyelids, after thy going to bed, Till thou hast examined by thy reason all thy actions of the day. Wherein have I done amiss? What have I done? What have I omitted that I ought to have done? If in this examination thou find that thou hast done amiss, reprimand thyself severely for it; And if thou hast done any good, rejoice.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-aab151d8af460464ee70b165.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-aab151d8af460464ee70b165.body:
(Prayer before beginning a task in the Pythagorean tradition) But never begin to set thy hand to any work, till thou hast first prayed the gods to accomplish what thou art going to begin.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-5ed41975cc5259fa92c3d7e7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5ed41975cc5259fa92c3d7e7.body:
(Ignorance of one’s own good as a source of misfortune) Thou wilt likewise know, that men draw upon themselves their own misfortunes voluntarily, and of their own free choice. Unhappy that they are! They neither see nor understand that their good is near them. Few know how to deliver themselves out of their misfortunes.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-f2dace42cbdad95c79af402e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f2dace42cbdad95c79af402e.body:
(Ignorance of one’s good and strife as sources of human troubles) Such is the fate that blinds mankind, and takes away his senses. Like huge cylinders they roll to and fro, and always oppressed with ills innumerable. For fatal strife, innate, pursues them everywhere, tossing them up and down; nor do they perceive it. Instead of provoking and stirring it up, they ought, by yielding, to avoid it.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-fb0d6f6952e6629770af9b6a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fb0d6f6952e6629770af9b6a.body:
(Jupiter means Zeus; daimon here means a divine guardian) Oh! Jupiter, our Father! if Thou would'st deliver men from all the evils that oppress them, Show them of what dæmon they make use.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-02f33c49caf31b31a1e5a7fe.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-02f33c49caf31b31a1e5a7fe.body:
(Aether: the heavenly realm of the soul’s immortality after death) And when, after having divested thyself of thy mortal body, thou arrivest at the most pure Æther, Thou shalt be a God, immortal, incorruptible, and Death shall have no more dominion over thee.
Pythagorean tradition

advice-00aba52c7aecd0c9ebf665de.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-00aba52c7aecd0c9ebf665de.body:
(Virtues as reliable anchors against life’s storms) Pythagoras said, it is requisite to choose the most excellent life; for custom will make it pleasant. Wealth is an infirm anchor, glory is still more infirm; and in a similar manner, the body, dominion, and honour. For all these are imbecile and powerless. What then are powerful anchors. Prudence, magnanimity, fortitude. These no tempest can shake. This is the Law of God, that virtue is the only thing that is strong; and that every thing else is a trifle.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Pythagorean Ethical Sentences from Stobaeus, §6 (Firth numbering)

advice-24f676e9e83cdfa1f1ad0bc6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-24f676e9e83cdfa1f1ad0bc6.body:
(Desires that are improper, excessive, or untimely) Of desire also, he (Pythagoras) said as follows:--This passion is various, laborious, and very multiform. Of desires, however, some are acquired and adventitious, but others are connascent. But he defined desire itself to be a certain tendency and impulse of the soul, and an appetite of a plentitude or presence of sense, or an emptiness and absence of it, and of non-perception. He also said, that there are three most known species of erroneous and depraved desire, viz., the indecorous, the incommensurate, and the unseasonable. For desire is either immediately Indecorous, troublesome, and illiberal, or it is not absolutely so, but is more vehement and lasting than is fit. Or in the third place, it is impelled when it is not proper, and to objects to which it ought not to tend.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Pythagorean Ethical Sentences from Stobaeus, §21 (Firth numbering)

advice-d45d6bf7ba6c6f4b12af2322.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d45d6bf7ba6c6f4b12af2322.body:
(Intoxication as practice in losing one’s reason) Pythagoras said, that intoxication is the meditation of insanity.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Pythagorean Ethical Sentences from Stobaeus, §34 (Firth numbering)

advice-0b46b5831535097aac25cc44.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0b46b5831535097aac25cc44.body:
(Observing the consequences of one’s own intoxication) Pythagoras being asked, how a lover of wine might be cured of intoxication, answered, if he frequently surveys what his actions were when he was intoxicated.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Pythagorean Ethical Sentences from Stobaeus, §35 (Firth numbering)

advice-d68235f17ab366876df5b37a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d68235f17ab366876df5b37a.body:
(On worthwhile conversation and appropriate silence) Pythagoras said, that it was requisite either to be silent, or to say something better than silence.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Pythagorean Ethical Sentences from Stobaeus, §36 (Firth numbering)

advice-7568060ea77c77e5556f65ea.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7568060ea77c77e5556f65ea.body:
(One’s country as a mother: responding to its injustice) Pythagoras being asked how a man ought to conduct himself towards his country, when it had acted iniquitously with respect to him, replied, as to a mother.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Pythagorean Ethical Sentences from Stobaeus, §40 (Firth numbering)

advice-afbcc4b8de4d1fbe622c90ad.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-afbcc4b8de4d1fbe622c90ad.body:
(Luxury and excess as causes of a city’s decline) Pythagoras said that luxury entered into cities in the first place, afterwards satiety, then lascivious insolence, and after all these, destruction.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Pythagorean Ethical Sentences from Stobaeus, §43 (Firth numbering)

advice-265713e9076fdea99c4c6e45.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-265713e9076fdea99c4c6e45.body:
(The worth of citizens as the measure of a city’s worth) Pythagoras said, that of cities that was the best which contained most worthy men.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Pythagorean Ethical Sentences from Stobaeus, §44 (Firth numbering)

advice-c052c6c0989af3206e92d464.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c052c6c0989af3206e92d464.body:
(Pythagoras as reported: life as a festival, the philosopher as spectator) And Sosicrates, in his Successions, relates that he, having being asked by Leon, the tyrant of the Phliasians, who he was, replied, “A philosopher.” And adds, that he used to compare life to a festival. “And as some people came to a festival to contend for the prizes, and others for the purposes of traffic, and the best as spectators; so also in life, the men of slavish dispositions,” said he, “are born hunters after glory and covetousness, but philosophers are seekers after truth.”
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 13, excerpt 1

advice-edb44d1a2d9c270a28fc93a5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-edb44d1a2d9c270a28fc93a5.body:
(Pythagoras’s advice: prayer without demanding specific benefits) He forbids men to pray for anything in particular for themselves, because they do not know what is good for them.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 14, excerpt 1

advice-b85e6a812e5b02e7774d905b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b85e6a812e5b02e7774d905b.body:
(Pythagoras divides life into four ages resembling the seasons) And he divides the life of man thus. A boy for twenty years; a young man (νεάνισκος) for twenty years; a middle-aged man (νεανίας) for twenty years; an old man for twenty years. And these different ages correspond proportionably to the seasons: boyhood answers to spring; youth to summer; middle age to autumn; and old age to winter.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 15, excerpt 1

advice-f8ddca03060ace5795f0da94.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f8ddca03060ace5795f0da94.body:
(Shared property and equality among friends, attributed to Pythagoras) He was the first person, as Timæus says, who asserted that the property of friends is common, and that friendship is equality.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 16, excerpt 1

advice-b52fd4decaa5bd682c577bd7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b52fd4decaa5bd682c577bd7.body:
(The doctrine of souls moving between bodies, attributed to Pythagoras) They say, too, that he was the first person who asserted that the soul went a necessary circle being changed about and confined at different times in different bodies.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 22, excerpt 1

advice-364d8088a3274dbe4fd047cb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-364d8088a3274dbe4fd047cb.body:
(Fire and sword: an image of the danger of provoking power) Now the precept not to stir fire with a sword meant, not to provoke the anger or swelling pride of powerful men.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 30, excerpt 1

advice-bfaed0fb04846f09d1a8cc5f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bfaed0fb04846f09d1a8cc5f.body:
(The balance as a symbol of justice) Not to violate the beam of the balance meant, not to transgress fairness and justice.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 30, excerpt 2

advice-faacdc99943531f8768f83cc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-faacdc99943531f8768f83cc.body:
(The grain measure here symbolises sustenance and foresight) Not to sit on a bushel is to have an equal care for the present and for the future, for by the bushel is meant one’s daily food.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 30, excerpt 3

advice-cc4cf54f12dea33b092f8831.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cc4cf54f12dea33b092f8831.body:
(Pythagoras: not devouring the heart means not exhausting oneself with grief) By not devouring one’s heart, he intended to show that we ought not to waste away our souls with grief and sorrow.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 30, excerpt 4

advice-7333aaacb0a700c50d2f0051.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7333aaacb0a700c50d2f0051.body:
(Pythagoras’s image of a journey means departing from life) In the precept that a man when travelling abroad should not turn his eyes back, he recommended those who were departing from life not to be desirous to live, and not to be too much attracted by the pleasures here on earth.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 30, excerpt 5

advice-7a3c281b256299d24d8bbc91.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7a3c281b256299d24d8bbc91.body:
(Pythagoras on truthfulness that needs no oath) He forbade them also to swear by the Gods; saying, “That every man ought so to exercise himself, as to be worthy of belief without an oath.”
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 37, excerpt 1

advice-bee855d68638539ef0a90a29.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bee855d68638539ef0a90a29.body:
(Pythagoras on honouring elders and life’s beginning) He also taught men that it behoved them to honour their elders, thinking that which was precedent in point of time more honourable; just as in the world, the rising of the sun was more so than the setting; in life, the beginning more so than the end; and in animals, production more so than destruction.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 37, excerpt 2

advice-890d3786301379c6991d413e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-890d3786301379c6991d413e.body:
(Another Pythagorean precept: turning enemies into friends) Another, that people should associate with one another in such a way as not to make their friends enemies, but to render their enemies friends.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 38, excerpt 1

advice-865278885cd4930b3955aa5b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-865278885cd4930b3955aa5b.body:
(Pythagorean defence of law against lawlessness) Another was to assist the law, and to make war upon lawlessness.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 38, excerpt 2

advice-737fac9f6c3cae69b53ae3b3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-737fac9f6c3cae69b53ae3b3.body:
(Pythagorean care for plants and harmless animals) Not to destroy or injure a cultivated tree, nor any animal either which does not injure men.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 38, excerpt 3

advice-455f791742e199beb53abc55.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-455f791742e199beb53abc55.body:
(Pythagorean advice: refrain from laughter without looking stern) That modesty and decorum consisted in never yielding to laughter, and yet not looking stern.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 38, excerpt 4

advice-41340617b9fac7fd3b0cea48.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-41340617b9fac7fd3b0cea48.body:
(Pythagoras teaches moderation, memory training, self-control, and music) He taught that men should avoid too much flesh, that they should in travelling let rest and exertion alternate; that they should exercise memory; that they should never say or do anything in anger; that they should not pay respect to every kind of divination; that they should use songs set to the lyre; and by hymns to the Gods and to eminent men, display a reasonable gratitude to them.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 38, excerpt 5

advice-fe38bed506ecdb4226a95959.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fe38bed506ecdb4226a95959.body:
(The monad is unity; the indefinite dyad is the source of multiplicity) That the monad was the beginning of everything. From the monad proceeds an indefinite duad, which is subordinate to the monad as to its cause. That from the monad and the indefinite duad proceed numbers.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 40, excerpt 1

advice-e828aaf7d75c1df91f3ab41d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e828aaf7d75c1df91f3ab41d.body:
(The Pythagoreans on the soul’s ability to choose good or evil) They also say, that the most important privilege in man is, the being able to persuade his soul to either good or bad.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 48, excerpt 1

advice-b56ec222a5ed45d8c19685dc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b56ec222a5ed45d8c19685dc.body:
(Pythagorean harmony as the basis of virtue and cosmic order) Also, that virtue is harmony, and health, and universal good, and God; on which account everything owes its existence and consistency to harmony.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 48, excerpt 2

advice-b06c9ac53f319924f63511a4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b06c9ac53f319924f63511a4.body:
(Shared bread as a symbol of friendship and unity) Another of the precepts of Pythagoras was, that men ought not to break bread; because in ancient times friends used to assemble around one loaf, as they even now do among the barbarians. Nor would he allow men to divide bread which unites them.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 54, excerpt 1

advice-3f800f0ee70ac035ad08b24d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3f800f0ee70ac035ad08b24d.body:
(The Pythagorean beauty of the circle and sphere) Another of his doctrines was, that of all solid figures the sphere was the most beautiful; and of all plane figures, the circle.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 55, excerpt 1

advice-96dfebc29ea07e9095e0bf04.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-96dfebc29ea07e9095e0bf04.body:
(Salt as a Pythagorean symbol of preservation and justice) Of salt his opinion was, that it ought to be set before people as a reminder of justice; for salt preserves everything which it touches, and it is composed of the purest particles of water and sea.
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 55, excerpt 2

advice-829f4da1c0260b9195ad7b82.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-829f4da1c0260b9195ad7b82.body:
(Xenophanes on Pythagoras: a friend’s soul in a dog) They say that once, as passing by he saw A dog severely beaten, he did pity him, And spoke as follows to the man who beat him:— “Stop now, and beat him not; since in his body, Abides the soul of a dear friend of mine, Whose voice I recognized as he was crying.”
Pythagorean tradition

sources.author: Pythagorean tradition
sources.reference: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book VIII, Life of Pythagoras; source paragraph 62, excerpt 1

advice-17324404d8ba659f92e261da.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-17324404d8ba659f92e261da.body:
Excellence of soul can correct the body's faults, but physical strength without reason does not make the soul better.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-73503b75a1570dfeb90d07cb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-73503b75a1570dfeb90d07cb.body:
(The body as the soul’s temporary dwelling) He who loves the goods of the soul will love things more, divine; but he who loves the goods of its transient habitation will love things human.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-e76e802dcf3f8560742299eb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e76e802dcf3f8560742299eb.body:
(Justice and moral conduct) It is beautiful to impede an unjust man; but, if this be not possible, it is beautiful not to act in conjunction with him.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-c7a40dd11b90d33fe912e139.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c7a40dd11b90d33fe912e139.body:
(The difference between moral words and deeds) It is necessary to be good, rather than to appear so.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-89f08baa09c34863b7348704.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-89f08baa09c34863b7348704.body:
(Justice and moral conduct) The felicity of a man does not consist either in body or in riches, but in upright conduct and justice.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-c988ae8a81a8e59dc50f1d26.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c988ae8a81a8e59dc50f1d26.body:
(Justice and moral conduct) Sin should be abstained from, not through fear, but for the sake of the becoming.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-678cd2fdf06aa945516fc176.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-678cd2fdf06aa945516fc176.body:
(Wisdom acquired through adversity) It is a great thing to be wise where we ought in calamitous circumstances.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-4b456e49b254aee551dc9ad1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4b456e49b254aee551dc9ad1.body:
(Repentance after wrongdoing) Repentance after base actions is the salvation of life.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-a6f41f33d2a22718a9056597.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a6f41f33d2a22718a9056597.body:
(Truthfulness and the rejection of falsehood) It is necessary to be a speaker of the truth, and not to be loquacious.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-8bdcc185c6f54eebd850c05e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8bdcc185c6f54eebd850c05e.body:
(Injustice as a disease of the soul) He who does an injury is more unhappy than he who receives one.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-a585860e19c26886ba77020b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a585860e19c26886ba77020b.body:
(Rejecting revenge and tolerating mistakes) It is the province of a magnanimous man to bear with mildness the errors of others.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-9af8b45b23492876e5482936.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9af8b45b23492876e5482936.body:
(The ability to listen and learn from others) It is comely not to oppose the law, nor a prince, nor one wiser than yourself.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-78650b7c573236dcd9843027.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-78650b7c573236dcd9843027.body:
(A person who understands justice and the majority’s opinion) A good man pays no attention to the reproofs of the depraved.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-0ae7f7709ea3b649b3b2a2bb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0ae7f7709ea3b649b3b2a2bb.body:
(Being ruled by someone morally worse) It is hard to be governed by these who are worse than ourselves.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-f37fb526a03a7fb1cda6fbaa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f37fb526a03a7fb1cda6fbaa.body:
(Wealth, wisdom, and virtue) He who is perfectly vanquished by riches, can never be just.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-38e1ceda58197077a615fa1c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-38e1ceda58197077a615fa1c.body:
(Reasoned persuasion instead of compulsion) Reason is frequently more persuasive than gold itself.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-1720a43557ba1d4f696850a5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1720a43557ba1d4f696850a5.body:
(The ability to listen and learn from others) He who admonishes a man that fancies he has intellect, labours in vain.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-17e706f8b4220ac9bbb63189.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-17e706f8b4220ac9bbb63189.body:
(Reason, wisdom, and mere learning) Many who have not learnt to argue rationally, still live according to reason.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-536ec10d78e5299d136334df.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-536ec10d78e5299d136334df.body:
(The difference between moral words and deeds) Many who commit the basest actions often exercise the best discourse.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-ea30364b0fbd645222cee79c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ea30364b0fbd645222cee79c.body:
(Wisdom acquired through adversity) Fools frequently become wise under the pressure of misfortunes.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-4f2afe7eeab79b77aa0f43c8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4f2afe7eeab79b77aa0f43c8.body:
(Following a better moral example) It is necessary to emulate the works and actions, and not the words of virtue.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-9eb45f02282221fa69430bad.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9eb45f02282221fa69430bad.body:
(Following a better moral example) Those who are naturally well disposed, know things beautiful, and are themselves emulous of them.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-1cca6702f7600eec572fdd8d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1cca6702f7600eec572fdd8d.body:
(Outward beauty and inner worth) Vigour and strength of body are the nobility of cattle; but the rectitude of manners is the nobility of man.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-b97704a491fffe00cfd93423.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b97704a491fffe00cfd93423.body:
(Learning, experience, and wise guidance) Neither art nor wisdom can be acquired without preparatory learning.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-312d7ebb8113af1a0b09dfd1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-312d7ebb8113af1a0b09dfd1.body:
(Correcting one’s own faults) It is better to reprove your own errors, than those of others.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-c53d334e227dbde94476b877.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c53d334e227dbde94476b877.body:
(The difference between moral words and deeds) Those whose manners are well ordered will also be orderly in their lives.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-c0572122714b39c731c54218.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c0572122714b39c731c54218.body:
(Justice and moral conduct) It is good not only to refrain from doing an injury, but even from the very wish.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-7a86d401da92aacc0a3f5130.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7a86d401da92aacc0a3f5130.body:
(Praise, flattery, and fair assessment) It is proper to speak well of good works; for to do so of such as are base is the property of a fraudulent man and an impostor.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-36118d3c89f98c742016703c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-36118d3c89f98c742016703c.body:
(Reason, wisdom, and mere learning) Many that have great learning have no intellect.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-591b4e64724635affedf0aca.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-591b4e64724635affedf0aca.body:
(Reason, wisdom, and mere learning) It is necessary to endeavour to obtain an abundance of intellect, and not pursue an abundance of erudition.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-05c98a96d65ec92875fdad9e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-05c98a96d65ec92875fdad9e.body:
(Foresight before trouble occurs) It is better that counsel should precede actions, than that repentance should follow them.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-700b85e6895e03a029c07530.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-700b85e6895e03a029c07530.body:
(True friendship and how it is tested) Put not confidence in all men, but in those that are worthy; for to do the former is the province of a stupid man, but the latter of a wise man.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-cf3dd923d973f9a64cc4a576.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cf3dd923d973f9a64cc4a576.body:
(Justice and moral conduct) A worthy and an unworthy man are to be judged not from their actions only, but also from their will.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-a45418a8547607ee7e83f0a5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a45418a8547607ee7e83f0a5.body:
(Moderation in desires and pleasures) To desire immoderately is the province of a boy, and not of a man.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-4ca7b65889508be9f64fab09.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4ca7b65889508be9f64fab09.body:
(Moderation in desires and pleasures) Unseasonable pleasures bring forth pains.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-b5835b04ee5b1e1abd6c9274.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b5835b04ee5b1e1abd6c9274.body:
(Moderation in desires and pleasures) Vehement desires about any one thing render the soul blind with respect to other things.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-ffa3d4a275396fd6faff7b7f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ffa3d4a275396fd6faff7b7f.body:
(Love, desires, and character) The love is just which, unattended with injury, aspires after things becoming.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-d3c9c9ec07b538fe0f5a6b29.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d3c9c9ec07b538fe0f5a6b29.body:
(The distinction between good and pleasure) Admit nothing as pleasant which is not advantageous.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-eabc20491a7be60c683b478d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-eabc20491a7be60c683b478d.body:
(The difficulty of ruling foolish people) It is better to be governed by, than to govern, the stupid.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-ef3ae7c7749de8a8d6a4491e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ef3ae7c7749de8a8d6a4491e.body:
(Wisdom acquired through adversity) Not argument but calamity is the preceptor to children.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-715a6ec94ce9b9d41be64d26.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-715a6ec94ce9b9d41be64d26.body:
(Wealth, wisdom, and virtue) Glory and wealth without wisdom are not secure possessions.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-f02a088b771d0a34ae69c7be.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f02a088b771d0a34ae69c7be.body:
(Wealth, wisdom, and virtue) It is not indeed useless to procure wealth, but to procure it from injustice is the most pernicious of all things.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-28a45507eb8f29c7fb4fb217.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-28a45507eb8f29c7fb4fb217.body:
(Following a better moral example) It is a dreadful thing to imitate the bad, and to be unwilling to imitate the good.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-4cf31039c21f0d7ecdd09d74.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4cf31039c21f0d7ecdd09d74.body:
(Self-knowledge before other people’s affairs) It is a shameful thing for a man to be employed about the affairs of others, but to be ignorant of his own.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-54798f1827d3982aa219a39e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-54798f1827d3982aa219a39e.body:
(Effort and willingness to become better) To be always intending to act renders action imperfect.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-051132ceda01f774471036d4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-051132ceda01f774471036d4.body:
(The difference between moral words and deeds) Fraudulent men, and such as are only seemingly good, do all things in words and nothing in deeds.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-7c4796b62ddbc695dfa56692.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7c4796b62ddbc695dfa56692.body:
(Wealth, wisdom, and virtue) He is a blessed man who has both property and intellect, for he will use them well in such things as are proper.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-11cc40586cdbebf6fbb72358.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-11cc40586cdbebf6fbb72358.body:
(Knowledge of the good as a basis for moral judgment) The ignorance of what is excellent is the cause of error.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-c4ae2db997533f875cb23314.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c4ae2db997533f875cb23314.body:
(Shame, conscience, and self-respect) Prior to the performance of base things, a man should reverence himself.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-4d977ce376af9982bd324832.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4d977ce376af9982bd324832.body:
(The ability to listen and learn from others) A man given to contradiction, and very attentive to trifles, is naturally unadapted to learn what is proper.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-69e77a83d9105397a4a4df1a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-69e77a83d9105397a4a4df1a.body:
(The ability to listen and learn from others) Continually to speak without being willing to hear, is arrogance.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-73e7a7f1b652266f6b12dad1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-73e7a7f1b652266f6b12dad1.body:
(Trust and caution in relationships) It is necessary to guard against a depraved man, lest he should take advantage of opportunity.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-93d141f8fa9015c81a4c94b4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-93d141f8fa9015c81a4c94b4.body:
(Striving for virtue without envy) An envious man is the cause of molestation to himself, as to an enemy.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-d3363861a33fce04a2d84af0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d3363861a33fce04a2d84af0.body:
(Justice and moral conduct) Not only he is an enemy who acts unjustly, but even he who deliberates about so acting.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-0c619d91c17dbbbf5715ca81.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0c619d91c17dbbbf5715ca81.body:
(Hostility among relatives) The enmity of relations is far more bitter than that of strangers.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-5a9a0d0ea66c46556cf3889f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5a9a0d0ea66c46556cf3889f.body:
(Trust and caution in relationships) Conduct yourself to all men without suspicion; and be accommodating and cautious in your behaviour.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-6dd6a6dbd1371f0b85de4f42.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6dd6a6dbd1371f0b85de4f42.body:
(Giving, help, and gratitude) It is proper to receive favours, at the same time determining that the retribution shall surpass the gift.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-581510695047591a9f515220.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-581510695047591a9f515220.body:
(Giving, help, and gratitude) When about to bestow a favour, previously consider him who is to receive it, lest being a fraudulent character he should return evil for good.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-89f01cf1ecdebbac57a4e375.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-89f01cf1ecdebbac57a4e375.body:
(Giving, help, and gratitude) Small favours seasonably bestowed, become things of the greatest consequence to those who receive them.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-0b69184be6ecc2d53118c2a2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0b69184be6ecc2d53118c2a2.body:
(Giving, help, and gratitude) Honours with wise men are capable of effecting the greatest things, if at the same time they understand that they are honoured.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-c53c8bccea52ccfd06b0ace4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c53c8bccea52ccfd06b0ace4.body:
(Giving, help, and gratitude) The beneficent man is one who does not look to retribution, but who deliberately intends to do well.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-9693523660280420950e88a7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9693523660280420950e88a7.body:
(True friendship and how it is tested) Many that appear to be friends are not, and others, who do not appear to be friends, are so.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-5ae8631ba5e8d03e39f3eccd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5ae8631ba5e8d03e39f3eccd.body:
(True friendship and how it is tested) The friendship of one wise man is better than that of every fool,
Democritus (attributed)

advice-038f6641c5c8d4ac270bacd8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-038f6641c5c8d4ac270bacd8.body:
(True friendship and how it is tested) He is unworthy to live who has not one worthy friend.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-f488f31ba51f9939ab36d595.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f488f31ba51f9939ab36d595.body:
(True friendship and how it is tested) Many turn from their friends, if, from affluence, they fall into adversity.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-1dbaa00674e0dbf31d1d67ce.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1dbaa00674e0dbf31d1d67ce.body:
(Moderation in desires and pleasures) The equal is beautiful in everything; but excess and defect to me do not appear to be so.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-e81f42426b33998e9e3f6242.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e81f42426b33998e9e3f6242.body:
(True friendship and how it is tested) He who loves no one does not appear to me to be loved by any one.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-8776d1986ab79183c444102a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8776d1986ab79183c444102a.body:
(The strengths and experience of old age) He is an agreeable old man who is facetious, and abounds in interesting anecdote.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-5240487e931485ee32e7c128.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5240487e931485ee32e7c128.body:
(Outward beauty and inner worth) The beauty of the body is merely animal unless supported by intellect.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-1be17d1863e6d56d8492b5f7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1be17d1863e6d56d8492b5f7.body:
(True friendship and how it is tested) To find a friend in prosperity, is very easy; but in adversity, it is the most difficult of all things.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-d6c3db00b36c0aa3491cb7c0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d6c3db00b36c0aa3491cb7c0.body:
(True friendship and how it is tested) Not all relations are friends, but those who accord with what is mutually advantageous.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-b9f7917c253435765215bd68.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b9f7917c253435765215bd68.body:
(Compassion for others’ misfortunes and mistakes) Since we are men, it is becoming, not to deride, but bewail, the calamities of men.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-a2251f8c1c172d7a50818992.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a2251f8c1c172d7a50818992.body:
(Living beings’ desire for the good) Good scarcely presents itself, even to those who investigate it; but evil is obvious without investigation.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-dbb08d1b58e2ab61ace18d88.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-dbb08d1b58e2ab61ace18d88.body:
(True friendship and how it is tested) Men who delight to blame others are not naturally adapted to friendship.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-d2919a02dcf7418cab231daf.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d2919a02dcf7418cab231daf.body:
(Ancient patriarchal views of women’s roles) A woman should not be given to loquacity; for it is a dreadful thing.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-3c5384681b0babfef60d5a36.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3c5384681b0babfef60d5a36.body:
(Ancient patriarchal views of women’s roles) To be governed by a woman is the extremity of insolence and unmanliness.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-57917e2ba0471d0d27118e53.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-57917e2ba0471d0d27118e53.body:
(Contemplation of the beautiful) It is the property of a divine intellect to be always intently thinking about the beautiful.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-d0e776a61c4c3bab4c4902eb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d0e776a61c4c3bab4c4902eb.body:
(The divine and human virtue) He who believes that Divinity beholds all things, will not sin either secretly or openly.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-8672654d3c2ee5d5c9f2d7fa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-8672654d3c2ee5d5c9f2d7fa.body:
(Reason, wisdom, and mere learning) Those who praise the unwise do them a great injury.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-7ca43f36e81694658a23dec7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7ca43f36e81694658a23dec7.body:
(Praise, flattery, and fair assessment) It is better to be praised by another than by oneself.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-23a97580df10cfb5aadc6bba.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-23a97580df10cfb5aadc6bba.body:
(Praise, flattery, and fair assessment) If you cannot reconcile to yourself the praises you receive, think that you are flattered.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-21a641468133497a609adcfc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-21a641468133497a609adcfc.body:
(The limits of certain knowledge) In reality we know nothing about anything; for each person, opinion is formed by the influences that reach him.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-128599e957ce0db181f90ce5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-128599e957ce0db181f90ce5.body:
(The limits of certain knowledge) It is difficult to discover what each thing is in reality.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-bfe1ea9074de311eccabf0bc.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bfe1ea9074de311eccabf0bc.body:
(Ancient atomism: atoms and the void) Sweetness is a matter of convention, and so are bitterness, heat, cold, and color; in reality there are atoms and the void.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-a4e885ad9a24c9fca95070f5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a4e885ad9a24c9fca95070f5.body:
(The relation between sensory and rational knowledge) There are two kinds of knowledge: one genuine, the other obscure. Sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch belong to the obscure kind; genuine knowledge is distinct from them.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-1a12f1c98bc3686d9b4e79b3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1a12f1c98bc3686d9b4e79b3.body:
(Divine ecstasy and inspiration) Whatever a poet writes with inspiration and a sacred breath is exceedingly beautiful.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-ea90a07d7dec39a23e64ccd3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ea90a07d7dec39a23e64ccd3.body:
(The rule of passions over the soul) Medicine treats the diseases of the body; wisdom frees the soul from its passions.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-34e122d0e1944696d6f38a9e.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-34e122d0e1944696d6f38a9e.body:
(Learning, experience, and wise guidance) Nature and teaching resemble one another. Teaching reshapes a person, and by reshaping him it creates his nature.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-4992c62310de7c760608df48.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4992c62310de7c760608df48.body:
(The human being as a small cosmos) A human being is a small world.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-85db6974440deaf2c1c9f123.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-85db6974440deaf2c1c9f123.body:
(The limits of certain knowledge) In reality we know nothing, for truth lies in the depths.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-fef39a41224d7b29fd3de10b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-fef39a41224d7b29fd3de10b.body:
(The value of understanding causes) I would rather discover one explanation of a cause than possess the kingdom of Persia.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-78656dbe1e589a02588c8c84.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-78656dbe1e589a02588c8c84.body:
(Responsibility for one’s own mistakes) People have made an image of chance to excuse their own lack of judgment. Chance seldom conflicts with intelligence; clear judgment guides most things in life.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-99d5e5c96f5da78e87553e90.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-99d5e5c96f5da78e87553e90.body:
(The relation between sensory and rational knowledge) The senses say to the mind: Poor mind, you take your evidence from us and then overthrow us! Our overthrow is your own defeat.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-f18606dae0df29526a2cd5bd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-f18606dae0df29526a2cd5bd.body:
(Music’s emergence through abundance) Music did not arise from necessity; it came into being from a surplus of resources.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-cfacdfce13e8cdf06deaac66.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cfacdfce13e8cdf06deaac66.body:
(The difference between moral words and deeds) Speech is the shadow of action.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-2c40867bbc20ee567c985237.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2c40867bbc20ee567c985237.body:
(Inner joy and the value of the present) Learn to find your pleasures within yourself.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-58c70d5e48365f5851f49f70.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-58c70d5e48365f5851f49f70.body:
(Learning, experience, and wise guidance) We have become pupils of the animals in important matters: of the spider in weaving and mending, of the swallow in building, and of the singing birds in song.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-e6cd7db70641c5a77a3bfcf4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e6cd7db70641c5a77a3bfcf4.body:
(Ancient atomism: atoms and the void) Being exists no more than nonbeing: body exists no more than the void.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-884be6ccf67fd33e979befd0.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-884be6ccf67fd33e979befd0.body:
(Practice, effort, and perseverance) Pursue the labors from which great and splendid deeds arise.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-3af5084b422e5e1c40798ff7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-3af5084b422e5e1c40798ff7.body:
(The rule of passions over the soul) If the body sued the soul for the pains and injuries it had suffered throughout life, I would condemn the soul: it has damaged the body through neglect, weakened it through drunkenness, and ruined it through the pursuit of pleasures.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-b9653007aa6e55c6a425b733.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b9653007aa6e55c6a425b733.body:
(Moderation, self-knowledge, and wisdom) A life without wisdom, self-restraint, and reverence is not merely a bad life; it is a long dying.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-2fc6cb9fe6c1bb51a5e7abb9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2fc6cb9fe6c1bb51a5e7abb9.body:
(Learning, experience, and wise guidance) Do not be eager to know everything, lest you become ignorant of everything.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-9fbc94daf82c7415b6d83ca9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9fbc94daf82c7415b6d83ca9.body:
(Happiness and the condition of the soul) Happiness and unhappiness belong to the soul.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-4bba4092659af6921b94d456.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4bba4092659af6921b94d456.body:
(Happiness and the condition of the soul) Happiness does not dwell in cattle or in gold. The soul is the dwelling place of our fortune.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-24d71cc35f58d5139009ec82.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-24d71cc35f58d5139009ec82.body:
(External goods and knowing how to use them) The same things can bring us good or harm. Deep water is useful in many ways, yet it is dangerous; learning to swim provides a remedy.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-e9969d38bfeb689ecf799991.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e9969d38bfeb689ecf799991.body:
(External goods and knowing how to use them) Good things can bring harm when a person does not know how to manage them. Do not blame the good things; use what is good to defend yourself against what is bad.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-e229de3a3e9fa48841bfa726.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e229de3a3e9fa48841bfa726.body:
(Justice and moral conduct) A cheerful person, moved toward just and lawful actions, rejoices both waking and asleep. Whoever disregards justice and fails to do what ought to be done is troubled by fear and self-reproach whenever he remembers it.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-9fa509a76abacf42f46c778a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9fa509a76abacf42f46c778a.body:
(External goods and knowing how to use them) The gods give human beings good things, not harmful ones. People fall into harm through their own blindness and lack of understanding.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-cc26e70b1a3e332d278ba744.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cc26e70b1a3e332d278ba744.body:
(Uncertain fortune and unfounded hopes) Fortune gives generously but cannot be relied on. Nature is sufficient to itself: its smaller certainty is stronger than the larger promises of hope.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-0cda17f7f661b7dcbf051152.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0cda17f7f661b7dcbf051152.body:
(The difference between moral words and deeds) Fine words cannot conceal a bad deed, nor can slander spoil a good one.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-5099b4cc2173cca83e2dfe4f.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5099b4cc2173cca83e2dfe4f.body:
(The harm of an overindulgent upbringing) Ease is the worst teacher of the young: it produces the pleasures from which wrongdoing grows.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-b609522913a06895f9044758.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b609522913a06895f9044758.body:
(Practice, effort, and perseverance) Children cannot learn letters, music, or athletics without effort, nor can they learn the respect that holds virtue together.
Democritus (attributed)

advice-af6d9625208982d4669facf7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
