sources.reference: Of Eating of Flesh, section 1, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-17f5941dff9931e885c7f6b1.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-17f5941dff9931e885c7f6b1.body:
(On the listener as a participant and helper) Yet it is known that even a guest has some things required of him to make him suitable and agreeable, and certainly a hearer has much more; because he ought to be a sharer in the discourse and an assistant to the speaker.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Hearing, section 14, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-bce3d9fd9380c8538f7013e5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-bce3d9fd9380c8538f7013e5.body:
(On fears produced by superstition) But of all fears, none so dozes and confounds as that of superstition.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Superstition, section 3, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-b2f63c010af4032254f323a5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b2f63c010af4032254f323a5.body:
(On truth as distinct from pleasing fiction) For real truth, though it disgust never so much, must be told as it is, without alteration; but that which is feigned in a discourse can easily yield and shift its garb from the distasteful to that which is more pleasing.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: How a Young Man Ought to Hear Poems
sources.reference: How a Young Man Ought to Hear Poems, section 2, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 2)

advice-0ddce46436c5b468a851a3d6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0ddce46436c5b468a851a3d6.body:
(On slander as a sign of ill will) For the only reason of our dislike to detraction is that we look upon it as a token of ill-will to us; and we therefore take those for our enemies that misrepresent us, because we look upon them as untrusty and disaffected.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Superstition, section 11, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-c078ca29af916be4fd55a864.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c078ca29af916be4fd55a864.body:
(On freedom grounded in rational desires) For they only live at their own will who have learned to will as they ought; and that freedom of will which appears in unconstrained appetites and unreasonable actions is mean and narrow, and accompanied with much repentance.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Hearing, section 1, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-702d8fa022cdf3652dd9e1fb.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-702d8fa022cdf3652dd9e1fb.body:
(On respect between elder and younger brothers) For, whilst the elder justly claim the privilege of pre-eminence and authority over the younger, they become troublesome and uneasy to them; and the younger, growing pert and refractory, begin to slight and contemn the elder.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 16, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-0374c3f893a52ddcd5c342a6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0374c3f893a52ddcd5c342a6.body:
(On patience while another pupil asks a question) But to wait civilly while another proposes his scruples argues a studious spirit and willingness that others should be informed, unless some sudden perturbation of mind require to be repressed or some distemper to be assuaged.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Hearing, section 12, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-31280ded6d522c0c0070da55.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-31280ded6d522c0c0070da55.body:
(On the philosophical education of a ruler) In like manner the discourses and rules of philosophy, being once deeply stamped and imprinted on the minds of great personages, will stick so close, that the prince shall seem no other than justice incarnate and animated law.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: That a Philosopher Ought Chiefly to Converse with Great Men
sources.reference: That a Philosopher Ought Chiefly to Converse with Great Men, section 4, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 2)

advice-5fdaeb1bd9ba839e32ca4bc7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5fdaeb1bd9ba839e32ca4bc7.body:
(On preserving ties during a quarrel between brothers) Again, this rule is to be observed, that, whenever any difference happens betwixt brothers, during the time of strangeness especially they hold a correspondence with one another’s friends, but by all means avoid their enemies.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 19, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-aa0e3eb9fd486ed4b3f3c01b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-aa0e3eb9fd486ed4b3f3c01b.body:
(On enemies who inflame hostility between brothers) For there are some who, like waters running among loose and chinky grounds, overthrow all familiarity and friendship; enemies to both parties, but especially bent upon the ruining of him whose weakness exposes him most to danger.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 19, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-4a02faa0be8741057358e6aa.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4a02faa0be8741057358e6aa.body:
(On a statesman's responsibility for his friends' conduct) Since friends are the living and intelligent instruments of statesmen, who ought to be so far from bearing them company in their slips and transgressions, that they must be careful they do not, even unknown to them, commit a fault.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Political Precepts, section 13, paragraph 3 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-d51e6bbcda03c867eb462a27.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d51e6bbcda03c867eb462a27.body:
(On a pupil unfairly reproved by a teacher) Or suppose he be wrongfully chidden, it is but handsome to expect the conclusion; after that he may make his defence, and desire that such freedom and violence may be reserved to repress some other misdemeanor which really deserves it.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Hearing, section 16, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-a5caf91226c071d667f462a9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a5caf91226c071d667f462a9.body:
(On family affection as a model for friendship) For a great deal of friendship in the world is really no better and no more than the mere imitation and resemblance of that first affection that Nature wrought in parents towards their children, and in their children towards one another.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 3, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-ad07182a27cd7d1c3796e91a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ad07182a27cd7d1c3796e91a.body:
(On praise that makes friendly correction acceptable) For reprehension mixed with praise, and accompanied not with opprobriousness but liberty of speech, working not animosity but remorse and repentance, appears both kind and salutary; but railing expressions do not at all beseem statesmen.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Political Precepts, section 14, paragraph 7 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-1a629f37af06d97d9cf13844.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-1a629f37af06d97d9cf13844.body:
(On tactfully declining food or drink harmful to oneself) Whereas an excuse ingeniously and dexterously made is no less acceptable than compliance.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: Rules for the Preservation of Health
sources.reference: Rules for the Preservation of Health, section 5, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-813cc5bcce6aed47089dfd31.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-813cc5bcce6aed47089dfd31.body:
(On improving one's speech through others' mistakes) We must trace out our own way of writing in the discourses of other men, as in another’s eyes we see the reflection of our own; that we may learn not to be too free in censuring others, and may use more circumspection ourselves in speaking.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Hearing, section 6, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-9097be645db647554daddd0a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9097be645db647554daddd0a.body:
(On custom that conceals cruelty to animals) But (as it seems) we are more sensible of what is done against custom than against Nature.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Eating of Flesh, section 7, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-6cb23e5762ef4a2be5c5cebd.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6cb23e5762ef4a2be5c5cebd.body:
(On the listener as a participant and helper) Neither will it become him to be severe at all turns upon every slight miscarriage or perpetually putting the speaker’s elocution and action to the test, while he himself is guilty of grosser enormities in hearing, without danger or control.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Hearing, section 14, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-0cc1610fd0d33f400dce3c0c.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-0cc1610fd0d33f400dce3c0c.body:
(On impartial assistance during civil strife) For you will not seem a stranger by not being a partaker in injustice, but a common friend to them all by your assistance; nor will you be envied for your not sharing in the calamity, when you appear equally to condole with every one of them.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Political Precepts, section 32, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-ae591f7b9e041d59a03347a3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ae591f7b9e041d59a03347a3.body:
(On receiving reproach with dignity and attention) Admonitions and reprimands ought to be taken neither altogether insensibly nor yet sheepishly.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Hearing, section 16, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-95c106e5841c07896eb78655.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-95c106e5841c07896eb78655.body:
(On fears produced by superstition) Thus do these sottish fears oftentimes convert tolerable evils into fatal and insupportable ones.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Superstition, section 8, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-9d04ace7b3d6ff716b23fd6b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9d04ace7b3d6ff716b23fd6b.body:
(On philosophy's effects on different dispositions) The effects of philosophy, however, are different according to the difference of inclinations in men.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: That a Philosopher Ought Chiefly to Converse with Great Men
sources.reference: That a Philosopher Ought Chiefly to Converse with Great Men, section 1, paragraph 3 (Goodwin edition, vol. 2)

advice-2cfe076aab2e7ce12a2c7d26.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2cfe076aab2e7ce12a2c7d26.body:
(On goods of the soul that money cannot buy) We may say the same to those that esteem so extravagantly and repute it so great a felicity to possess fair fields, stately mansion-houses, and a great deal of money lying by them,—that they were in the right, if happiness were to be bought and sold.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of the Love of Wealth, section 1, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 2)

advice-14f88a318edfa72aa0a07a18.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-14f88a318edfa72aa0a07a18.body:
(On the harm ambition does to a state) Now ambition, though it is more specious than covetousness, brings yet no less plagues into a state.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Political Precepts, section 27, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-5fca917c923fdded42a57138.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5fca917c923fdded42a57138.body:
(On entering public service with preparation and purpose) First then for the administration of state affairs, let there be laid, as a firm and solid foundation, an intention and purpose, having for its principles judgment and reason, and not any impulse from vain-glory, emulation, or want of other employment.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Political Precepts, section 2, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-2f68c8e1ff0eaeea6c2442c7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2f68c8e1ff0eaeea6c2442c7.body:
(On preventing petty quarrels between brothers) Wherefore there is no small care to be taken by brothers in subduing their passions and preventing quarrels about small matters, yielding rather for peace’s sake, and taking greater pleasure in indulging than crossing and conquering one another’s humors.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 17, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-14d3220c86981a14683887f7.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-14d3220c86981a14683887f7.body:
(On public scrutiny of a statesman's private life) For it is not possible that the vices and faults of persons in authority can be concealed in obscurity.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: A Discourse to an Unlearned Prince
sources.reference: A Discourse to an Unlearned Prince, section 7, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 4)

advice-2eef6fda3dfbd69b94cf0df8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-2eef6fda3dfbd69b94cf0df8.body:
(On maintaining marital fidelity in old age) but he who should think, that a man which has long co-habited and lived irreprehensibly with his wife ought, because he is grown old, to dismiss her and live alone, or take a concubine in her place, would have attained the utmost excess of perverseness.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: Whether an Aged Man Ought to Meddle in State Affairs
sources.reference: Whether an Aged Man Ought to Meddle in State Affairs, section 9, paragraph 5 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-ee965618271eb48c3fff4496.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ee965618271eb48c3fff4496.body:
(On seeking excellence in what is most worthy) Whereas glory that ariseth from things in themselves small and inconsiderable is inglorious and contemptible.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: How a Young Man Ought to Hear Poems
sources.reference: How a Young Man Ought to Hear Poems, section 13, paragraph 10 (Goodwin edition, vol. 2)

advice-5534ab818a5b7c0f2b309229.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5534ab818a5b7c0f2b309229.body:
(On the irreplaceable loss of a brother) But there is no more regaining of a lost brother, than of a hand that is cut off or an eye that is beaten out.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 7, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-db65de5f52cdc9ca96c53e78.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-db65de5f52cdc9ca96c53e78.body:
(On power that magnifies a person's vices) But power joined with a corrupt and depraved inclination adds the fuel of madness to the fire of the passions.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: A Discourse to an Unlearned Prince
sources.reference: A Discourse to an Unlearned Prince, section 6, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 4)

advice-86cb699d69ccbba33ca669ba.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-86cb699d69ccbba33ca669ba.body:
(On errors caused by trusting a speaker's authority) For many false and dangerous principles steal upon us through the authority of the speaker and our own credulity.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Hearing, section 7, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-5ef6d269356923b00798493d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-5ef6d269356923b00798493d.body:
(On a brother who has wronged his parents) For as such guilty brothers are not to be allowed in their faults, neither are they to be insulted with raillery.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 10, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-de78532e47067b1076d4cb1a.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-de78532e47067b1076d4cb1a.body:
(On mutual assistance between brothers) And this also is most manifest to every one, that the reason why Nature out of one seed and source formed two, three, and more brethren was not for difference and opposition, but that their being apart might render them the more capable of assisting one another.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 2, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-ed79aee0bd0c87ffebc0110b.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-ed79aee0bd0c87ffebc0110b.body:
(On defending a brother and thereby earning his trust in correction) Now he is the fittest person to school his brother smartly who has been a ready and earnest advocate in his behalf.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 10, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-6182ac5e7db345d322104199.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6182ac5e7db345d322104199.body:
(On testing poetic teachings by reason) Whensoever therefore any thing is spoken in poems by any noted and eminently famous man, concerning Gods or Daemons or virtue, that is absurd or harsh, he that takes such sayings for truths is thereby misled in his apprehension and corrupted with an erroneous opinion.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: How a Young Man Ought to Hear Poems
sources.reference: How a Young Man Ought to Hear Poems, section 2, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 2)

advice-b009e07751cd2365774c8e5d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-b009e07751cd2365774c8e5d.body:
(On love for parents and between brothers) For he that hates and plagues his brother can hardly forbear blaming the father who begot and the mother who bare him.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 5, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-77d6a1ac7c3d04b3e4867876.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-77d6a1ac7c3d04b3e4867876.body:
(On moderation and modesty in asking questions) Be cautious also how you ask questions yourself, or ask too often; for that betrays somewhat of conceit and ostentation.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Hearing, section 12, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-e02d41ae73e7c04b4960c0e3.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e02d41ae73e7c04b4960c0e3.body:
(On empty eloquence that gives only brief pleasure) But most Sophists in their declamations and speeches not only make use of words to veil and muffle their design; but with affected tone and softness of voice they draw aside and bewitch their followers, for the empty pleasure which they create reaping a more empty glory.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Hearing, section 7, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-756d30f25fd7482c1a1473ed.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-756d30f25fd7482c1a1473ed.body:
(On envy of one's brother's success) The elder again, being fond of superiority, are jealous of their brothers’ advancement, as though it tended to lessen them.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 16, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-d5eb44b41c8313218dfda1f6.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-d5eb44b41c8313218dfda1f6.body:
(On a pupil asking the speaker a meaningful question) But when the speaker encourages them to propose their objections, he must take care that the question be of some consequence.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Hearing, section 10, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-290b2f9cf4225d3647e622a4.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-290b2f9cf4225d3647e622a4.body:
(On fears produced by superstition) Thus does wretched superstition bring inevitably upon itself by its fancies even those calamities which it has once escaped.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Superstition, section 4, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-005a3877494d60ea67fe5aed.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-005a3877494d60ea67fe5aed.body:
(On envious people scorning someone retired from public life) For envious persons do not so much assail those who contend against them, as they do by contempt insult over such as retire.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: Whether an Aged Man Ought to Meddle in State Affairs
sources.reference: Whether an Aged Man Ought to Meddle in State Affairs, section 7, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-9c2d6f544b96c76d02f333b2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9c2d6f544b96c76d02f333b2.body:
(On tolerating a brother's familiar shortcomings) But brothers would do well to bear with one another’s familiar failings, rather than to adventure upon the trial of strangers.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 8, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-e819950b16ed7eac8af1b063.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-e819950b16ed7eac8af1b063.body:
(On the deceptive charm of beautiful speech) The very expression, if sweet and full and representing things with some pomp and greatness, has a secret power to impose upon us.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Hearing, section 7, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-4fbd985560893b0450d9c7f9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-4fbd985560893b0450d9c7f9.body:
(On sharing public responsibilities among people) For as the division of the hand into fingers has not weakened it, but rendered it more commodious and instrumental for the uses to which it serves; so he who in the administration of a state gives part of the affairs to others renders the action more efficacious by communicating it.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Political Precepts, section 15, paragraph 4 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-794ce7e4ff5dc15ab71465c2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-794ce7e4ff5dc15ab71465c2.body:
(On an elderly statesman mentoring the young) But if it were for nothing else, yet ought an old man to manage in public affairs, that he may instruct and teach those who are young.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: Whether an Aged Man Ought to Meddle in State Affairs
sources.reference: Whether an Aged Man Ought to Meddle in State Affairs, section 12, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-6022df61b6cee08098141716.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-6022df61b6cee08098141716.body:
(On avoiding in advance the temptations of one's weakness) And after the same manner must the man that is apt to be drunken forearm himself against that vice; and he that is given to wantonness, against lust, as Agesilaus refused to receive a kiss from a beautiful person addressing to him, and Cyrus would not so much as endure to see Panthea.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: How a Young Man Ought to Hear Poems
sources.reference: How a Young Man Ought to Hear Poems, section 11, paragraph 8 (Goodwin edition, vol. 2)

advice-785d083f56cdc529970fcf46.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-785d083f56cdc529970fcf46.body:
(On a brother defending his innocent brother before their parents) But suppose the brother wrongfully charged, it is fitting he should be obsequious to his parents in all other things whatsoever, and to bear with their angry humors; but a defence made before them for a brother that suffers by slander and false accusation is unreprovable and very good.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 10, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-33f5e3e433b9d170bd5d0039.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-33f5e3e433b9d170bd5d0039.body:
(On taking good care of one's health) When another is in sickness, let it teach us how valuable a treasure health is, which we ought to keep and preserve with all possible care.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: Rules for the Preservation of Health
sources.reference: Rules for the Preservation of Health, section 15, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-c00aded322aa3966789d7e64.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c00aded322aa3966789d7e64.body:
(On admitting fault and forgiving between brothers) Now the acknowledgments of the offender and the begging pardon for the crime express a kind and amicable nature no less than the remitting of it.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 18, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-a43763a6f47e1f4e6127910d.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a43763a6f47e1f4e6127910d.body:
(On generously encouraging young people's best qualities) For young men indeed always venerate and follow those who increase and cherish the neatness and generosity of their disposition without any envy.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: Whether an Aged Man Ought to Meddle in State Affairs
sources.reference: Whether an Aged Man Ought to Meddle in State Affairs, section 24, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-7afbce464db50af815901110.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7afbce464db50af815901110.body:
(On power that magnifies a person's vices) And as amongst empty vessels it cannot easily be discerned which are whole and which are leaky, but by the pouring in of any liquor; so corrupt and exulcerated minds, after the infusion of power, are not able to contain it, but immediately overflow with concupiscence, anger, arrogance, and folly.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: A Discourse to an Unlearned Prince
sources.reference: A Discourse to an Unlearned Prince, section 7, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 4)

advice-a832fcf172023d123a26ded2.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a832fcf172023d123a26ded2.body:
(On mistaken judgments intensified by passion) And as a dislocation is the more painful when it is attended with a bruise, so are the perversions of our understandings, when attended with passion.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Superstition, section 1, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-a6ab6987fdb2b9d6b124aaba.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a6ab6987fdb2b9d6b124aaba.body:
(On pointlessly exhausting oneself through envy and chasing glory) For most men upon accident torment themselves with watchings, journeyings, and running up and down, for no advantage and with no good design, but only that they may do others an injury, or because they envy them or are competitors with them, or because they hunt after unprofitable and empty glory.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: Rules for the Preservation of Health
sources.reference: Rules for the Preservation of Health, section 24, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-c2814a02683274dcb5ec5e91.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-c2814a02683274dcb5ec5e91.body:
(On respect between elder and younger brothers) Therefore, as we judge of a kindness that it ought to be valued more by the party obliged than by him who bestows it, so, if the elder would be persuaded to set less by his seniority and the younger to esteem it more, there would be no supercilious slighting and contemptuous carriage betwixt them.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 16, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-a32a15de5d0892dd82640152.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-a32a15de5d0892dd82640152.body:
(On superstitious fear of a lunar eclipse) There was nothing formidable in the inter-position of the earth betwixt the sun and the moon, neither was there any thing dreadful in the shadow’s meeting the moon at the proper time: no, the dreadfulness lay here, that the darkness of ignorance should blind and befool a man’s reason at a time when he had most occasion to use it.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Superstition, section 8, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 1)

advice-547fb6ec1773b81f12b24457.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-547fb6ec1773b81f12b24457.body:
(On the philosophical education of a ruler) In like manner, he who instructs an ordinary man makes him to pass his life decently and with comfort; but he who instructs a prince, by correcting his errors and clearing his understanding, is a philosopher for the public, by rectifying the very mould and model by which whole nations are formed and regulated.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: That a Philosopher Ought Chiefly to Converse with Great Men
sources.reference: That a Philosopher Ought Chiefly to Converse with Great Men, section 2, paragraph 7 (Goodwin edition, vol. 2)

advice-73e837cccf8ddec8be1206e5.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-73e837cccf8ddec8be1206e5.body:
(On the moral value of attentive reading of poetry) Again, boys may be instructed, by reading the poets as they ought, to draw something that is useful and profitable even from those passages that are most suspected as wicked and absurd; as the bee is taught by Nature to gather the sweetest and most pleasant honey from the harshest flowers and sharpest thorns.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.work: How a Young Man Ought to Hear Poems
sources.reference: How a Young Man Ought to Hear Poems, section 12, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 2)

advice-7efae01e41b9b90b05c53035.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-7efae01e41b9b90b05c53035.body:
(On admitting fault and forgiving between brothers) Wherefore it is not for us to slight the anger of those whom we have incensed through our folly, neither should they be so implacable as to refuse an humble submission; but rather, where we have done the wrong, we should endeavor to prevent a distaste by the earliest and humblest acknowledgments and impetrations of pardon, and where we have received any, to be as ready and free in the forgiving of it.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Of Brotherly Love, section 18, paragraph 2 (Goodwin edition, vol. 3)

advice-cb110321bab63fe97c65bcf8.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-cb110321bab63fe97c65bcf8.body:
(On a brief and calm reply to an insult) But since many persons can hardly contain themselves on such occasions, and since railers have often their mouths not impertinently stopped by replies; let the answer be short and pithy, not showing any indignation or bitterness of anger, but mildness joined with raillery and gracefulness, yet somewhat tart and biting.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Political Precepts, section 14, paragraph 8 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)

advice-9403fe64e54944b8068122d9.title: Philosophers’ aphorisms
advice-9403fe64e54944b8068122d9.body:
(On public benefactions within one's means, without debt) But if your estate be but indifferent, and by its centre and circumference confined to your necessary use, it is neither ungenerous nor base to confess your poverty and give place to such as are provided for those honorary expenses, and not, by taking up money on usury, to render yourself at the same time both miserable and ridiculous by such services.
Plutarch

sources.author: Plutarch
sources.reference: Political Precepts, section 31, paragraph 1 (Goodwin edition, vol. 5)
